# Ada Calendar & Tasks

Provider-agnostic calendar/tasks tools for Ada — Google adapter live, CalDAV/MS Graph pluggable via registry

## File Path
`apps/ssot.apps.ada-calendar.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Ada Calendar & Tasks
subtitle: Provider-agnostic calendar/tasks tools for Ada — Google adapter live, CalDAV/MS Graph pluggable via registry
icon: 📅
sections:
  - title: Concept
    icon: "💡"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Provider-agnostic tools
        text: "Gemini-visible tools (calendar_*, tasks_*, plan_day) never name a provider. backend/calendar_providers.py defines CalendarProvider/TasksProvider protocols and normalized CalendarEvent/Task models; adapters normalize each service."
      - label: Registry-driven
        text: "The calendar: block below is rendered to ~/.config/ada/calendar.json by scripts/ada/render-calendar-providers.py (ADA_CALENDAR_FILE overrides). Same pattern as memory banks: instances: + status: filter per ADA_INSTANCE_ID; unknown adapter on an active provider fails loudly."
      - label: Aggregate reads, routed writes
        text: "read: aggregate fans out list calls across active providers and merges; write: names the default write provider. Explicit 'provider:calendar_id' overrides both. Events are never replicated between providers — aggregation is the sync model."
      - label: Qualified ids
        text: "Everything returned to the model carries provider-qualified ids ('google:primary/abc123', 'google:@default/xyz') so delete/complete calls route back to the right adapter."
  - title: Auth Model
    icon: "🔐"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: OAuth client
        text: "Reuses the Desktop-app client in ~/.config/secrets/google_credentials.json — project gen-lang-client-0694401188, the same project as GEMINI_API_KEY. Calendar API + Tasks API must be enabled on that project."
      - label: Token file
        text: "Per-ada refresh token at ~/.config/secrets/ada-google-calendar-token.json (override ADA_GOOGLE_TOKEN_FILE or per-provider token_file). Minted by scripts/ada/google-calendar-auth.py; scopes: calendar.readonly, calendar.events, tasks."
      - label: Consent screen
        text: "OAuth consent screen must be Publishing status=production — 'Testing' status expires refresh tokens after 7 days."
      - label: API key is not auth
        text: "GEMINI_API_KEY identifies the project for billing only; it can never read user calendar data. Calendar/Tasks require OAuth."
  - title: Tool Contract
    icon: "🛠️"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Reads (ungated)
        text: "calendar_list_calendars, calendar_list_events, calendar_freebusy, tasks_list, plan_day — NON_BLOCKING, partial results include per-provider errors list."
      - label: Writes (confirmed=true)
        text: "calendar_create_event, calendar_delete_event, tasks_add, tasks_complete — in CALENDAR_WRITE_TOOLS; _check_calendar_write_allowed requires confirmed=true and honors ADA_READ_ONLY."
      - label: Dispatch
        text: "ToolRunner.calendar lazily loads CalendarService from the rendered registry; None means not configured on this instance (tools return a 'not configured' error, not a crash)."
      - label: Timezone
        text: "All 'today/tomorrow' parsing and naive datetimes resolve in ADA_TIMEZONE (default Asia/Bangkok)."
  - title: Adapter Capability Matrix
    icon: "🧩"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: google (live)
        text: "backend/google_calendar.py — httpx-native Calendar API v3 + Tasks API. Events list/create/delete, freebusy, task lists/tasks/complete. tasks: true."
      - label: caldav (planned)
        text: "python-caldav covers iCloud + Fastmail + Nextcloud in one adapter. iCloud tasks = VTODO (Apple Reminders). No freebusy on iCloud. Credentials pattern mirrors icloud-mcp (app-specific password)."
      - label: msgraph (planned)
        text: "Microsoft Graph for Outlook/Hotmail events + To Do tasks via msal OAuth. Build only when an Outlook calendar is actually in play."
      - label: home-assistant (rejected as primary)
        text: "HA calendar.*/todo.* integrations could proxy providers, but create-event support is per-integration and weaker; kept as a possible read adapter, not the primary path. See decision record ada-calendar-provider-backend."
  - title: Files
    icon: "📁"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: backend/calendar_providers.py
        text: "Models, protocols, CalendarService (registry load, aggregate reads, write routing, plan_day)."
      - label: backend/google_calendar.py
        text: "Google adapter: refresh-token exchange, events, freebusy, tasks."
      - label: backend/tool_runner.py
        text: "CALENDAR_WRITE_TOOLS gate + calendar_*/tasks_*/plan_day methods."
      - label: backend/realtime_provider.py
        text: "function_declarations + instruction paragraph (calendar workflow playbook)."
      - label: scripts/ada/google-calendar-auth.py
        text: "One-time consent flow + --check verifier + --host scp to runtime hosts."
      - label: scripts/ada/render-calendar-providers.py
        text: "SSOT -> ~/.config/ada/calendar.json renderer (--host, --check), same shape as render-memory-banks.py."
  - title: Runbooks
    icon: "📖"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: ssot.ada.howto.yml
        text: "google_calendar_reauth, add_calendar_provider, calendar_tool_debug live in the ada howto SSOT."
  - title: Known Issues
    icon: "⚠️"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Google Tasks limits
        text: "Tasks API due is date-only (time ignored); no subtasks/recurrence exposed in the normalized Task model."
      - label: All-day end date
        text: "Google all-day events use exclusive end dates — pass the day after for a one-day event; the adapter passes dates through verbatim."

# Machine-readable registry — rendered to ~/.config/ada/calendar.json by
# scripts/ada/render-calendar-providers.py. Edit here, re-render, deploy.

  read: aggregate

  providers:
    google:
      adapter: google

        - 3c31ljkn7vs1ea05vt9sd1dfdg@group.calendar.google.com           # CallTrack

        - lmniec088vkvphpjdluvl1nmn4@group.calendar.google.com           # Jobs (periodics)
        - 28124f2c289d2d53faeef2ab3e30c5e81255d5a51163660218af97ae9e24f0d7@group.calendar.google.com  # Jarvis Reminders
        - e468a444120e07570cdd58c5123052af2612f8280a5591c028479a514520adc5@group.calendar.google.com  # ${GOOGLE_CALENDAR_JARVIS_CALENDAR_NAME} (literal name — old script bug)
        - cd18e8b64e3bc42c4bae1af349cfab2a1f329c76817595e5339600d150ba1de9@group.calendar.google.com  # Noble Park - Working
        - edadaa3903a82265a3684223a9dedcf741ef689f3c66f910f66d5440fce45abe@group.calendar.google.com  # Noble Park - Planning
        - 5376a2affe56e30e7fabea676c42bdaab52326e6d9b0556e478d6597fdacde82@group.calendar.google.com  # Noble Park - Event
        - 12dfebf81f112ab1b42ca73c650b896c892b7717dab8590756cec35cca64a0bc@group.calendar.google.com  # Noble A - Working
        - 332136e2292f48b7d97a9bb3a3c9b84359e44d550f8b1dba75376c7f39f8726e@group.calendar.google.com  # Noble A - Planning

config:
```

# Ada Memory Audit Model

What is recorded when memory-bank documents change — storage-level revisions, semantic status links, and the planned write log

## File Path
`apps/ssot.apps.ada-memory-audit.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Ada Memory Audit Model
subtitle: What is recorded when memory-bank documents change — storage-level revisions, semantic status links, and the planned write log
icon: 🕵️
sections:
  - title: Storage-Level Audit (exists today)
    icon: "🗄️"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Revisions
        text: MDDB keeps a revision per document update — old content is retained in the DB (12k+ revisions observed in stats). Every correct-in-place write is therefore auditable at storage level.
      - label: Access paths
        text: "HTTP: POST /v1/revisions (list), POST /v1/revisions/restore. Builtin MCP tools in current mddbd: list_revisions, restore_revision, truncate_revisions. Caveat: verify the deployed mddbd version exposes them — older MCP surfaces did not."
      - label: Retention
        text: max_revisions on collection creation caps history per doc (0 = unlimited). Bank collections should keep unlimited until size demands otherwise — memory corrections are the audit trail.
  - title: Semantic-Level Audit (designed)
    icon: "📄"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Status field
        text: 'status: active | superseded | retracted | expired on every doc — recall filters on active, so history stays queryable via metadata filters without polluting answers.'
      - label: Linkage
        text: supersedes / superseded_by doc keys preserve the chain when a fact is re-scoped or misattributed — provenance is explicit, not inferred.
      - label: Provenance fields
        text: 'source: voice | manual | import, plus valid_from / last_verified — shows where a memory came from and when it was last confirmed true.'
  - title: Gap — Write Log
    icon: "⚠️"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: What's missing
        text: No record of WHO wrote WHAT, WHEN, via WHICH tool. Revisions capture content deltas but not actor/tool/session.
      - label: Option A — meta fields
        text: Add written_by (tool name), session_id, updated_by to each doc's meta. Cheap, rides existing writes; weakest for multi-actor forensics.
      - label: Option B — audit collection
        text: "Dedicated ada-ha-bank-audit-{instance} collection: one doc per write {ts, instance, tool, bank, key, verb, old_status, new_status}. Queryable, but adds a write per write — decide before runtime lands."
      - label: Recommendation
        text: Start with Option A meta fields (written_by/session_id) — revisit Option B if cross-session forensics are actually needed.
  - title: Not Audited
    icon: "📓"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: NotebookLM tier
        text: "Append-only archive — no edit audit beyond 'Correction: <key> (date)' source titles. Acceptable: NLM is historical, MDDB is the answer."
      - label: Registry changes
        text: Bank definition changes are audited by git history on this repo (SSOT), not by MDDB.
config:
  version: 1
  created: "2026-09-19"
  updated: "2026-09-19"
  maintainer: tony
  status: draft
  deployment: mn01

```

# Ada Memory Banks

Declarative registry of named memory banks for Ada (MDDB fast tier + optional NotebookLM deep tier), each assignable per instance (tony/michael)

## File Path
`apps/ssot.apps.ada-memory-banks.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Ada Memory Banks
subtitle: Declarative registry of named memory banks for Ada (MDDB fast tier + optional NotebookLM deep tier), each assignable per instance (tony/michael)
icon: 🧠
sections:
  - title: Concept
    icon: "💡"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Memory bank
        text: A named logical memory store. Each bank owns one MDDB collection (fast recall/write tier) and optionally one NotebookLM notebook (deep-recall/archive tier). Banks are the user-facing knowledge layer; the internal operational collections (ada-ha-snapshots-*, ada-ha-events-*, ada-ha-device-*, ada-ha-recall-summary-*) stay unchanged.
      - label: Assignment
        text: Every bank lists the instance IDs allowed to use it. A service loads only banks whose instances list contains its own ADA_INSTANCE_ID. Shared banks appear in both tony and michael; per-instance or single-instance banks are private.
      - label: Identity rule
        text: Same fail-fast policy as ADA_INSTANCE_ID — a bank that cannot resolve its collection name or is not assigned to the running instance is skipped loudly (logged + surfaced via /api/health degraded flag), never silently routed elsewhere.
  - title: Naming
    icon: "🏷️"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Shared banks
        text: "MDDB collection ada-ha-bank-<name> with no instance suffix. Example: ada-ha-bank-general."
      - label: Per-instance banks
        text: "scope: instance expands {instance} in mddb_collection, e.g. ada-ha-bank-personal-{instance} → ada-ha-bank-personal-tony."
      - label: Separation
        text: The ada-ha-bank-* prefix keeps curated knowledge distinct from operational telemetry (snapshots/events/device-*) so recall and retention policies can differ.
  - title: Document Metadata
    icon: "📄"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: kind
        text: fact | preference | person | procedure | note — drives recall ranking and summary prompts.
      - label: scope
        text: shared | tony | michael — mirrors the bank assignment; private transcripts, secrets, and live sensor state never enter shared banks.
      - label: confidence
        text: 0.0–1.0; low-confidence hits escalate to the NotebookLM tier instead of being spoken as fact.
      - label: validity
        text: valid_from and last_verified (ISO dates) let recall prefer fresh facts and flag stale ones.
      - label: applies_to
        text: Optional entity_id/area list tying a fact to HA objects (e.g. cover.gate_motor).
      - label: subject / attribute
        text: Optional "what it's about" + "which aspect" pair (e.g. gate-remote / location) — the join key that lets search find differently-phrased facts about the same thing for update/conflict detection.
      - label: status
        text: active | superseded | retracted | expired — recall surfaces only active docs; superseded docs link via supersedes/superseded_by keys.
      - label: valid_until
        text: 'Optional TTL date ("pump is being repaired this week") — expiry is applied lazily at recall time as status: expired.'
      - label: source
        text: voice | manual | import — provenance for audits and later consolidation.
  - title: Runtime Wiring
    icon: "⚙️"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Registry file
        text: Authored here in SSOT; rendered to ADA_MEMORY_BANKS_FILE (default ~/.config/ada/memory-banks.json) on mn01 and tony-dell at deploy time. Services read the file, filter by ada_instance_id().
      - label: backend/memory_banks.py
        text: "Planned module in ada-pi: loads the registry, resolves mddb_collection ({instance} expansion), exposes banks(), collection_for(bank), notebook_for(bank). Fail-fast on missing registry for any bank marked required."
      - label: ada_remember tool
        text: Planned Gemini tool ada_remember(bank, text) → writes to the bank's MDDB collection with metadata above; optionally mirrors to the bank's NotebookLM notebook as a text source.
      - label: Recall routing
        text: ada_session_recall gains a bank param (superset of today's group). MDDB semantic search on the bank's collection first; low confidence or explicit detail requests escalate to the bank's notebook (~20s, background) — same tiered policy as now.
      - label: Introspection
        text: GET /api/memory/banks returns the banks assigned to the running instance with collection/notebook resolution for debugging.
      - label: ada-pi-pwa
        text: Runs ADA_INSTANCE_ID=tony, so it automatically sees every bank assigned to tony — consistent with today's shared-memory behavior.
  - title: NotebookLM Tier
    icon: "📓"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: notebooklm_group
        text: Optional group name resolved per-instance via NOTEBOOKLM_NOTEBOOK_IDS_JSON (memory/infra/apps/kb/ops). Use this when each instance should keep its own deep-tier notebook.
      - label: notebooklm_id
        text: Optional literal notebook ID for a genuinely shared deep tier (one notebook both instances read). Mutually exclusive with notebooklm_group.
      - label: 'Gotcha: key scopes'
        text: 'notebooklm-rest enforces a per-key notebook allowlist (NOTEBOOKLM_REST_KEY_SCOPES in ~/.config/secrets/notebooklm-rest-api.env on tony-dell). A group mapping alone is not enough — each new notebook must also be added to the calling key''s scope or every call returns 403. Michael''s set: memory=1c12d5c8…, infra=31fba197…, apps=1aa3e5be…, kb=5f52938d…, ops=7a970489… (created 2026-09-22).'
      - label: Back-compat
        text: NOTEBOOKLM_NOTEBOOK_IDS_JSON keeps working; a recall group with no matching bank falls back to today's behavior and maps to a default ada-ha-bank-<group> collection if ever persisted.
  - title: Write & Update
    icon: "✏️"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Find-then-update
        text: Updates require a read first — ada_memory_search returns doc keys. A match gets corrected in place (same key, revision +1, last_verified bumped); no match creates a new doc with a derived slug key.
      - label: Three update verbs
        text: "Correct = overwrite same key in place (MDDB revision history is the audit trail). Supersede = write a new key, mark the old doc status: superseded with superseded_by/supersedes links. Retract = status: retracted, preferred over delete; hard delete only for privacy/secret leaks."
      - label: Per-bank write policy
        text: "writable gates writes entirely (false = read-only bank). write_policy reuses the ToolRunner confirmed=true gate — same pattern as dangerous HA entities: confirmed = Ada must ask before writing, direct = write immediately. allowed_tools lists which write tools may touch the bank."
      - label: NotebookLM is append-only
        text: "NLM sources can't be edited, so updates are never mirrored in place — MDDB is the mutable current truth, NotebookLM is the append-only archive. On update, optionally add a 'Correction: <key> (date)' text source."
      - label: Full schema
        text: The formal meta schema and verb semantics live in ssot.apps.ada-memory-schema.yml.
  - title: Visibility
    icon: "👁️"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: public
        text: "true = served when the vault UI runs with ADA_DEPLOY=public; absent/false = tailnet-only. Deny-by-default: a bank must be consciously marked public. Applies to vault tree/note/graph metadata, not just bodies — hidden banks are dropped before any node/edge emission."
      - label: Host vs policy
        text: "ADA_DEPLOY env declares where the service runs (context, per-host); public: declares what may leave the tailnet (policy, in SSOT). See docs/ada-memory/tony-projects/public-host-plan.md."
  - title: Status
    icon: "🚦"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Registry
        text: "This file is the source of truth for bank definitions; the banks: block below is machine-readable and rendered to the runtime JSON."
      - label: Implementation
        text: "memory_banks.py, ada_remember, and bank-aware recall are LIVE (deployed 2026-09-20) — banks marked status: active are serving recall/writes."
      - label: Adjusting banks
        text: "Add/remove/rename banks by editing the banks: block; flip instances to move a bank between tony and michael; no code change needed for assignment-only edits."

banks:
  general:
    title: General knowledge
    description: Free-form facts, preferences, and "remember that…" notes
    scope: shared
    instances: [tony, michael]
    mddb_collection: ada-ha-bank-general
    notebooklm_group: memory
    notebooklm_id: null
    kinds: [fact, preference, note]
    writable: true

  home:
    title: Household knowledge
    description: Home topology, device aliases, procedures, status notices (the planned shared 'home' group)
    scope: shared

    notebooklm_group: null

    scope: instance

    scope: person
```

docs.contentMd:
# Ada Memory Document Schema & Write Semantics

Formal meta schema for memory-bank documents and the write/update verb contract used by ada_remember/ada_forget

## File Path
`apps/ssot.apps.ada-memory-schema.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Ada Memory Document Schema & Write Semantics
subtitle: Formal meta schema for memory-bank documents and the write/update verb contract used by ada_remember/ada_forget
icon: 📐
sections:
  - title: Document Meta Schema
    icon: "📄"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: kind
        text: fact | preference | person | procedure | note — drives recall ranking and summary prompts.
      - label: scope
        text: shared | tony | michael — mirrors the bank assignment; private transcripts, secrets, and live sensor state never enter shared banks.
      - label: subject / attribute
        text: "Optional 'what it's about' + 'which aspect' pair (e.g. subject: gate-remote, attribute: location). The join key for conflict detection — lets search find a differently-phrased fact about the same thing."
      - label: status
        text: 'active | superseded | retracted | expired — recall filters on status: active. Superseded docs keep superseded_by/supersedes key links; expired is applied lazily when valid_until passes.'
      - label: confidence
        text: 0.0–1.0; low-confidence hits escalate to the NotebookLM tier instead of being spoken as fact.
      - label: validity
        text: valid_from and last_verified (ISO dates) — recall prefers fresh facts; last_verified is bumped on every user confirmation. valid_until is an optional TTL.
      - label: applies_to
        text: Optional entity_id/area list tying a fact to HA objects (e.g. cover.gate_motor).
      - label: provenance
        text: "source: voice | manual | import. Planned extensions for write auditing: written_by (tool name), session_id, updated_by — see ssot.apps.ada-memory-audit.yml."
      - label: linkage
        text: supersedes / superseded_by — doc keys linking a fact to its replacement/replaced versions, preserving provenance across re-scoped facts.
  - title: Write Verbs
    icon: "✏️"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Find-then-update
        text: "Updates require a read first: ada_memory_search(bank, query) returns doc keys + content. Match found → correct in place (same key, revision +1, last_verified bumped). No match → new doc with a derived slug key."
      - label: Correct (in-place)
        text: Same fact, new value → overwrite the same key. MDDB revision history is the audit trail; the common case.
      - label: Supersede (new doc)
        text: 'The fact itself was misattributed or re-scoped → write a new key, set old doc status: superseded + superseded_by: <new-key>, new doc gets supersedes: <old-key>. Preserves identity instead of rewriting it.'
      - label: Retract
        text: 'Fact no longer true → status: retracted (+ reason in content). Preferred over delete_document — retracted docs stop surfacing (status: active filter) but stay auditable. Hard delete only for privacy/secret leaks.'
      - label: Expiry
        text: 'valid_until expiry is just status: expired applied lazily at recall time.'
  - title: Per-Bank Write Policy
    icon: "🔐"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: writable
        text: Master switch per bank. false = read-only bank; write tools are rejected loudly (curated banks like home start here until trusted).
      - label: write_policy
        text: "confirmed | direct — reuses the ToolRunner confirmed=true gate, the same pattern as dangerous HA entities. confirmed = Ada must ask the user before writing (shared banks); direct = write immediately (private/test banks)."
      - label: allowed_tools
        text: "Which write tools may touch the bank, e.g. [ada_remember, ada_forget]. Empty = nothing can write even if writable: true."
      - label: Fail-fast
        text: A write to a bank that is unassigned, not writable, or unresolvable is rejected with a clear error — never silently routed to another collection.
  - title: NotebookLM Boundary
    icon: "📓"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Append-only
        text: NLM sources cannot be edited — updates are never mirrored in place. MDDB is the mutable current truth; NotebookLM is the append-only archive.
      - label: Correction sources
        text: "On update, optionally add a text source titled 'Correction: <key> (YYYY-MM-DD)'. The archive preserves the evolution while MDDB always answers with the latest."
      - label: No delete
        text: Retracted docs are NOT removed from NotebookLM — recall always consults MDDB first and treats the archive as historical.
  - title: Voice Flow Example
    icon: "🎙️"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Update path
        text: '"The gate remote isn''t in the drawer anymore, it''s in the cabinet" → ada_memory_search(note, "gate remote") → key match → (confirmed policy) "You told me it was in the drawer — update?" → ada_remember same key, revision +1, last_verified bumped.'
      - label: Contradiction detection
        text: subject+attribute meta lets search find "a fact about the same thing" even when phrased differently — contradictions surface as update candidates, not duplicates.
config:
  version: 2
  created: "2026-09-19"
  updated: "2026-09-20"
  maintainer: tony
  status: draft
  deployment: mn01

# Machine-readable meta schema — the single source of truth for document
# meta fields. Consumed by:
#   scripts/ada/render-memory-banks.py  -> ~/.config/ada/memory-banks.json (schema key)
#   scripts/ada/sync-ada-memory-to-mddb.py (reads this file directly)
#   ada-pi backend/memory_ops.py        (validates written meta)
# Adding a field here is how you extend the schema everywhere.
meta_schema:
  fields:
    bank: {role: system, required: true}
    scope: {role: system, required: true, enum: [shared, tony, michael]}
    kind: {required: true, default: note, enum: [fact, preference, person, procedure, note, check]}
    status: {required: true, default: active, enum: [active, draft, superseded, retracted, expired]}
    source: {role: provenance, required: true, enum: [voice, manual, import, extract, api]}
    written_by: {role: provenance, required: true}
    subject: {required: false}
    attribute: {required: false}
    valid_from: {required: true, type: date}
    last_verified: {required: true, type: date}
    valid_until: {required: false, type: date}
    applies_to: {required: false, type: list}
    supersedes: {required: false, type: key}
    superseded_by: {required: false, type: key}
    retracted_reason: {required: false}
    confidence: {required: false, type: float}
    origin_source: {role: provenance, required: false}
    origin_written_by: {role: provenance, required: false}
    session_id: {role: provenance, required: false}
    retracted_by_session: {role: provenance, required: false}
    # knowledge-circle reinforcement fields — see
    # docs/ada-memory/tony-projects/knowledge-circle.md
    use_count: {required: false, type: int}
    last_used: {required: false, type: date}
    outcome: {required: false}
    outcome_note: {required: false}
    outcome_session: {role: provenance, required: false}
    # decision-check docs (kind: check) — written by /api/decision/check
    verdict: {required: false, enum: [buy, caution, avoid]}
    product: {required: false}
    mode: {required: false, enum: [quick, deep]}
    checked_by: {role: provenance, required: false}
  # Frontmatter-only field (pins the MDDB key on the vault side; stored as
  # the MDDB doc key, not as meta).
  vault_only_fields: [key]

```

# Ada Memory Architecture

Parent SSOT for Ada's memory system — bank registry, document schema, write/update semantics, audit model, and implementation progress across tony-ha and michael-ha

## File Path
`apps/ssot.apps.ada-memory.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Ada Memory Architecture
subtitle: Parent SSOT for Ada's memory system — bank registry, document schema, write/update semantics, audit model, and implementation progress across tony-ha and michael-ha
icon: 🧠
sections:
  - title: Overview
    icon: "💡"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Purpose
        text: Ada has two memory tiers — MDDB collections (fast, mutable, semantic-search tier) and NotebookLM notebooks (deep, append-only archive tier). This family of SSOT files defines how memory is organized, written, updated, and audited.
      - label: Motivation
        text: Memory collection names were previously derived from HOME_ASSISTANT_URL — a URL change orphaned all existing memories. Identity is now pinned by ADA_INSTANCE_ID (fail-fast in backend/instance.py), and curated knowledge is separated from operational telemetry.
      - label: Instances
        text: tony (ada-ha-tony.service :8002, ada-pi-pwa :8001) and michael (ada-ha-michael.service :8003). Every memory bank lists which instances may use it; a service loads only banks assigned to its own ADA_INSTANCE_ID.
      - label: Fail-fast rule
        text: A bank not assigned to the running instance, or one whose collection template cannot resolve, is rejected loudly (log + degraded health flag) — never silently routed elsewhere. Same policy as ADA_INSTANCE_ID.
  - title: Tiers
    icon: "🗄️"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: MDDB fast tier
        text: Operational collections (ada-ha-snapshots-*, ada-ha-events-*, ada-ha-device-*, ada-ha-recall-summary-*) are unchanged. Curated bank collections use the separate ada-ha-bank-* prefix so recall and retention policies can differ. MDDB is the mutable current truth.
      - label: NotebookLM deep tier
        text: Append-only archive routed via NOTEBOOKLM_NOTEBOOK_IDS_JSON groups (memory/infra/apps/kb/ops) or a literal notebook ID per bank. Sources can't be edited — updates are never mirrored in place; optionally a 'Correction:' text source is added.
      - label: Obsidian vault authoring tier
        text: 'docs/ada-memory/ is the human-curated, git-tracked authoring surface (folder = bank, frontmatter = meta schema). scripts/ada/sync-ada-memory-to-mddb.py pushes vault→MDDB and exports voice-written docs to inbox/ for review. The vault is never in the voice latency path — MDDB serves recall.'
      - label: Other databases
        text: MDDB is the document/memory tier only — it does NOT cover Postgres (trade/yomi), Redis, Weaviate, per-app SQLite, or HA .storage. The bank registry itself is a YAML→JSON file, not a database.
  - title: SSOT Family
    icon: "📚"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: ssot.apps.ada-memory-banks.yml
        text: 'Declarative bank registry — the machine-readable banks: block rendered to ~/.config/ada/memory-banks.json at deploy time. Assignment, collections, NotebookLM routing, write policies per bank.'
      - label: ssot.apps.ada-memory-schema.yml
        text: Document meta schema (kind/scope/status/subject/attribute/validity/provenance) and the three write verbs (correct/supersede/retract) with per-bank write-policy fields.
      - label: ssot.apps.ada-memory-audit.yml
        text: Audit model — MDDB revision history, semantic status links, the planned write-log, and what is NOT audited (NotebookLM).
      - label: ssot.apps.ada-memory-progress.yml
        text: Machine-readable milestone/task tracker for the implementation. Update statuses here as work lands.
  - title: Runtime
    icon: "⚙️"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: backend/memory_banks.py (ada-pi)
        text: LIVE — loads the rendered registry, filters by ada_instance_id(), expands {instance}, exposes banks()/bank()/notebook(). Fail-loud errors surface in /api/health.
      - label: Tools
        text: LIVE — ada_memory_search (vector + listing fallback), ada_remember (find-then-update correct/supersede), ada_forget (retract); ada_session_recall bank param does MDDB fast tier → bank notebook NLM escalation. Write path honors writable/write_policy/allowed_tools via confirmed=true.
      - label: Introspection
        text: LIVE — GET /api/memory/banks (ADA_API_KEY) returns banks assigned to the running instance with collection/notebook resolution; registry errors fold into /api/health degraded.
      - label: Cross-bank search
        text: "ada_memory_search bank defaults to 'all' — fans out across the instance's banks and merges hits by score; the model no longer has to guess which bank. Same for ada_session_recall bank='all'."
      - label: Per-instance tool schemas
        text: "Tool descriptions fill {banks}/{writable_banks} from the registry at connect, so each instance only ever sees its own bank names."
      - label: Draft visibility
        text: "status=draft docs surface in recall for DRAFT_VISIBLE_BANKS (default personal,general) only when scope==own instance, score>=0.55, age<=7d — tagged [unverified draft]. Env: ADA_DRAFT_VISIBLE_BANKS/ADA_DRAFT_MIN_SCORE/ADA_DRAFT_MAX_AGE_DAYS."
      - label: Session priming
        text: "At ws connect (and on non-resumed reconnects) a system turn injects the rolling recent-sessions summary + top personal/general facts (memory_ops.session_prime_text, ADA_SESSION_PRIME=0 disables)."
      - label: Coreference expansion
        text: "Short/anaphoric tool queries get the last 4 transcript turns appended before embedding (ConversationMemory.expand_query) — fixes 'the other one' misses. Instructions also require self-contained tool queries."
      - label: Deep-tier cache
        text: "NLM chat/ask answers are cached per instance in ada-ha-nlm-answers-{instance} (score>=0.90 question match, 7d TTL, keyed by bank/group ctx). Repeat misses return in <1s."
      - label: Trace events
        text: "Every tool call/result is emitted as a ProviderEvent and forwarded to ws clients as {type: tool_call|tool_result} — drives the live scenario driver's assertions."
      - label: Test sandbox
        text: 'The note bank (tony-only, write_policy: direct) is the friction-free target for exercising the write/update path first.'
      - label: Scenario tests
        text: "tests/scenarios/*.yaml run offline against ToolRunner+FakeMddb (unittest discover); tests/scenarios-live/*.yaml replay real /ws text turns via scripts/scenario-live.py against a live service."
      - label: Vault sync
        text: 'scripts/ada/sync-ada-memory-to-mddb.py — vault→MDDB upsert with unchanged-skip, remote-only report, --export-inbox pulls source=voice docs to inbox/, --delete-remote removes remote-only non-voice docs. Mapping derives from the banks registry.'
      - label: Devin-bank distillation
        text: 'scripts/ada/distill-devin-bank.py rolls raw subject=devin-session transcripts into devin/weekly-<ISOweek> digests (chunked Gemini passes when a week exceeds the prompt budget, source_keys idempotency), then marks sources status=superseded + superseded_by. The current ISO week is never distilled. Health audited weekly by scripts/audits/memory-banks-audit.mjs (memory-suite).'
config:
  version: 2
  created: "2026-09-19"
  updated: "2026-09-22"
  maintainer: tony
  status: draft
  deployment: mn01
```

# Ada Scenario Testing

Offline + live scenario framework for Ada's memory/tooling layer, and the reconnect away-time tiers it covers

## File Path
`apps/ssot.apps.ada-testing.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Ada Scenario Testing
subtitle: Offline + live scenario framework for Ada's memory/tooling layer, and the reconnect away-time tiers it covers
icon: 🧪
sections:
  - title: Surfaces
    icon: "🧱"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Offline engine
        text: tests/scenario_engine.py + tests/test_scenarios.py (ada-pi). Every tests/scenarios/*.yaml runs deterministically against an in-memory FakeMddb + real ToolRunner + ConversationMemory — no network, no Gemini.
      - label: Live driver
        text: scripts/scenario-live.py + tests/scenarios-live/*.yaml. Replays scripted text turns against a running /ws endpoint and checks ws trace events (tool_call/tool_result/assistant_transcript_delta). LLM phrasing varies — live expectations are deliberately soft.
      - label: Why two tiers
        text: Offline scenarios pin deterministic state (tier, directive text, tool semantics). Live scenarios verify the real pipeline end-to-end — Gemini decides tools, ws transport, reconnect greeting — but can only assert loosely.
  - title: Offline Step DSL
    icon: "📝"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: say / assistant
        text: Append a user/assistant turn to the ConversationMemory transcript (feeds query-expansion and reconnect-tail context).
      - label: expand_query
        text: Runs the coreference expander; check with expanded_contains.
      - label: tool + args
        text: Executes a real tool through ToolRunner (ada_memory_search, ada_remember, ada_forget, ada_outcome); check verb/count_min/hits_contain/hit_banks/draft_hits_min/error_contains/no_error.
      - label: reconnect_after
        text: Simulates a websocket disconnect+reconnect. Duration '90s'/'5m'/'4h'/'2d'/'1w' or bare seconds; null/'none' = first-ever session. Snapshots the transcript tail, resets ConversationMemory, and runs the real session_prime_text with the simulated gap. Result exposes tier/away_seconds/prime — check with output_contains / output_not_contains.
      - label: seed
        text: Pre-loads FakeMddb collections (by bank name or raw collection); meta lists support __TODAY__.
  - title: Expectations
    icon: "🎯"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: output_contains / output_not_contains
        text: >
          Substring checks over the JSON step result — the primary reconnect
          assertion ("tier": "resume", directive phrases, transcript-tail fragments).
      - label: Live-only keys
        text: >
          calls_any, calls, no_calls, result_contains, response_contains,
          response_nonempty, timeout_s (default 90), settle_s (default 5).
          Reconnect turn: "- reconnect: {away_s: 300}" re-opens /ws with
          ?simulate_away_s=N and checks the unprompted greeting turn.
  - title: Reconnect Tiers
    icon: "🔁"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: resume (<15 min)
        text: Brief disconnect — same conversation. Directive injects the pre-disconnect transcript tail; Ada greets briefly and picks up where she left off.
      - label: return (<4 h)
        text: Same-day hours — welcome back, offer to continue the earlier topic.
      - label: recap (<24 h)
        text: Most of a day — welcome back, offer a one-line recap, ask to continue.
      - label: days (<7 d)
        text: Several days — greet, mention what was last discussed, don't assume the old task is still active.
      - label: long (>=7 d)
        text: A week or more — treat as a fresh start; prior context is background only.
      - label: none
        text: First-ever session (no end marker) — generic prime, no session note.
  - title: Implementation
    icon: "⚙️"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: backend/memory_ops.py
        text: away_tier() classifies the gap; reconnect_directive() builds the session note; session_prime_text(away_seconds, last_tail) prepends it and switches the header to "act on the session note".
      - label: pwa_server.py
        text: _reconnect_context() resolves away time — in-memory _last_session_end first, persisted MDDB marker after restarts, ?simulate_away_s= test hook. _mark_session_end() snapshots the tail on ws close and upserts key 'last-session-end' into ada-ha-recall-summary-<instance> (meta kind=session-end, ended_at, ended_at_ts, last_tail).
      - label: Provider reconnects
        text: A mid-session Gemini Live reconnect (go_away/resumption) re-primes WITHOUT the reconnect directive — it is the same live conversation, only the websocket boundary counts as away.
      - label: backend/conversation_memory.py
        text: record_session_end() / last_session_end() own the marker doc read/write.
  - title: Run Commands
    icon: "▶️"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Offline suite
        text: "cd ~/CascadeProjects/ada-pi && .venv/bin/python -m unittest tests.test_scenarios -v"
      - label: Live suite
        text: "cd ~/CascadeProjects/ada-pi && .venv/bin/python scripts/scenario-live.py tests/scenarios-live/reconnect_continuity.yaml --url ws://127.0.0.1:8001/ws --api-key \"$ADA_API_KEY\""
      - label: Manual simulation
        text: "Connect to /ws with the usual api_key auth plus &simulate_away_s=432000 — the server greets as if the user was away that many seconds."
      - label: Distill benchmark
        text: "cd ~/CascadeProjects/chaba && GEMINI_API_KEY=... python3 scripts/ada/memory-distill-benchmark.py --dump — 11 fixture sessions through the real extraction prompt; recall/precision scoring, no MDDB writes."
      - label: Distill dry-run
        text: "python3 scripts/ada/memory-distill.py --dry-run — prints what the batch job would draft from real session summaries; nothing is written."
  - title: Coverage
    icon: "🗂️"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: tests/scenarios/
        text: memory_lifecycle.yaml (remember/correct/forget lifecycle), michael_technician.yaml (HA recall + remember), reconnect_continuity.yaml (all 5 tiers + first-session + bad duration).
      - label: tests/scenarios-live/
        text: michael_technician.yaml (live recall + remember roundtrip), reconnect_continuity.yaml (resume-tier topic reference + long-gap greeting).
      - label: scripts/ada/memory-distill-*
        text: "memory-distill-scenarios.yml (11 fixtures: durable kinds + noise rejection + no-save + dedup) and memory-distill-benchmark.py (recall/precision, thresholds 0.75/0.50). Baseline 2026-09-22: 100%/100%."
      - label: Known gaps
        text: Live greeting text is not asserted verbatim (model-dependent). test-manifest's shell runner has hardcoded per-system sections — the ada-pi suite is not auto-run by test-ssot-kb-memory.sh; run it directly or wire it into CI later.
```

```yaml
    icon: "🎓"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Live config is not versioned
        text: User systemd units and Caddyfile snippets were only on tony-dell. They are now versioned under chaba/stacks/mn01/.
      - label: HA URLs were host-local
        text: The Tony env used 127.0.0.1:8123. On mn01 it must use a tailnet-reachable URL such as https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net:8123/.
      - label: mn01 lacked a stack
        text: Creating chaba/stacks/mn01/ makes the Ada HA deployment reproducible on tony-dell or tony-omen in a failure.
      - label: Audit did not cover Ada HA
        text: ssot.audit.hosts.yml now expects ada-ha-tony.service and ada-ha-michael.service on mn01.
      - label: Secrets and tokens are not in git
        text: ~/.config/secrets/ada-ha-*.env and notebooklm-rest-api.env are still host-local and must be backed up separately.
      - label: URL-derived collection names orphan memory
        text: MDDB collections were once keyed by HOME_ASSISTANT_URL slug; moving tony from 127.0.0.1 to the tailnet URL abandoned the old collections. ADA_INSTANCE_ID now pins identity; rule is fail quick and report, never silently fall back for identity config.
      - label: Funnel makes auth mandatory
        text: mn01 and tony-dell both run Tailscale Funnel on 443, so /apps/ada_ha_* and /apps/ada_pi are public-internet paths. confirmed=true only gates the model — direct REST callers self-assert it — which is why ADA_API_KEY covers /api/tools/call AND /ws.
      - label: EnvironmentFile order overrides keys
        text: "ada-ha-*.service load ada-ha-<inst>.env THEN notebooklm-rest-api.env; a stale NOTEBOOKLM_REST_API_KEY in the second file silently overrode the per-instance scoped key, so every notebooklm-rest call returned 401 Invalid API key (key-gate runs before handlers, so the write queue never engaged). Fixed 2026-09-17 by commenting the stale key on mn01. Rule: notebooklm-rest-api.env must never carry a singular NOTEBOOKLM_REST_API_KEY on mn01 — scoped per-instance keys live only in ada-ha-*.env; the server side authenticates with NOTEBOOKLM_REST_API_KEYS + NOTEBOOKLM_REST_KEY_SCOPES."

    icon: "🧩"
    layout: list
```

```yaml
    icon: "*"
```

```yaml
title: Map3D - 3D Map Viewer
subtitle: Dedicated app for 3D visualization including point clouds, Gaussian splats, and tiltable map overlays

ideas:

sections:
  - title: Purpose
    icon: 🎯
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Isolation
        text: "Separate 3D visualization development from Track4 racing simulator to avoid cluttering the racing-focused codebase."
      - label: Testing platform
        text: "Dedicated environment for testing point cloud rendering, Gaussian splat viewers, and 3D map overlays without affecting production racing app."
      - label: Scene management
        text: "Scene-based configuration allows quick switching between different 3D datasets for testing and comparison."

  - title: Architecture
    icon: 🏗️
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Core components
        text: "index.html: UI with map container and controls. main.js: App logic, scene management, Leaflet integration. splat-layer.js: Three.js point cloud/Gaussian splat renderer (moved from Track4)."
      - label: Map engine
        text: "Leaflet.js for 2D map tiles (CARTO Dark basemap). Three.js for 3D content overlay via custom SplatLayer."
      - label: Data storage
        text: "Scene definitions in main.js. PLY/splat files in data/ directory. GPS bounds and center per scene for georeferencing."

  - title: Features
    icon: ✨
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Point cloud rendering
        text: "Three.js PointsMaterial with vertex colors from ASCII PLY files. Supports position (x,y,z) and color (r,g,b) per vertex."
      - label: Transparent walls
        text: "Auto-generated bounding box walls around point clouds. Configurable height, opacity, and visibility toggle."
      - label: Scene tilt
        text: "Rotates the 3D scene group (not camera) for oblique viewing. 0-60 degree range via slider. Keeps map alignment correct."
      - label: Scene selector
        text: "Dropdown to switch between predefined scenes. Each scene has file, bounds, center, and name."
      - label: 3D toggle
        text: "Enable/disable 3D rendering without unloading the scene. Useful for comparing 2D vs 3D views."

  - title: Point Cloud Format
    icon: 📄
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: PLY ASCII format
        text: "Standard ASCII PLY with element vertex, properties x/y/z (float) and red/green/blue (uchar). Header: ply, format ascii 1.0, element vertex N, property declarations, end_header."
      - label: Example header
        text: 'ply\nformat ascii 1.0\nelement vertex 100\nproperty float x\nproperty float y\nproperty float z\nproperty uchar red\nproperty uchar green\nproperty uchar blue\nend_header'
      - label: Coordinate system
        text: "Local 3D coordinates mapped to GPS via scene bounds and center. SplatLayer handles GPS-to-world conversion using Haversine formula."
      - label: Test data
        text: "data/test-points.ply: 400-point cube (13x13x3 grid) for testing. Colors fade from red (bottom) to pink (top)."

  - title: Gaussian Splat Status
    icon: 🎥
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Current status
        text: "Not yet implemented. SplatLayer has infrastructure but Gaussian splat parsing fails with all tested libraries."
      - label: Library issues
        text: '@mkkellogg/gaussian-splats-3D (v0.4.0, v0.3.0): "Offset is outside the bounds of the DataView" in PlyParser.js. three-gaussian-splats (v0.0.7): same error. iframe with esm.sh CDN: "Invalid typed array length: 4".'
      - label: Root cause
        text: "Issue appears fundamental to browser environment or file format compatibility. Official room.splat from graphdeco-inria/gaussian-splatting repo fails in all approaches."
      - label: Future approach
        text: "Wait for library updates, use official desktop viewer, or implement custom parser with specific format requirements. Point cloud fallback is reliable alternative."

  - title: Scene Configuration
    icon: ⚙️
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Scene object structure
        text: "{ id: string, name: string, file: string (path to PLY), bounds: [[south,west],[north,east]], center: [lat,lon] }"
      - label: Adding scenes
        text: "Add scene object to scenes array in main.js. Place PLY file in data/ directory. Determine GPS bounds from training data or manual measurement."
      - label: Bounds calculation
        text: "Use GPS coordinates of scene corners. For synthetic data, estimate based on desired map coverage. Center should be midpoint of bounds."
      - label: Example scene
        text: '{ id: "test-cube", name: "Test Cube", file: "./data/test-points.ply", bounds: [[13.2435, 100.9280], [13.2450, 100.9300]], center: [13.2442, 100.9292] }'

  - title: Controls
    icon: 🎛️
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Scene selector
        text: "Dropdown in top-right panel. Loads scene bounds, centers map, prepares 3D data (but does not enable 3D until checkbox checked)."
      - label: Enable 3D checkbox
        text: "Toggles Three.js rendering. When unchecked, shows only 2D Leaflet map. When checked, overlays 3D content."
      - label: Tilt slider
        text: "Range 0-60 degrees. Rotates scene group around X-axis. 0° = flat (top-down), 60° = maximum oblique angle."
      - label: Show Walls checkbox
        text: "Toggles visibility of auto-generated bounding box walls. Walls are hidden by default."
      - label: Status display
        text: "Shows current state: Ready, Loading scene, 3D enabled/disabled, error messages."

  - title: File Structure
    icon: 📁
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: public/apps/map3d/
        text: "Main app directory."
      - label: index.html
        text: "UI shell with map container and control panel."
      - label: main.js
        text: "App logic, scene management, Leaflet integration, event handlers."
      - label: splat-layer.js
        text: "Three.js renderer (Leaflet layer wrapper). Handles PLY parsing, wall generation, camera sync, scene tilt."
      - label: data/
        text: "Directory for PLY and splat files."
      - label: data/test-points.ply
        text: "Test point cloud (400-point cube) for initial testing."

  - title: Development Workflow
    icon: 🔧
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Adding new point clouds
        text: "1. Generate or export PLY file. 2. Place in data/ directory. 3. Add scene definition to main.js. 4. Test in map3d app. 5. If for Track4, copy to track4/splats/ and add to course YAML."
      - label: Testing Gaussian splats
        text: "1. Export .splat or .ply from training. 2. Place in data/ directory. 3. Add scene definition. 4. Enable 3D and test. 5. Debug in isolated environment without affecting Track4."
      - label: Debugging rendering
        text: "Use browser console for Three.js errors. Check network tab for file loading. Verify GPS bounds match actual location. Test tilt and wall visibility separately."
      - label: Performance tuning
        text: "Reduce point count for testing. Adjust wall opacity/height. Limit tilt angle for better performance on low-end devices."

  - title: Integration with Track4
    icon: 🔗
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Code sharing
        text: "splat-layer.js originally developed in Track4, moved to map3d for isolation. Can be copied back to Track4 when 3D features are production-ready."
      - label: Data sharing
        text: "PLY files in map3d/data/ can be copied to track4/splats/ for use in racing courses. Scene definitions map to course YAML splat section."
      - label: Feature parity
        text: "map3d has tilt and wall controls. Track4 had these too but they were removed during isolation. Can be re-added if needed for racing visualization."
      - label: Future integration

  - title: Known Issues
    icon: ⚠️
    layout: list

      - label: GPS accuracy
```

```yaml
icon: 🎭
sections:
  - title: Purpose
    icon: 🎯
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: What it is
        text: A remote browser-control facility that lets multiple AI clients drive Chrome/Playwright sessions through a shared daemon.
      - label: Primary uses
        text: E2E verification, UI testing, screenshots, page navigation, form interaction, and live remote debugging.

  - title: Architecture
    icon: 🏗️
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Daemon (consolidated 2026-08-10)
        text: playlived runs on tony-dell:9230 (primary) and tony-omen:9230 (fallback). See docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.host-roles.yml for the canonical host priorities.
      - label: MCP client
        text: mcp-playlive (chaba-tony-dell/mcp-servers/mcp-playlive/playlive-server.py) forwards tool calls from Windsurf to the daemon via single "playlive" MCP server.
      - label: Target flexibility
        text: Single daemon supports local headless Playwright (default) and remote CDP-attached Chrome sessions via target parameter.
      - label: Playwright relationship
        text: PlayLive is built on Playwright - see docs/kb/playwright-vs-playlive.md for detailed comparison.
      - label: Default mode
        text: Defaults to headless Playwright (local) for better performance (~50-100MB RAM savings, faster startup). Use chrome-live/playwright-chrome for visual debugging.

  - title: Per-host configuration
    icon: 🖥️
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Preferred daemon
        text: docs/ssot/infrastructure/playlive-hosts.yml has a per_host section. tony-dell prefers 127.0.0.1:9230 (itself) and tony-omen prefers tony-dell:9230.
      - label: Failover
        text: playlive-hosts.yml has a failover section. tony-dell falls back to tony-omen:9230; tony-omen falls back to 127.0.0.1:9230 (itself). The loader switches PLAYLIVE_URL automatically.
      - label: Self-heal
        text: playlive-hosts-loader.py checks daemon health on startup and, if unhealthy, runs the host-specific systemd restart command from playlive-hosts.yml. playlive_self_heal provides the same on demand.
      - label: Focus escalation
        text: If both the primary and the failover are unreachable after self-heal and focus is enabled in playlive-hosts.yml, a focus-inbox item is written so the outage is triaged manually.

    icon: 🌐
    layout: table
    headers: [Name, Host, Endpoint, Purpose]
    rows:

      - [playlived, tony-omen, http://tony-omen:9230, Fallback session daemon]

          forwarded to tony-dell via 127.0.0.1:9228 (SSH tunnel),
        ]

  - title: Authentication
    icon: 🔐
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Basic auth support
        text: PlayLive sessions can be configured with basic authentication credentials for accessing protected pages.
      - label: Credential configuration
        text: Credentials passed via playlived configuration or session creation parameters (username/password).
      - label: Use case
        text: Enables verification of Caddy-protected pages like /apps/yomi/* which require basic auth.

  - title: Tools
    icon: 🛠️
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Session lifecycle
        text: playlive_create_chrome_live, playlive_create_playwright_chrome, playlive_create_playwright, playlive_list_sessions, playlive_close_session
      - label: Page interaction
        text: playlive_navigate, playlive_click, playlive_fill, playlive_select, playlive_eval, playlive_state
      - label: Capture
        text: playlive_screenshot, playlive_screenshot_image
      - label: Hosts & self-heal
        text: playlive_verify_host, playlive_discover_hosts, playlive_reload_hosts, playlive_self_heal

  - title: Verified workflow
    icon: ✅
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Start daemon
        text: tony-omen runs playlived as a systemd service on port 9230. On tony-dell, the playlived systemd service also runs on port 9230.
      - label: Create session (default)
        text: playlive_create_playwright defaults to headless local mode for better performance.
      - label: Create session (live)
        text: Use playlive_create_chrome_live or playlive_create_playwright_chrome with target="remote" for visual debugging with remote CDP.
      - label: Navigate
        text: playlive_navigate to the target URL (default page.goto timeout 15s).
      - label: Authenticated access
        text: For protected pages, configure basic auth credentials before navigation to bypass Caddy basic auth prompts.
      - label: Verify
        text: playlive_state returns url and title.

  - title: Decision guide
    icon: 🌲
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Default first move
        text: When a task needs any browser interaction, start with playlive_create_playwright on tony-dell. It is headless, fastest (~50-100MB less RAM, quicker startup), and does not require Chrome CDP to be running.
      - label: Use chrome-live only when
        text: You need to see or interact with a visible browser window, capture a human-readable screenshot of a live session, or debug rendering. Use target tony-dell with remote_url http://127.0.0.1:9222.
      - label: Use playlive-macbook only when
        text: The target is macOS-specific, Safari/WebKit-only, or an iOS-style preview. Use the tony-omen SSH tunnel on 127.0.0.1:9229.
      - label: Skip PlayLive when
        text: You only need raw HTML/JSON, an HTTP status, or a REST check. Use curl or mcp-debug instead; it is faster and lighter.
      - label: Auth shortcut
        text: For Caddy basic-auth pages, create the session first, then pass credentials during navigation instead of pre-configuring the daemon.

  - title: Maintenance
    icon: 🔧
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Pinned Playwright version
        text: playwright is pinned to 1.62.0 in /home/tony/.local/playlive/package.json on both tony-omen and tony-dell to avoid package/browser binary mismatches.
      - label: Browser install
        text: Run 'npx playwright install chromium' from /home/tony/.local/playlive after any Playwright version change.
      - label: Package-lock
        text: Use 'npm install' or 'npm ci' from /home/tony/.local/playlive to keep package-lock.json in sync.
      - label: Remote CDP override
        text: playlived's default remote CDP is 127.0.0.1:9223, but the headless Chrome CDP on tony-dell is on 127.0.0.1:9222. When using the tony-dell daemon, create chrome-live or playwright-chrome sessions with `remote_url` `http://127.0.0.1:9222` (or use the `tony-dell` host from `playlive-hosts.yml`). For tony-omen Chrome, use the `tony-omen` host from `playlive-hosts.yml` which maps to the `127.0.0.1:9228` SSH tunnel.
      - label: Daemon restart
        text: Restart playlived.service after browser or package updates.

  - title: Limitations & cautions
    icon: ⚠️
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Security
        text: CDP and playlived are unauthenticated on the LAN; basic auth is for target page access only, not daemon security. Do not expose to untrusted networks.
      - label: Resource contention
        text: Browser automation on tony-omen shares resources with GPU/interactive workloads; use the tony-dell daemon to offload UI verification.
      - label: Windsurf reload
        text: Reload Windsurf after mcp_config.json changes for tools to appear.
      - label: Remote Chrome availability
        text: chrome-live/playwright-chrome require remote Chrome CDP (tony-dell:9222) which may not be available if Chrome is not running with remote debugging enabled.
      - label: Consolidated architecture
        text: playlive MCP server is configured for tony-dell by default. playlive.tony-omen can be enabled as a fallback if needed.
```

# Technical Decisions Archive 2026

Archived decision records moved out of ssot.technical-decisions.yml

## File Path
`decisions/ssot.technical-decisions.archive.2026.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Technical Decisions Archive 2026
subtitle: Archived decision records moved out of ssot.technical-decisions.yml
icon: archive
source: docs/ssot/decisions/ssot.technical-decisions.yml
archived_at: '2026-09-18'
decisions:
- id: mcp-debug-cors-proxy
  date: '2026-08-16'
  title: How to serve live mcp-savings.json to the HTTPS chaba.h3 page
  status: accepted
  context: 'The chaba.h3 page is served over HTTPS. Browsers block the public page from

    fetching the tony-omen/tony-dell CORS HTTP endpoint (mixed-content and .local

    mDNS resolution issues). The report must still refresh without a full page

    reload.

    '
  options:
  - label: HTTPS CORS endpoint on tony-dell
    pros:
    - simple fetch from the page
    - no server-side proxy
    cons:
    - requires TLS termination and certificate on tony-dell
    - opens tony-dell port to HTTPS
  - label: Same-origin PHP proxy on chaba.h3
    pros:
    - avoids mixed-content
    - hides upstream HTTP URL from browser
    - fast to deploy
    - falls back to cached snapshot
    cons:
    - adds PHP dependency
    - one more network hop
    - proxy must be maintained
  - label: Disable live URL until a secure endpoint is available
    pros:
    - no mixed-content risk
    - no extra code
    cons:
    - page never shows live data
    - must regenerate and commit snapshot manually
  chosen: Same-origin PHP proxy on chaba.h3
  reasoning: 'The PHP proxy gives the page live data without waiting for TLS infrastructure

    on tony-dell. It keeps the upstream HTTP endpoint inside the server network

    and lets the browser make a same-origin HTTPS request. A cached snapshot

    fallback means the page still renders if tony-dell is unreachable. The proxy

    can be replaced by a direct HTTPS endpoint later without changing the public

    contract because callers use /api/mcp-savings.php.

    '
  consequences:
  - chaba-h3/public/api/mcp-savings.php fetches http://100.68.142.13:9100/mcp-savings.json
  - app.js sets LIVE_DATA_URL to "/api/mcp-savings.php"
  - CORS server remains on tony-dell for now
  - Future option to add TLS to tony-dell and switch the proxy upstream
  related:
  - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.mcp-debug.cors.yml
  - chaba-h3/public/api/mcp-savings.php
  - chaba-h3/public/apps/docs/mcp_debug/app.js
- id: mcp-debug-unified-commands
  date: '2026-08-17'
  title: Add unified cross-platform commands to mcp-debug
  status: accepted
  context: 'The mcp-debug command list has grown and now includes multiple tools that

    have equivalent implementations on Linux, macOS, or different runtimes

    (e.g., podman vs docker, systemctl vs launchctl, ss vs netstat, nvidia-smi

    vs rocm-smi). We want fewer command variants and more host-agnostic

    diagnostics without losing the ability to tell which backend answered.

    '
  options:
  - label: Keep every runtime-specific command separate
    pros:
    - exact output per tool
    - no parser abstraction
    - simple wrappers
    cons:
    - long allowlists
    - presets must branch per host
    - harder for sub-agents
  - label: Add one abstract command per concept with backend auto-detection
    pros:
    - shorter allowlists
    - host-agnostic presets
    - consistent compact JSON
    cons:
    - more complex wrappers
    - parsers may differ
    - can mask runtime details
  chosen: Add one abstract command per concept with backend auto-detection
  reasoning: 'The compact layer already normalizes raw text into JSON. Auto-detecting a

    backend inside a single `containers`, `services`, `sockets`, or `gpu` command

    keeps the user-facing command list small while still exposing the actual

    backend in a `runtime` key. Commands will be vetted with `mcp_stats` before

    promotion to `recommended: true`.

    '
  consequences:
    immediate:
    - New `containers`, `services`, `sockets`, and `gpu` commands in mcp-debug
    - Backend runtime recorded in compact JSON output
    - New suggested extensions and active focus created
    future:
    - May add `memory` and `block_devices` abstractions if these prove useful
    - Raw allowlist can shrink as abstract commands replace duplicates
  related:
  - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.mcp-debug.yml
  - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.mcp-tools.yml
  - scripts/mcp_debug/mcp-debug-macos
  - ~/.local/bin/mcp-debug
- id: ada-memory-mddb-first-tiered-summaries
  date: '2026-09-18'
  title: Ada recall serves MDDB-first with tiered summaries; NotebookLM is deep-recall/archive
  status: accepted
  context: 'ada_session_recall answers every history question through NotebookLM

    via notebooklm-rest (~26s per query) with a single MDDB rolling summary

    (recent-sessions) as the fast path. One rolling summary cannot answer

    specific topic/date questions, and routing all recall through NotebookLM

    keeps common answers slow and coupled to an external service.

    '
  options:
  - label: Keep NotebookLM as primary recall path
    pros:
    - deep semantic recall over full transcripts
    - no new pipeline
    cons:
    - ~26s for common questions
    - external dependency on every recall
  - label: MDDB-first with tiered summaries, NotebookLM as deep-recall/archive
    pros:
    - fast common recall
    - survives restarts
    - NotebookLM stays transcript SoT
    cons:
    - needs per-session summaries
    - rollup jobs
    - escalation rules
  chosen: MDDB-first with tiered summaries, NotebookLM as deep-recall/archive
  reasoning: 'MDDB already hosts the persisted recent-sessions summary (~0.2s warm,

    ~0.6s write). Extend it to per-session summaries plus daily/weekly/

    monthly/yearly rollups generated by local Gemini, and serve recall

    from the cheapest tier with coverage. NotebookLM is invoked only for

    explicit detail requests ("what exactly did we decide"), low MDDB

    confidence, or long-range consolidation. Fail-quick semantics hold:

    a failed lookup is reported, never silently shown as "nothing found".

    '
  consequences:
  - Add per-session summary docs to per-instance MDDB recall collections
  - Add daily/weekly/monthly/yearly rollup jobs via local Gemini
  - Add confidence/coverage metadata and MDDB->NotebookLM escalation rules
  - NotebookLM = transcript archive + explicit deep-recall path only
  related:
  - docs/ssot/apps/ssot.apps.ada_ha.yml
  - ~/CascadeProjects/ada-pi/backend/conversation_memory.py
```

```yaml
title: Technical Decisions
subtitle: Record of significant design trade-offs and the reasoning behind them
icon: ⚖️
version: 1

overview:
  purpose: |
    Keep a durable, searchable record of why a particular design or implementation
    choice was made, what options were considered, and what the consequences were.
    This is not a discussion log; it is a concise decision record that other SSOTs
    can reference.
  scope:
    - Cross-cutting architecture choices
    - Security and deployment trade-offs
    - Tooling and host selection decisions
    - Focus and workflow policy changes
  out_of_scope:
    - Routine bug fixes with no design options
    - Focus history (see ssot.focus.yml)
    - Session notes (see ssot.focus.sessions.yml)

archive: docs/ssot/decisions/ssot.technical-decisions.archive.2026.yml

decisions:
  - id: mcp-debug-file-clipboard-bridge
    date: '2026-08-17'
    title: How to add auditable remote file get/put to mcp-debug
    status: accepted
    context: |
      The assistant frequently needs to fetch remote logs/configs and push small scripts
      to tony-omen and tony-dell without leaving the MCP workflow. Existing `mcp_raw` is
      too permissive and does not enforce path allowlists, size caps, or base64 transport.
    options:
      - label: Extend mcp_raw with allowlist and size arguments
        pros: [reuses the existing raw-command path, minimal new code]
        cons: [blurs the line between raw and auditable commands, harder to log, harder to vet]
      - label: Add dedicated mcp_get_file and mcp_put_file tools
        pros: [clear contract, path-allowlist per host, hard size cap, base64 payload, overwrite control, detailed logging]
        cons: [new tool schemas, new SSOT file, more code in tools.py]
      - label: Use a separate file-transfer MCP server
        pros: [isolated security surface, could reuse scp/sftp]
        cons: [extra process, extra configuration, tailnet auth complexity]
    chosen: Add dedicated mcp_get_file and mcp_put_file tools
    reasoning: |
      A dedicated tool gives a precise contract and security defaults: per-host
      allowed_path_prefixes, 1 MiB hard cap, overwrite=false by default, and base64
      transport so binary content is safe over JSON. It lives in the same mcp-debug
      server, reusing existing `run_on_host` SSH transport, but is auditable and
      user-confirmable. Clipboard support is kept as an experimental, disabled-by-default
      add-on after file transfer is stable.
    consequences:
      - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.mcp-debug.files.yml added with tool contract, allowlists, and limits
      - tools.py already contains mcp_get_file, mcp_put_file, mcp_clipboard_get, mcp_clipboard_set
      - server.py already exposes the tool schemas and dispatch
      - Round-trip smoke tests succeeded on tony-omen and tony-dell
    related:
      - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.mcp-debug.files.yml
      - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.mcp-debug.yml
      - scripts/mcp_debug/tools.py
      - scripts/mcp_debug/server.py

  - id: migrate-core-services-to-tony-dell-podman
    date: '2026-08-17'
    title: Migrate core chaba services from tony-omen Docker to tony-dell rootless Podman with Quadlet
    status: accepted
    context: |
      Several long-running chaba services (mddb, mddb-panel, redis, yomi-api, weaviate, raceman, postgres)
      had been running on tony-omen under Docker. To consolidate hosting, improve startup reliability,
      and run containers as an unprivileged user, we moved the workload to tony-dell using rootless Podman
      with Quadlet systemd units.
    options:
      - label: Keep Docker on tony-omen
        pros: [no migration work, existing volumes and compose files keep working]
        cons: [continues to rely on tony-omen for critical data services, no rootless isolation]
      - label: Move to tony-dell Docker with compose
        pros: [familiar docker compose tooling, direct volume migration]
        cons: [still requires rootful Docker or complex rootless setup, no native systemd integration]
      - label: Move to tony-dell rootless Podman with Quadlet
        pros: [systemd user units auto-start on boot, no root privileges, host-network simplifies known ports, aligns with existing Quadlet work]
        cons: [new Quadlet units to write, image imports via docker save | podman load, port conflicts must be resolved per service]
    chosen: Move to tony-dell rootless Podman with Quadlet
    reasoning: |
      Rootless Podman with Quadlet gives native systemd user integration, starts containers at boot without
      root, and keeps the network model simple by using --network host for most services. The migration
      reused already-built Docker images where possible (docker save | podman load) and copied data volumes
      to per-service paths under ~/.config/containers on tony-dell. Known port conflicts were resolved by
      explicit port assignments: mddb API 11023, mddb MCP 9000, raceman-php 9001, mddb-panel 3002,
      weaviate 8084 (because chaba-funnel uses 8082), and raceman-web 8083. Caddy on tony-omen now
      reverse-proxies these services from 100.68.142.13. Client MCP configs were repointed from
      localhost:9001 to 100.68.142.13:9000.
    consequences:
      - Quadlet units created at ~/.config/containers/systemd/ and enabled user services
      - Service data copied to tony-dell under /home/tony/.config/containers/<service>
      - Caddy /mddb/*, /apps/raceman/*, /apps/weaviate, and other routes now proxy to 100.68.142.13

      - Recovery actions in ssot.health.*.yml still reference old docker compose paths and should be updated

  - id: rview-view-number-and-media-fallback
    date: '2026-08-22'
    title: Auto-number RView views and fall back to iframe on media load failure
    status: accepted
    context: |
      RView views were referenced only by opaque view_id. Users wanted to open
      any view by a stable number and have a fallback when remote images/videos
      failed to load.
    options:
      - label: Keep view_id only and expose a separate number mapping
        pros: [no schema change, simple lookup table]
        cons: [extra API surface, number can drift when views are deleted]
      - label: Add view_number to each view and resolve numeric view_id as view_number
        pros: [stable auto-number, backward-compatible view_id support, easy URL sharing]
        cons: [requires migration for persisted views without view_number]
      - label: Fail visibly and require the user to pick a different URL
        pros: [no UI complexity]
        cons: [poor UX for Gemini-generated or third-party media]
      - label: Replace failed media with an iframe fallback
        pros: [handles broken images/videos/PDFs gracefully, keeps viewer visible]
        cons: [iframing some URLs may still fail or show mixed-content errors]
    chosen: Add view_number and use iframe fallback
    reasoning: |
      Auto-numbering gives every view a stable, shareable `?view=<number>` URL
      while preserving `view_id` compatibility. Interpreting a numeric `view_id`
      as `view_number` is intuitive and matches the URL parameter. Falling back
      to an iframe lets Gemini-supplied or third-party URLs still render even
      when the browser cannot decode them natively.
    consequences:
      - rview-api.mjs assigns view_number on creation and migrates existing state
      - RView UI uses VIEW_KEY ('view_number' for numeric, 'view_id' otherwise)
      - Failed image/video/audio/PDF elements are replaced by an iframe with the same URL
      - SSOT and MCP tool schemas updated to expose view_number
    related:

    status: accepted

        pros: [fresh container state for each call, simple wrapper script]

        pros: [faster connection, stable logs, single container lifecycle, same model as mcp-health]

      MCP wrapper uses `podman exec -i workflows-mcp workflows-mcp` to connect over

  - id: tony-ha-tailscale-only-access
    date: '2026-09-18'
    title: tony-ha reachable only via Tailscale HTTPS; use one URL for internal and external
    status: accepted
    context: |
      Setting up the Home Assistant companion app surfaced that tony-ha had no
      working LAN URL. HA binds loopback only (configuration.yaml http.server_host:
      127.0.0.1), so http://tony-dell:8123 and http://tony-dell.local:8123 fail —
      tailscaled owns 8123 on the tailnet IP and answers plain HTTP with
      "Client sent an HTTP request to an HTTPS server". tailscale serve provides
      the TLS-terminating proxy https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net:8123 ->
      127.0.0.1:8123 (tailnet only, no Funnel on this port).
    options:
      - label: Expose plain HTTP on the LAN interface
        pros: [works without Tailscale, simple http://192.168.2.67:8123]
        cons: [widens LAN attack surface, duplicates the existing tailnet path, needs http.server_host change + restart]
      - label: Path-prefixed Caddy route (/apps/ha/tony-ha/)
        pros: [LAN HTTP via existing Caddy]
        cons: [HA UI absolute redirects break path-prefixed proxying — already rejected for michael-dev]
      - label: Use the tailscale serve HTTPS URL for both internal and external
        pros: [single canonical URL, works on LAN and remote, TLS everywhere, no HA change]
        cons: [requires Tailscale client connected on the device]
    chosen: Use the tailscale serve HTTPS URL for both internal and external
    reasoning: |
      One URL (https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net:8123) covers home WiFi and
      remote access as long as the client is on the tailnet. No HA or proxy
      changes are needed and it avoids reopening a plain-HTTP listener on the
      LAN. The path-prefixed Caddy option was previously abandoned for
      michael-dev because HA absolute redirects break under a path prefix.
    consequences:
      - 'HA app: set both internal and external URL to https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net:8123'
      - 'Client devices must run Tailscale; no TOTP/MFA on tony-ha (password-only login)'
      - 'Stale http://tony-dell:8123 references fixed in instances/services/health/node-red SSOTs and AGENTS.md'
```
