```yaml
  - id: ada-calendar-provider-backend
    date: '2026-09-21'
    title: How ada gets calendar + tasks tools that can switch between Google, iCloud, and Outlook
    status: accepted
    context: |
      Ada needed calendar reading and task planning tools. The natural instinct
      was to find an MCP repo, but ada's ToolRunner dispatches tool calls to
      native Python methods — MCP servers cannot plug in without a client
      bridge. The user also wants the ability to switch providers (Google →
      iCloud/Hotmail) or read several at once, so the provider had to be
      modular from day one. A second constraint: GEMINI_API_KEY cannot
      authenticate calendar calls (API keys carry no user identity), but the
      OAuth Desktop client in ~/.config/secrets/google_credentials.json lives
      in the same gen-lang-client project and is reusable for consent.
    options:
      - label: Direct provider adapters behind a CalendarProvider protocol
        pros: [async-native httpx fits ada's FastAPI/asyncio design, full API
               fidelity (freebusy, per-calendar routing), zero new runtime deps,
               new provider = one file + one registry block]
        cons: [ada owns OAuth per provider; one token file per service]
      - label: Home Assistant as the provider abstraction
        pros: [zero new auth in ada — HA owns OAuth per integration;
               reuses existing home_assistant.py client]
        cons: [calendar.create_event/todo support is patchy per HA integration,
               every call inherits HA latency on top of Gemini's round trip,
               tool surface capped at what HA exposes]
      - label: MCP server bridge in ToolRunner
        pros: [unlocks the whole MCP ecosystem (nspady/google-calendar-mcp etc.)]
        cons: [new MCP client machinery inside a voice-latency path, extra
               process lifecycle to manage on mn01, overkill for v1]
      - label: Bidirectional sync between providers
        pros: [same events visible in every native app]
        cons: [conflict resolution and duplicate handling forever; rejected —
               aggregation at read time gives the same user-visible answer]
    chosen: Direct provider adapters behind a CalendarProvider protocol, Google first
    reasoning: |
      The protocol + aggregator (backend/calendar_providers.py) gives provider
      switching via the rendered registry (read: aggregate|name, write: name,
      instances:) — the same shape as memory banks. Google gets a real adapter
      (httpx + refresh token, no google-api-python-client weight on the Pi);
      CalDAV covers iCloud/Fastmail/Nextcloud as one adapter later; MS Graph
      only when actually needed. Writes require confirmed=true server-side.
      HA-mediation stays available as a future read-only adapter if a provider
      is easier to wire in HA than directly.
    consequences:
      - backend/calendar_providers.py + backend/google_calendar.py added
      - CALENDAR_WRITE_TOOLS gate in tool_runner.py; declarations + instruction
        paragraph in realtime_provider.py
      - 'Registry SSOT: docs/ssot/apps/ssot.apps.ada-calendar.yml rendered to
        ~/.config/ada/calendar.json by scripts/ada/render-calendar-providers.py'
      - 'Auth: scripts/ada/google-calendar-auth.py mints
        ~/.config/secrets/ada-google-calendar-token.json from the shared
        google_credentials.json client (scopes: calendar.readonly,
        calendar.events, tasks); consent screen must be published or tokens
        expire in 7 days'
      - Calendar/Tasks APIs must be enabled on project gen-lang-client-0694401188
    related:
      - docs/ssot/apps/ssot.apps.ada-calendar.yml
      - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.ada.howto.yml
      - 'ada-pi: backend/calendar_providers.py, backend/google_calendar.py,
        backend/tool_runner.py, backend/realtime_provider.py'
```

```yaml
title: mcp-debug File & Clipboard Bridge
subtitle: Add safe small-file transfer and optional clipboard tools to mcp-debug
icon: inbox

focus:
  label: mcp-debug file & clipboard bridge
  text: |
    Extend mcp-debug with small, auditable file-transfer tools so the assistant can
    fetch remote logs/configs and push small scripts without leaving the MCP workflow.
    Clipboard support is out-of-scope for the first pass and should be added as a
    separate, experimental tool after file transfer is stable.

    Proposed design for the complicated bits (so this session does not need to solve them again):
    - `mcp_get_file(host, path, max_bytes=65536)` returns `{ok, encoding, content_base64, size, truncated}`.
      Transport: existing SSH exec with `cat` or `head -c`, base64-encode the payload.
    - `mcp_put_file(host, path, content_base64, mode="644", overwrite=false)` returns `{ok, path, bytes_written}`.
      Transport: existing SSH exec with a heredoc after path-allowlist vetting.
    - `mcp_clipboard_get(host)` / `mcp_clipboard_set(host, text)` are macOS `pbpaste`/`pbcopy`
      or Linux `xclip`/`xsel`/`wl-clipboard`. Disabled by default; per-host opt-in only.

    Security defaults:
    - Per-host `allowed_path_prefixes` (e.g. `~/.local`, `/tmp`, `~/.config`, project dirs).
    - Hard `max_bytes` cap and a `truncated` flag.
    - `overwrite=false` by default; confirmation required for writes outside the allow-list.
    - All get/put calls logged with host, path, size, and result.
```

```yaml
title: mcp-debug Visual Capture Bridge
subtitle: Add screenshot, window list, and clipboard-image capture to mcp-debug
icon: inbox

focus:
  label: mcp-debug visual capture bridge
  text: |
    Extend mcp-debug with lightweight, opt-in visual capture tools so the assistant
    can see remote host state without switching to PlayLive or another MCP server.
    Start with non-interactive capture tools; avoid duplicating PlayLive's browser
    automation and click/keyboard control.

    Proposed design for the complicated bits (so this session does not need to solve them again):
    - `mcp_screenshot(host, region, format=png)` returns `{ok, content_base64, width, height, bytes, error}`.
      Transport: macOS `screencapture -x -`; Linux `gnome-screenshot -f -`, `grim`, or `import`;
      always base64-encode and cap at 2 MB (resize/compress if larger).
    - `mcp_window_list(host)` returns `{ok, windows: [{id, app, title, pid, focused}]}`.
      Transport: macOS `lsappinfo`/`osascript`; X11 `xwininfo -root -tree`; Wayland `swaymsg -t get_tree`.
    - `mcp_clipboard_image_get(host)` returns `{ok, content_base64, format, bytes, error}`.
      Transport: macOS `pbpaste -Prefer rtf` image path/NSPasteboard read; Linux `xclip -selection clipboard -t image/png -o`.
    - `mcp_a11y_tree(host, app)` returns a JSON UI element tree of a given app/window.
      Transport: macOS AppleScript accessibility APIs; optional for later.

    Security defaults:
    - Per-host `capture: true` opt-in; default false on all hosts.
    - `mcp_screenshot` must support `region` cropping to avoid leaking full displays.
    - Hard cap on image size (2 MB default, 4 MB hard) with downscale for oversize.
    - All capture calls logged with host, type, region, and size.
    - clipboard-image is opt-in alongside clipboard text; never called automatically.

    Implementation order:
    1. macbook first (pbcopy/pbpaste + screencapture are safest and well documented).
    2. Add Linux screenshot fallbacks only after macOS path is stable.
    3. Do not add click/drag/keyboard automation; that stays in PlayLive.
```

# Ada How-To Runbooks

Step-by-step procedures for ada-pi tools, calendar providers, and memory banks

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.ada.howto.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Ada How-To Runbooks
subtitle: Step-by-step procedures for ada-pi tools, calendar providers, and memory banks

prerequisites:
  - ssot: ssot.apps.ada-calendar.yml
  - ssot: ssot.apps.ada-memory-banks.yml
  - ssot: ssot.apps.ada_pi.yml
  - decisions: ssot.technical-decisions.yml (ada-calendar-provider-backend)

runbooks:
  add_ada_tool:
    purpose: Add a new Gemini Live tool to ada — all three layers must move together.
    steps:
      - "Add the method to ToolRunner in ada-pi/backend/tool_runner.py (async, simple typed args)"
      - "If it mutates anything, add its name to the right gate set (CONTROL_TOOLS / MEMORY_WRITE_TOOLS / CALENDAR_WRITE_TOOLS) and give it a confirmed arg"
      - "Add a function_declaration in backend/realtime_provider.py — description written as WHEN to use it, parameters_json_schema with additionalProperties: false"
      - "Extend the instruction paragraph in GeminiLiveProvider.__init__ with the workflow (call order, confirm protocol, which tool family to prefer)"
      - "Add a unit test; deploy via chaba/scripts/deploy-ada.sh"
    note: |
      The description is the primary steering mechanism; the instruction
      paragraph teaches sequencing. The gate enforces the contract server-side
      even if the model misbehaves. Keep declarations and instructions in sync —
      ADA_EXCLUDED_TOOLS removes both.

  google_calendar_reauth:
    purpose: Re-mint the Google refresh token when calendar tools return auth errors.
    steps:
      - "Confirm the consent screen is published (Testing status = tokens die in 7 days): console.cloud.google.com -> project gen-lang-client-0694401188 -> OAuth consent screen"
      - "Confirm Google Calendar API and Google Tasks API are enabled on that project"
      - "Run: python3 scripts/ada/google-calendar-auth.py --host mn01 (opens a browser; approve with the Google account)"
      - "Verify: python3 scripts/ada/google-calendar-auth.py --check"
      - "No service restart needed — the adapter re-reads the token file on the next call"
    note: |
      The token file is per-ada (ada-google-calendar-token.json); the OAuth
      client (google_credentials.json) is shared with the Drive backup — do
      not overwrite it.

  add_calendar_provider:
    purpose: Add a calendar/tasks provider (e.g. iCloud via CalDAV) to ada.
    steps:
      - "Write the adapter in ada-pi/backend/<provider>_calendar.py implementing CalendarProvider (and TasksProvider if it has tasks)"
      - "Register the adapter name in CalendarService._build (backend/calendar_providers.py)"
      - "Add the provider block under calendar.providers in ssot.apps.ada-calendar.yml (adapter, instances, status: active, secrets pointer)"
      - "Store credentials under ~/.config/secrets/ on the ada host"
      - "Render: python3 scripts/ada/render-calendar-providers.py --host mn01"
      - "Verify: ada 'which calendars do I have' should list the new provider's calendars"
    note: |
      Switching entirely: set calendar.read + calendar.write to the new
      provider name. Running several: leave read: aggregate; writes go to
      write: unless the user names 'provider:calendar_id'.

  save_decision_to_memory:
    purpose: Capture a decision or Q&A outcome so ada, Devin, and the vault can all recall it later.
    steps:
      - "By voice: tell ada 'remember that <fact>' — she calls ada_remember (confirmed banks ask first)"
      - "From scripts/devin: POST /api/tools/call {tool: ada_remember, args: {bank, subject, attribute, kind, text, confirmed: true}} on any running service (mn01:8002, tony-dell:8001, idc01:8001/8002)"
      - "Recall: ada_memory_search by voice, MDDB semantic_search for Devin, vault note after the next sync-ada-memory-to-mddb run"
      - "For superseding facts pass key or subject+attribute — remember() does find-then-update; use ada_forget to retract, ada_outcome to record how it turned out"
    note: |
      New docs take ~3-4 min to become searchable (async embedding via
      gemini-ollama-proxy) — a direct /v1/get confirms the write immediately.
      Verified live 2026-09-21: general/google-tasks written via HTTP
      ada_remember, recalled rank-1 at score 0.73.

  distill_memory_backstop:
    purpose: Sweep voice session summaries for durable facts the inline extraction missed; draft them for review.
    steps:
      - "Dry-run first: python3 scripts/ada/memory-distill.py --dry-run (prints candidates, writes nothing)"
      - "Real run: python3 scripts/ada/memory-distill.py [--instance tony] [--since-days 14] [--emit]"
      - "Needs GEMINI_API_KEY in env (source ~/.config/secrets/ada-pi-pwa.env); MDDB via ADA_MEMORY_MDDB_URL"
      - "Review drafts: sync-ada-memory-to-mddb.py --export-inbox -> docs/ada-memory/inbox/ -> promote with consolidate-memory.py"
      - "Regression-gate prompt changes: python3 scripts/ada/memory-distill-benchmark.py (--dump to see candidates)"
    note: |
      Backstop for inline ADA_EXTRACT_CANDIDATES (session-close, on by
      default). Writes are status=draft — invisible to ada_memory_search
      until promoted. Dedup: same subject+attribute in the bank, or a
      vector hit above 0.82. First live run caught 2 facts inline missed.

  calendar_tool_debug:
    purpose: Diagnose calendar tools failing or returning empty results.
    steps:
      - "Check the registry rendered: python3 scripts/ada/render-calendar-providers.py --check (drift = re-render + deploy)"
      - "Check ~/.config/ada/calendar.json on the ada host lists the provider with status: active and the right instances:"
      - "Check the token: python3 scripts/ada/google-calendar-auth.py --check on a host with the token file"
      - "Check service logs: journalctl --user -u ada-ha-tony -n 100 | grep -i calendar"
      - "Confirm ADA_INSTANCE_ID matches the provider's instances list"
    note: |
      A missing registry or no providers for the instance makes tools return
      'not configured' — deliberate, not a bug. Per-provider failures surface
      in the 'errors' list of list results rather than failing the whole call.

config:
  version: 1
  created: "2026-09-21"
  maintainer: tony
  status: active
```

# Audit Framework

Consolidated testing, validation, and security audit suite

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.audit.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Audit Framework
subtitle: Consolidated testing, validation, and security audit suite
icon: 🕵️
version: 1

overview:
  purpose: |
    Centralize all project audits (KB, SSOT, security) under one runner and one
    normalized report format. The framework is SSOT-driven: this file defines
    which audits exist, how to run them, and where they are scheduled.

config:
  version: 1
  last_updated: "2026-09-18"
  maintainer: tony
  status: active

runner:
  script: scripts/audits/run.mjs
  command: node
  default_args: []
  full_args:
    - --full
  report_dir: reports/audits
  outputs:
    - reports/audits/summary.json
    - reports/audits/summary.md
    - reports/audits/history/history.json

ci:
  pipeline_stage: audits
  pipeline_script: scripts/ci-pipeline.sh

schedule:
  default:
    frequency: weekly
    timer: systemd/chaba-audit.timer
    service: systemd/chaba-audit.service
    args: default_args
    runs:
      - kb-suite
      - ssot-suite
      - caddy
      - infrastructure-suite
      - standardization-suite
      - code-suite
      - dev-system
      - ssot-kb-memory
      - memory-suite
    note: groups are expanded to individual audits by the runner
  full:
    frequency: monthly
    timer: systemd/chaba-audit-full.timer
    service: systemd/chaba-audit-full.service
    args: full_args
    runs:
      - kb-suite
      - ssot-suite
      - caddy
      - infrastructure-suite
      - security-suite
      - standardization-suite
      - code-suite
      - dev-system
      - ssot-kb-memory
      - memory-suite
    note: installed and enabled on tony-dell; security-audit may need privileges

audits:
  - name: kb
    script: scripts/kb-audit.mjs
    command: node
    args:
      - --json
    schedule: weekly
    severity_on_fail: warning
    description: KB coverage, freshness, and section quality
    last_run:
    last_result:

  - name: ssot
    script: scripts/ssot-validate-all.mjs
    command: node
    args: []
    schedule: weekly
    severity_on_fail: error
    description: SSOT YAML syntax and cross-reference validation
    last_run:
    last_result:

  - name: kb-modularity
    script: scripts/audits/kb-modularity-audit.mjs
    command: node
    args: []
    schedule: weekly
    severity_on_fail: warning
    description: KB entry focus, size, and duplicate detection
    last_run:
    last_result:
    thresholds:
      max_words: 1500
      max_headings: 25
      min_links: 0
      max_similarity: 0.85
      excluded_files:
        - docs/kb/.template.md
        - docs/kb/README.md
      excluded_patterns:
        - '^docs/kb/auto-.*\.md$'
        - '^docs/kb/task-.*\.md$'

  - name: ssot-modularity

    args: []
    schedule: weekly

    last_run:
    last_result:
    thresholds:
      max_words: 3000

  - name: http-health
    script: scripts/audits/http-health-audit.mjs

      Timeout retries once at 2x before failing. Also checks TLS cert
      expiry (<30d warn, <7d fail). HEALTH_PROFILE selects the profile set.
    last_run:
    last_result:

  - name: smoke

      systems.mcp.scripts (mcp-debug, focus, verify-all-mcp-servers).
      Non-zero exit or 120s timeout fails. Overlaps the ssot-kb-memory T1
      mcp section by design: this reports per-script exits in the suite.
    last_run:
    last_result:

  - name: staleness

    command: node

      security baseline last_verified >90d, bloat_exemptions quarterly review
      overdue, and audit-hosts last_observed snapshots >14d old.
    last_run:
    last_result:

  - name: ssot-kb-memory
    script: scripts/test-ssot-kb-memory.sh
    command: bash
    args:

    schedule: weekly
    severity_on_fail: warning
    description: >
      Drift/failure checks for SSOT, Devin DB, local memory layer, NotebookLM
      archive, MDDB, Weaviate, and MCP smoke suite. Expected state is declared
      in docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.test-manifest.yml; DRIFT lines mean live
      state differs from declared expectations (update the manifest if
      intentional). NotebookLM checks SKIP when nlm auth is expired.
    last_run:
    last_result:

  - name: memory-banks
    script: scripts/audits/memory-banks-audit.mjs
    command: node
    args: []
    schedule: weekly
    severity_on_fail: warning
    description: >
      Ada memory-bank health: registry <-> MDDB collection drift (expected
      state derived from ssot.apps.ada-memory-banks.yml), schema hygiene on
      ada-ha-bank-* docs, NotebookLM group routing env coverage, devin-bank
      sync freshness, and devin distillation backlog. DRIFT warns mean live
      state differs from the registry — fix the registry or the system.
    thresholds:
      max_undistilled_devin: 200
      max_doc_bytes: 51200
      max_missing_core_docs: 0
      devin_sync_stale_days: 2
      revision_bloat_ratio: 20
    last_run:
    last_result:

groups:
  - name: kb-suite
    description: All KB health, quality, categorization, and modularity audits
    children:
      - kb
      - auto-kb-quality
      - kb-categorize
      - kb-modularity
  - name: ssot-suite
    description: All SSOT validation and modularity audits
    children:
      - ssot
      - ssot-modularity
  - name: caddy
    description: Caddy reverse proxy checks
    children:
      - caddy
  - name: security-suite
    description: Secret scan and system-level security review
    children:
      - security-scan
      - security-audit
  - name: infrastructure-suite
    description: Health SSOT and infrastructure configuration consistency
    children:
      - infrastructure
      - http-health
      - mddb
      - smoke
  - name: code-suite
    description: Code formatting, spell, and dependency security
    children:
      - code-quality
  - name: standardization-suite
    description: Cross-reference and naming consistency checks
    children:
      - standardization
      - doc-links
      - staleness
  - name: memory-suite
    description: Ada memory-bank registry/health audits (MDDB banks, vault, NLM routing)
    children:
      - memory-banks

semantics:
  description: >
    Verdict taxonomy across the audit tracks. PASS means the declared
    invariant holds. FAIL (exit 1) means a hard invariant broke — a missing
    file, unreachable required service, or parse error. WARN means a
    warning-severity audit failed: reported in the summary but the suite
    still exits 0 (run.mjs honors severity_on_fail). DRIFT (manifest-driven
    checks only) means live state differs from declared expectations and is
    usually fixed by updating the manifest, not the system. SKIP means a
    precondition (auth, host scope) was absent.
  overlap:
    - mddb: the `mddb` audit checks the live API contract (health, stats, search, proxy); the `ssot-kb-memory` mddb section checks declared manifest expectations (collections, score threshold). Both run; mddb-audit verdicts are harder (live probes), manifest verdicts are DRIFT-style.
    - ssot_yaml: the `ssot` audit and the ssot-kb-memory T0 block both run ssot-validate-all; results are cached so the overlap is cheap.
    - mcp smoke: the `smoke` audit and ssot-kb-memory T1 mcp section run the same manifest-declared scripts; smoke reports per-script exits in the suite, T1 reports them inside the drift suite.

plan:
  current_state:
    - scripts/audits/run.mjs derives PROJECT_ROOT from import.meta.url (runs on any checkout)
    - run.mjs honors severity_on_fail: error-severity failures gate the suite; warning-severity failures report WARN without failing
    - run.mjs writes a focus-inbox alert (audit-failures.yml) on error-severity failures and auto-resolves it when green
```

# Devin Session Modes

Operational modes that shape how the assistant behaves in a session

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.devin-modes.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
id: ssot.devin-modes
title: Devin Session Modes
subtitle: Operational modes that shape how the assistant behaves in a session
category: infrastructure
status: operational
source_of_truth: true

modes:
  - id: normal
    name: Normal
    description: |
      Default session behavior. Plan when needed, then execute.
    behavior: |
      - Load the active focus and applicable rules.
      - Use the todo tool for multi-step work.
      - Implement, edit, and run commands when the request is clear.
      - Validate and commit completed work.

  - id: plan
    name: Plan
    description: |
      Plan only. Do not write files, run commands, or make commits.
    behavior: |
      - Ask clarifying questions until the task is well-defined.
      - Produce a step-by-step plan with estimates and risks.
      - Do not perform any file edits, shell commands, or git operations.
      - End by summarizing the plan and recommend switching to build mode for execution.

  - id: build
    name: Build
    description: |
      Execute an existing plan or approved task. Ask before destructive operations.
    behavior: |
      - Implement the approved plan or active focus.
      - Use the todo tool to track progress.
      - Ask for confirmation before destructive operations (rm, force pushes, etc.).
      - Validate and commit completed work.

  - id: review
    name: Review
    description: |
      Inspect and comment on code, diffs, or SSOT. Do not modify unless asked.
    behavior: |
      - Read the relevant files or git diff.
      - Provide concise, objective feedback.
      - Do not modify files unless the user explicitly asks for a change.

config:
  locations:
    - ~/.config/devin/config.json
    - .devin/config.local.json
    - .devin/config.json
  key: mode.current
  override_env: DEVIN_MODE
  default: normal
  notes: |
    Devin Desktop does not expose session modes natively, so the active mode is
    read from the session configuration. `DEVIN_MODE` overrides any file value
    for ad-hoc sessions (e.g. `DEVIN_MODE=plan devin`).

rules:
  - At the start of every session, read the active mode from the configuration.
  - If the mode is plan, build, or review, follow the behavior above.
  - If the mode is missing or unknown, default to normal and note it.

```

# Devin Sessions DB Maintenance

Cleanup, retention, and vacuum policy for Devin desktop/cli session databases

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.devin.maintenance.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
id: ssot.devin.maintenance
title: Devin Sessions DB Maintenance
subtitle: Cleanup, retention, and vacuum policy for Devin desktop/cli session databases
category: infrastructure
status: operational
source_of_truth: true

overview: |
  Devin stores sessions, message nodes, and tool-call state in a local SQLite
  database (`~/.local/share/devin/cli/sessions.db`). On active workstations this
  database can grow quickly because message nodes may contain large base64
  screenshots, code output, and card/dashboard JSON. This SSOT defines the
  maintenance policy, cleanup timers, and manual runbook for keeping the DB under
  control.

hosts:
  tony-dell:
    path: /home/tony/.local/share/devin/cli/sessions.db
    description: Secondary workstation, headless browser/cast target
    current_size: 45Mi
    service: devin-cleanup.timer
    retention_days: 7
    notes:
      - Cleanup timer runs Sundays at 04:00.
      - Service skips VACUUM if Devin code.lock is present.
      - Devin desktop updated to 3.10.23-1789035177 on 2026-09-12.
      - devin-desktop-watchdog.sh runs every 10 minutes to kill a renderer stuck above 50% CPU for 10 seconds.
      - cast-desktop@1.service, playlived.service, go2rtc.service, and Wine VMS.exe reniced to 10 to reduce UI contention.

  tony-omen:
    path: /home/tony/.local/share/devin/cli/sessions.db
    description: Primary dev workstation
    current_size: 6.6Gi
    service: devin-cleanup.timer
    retention_days: 3
    notes:
      - Cleanup timer runs daily at 03:00 with up to 1h randomized delay.
      - Retention reduced from 7 to 3 days on 2026-09-12 (DB had grown to 67 GiB).
      - Most DB size comes from active/recent sessions; 3-day retention does
        not free much space until those sessions age out or are deleted manually.
      - >
        2026-09-16 chunked NotebookLM offload reduced DB ~13.3 GiB -> ~6.6 GiB;
        largest sessions (utopian-pearl ~8 GiB, juvenile-umbra, ambiguous-rooster,
        seemly-graffiti, invincible-avatar, abundance-cattle, olive-lamb,
        blush-action, valuable-windflower) archived and deleted manually.

cleanup:
  timer_schedule:
    tony-dell: "Sun *-*-* 04:00:00"
    tony-omen: "*-*-* 03:00:00 (RandomizedDelaySec=1h)"
  service:
    tony-dell: devin-cleanup.service
    tony-omen: devin-cleanup.service
  script:
    tony-dell: /home/tony/.local/bin/devin-cleanup.sh
    tony-omen: /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba/scripts/prune-devin-sessions.sh
  retention_days:
    tony-dell: 7
    tony-omen: 3
  behavior: |
    1. Compute cutoff = now - retention_days.
    2. Delete child rows from `message_nodes` and `tool_call_state` for sessions
       with `last_activity_at < cutoff`.
    3. Delete sessions with `last_activity_at < cutoff`.
    4. VACUUM the database only when no Devin process has the file open.
  skip_conditions:
    - "Devin code.lock is present (tony-dell script checks this)."
    - "fuser reports the DB is open (tony-omen script checks this)."
    - "In those cases DELETE still runs, VACUUM is deferred."

offload_to_notebooklm:
  purpose: |
    Before old sessions are deleted from the local SQLite DB, their raw
    transcripts are uploaded to a NotebookLM archive so the history remains
    searchable and can be recalled by Devin in future sessions.
  notebook_id: 009b3efe-ff58-40bc-9a3b-9ec946b38deb
  scripts:
    - /home/tony/.config/devin/scripts/devin-extract-sessions.sh
    - /home/tony/.config/devin/scripts/devin-chunked-extract.sh
    - /home/tony/.config/devin/scripts/devin-archive-sessions.sh
    - /home/tony/.config/devin/scripts/vacuum-devin-db.sh
  workflow: |
    1. Extract (no delete):
       `bash /home/tony/.config/devin/scripts/devin-extract-sessions.sh --older-than 3`
       Uploads the most recent `MAX_SOURCE_CHARS` of each old session to
       NotebookLM and saves a local `.md` copy in
       `~/.local/share/devin/notebook-summaries/raw`.
    2. Extract and delete:
       `bash /home/tony/.config/devin/scripts/devin-extract-sessions.sh --older-than 3 --delete`
       Uploads to NotebookLM, then runs `devin rm --force <session-id>` for
       each session that was successfully archived.
    3. Final VACUUM:
       Close all Devin windows and run
       `bash /home/tony/.config/devin/scripts/vacuum-devin-db.sh`.
       It creates a local SQLite backup, optionally extracts sessions again
       (`DEVIN_EXTRACT_OLD_SESSIONS=1`), runs `VACUUM`, and keeps the backup
       local by default.
  chunked_archive:
    script: /home/tony/.config/devin/scripts/devin-chunked-extract.sh
    purpose: |
      For sessions too large for a single NotebookLM source, split the raw
      transcript into `MAX_SOURCE_CHARS` chunks, upload them to a temporary
      staging notebook, ask NotebookLM to summarize the chunks, save the
      summary to the archive notebook, and then delete the staging notebook.
      The full transcript is also saved locally in `~/.local/share/devin/notebook-summaries/raw`.
    limits:
      MAX_SOURCE_CHARS: 100000 (default)
      MAX_CHUNKS: 20 (default)
    notes:
      - >
        The current script summarizes and deletes the staging notebook immediately.
      - >
        For a 7-day chunk retention, keep the staging notebook and run a separate
        scheduled compactor that queries the staging notebook and deletes it
        once the summary is generated.
      - >
        The script tracks failures per stage (chunk upload, summary query,
        archive add, staging delete, session delete) and exits non-zero with
        `Incomplete: <id> — <reasons>` if anything failed. A metadata-stub
        `--summary.md` is still written locally when the query fails, and the
        orphan staging notebook ID is printed for manual cleanup. `--delete` is
        skipped unless every stage succeeded.
      - >
        ONE session-id per invocation — `Error: only one session-id may be
        provided` otherwise. Batch via a shell loop.
    progress_2026_09_18: |
      Archived + deleted: chivalrous-babcat, lacy-taxicab, statuesque-attack,
      expensive-button (archive notebook at 36 sources, 0 staging orphans,
      0 orphaned message_nodes). Pending next auth window: woolly-potato
      (partial archive — 15/20 chunks, summary in archive) and
      cooing-cyclamen (summary local-only, not in archive). Both keep their
      full.md transcripts locally regardless.

  environment:
    DEVIN_ARCHIVE_NOTEBOOK: |
      Notebook ID to upload raw transcripts to. Defaults to the shared
      Chaba archive (`009b3efe-ff58-40bc-9a3b-9ec946b38deb`).
    DEVIN_UPLOAD_BACKUP: |
      Set to `1` to upload the SQLite backup to GDrive using rclone.
      Default is `0` (local backup only).
    DEVIN_EXTRACT_OLD_SESSIONS: |
      Set to `1` inside `vacuum-devin-db.sh` to extract old sessions before
      the final VACUUM. Default is `0` to keep the vacuum fast.
    MAX_SOURCE_CHARS: |
      Cap on how much of each session transcript is uploaded. Default `100000`.
    NLM_HOST: |
      SSH host the `nlm` wrapper (`~/.local/bin/nlm`) delegates to. Default
      `mn01` (rootless podman `notebooklm-mcp` container, image
      `localhost/notebooklm-mcp:latest`, quadlet
      `~/.config/containers/systemd/notebooklm-mcp.container` on mn01).
      Set `NLM_HOST=tony-dell` to use the legacy host.
    DEVIN_KEEP_BACKUPS: |
      How many `sessions.db.*` backups `vacuum-devin-db.sh` keeps in
      `~/.local/share/devin/cli/backups/` (plus `-shm`/`-wal` sidecars).
      Default `2`.
  notes:
    - >
      `nlm` is a local wrapper that ssh's to `mn01` (was `tony-dell`) and runs
      the NotebookLM MCP container. Tailscale SSH must be authenticated for
      uploads to succeed.
    - >
      Deleting sessions while Devin is running is best done via `devin rm`;
      however `devin rm` cannot see sessions created by devin-desktop (it
      reports `no session found matching '<id>'` even though the row exists
      in `sessions`). All extract/archive scripts therefore fall back to a
      direct sqlite3 DELETE of `message_nodes`/`tool_call_state`/`sessions`
      rows when `devin rm` fails. The sqlite3 path needs the DB unlocked —
      close Devin first.
    - >
      The `devin-archive-sessions.sh` script still exists for the previous
      summary-and-delete flow; use it if you want condensed summaries rather
      than raw transcripts.

  reauth_runbook: |
    NotebookLM cookie auth expires frequently (observed ~15-60 min of API use;
    `__Secure-*PSIDTS` rotates fast, so hand-copied headers are often stale on
    arrival). When `nlm` reports "Authentication expired", do NOT paste a stale
    header — harvest a live one from the logged-in Chrome on tony-omen via the
    chrome-devtools MCP:

    1. `new_page https://notebook.google.com/` (loads authenticated; the user's
       Google session must be active in that Chrome profile).
    2. `list_network_requests` → find any POST to notebook.google.com
       (e.g. a `batchexecute` call).
    3. `get_network_request` → copy the `cookie:` request header value.
    4. Write it to `/tmp/nlm_cookies.txt`, then:
       `scp /tmp/nlm_cookies.txt mn01:~/.local/share/notebooklm/.notebooklm-mcp-cli/cookies_import.txt`
       `nlm login --manual -f /root/.notebooklm-mcp-cli/cookies_import.txt -p default`
    5. Verify: `nlm notebook list --json` should return notebooks.

    Caveats:
    - The container mounts `~/.local/share/notebooklm/.notebooklm-mcp-cli` on
      mn01 as `/root/.notebooklm-mcp-cli`; the `-f` path is container-side.
    - `nlm login` (browser flow) does not work inside the container — no Chrome.
    - Known open issue: notebooklm-rest logs `Failed to write updated cookies
      to /data/storage_state.json: OSError` — refreshed cookies may not persist,
      so re-auth is recurring until that mount/perm issue is fixed.

    Better paths (found 2026-09-18):
    - PREFERRED: `scripts/nlm-reauth.sh mn01` on tony-omen runs the REAL
      nlm binary (`~/.local/share/nlm-venv/bin/nlm`) — a full browser login —
      then scp's `cookies.json`/`metadata.json` to the container profile dir.
      A real login saves a Chrome profile, which is required for
      `nlm auth refresh` (non-interactive cookie reissue) to work; manual
      cookie imports can never use `auth refresh` ("saved Chrome profile may
      be missing or its login expired").
    - `nlm auth refresh` can keep a session alive indefinitely IF a saved
      Chrome profile exists — candidates: `nlm-reauth.sh` (real login) or
      `nlm login --provider openclaw --cdp-url <url>` (attaches to an external
      Chrome over CDP; tony-omen's debug Chrome listens on 127.0.0.1:9228 with
      `--user-data-dir=~/.config/google-chrome-debug`; the notebooklm-mcp
      container is host-networked, so `ssh -R <port>:localhost:9228 mn01`
      could expose it as http://127.0.0.1:<port> — unverified).
    - Sizing rule: one harvest buys ~20-60 min ≈ 1-2 archive sessions.
      Multi-session batches WILL hit expiry mid-run; either reauth per
      session or fix durable auth (real login + `auth refresh`) first.
    - Safety gates verified: sessions are never deleted unless the summary
      is archived AND the staging notebook is deleted; partial runs leave a
      `staging-*` orphan (list: `nlm notebook list --json` | grep staging;
      delete: `nlm notebook delete <id> --confirm`) and keep the session.
    - `devin-chunked-extract.sh` accepts ONE session-id per invocation —
      loop for batches. Extraction (full.md) works without auth; only the
      NotebookLM stages and `--delete` gate on it.

backup_policy: |
  `vacuum-devin-db.sh` now creates a local backup before VACUUM and keeps it
  on the host by default. Set `DEVIN_UPLOAD_BACKUP=1` to also copy the backup
  to the configured rclone GDrive remote (`gdrive:DevinBackups`).

  Automated cleanup does not back up the database before pruning.
  `prune-devin-sessions.sh` supports `NO_BACKUP=1` for large DBs to avoid
  duplicating a 50+ GiB file. If a pre-cleanup backup is required, set
  `NO_BACKUP=` and ensure the filesystem has at least 2x the DB size free.

vacuum_policy: |
  - VACUUM requires an exclusive lock; it cannot run while Devin is using the DB.
  - The timer-triggered cleanup will skip VACUUM when the DB is in use.
  - To force a one-time VACUUM, close Devin and run the cleanup script manually:
    - tony-dell: `systemctl --user start devin-cleanup.service`
    - tony-omen: `systemctl --user start devin-cleanup.service`

size_alerts:
  - threshold_gb: 20
    severity: warning
    action: Review largest sessions and consider shorter retention or manual cleanup.
  - threshold_gb: 50
    severity: critical
    action: |
      The DB is consuming a large portion of the root filesystem. Identify the
      largest active sessions, close Devin, and either delete those sessions or
      move the DB to a larger disk.

manual_cleanup_runbook: |
  1. Identify the largest sessions:
     SELECT m.session_id, s.title, COUNT(*) cnt,
            SUM(LENGTH(m.chat_message))/1024/1024 total_mb
     FROM message_nodes m
     JOIN sessions s ON m.session_id = s.id
     GROUP BY m.session_id
     ORDER BY total_mb DESC;
  2. Verify the session is not active by checking
     `~/.local/share/devin/cli/session_locks/<session_id>.lock`.
  3. Offload the sessions you want to keep to NotebookLM:
     `bash /home/tony/.config/devin/scripts/devin-extract-sessions.sh <session-id>`
     or for a batch:
     `bash /home/tony/.config/devin/scripts/devin-extract-sessions.sh --older-than 3 --delete`
  4. Close Devin and run the cleanup script with the desired retention, or delete
     specific sessions manually and then VACUUM.
  5. Re-open Devin and verify the DB size.

audit_checks:
  - Check `devin-cleanup.timer` is active on each host.
  - Check `devin-cleanup.service` is not in a failed state.
```

# Dynamic SSOT References

When and how to use ${ssot(...)} expressions, __ref__, and !ssot_ref

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.dynamic-references.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Dynamic SSOT References
subtitle: When and how to use ${ssot(...)} expressions, __ref__, and !ssot_ref
icon: link
version: 1

overview:
  purpose: |
    Define the boundary for using dynamic SSOT references so the project gets
    the benefits of a single source of truth without turning every SSOT file
    into a fragile template.

rule:
  use_when_all_true:
    - The value is a runtime address, URL, host:port, or IP composed from canonical values.
    - The same value appears in more than one SSOT file or is likely to be reused.
    - The file is a consumer, not the canonical source, and is read by mcp_query_ssot or mcp_ssot_get.
  do_not_use_for:
    - Canonical source files, especially docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.values.yml
    - Narrative notes, migration history, or explanations
    - Secrets, tokens, API keys, or credentials
    - File paths, UUIDs, IDs, or one-off identifiers
    - Values that only appear in one file
    - Files consumed by tools that do not understand the !ssot_ref YAML tag

syntax:
  preferred:
    - name: String interpolation with ${ssot(...)}
      for: Composed URLs, host:port strings, and health-check commands
      example: |
        tailscale_funnel: 'https://${ssot("docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.values.yml", "hosts.tony_dell.tailscale")}:${ssot("docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.values.yml", "ports.ha_live_public")}'
    - name: __ref__ object
      for: Simple single-value substitutions that must stay plain YAML
      example: |
        backend:
          __ref__:
            path: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.values.yml
            key: hosts.tony_dell.tailscale_ip
  allowed_with_care:
    - name: "!ssot_ref"
      for: Files that are guaranteed to only be loaded by mcp_debug/ssot.py
      warning: Other consumers (config.py, MDDB sync, plain yaml.safe_load) will fail unless they also register the !ssot_ref constructor.

canonical_source:
  file: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.values.yml
  note: |
    Keep hosts, ports, schedules, thresholds, paths, and other shared facts here.
    Consumer SSOTs should reference this file, not copy its values.

consumers:
  mcp_query_ssot:
    for: Exact, dotted-path, wildcard, and fuzzy lookup of a single value.
    resolves: true
    line: Use this when you need the canonical value, a URL, or a nested fact.
  mcp_ssot_get:
    for: Registry asset lookup across partitioned SSOT files.
    resolves: true
    line: Use this when the key is a registry asset rather than a file path.
  mcp_read_ssot:
    for: Bounded direct read of a whole SSOT file.
    resolves: false
    line: Use this when you need the raw file, not just one value.
  mddb:
    for: Semantic metadata and glossary search across indexed SSOT and KB text.
    resolves: false
    line: Use the chaba-glossary collection for exact values; use infrastructure-ssot for topic/keyword search.
  notebooklm-kb-sync:
    for: Natural-language search and synthesis over the textual KB and SSOTs.
    resolves: false
    line: Use this when the question is fuzzy, cross-file, or needs prose explanation.

notebooklm:
  use_for:
    - Fuzzy or natural-language questions across multiple KB/SSOT files.
    - '"How do I...?" and "Why is this configured this way?" questions.'
    - Discovering related concepts before drilling down with mcp_query_ssot.
  do_not_use_for:
    - Exact numeric values, ports, IPs, URLs, IDs, or secret paths.
    - Deterministic, reproducible answers required for automation.
    - Values that are not in the synced sources.
    - Any action that will be executed without verifying with mcp_query_ssot first.
  rule: |
    NotebookLM is a secondary, read-only consumer of SSOT. It can suggest answers,
    but canonical facts must still come from mcp_query_ssot or the resolver.

mddb:
  use_for:
    - 'Exact value lookups in chaba-glossary: "Tailscale IP of tony-dell", "notebooklm port".'
    - Keyword/title search across infrastructure-ssot.
    - Finding which SSOT file documents a host, app, or service.
  do_not_use_for:
    - Procedural "How do I...?" questions that need synthesis.
    - Natural-language questions not covered by the glossary.
    - Exact dynamic values that should come from mcp_query_ssot.
  rule: |
    MDDB is a fast first-pass search layer. It is not a reasoning engine.
    For exact canonical values, prefer mcp_query_ssot; for prose answers, prefer NotebookLM.

anti_patterns:
  - bad: "note: 'Migrated 2026-08-17 from tony-omen to 100.68.142.13:8084'"
    why: A historical note should remain literal and human-readable.
  - bad: "image: docker.io/homeassistant/home-assistant:stable"
    why: An external identifier is not derived from project infrastructure.
  - bad: "secret_path: /private_CtYuVkJEl28cp8qA8yXNCQ"
    why: Secrets and tokens must not be composed through SSOT references.
  - bad: "port: ${ssot('ssot.values.yml', 'ports.ha_tony')}"
    why: The canonical ssot.values.yml must not reference itself.

migration:
  steps:
    - Add the missing canonical value to ssot.values.yml first.
    - Replace the duplicated literal in consumer SSOTs with the chosen reference syntax.
    - Validate the file with python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('...'))".
    - Run mcp_query_ssot against the new reference to confirm it resolves.
  caution: |
    Do not batch-convert every repeated string at once. Convert one logical
    family (e.g., Home Assistant URLs) at a time, then evaluate the logs before
    the next family.

```

Runner, schedule, failure handling, and MCP/sub-agent integration for the focus-dispatcher script

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.focus-dispatcher.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Focus Dispatcher
subtitle: Runner, schedule, failure handling, and MCP/sub-agent integration for the focus-dispatcher script
icon: target
version: 2

runner:
  script: /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/scripts/focus-dispatcher.py
  note: Thin CLI that imports and calls the focus_dispatcher package. Legacy systemd/cron paths remain unchanged.
  entry_points:
    - no arguments: archive completed, validate limits, then select the highest-priority active or inbox focus
    - --inbox <path>: force-activate a specific inbox file
    - --park: park the existing active focus in the same section before activating a new one
    - --sub-agent: write a sub-agent contract for the selected active focus to reports/SUBAGENT_CONTRACT.md
    - --intake <request>: classify a new request and write it to the correct place
    - --decompose <request>: classify a large request, split it into subtasks, and write the resulting focus to the active focus or backlog
    - --safe-dispatch: find the highest-scoring safe-to-parallel item and add it to Ready (Safe)
    - --process-ready [--host tony_dell]: pick an unlocked Ready (Safe) item, lock it, and write a SUBAGENT_CONTRACT for that host
    - --host <host>: target host for --process-ready (default tony_dell)
    - --next: activate the highest-priority parked/deferred focus (fails if another focus is active)
    - --advance: archive completed focuses and then --next, if the current active focus is complete
    - --resume-session <name>: restrict --next / --advance to a named session
    - --dry-run: show selection without modifying files
  permissions:
    - read docs/ssot/ssot.focus.current.yml
    - read docs/ssot/ssot.focus.yml
    - read docs/ssot/focus-inbox/*.yml
    - write docs/ssot/ssot.focus.current.yml
    - write docs/ssot/ssot.focus.yml
    - write reports/NEXT_FOCUS.md
    - execute git mv for inbox files
    - execute git commit and git push when FOCUS_DISPATCHER_COMMIT/PUSH are set
  dependencies:
    - python3
    - PyYAML
    - git

package_design:
  package: /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/scripts/focus_dispatcher/
  cli: /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/scripts/focus-dispatcher.py
  layout:
    - state.py: repository paths, YAML I/O, section helpers, status predicates, validate_current
    - triage.py: priority_value, triage_score, next_from_active/inbox/backlog
    - history.py: archive helpers, _archive_section, outcome and tag helpers
    - actions.py: activate_inbox, suggest_intake, handle_intake, decompose_request
    - prompts.py: generate_prompt, generate_suggestion_prompt, generate_subagent_contract
    - git.py: git_mv_inbox, _is_allowed_staged_path, git_commit
    - cli.py: argument parser and main entry point
  conventions:
    - Each module owns one responsibility; avoid cross-circular imports.
    - Pure logic stays in triage/history/prompts; side effects live in actions/git/cli.
    - cli.py is a thin wrapper that imports package modules and calls their functions.
    - The public script path remains scripts/focus-dispatcher.py so systemd and cron units keep working.
    - Shared constants and file paths stay in state.py so tests and other scripts can import them.

selection_rules:
  - Active focuses are chosen first when they are not completed and have incomplete subtasks.
  - Inbox files are chosen when no active focus remains or when a specific inbox is requested.
  - Backlog items are sorted by triage_score, then priority, then started date.
  - triage_score comes from docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.focus.triage.yml (urgency 40%, importance 35%, simplicity 25%).
  - Priority order is high > medium > low and is only used as a tie-breaker when triage is missing.
  - Tie-breaker for active focuses: older started date first.
  - Inbox items are sorted by priority then filename for a stable order.

activation_behavior:
  - Runs validate_current() before any activation.
  - Loads the target inbox focus from docs/ssot/focus-inbox/.
  - Identifies shared vs branch by the presence of the branch field.
  - Without --park: refuses to activate if the target section already has an active item.
  - With --park: sets the existing active item(s) in the same section to status parked and records parked date.
  - Appends the new focus to the Active Shared Focus or Active Branch Focus section.
  - Archives completed active items to ssot.focus.yml Focus History before selecting.
  - Runs git mv to move the inbox file to docs/ssot/focus-inbox/processed/.
  - Writes a prompt to reports/NEXT_FOCUS.md for the assistant or sub-agent.

prompt_output:
  path: /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/reports/NEXT_FOCUS.md
  content:
    - Focus label and section
    - Branch or shared
    - Priority
    - Description
    - Incomplete and complete subtasks
    - Source file reference
    - Instructions for the assistant

auto_commit:
  - Set environment FOCUS_DISPATCHER_COMMIT=1 to auto-commit safe changes.
  - Set environment FOCUS_DISPATCHER_PUSH=1 to also push to origin.
  - Only docs/ssot/ssot.focus.current.yml, docs/ssot/ssot.focus.yml, and docs/ssot/focus-inbox/processed/* are committed.
  - The dispatcher now commits only its own paths and warns about any unexpected staged files it left behind, so user or overnight changes to other files no longer abort the run.
  - Auto-commit is disabled by default; enable by setting the variables in the systemd user service.

schedule:
  every_30_minutes:
    command: /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/scripts/focus-dispatcher.py
    purpose: Archive completed focuses, select the next active or inbox focus, and write reports/NEXT_FOCUS.md
    cron: "*/30 * * * * /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/scripts/focus-dispatcher.py >> /home/tony/var/chaba/focus-dispatcher.log 2>&1"
  overnight_review:
    command: /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/scripts/overnight-focus-review.py
    purpose: Generate health inbox drafts and update the next active focus sub-agent contract
    cron: "0 3 * * * /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/scripts/overnight-focus-review.py >> /home/tony/var/chaba/overnight-focus-review.log 2>&1"
    host: tony_dell
    systemd:
      - ~/.config/systemd/user/focus-dispatcher-overnight.service
      - ~/.config/systemd/user/focus-dispatcher-overnight.timer
      - OnCalendar=*-*-* 03:00:00
    notes:
      - mcp-health-to-inbox requires node and a local PostgreSQL (port 5432) on the runner host.
      - Set Environment="SKIP_HEALTH=1" on tony_dell to run only registry-drafts and focus-dispatcher --sub-agent.
      - When health is skipped, keep mcp-health-to-inbox on tony_omen or point it at a reachable Postgres host.
  auto_commit:
    note: Set FOCUS_DISPATCHER_COMMIT=1 and FOCUS_DISPATCHER_PUSH=1 in the service unit to enable hands-off commit/push

mcp_integration:
  - mcp-health: critical-failure or service-down events can create docs/ssot/focus-inbox/<service>-health.yml items.
  - mcp-debug / mcp_report: already generates savings reports; extend with mcp_focus to expose current active focus and backlog suggestions.
  - yomi: incoming LINE messages can be parsed and saved as inbox drafts when a user forwards a task or request.
  - workflows: schedule the dispatcher, auto-reload systemd units, and trigger the focus-dispatcher after an overnight assessment.
  - github: backlogged focuses can be mirrored to GitHub issues for public tracking.
  - mcp-gpu: GPU queue pressure can generate a focus-inbox item to review model selection or queue limits.

sub_agent:
  - NEXT_FOCUS.md is the default contract between the dispatcher and a sub-agent.
  - With --sub-agent the dispatcher also writes reports/SUBAGENT_CONTRACT.md with the same content plus sub-agent ground rules.
  - A sub-agent reads the contract, works inside the named focus, and updates subtask status before exiting.
  - The main session can then review the diff, validate YAML, and commit.
  - Future: invoke the sub-agent automatically from the dispatcher via a background runner.

failure_handling:
  - If ssot.focus.current.yml is missing or unparsable, exit with an error and do not modify files.
  - If an inbox YAML is invalid, log a warning and continue to the next file.
  - If git mv fails (e.g. uncommitted merge conflict), leave ssot.focus.current.yml updated but report the git error.
  - If no active or inbox focus is found, suggest the highest-priority backlog item in reports/NEXT_FOCUS.md and exit 0.
  - If ssot.focus.current.yml violates max_active_shared_focus or max_active_branch_focus, raise RuntimeError before selecting.
  - If activation is requested but no matching section exists or the limit is already reached, raise RuntimeError before any git or write.

```

# Focus Triage

Scoring rubric and selection formula for choosing the next backlog item

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.focus.triage.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Focus Triage
subtitle: Scoring rubric and selection formula for choosing the next backlog item
icon: triage
version: 1

purpose:
  - Replace the simple priority-based fallback with a numeric triage score.
  - Align with the existing impact scoring in docs/ssot/ssot.improvements.yml and service criticality in docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.health.yml.
  - Let the focus dispatcher rank backlog items by urgency, importance, and complication.

scoring:
  dimensions:
    - name: urgency
      description: Time pressure to act before damage spreads
      scale: 1-10
      rubric:
        9-10: already broken and actively affecting other people or systems
        6-8: will break or seriously degrade in the current cycle if not addressed
        3-5: could break soon or under load/edge cases; not failing yet
        1-2: stable and safe to defer; no known trigger
    - name: importance
      description: Downstream dependence of other systems on this focus
      scale: 1-10
      rubric:
        9-10: multiple critical systems depend on it
        6-8: important or several secondary systems depend on it
        3-5: a few minor systems depend on it
        1-2: isolated; little or no downstream impact
    - name: complication
      description: Friction and uncertainty to complete the work safely
      scale: 1-10
      rubric:
        8-10: wide blast radius, scheduling/coordination needed, missing info or unknowns
        4-7: touches a few related systems, possible short downtime, small info gaps
        1-3: single file or component, no downtime, all info in hand

  formula: |
    triage_score = urgency * 0.4 + importance * 0.35 + (10 - complication) * 0.25

  notes:
    - complication is inverted so simpler work scores higher.
    - Tie-breakers: triage_score, then priority, then started date.
    - For auto-generated health alerts, urgency and importance can be seeded from ssot.health.yml severity and service_criticality.

subagent_dispatch:
  description: Backlog and active items may be delegated to sub-agents when they are self-contained,
    low-interaction, and do not require real-time user approval.
  enabled: true
  item_fields:
    - subagent
    - safe_to_parallel
  subagent_schema:
    runnable: boolean
    profile: string
    parallel: boolean
    requires_approval: boolean
    can_change_host: boolean
    notes: string
    safe_to_parallel: boolean
    host: string
  dispatch_rules:
    - Only one foreground sub-agent may run at a time.
    - Background sub-agents may run in parallel if they touch different branches/hosts and no write conflicts.
    - Sub-agents must read the focus SSOTs and append a subagent_summary field to each subtask/focus they touch.
    - Sub-agents must not activate new foci or park existing ones without main-agent confirmation.
    - A focus with subagent.runnable false is foreground-only.

subagent_defaults:
  description: Default dispatch configuration for safe-to-parallel foci.
  host: tony_dell
  profile: subagent_general
  parallel: true
  requires_approval: false
  can_change_host: false
  notes: |
    The default execution host for safe foci is tony-dell. This keeps
    CPU/memory-heavy or multi-host work off the main workstation and lets
    background subagents run independently.
  exceptions:
    - host: local
      reason: Tasks that require the IDE, physical hardware, or user UI on tony-omen.
      requires_approval: true
    - host: macbook
      reason: Tasks that can only run on the macOS device.
      requires_approval: true

dispatch_host_policy:
  description: Where a focus or subtask must run.
  default: tony_dell
  rule: |
    Every focus, backlog item, inbox draft, and Ready (Safe) item must declare
    a subagent host. If the host is omitted, it is treated as tony_dell. The
    focus dispatcher will not process a Ready (Safe) item unless its
    subagent.host is tony_dell or an explicit local/macbook exception.

safe_to_parallel:
  description: A focus is safe to run in a parallel lane while another active focus remains in progress.
  enabled: true
  criteria:
    - id: branch_isolation
      label: No branch conflict
      rule: The focus branch must differ from both the active shared focus and active branch focus branches, or it is repo-neutral (chaba meta/docs only with no code changes on an active branch).
      weight: required
    - id: no_user_approval
      label: No real-time approval required
      rule: subagent.requires_approval must be false or missing; no step requires a user prompt mid-flight.
      weight: required
    - id: low_blast_radius
      label: Low blast radius
      rule: triage.complication must be 4 or lower, or the work is read-only (explore/research/validate only).
      weight: required
    - id: complete_info
      label: No missing info
      rule: missing_info must be empty or all items resolved before the safe focus runs.
      weight: required
    - id: active_focus_untouched
      label: Active focus state untouched
      rule: The safe focus must not modify ssot.focus.current.yml, ssot.focus.yml active section, or the active focus job_lifecycle.
      weight: required
    - id: session_lock
      label: Lock available
      rule: The focus must not already be owned by another session (owner or session fields empty or match the current session).
      weight: required
    - id: tony_dell_dispatch
      label: Dispatchable to tony-dell
      rule: |
        subagent must be present, subagent.runnable must be true,
        subagent.requires_approval must be false, and subagent.host must be
        tony_dell (or an explicit local/macbook exception).
      weight: required
  score:
    description: |
      safe_score = number of required criteria met (0-7). A focus is safe_to_parallel only if all required criteria are met.
    safe_threshold: 7

  parallel_rules:
    - A safe focus may be activated in Ready (Safe) without parking the active branch focus.
    - Only one safe focus may be active per session to avoid write races.
    - Safe foci must still be committed and validated before claiming completion.

dispatch_host_check:
  description: |
    Before any focus is added to Ready (Safe) or dispatched, the dispatcher
    must verify that subagent.host is either tony_dell or an approved
    exception. Any other value causes the focus to be treated as unsafe and
    requires decomposition.
  default_host: tony_dell
  allowed:
    - tony_dell
    - local
    - macbook
  fallback_action: Decompose the focus into smaller items with subagent.host tony_dell.

dynamic_decomposition:
  description: |
    When a focus is too large, unsafe, or not dispatchable to tony-dell, the
    focus system must break it into smaller, concrete, tony-dell-runnable
    sub-foci instead of activating it as a single large focus.
  trigger:
    any_of:
      - triage.complication > 4
      - missing_info is not empty
      - subagent is missing
      - subagent.runnable is not true
      - subagent.requires_approval is true
      - subagent.host is not in the allowed dispatch host list
      - any subtask lacks subagent.host tony_dell (or an explicit exception)
  action:
    - Do not activate the focus as a single active/branch focus.
    - Generate one or more focus-inbox/*.yml drafts, each with complication <= 4,
      subagent.runnable true, subagent.requires_approval false, and
      subagent.host tony_dell.
    - Add those drafts to the Ready (Safe) queue or leave them in the inbox for review.
  exceptions:
    - A user may override with an explicit local/macbook subagent block and
      requires_approval true, but that focus stays in the main active lane
      (not Ready (Safe)) and cannot be auto-dispatched.

mapping_to_health:
  urgency:
    from: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.health.yml alerts.severity
    critical: 9-10
    error: 6-8
    degraded: 3-5
  importance:
    from: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.health.yml service_criticality
    critical: 9-10
    important: 5-8
    optional: 1-3
  complication:
    from: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.health.yml dependencies and groups
    many dependencies or multiple groups: 8-10
    some dependencies or one group: 4-7
    no known dependencies: 1-3

usage:
  - Each Backlog - Triage Queue item in docs/ssot/ssot.focus.yml may include a triage block.
  - focus-dispatcher.py computes triage_score for each pending item and sorts by it.
  - For mcp_focus and subagent_focus_triage, the triage block can be returned as extra context.
validation:
  - triage is optional for backlog items; missing triage falls back to priority-based sorting.
  - When present, all three scores must be integers from 1 to 10.
  - subagent is required for any focus that is safe_to_parallel or intended for auto-dispatch.
  - When subagent is present, subagent.host is required and defaults to tony_dell.
  - subagent.runnable must be true and subagent.requires_approval false for tony-dell auto-dispatch.
  - safe_to_parallel is optional; when present, it must be a boolean or an object with criteria; if absent, it defaults to false.

```

# Gemini Embedding GPU Offload

Side-by-side experiment to use Google Gemini for text embeddings and free tony-omen GPU

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.gemini-embedding.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Gemini Embedding GPU Offload
subtitle: Side-by-side experiment to use Google Gemini for text embeddings and free tony-omen GPU
icon: "\u26a1"
config:
  version: 1
  created: "2026-08-17"
  updated: "2026-08-19"
  maintainer: tony
  status: validated
  branch: chaba

sections:
  - title: Goal
    icon: "\ud83c\udfaf"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Free tony-omen GPU
        text: Move embedding generation from local Ollama and the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 service to Google Gemini text-embedding-004 so GPU VRAM can be used for other workloads.
      - label: Side-by-side validation
        text: Keep current local embeddings running until a new Gemini-backed collection has been indexed and search quality is verified.

  - title: Current State
    icon: "\ud83d\udcca"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Ollama nomic-embed-text
        text: MDDB uses Ollama on tony-omen at port 11434 with nomic-embed-text (768 dims) for MDDB semantic search. GPU usage is ~388 MB and the container is currently running.
      - label: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 service
        text: Weaviate/Yomi originally used the local port-5000 all-MiniLM-L6-v2 service (384 dims). This service is not currently responding and likely needs to be repaired or retired.
      - label: Existing Gemini helper
        text: scripts/yomi/yomi-api.mjs now defaults getGeminiEmbedding to gemini-embedding-001 (was text-embedding-004), so the direct API call pattern is already proven.

  - title: Proposed Approach
    icon: "\u2699\ufe0f"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Gemini-Ollama proxy for MDDB
        text: Build a small adapter that exposes Ollama-compatible /api/embed endpoints and calls the Gemini API. MDDB can then switch by changing MDDB_EMBEDDING_API_URL without code changes.
      - label: New test collections
        text: Create new 768-dim test collections in both MDDB and Weaviate, re-index a representative subset, and compare search relevance and latency against the Ollama baseline.
      - label: Re-index before switching
        text: Do not mix embeddings from different models in the same collection. After validation, delete or archive the old collection and make the Gemini collection the default.

  - title: Gemini Model
    icon: "\ud83e\udde0"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: gemini-embedding-001
        text: Default output is 768 dimensions. outputDimensionality can be set to 1-768 for truncation to match other vector schemas.
      - label: gemini-embedding-002
        text: Same 768-dim default, same free-tier limits as gemini-embedding-001, but currently lower project usage. Available as an alternate when Gemini Embedding 1 is under pressure.
      - label: Free-tier limits
        text: Observed project quota from AI Studio on 2026-08-18 is 100 RPM, 30,000 TPM, and 1,000 RPD for both gemini-embedding-001 and gemini-embedding-002. This is far below the public 1,500 RPM figure and is the effective operational ceiling.
      - label: API endpoint
        text: POST https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-embedding-001:batchEmbedContents with a GEMINI_API_KEY to batch many inputs in a single request.

  - title: Known Risks
    icon: "\u26a0\ufe0f"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Dimension mismatch
        text: Yomi may already have a 384 vs 768 dimension mismatch between index-yomi-weaviate.mjs and yomi-api.mjs. This must be resolved before any switch.
      - label: Quota surprises
        text: Some free-tier accounts have reported embed_content quota set to 0. Confirm the quota before investing in a full re-index.
      - label: Higher latency
        text: Network round-trips to Gemini are much slower than the local 32ms GPU embedding. This is fine for batch indexing but may affect query responsiveness.

  - title: Results
    icon: "\ud83d\udcca"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Credentials
        text: Valid API key found in /etc/systemd/system/yomi-process.service.d/override.conf. The yomi-api.service key returned 401 and should be rotated.
      - label: Model availability
        text: text-embedding-004 is not available in this project. The Google API model names are gemini-embedding-001 and gemini-embedding-2 (not gemini-embedding-002). The proxy maps nomic-embed-text requests to gemini-embedding-2 by default and text-embedding-004 to gemini-embedding-001.
      - label: Proxy
        text: scripts/mddb/gemini-ollama-proxy.mjs migrated to a rootless Podman Quadlet on tony-dell port 11435 (healthy). It uses batchEmbedContents with a 100 RPM token-bucket limiter, 429 exponential backoff, and now automatically falls back from gemini-embedding-2 to gemini-embedding-001 on 429 rate-limit. GEMINI_API_KEY is injected from the podman secret gemini-api-key.
      - label: Comparison
        text: Side-by-side test collections in MDDB/Weaviate were not created because neither service is running on tony-omen. An embedding-API comparison was run instead; see reports/gemini-embedding-comparison.md.
      - label: Latency
        text: Gemini round-trip via the proxy is ~472 ms per embedding for gemini-embedding-001 and ~720 ms for gemini-embedding-2, versus ~127 ms for Ollama on the same host. batchEmbedContents reduces the effective request-per-text overhead, so bulk re-indexing is more efficient.
      - label: Switch decision
        text: Cut over MDDB_EMBEDDING_API_URL to http://100.68.142.13:11435 on tony-dell. The proxy is now the live embedding provider for MDDB. Ollama remains available as a fallback if needed.

  - title: Next Steps
    icon: "\ud83d\ude80"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Validate at scale
        text: Re-run the comparison with full MDDB and Weaviate test collections once those services are back on tony-omen or a test host.
      - label: Rotate yomi-api key
        text: The GEMINI_API_KEY in /home/tony/.config/systemd/user/yomi-api.service returned 401; replace it with the working key from yomi-process.service.d/override.conf or a new Google AI Studio key.
      - label: Rate-limit verification
        text: Confirm that the new proxy token-bucket and batchEmbedContents keep 429s under control during the next batch re-index.
      - label: Revisit switch
        text: Switch MDDB to the Gemini proxy only if batch latency and the 1,000 RPD per model cap (2,000 RPD combined if both gemini-embedding-2 and gemini-embedding-001 are used with fallback) are acceptable for the target workload.

```

# GPU Workload Policy

Rules and reservations for GPU workloads across hosts

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.gpu.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: GPU Workload Policy
subtitle: Rules and reservations for GPU workloads across hosts
icon: gpu

policy:
  rule: Only one GPU workload at a time
  reason: Combined usage (~3.7GB) exceeds available VRAM when multiple workloads run simultaneously

  workload_vram:
    llama: ~0.4GB
    imagen2: ~0.6GB
    txt2vid: ~2.7GB

  automated_queue:
    - When receive a new workload, check if there is already a GPU workload running
    - If there is, queue the new workload
    - If there is not, run the new workload
    - Llama switches to GPU when available, preserves context
    - When image generation starts, hold llama on CPU (mcp2_hold_llama)
    - After image generation completes, resume llama on GPU (mcp2_resume_llama)

  caveats:
    llama_switch:
      - mcp2_hold_llama waits up to 60s for /health to become reachable
      - mcp2_resume_llama waits up to 120s for /health to become reachable
      - CPU-only llama is significantly slower (10-100x latency increase)
      - Chat requests during CPU mode will be slow
      - Context preserved during switch (same container)

  chosen_approach:
    model_state: single_container_router
    reason: Single llama.cpp router serves multiple models with ~70MB overhead
    tools: mcp2_hold_llama, mcp2_resume_llama (for CPU fallback during GPU contention)
    models:
      - Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct-q4.gguf (2.3GB, MCP/chatllama, active)
      - thai-legal-gemma-4b-cpt.Q4_K_M.gguf (5GB, offline - GPU memory constraints)
    implemented: 2026-07-31, thai-legal offline (2026-08-06)

  implementation:
    queue_manager:
      status: not_implemented
      choice: Create new gpu-queue service
      persistence: Postgres (existing postgres container)
      queue_strategy: Let LLM job finish first, don't interrupt mid-job
      priority: txt2vid > imagen2 > llama (sorted, non-preemptive)
      monitoring: Queue status UI + log events to journald

    api_contract:
      submit_job: POST /api/gpu-queue/jobs {type, params}
      list_jobs: GET /api/gpu-queue/jobs
      job_status: GET /api/gpu-queue/jobs/{id}
      cancel_job: DELETE /api/gpu-queue/jobs/{id}
      queue_status: GET /api/gpu-queue/status

    database:
      table: gpu_queue_jobs
      columns: id, type, params, status, priority, created_at, started_at, completed_at, error

    testing_strategy:
      unit_tests:
        - Mock mcp-gpu/mcp-llama tools
        - Test queue logic without real GPU
        - Test Postgres operations with test DB
      integration_tests:
        - Test with real llama-server (CPU-only mode)
        - Test hold/resume workflow
        - Test priority ordering
      e2e_tests:
        - Submit imagen2 job, verify llama hold/resume
        - Submit concurrent jobs, verify queue behavior
        - Test job cancellation

    current_status:
      phase: operational
      completed:
        - Created gpu-queue service directory structure (scripts/gpu-queue/)
        - Created Postgres schema (gpu_queue_jobs table with indexes)
        - Implemented db.mjs (Postgres operations: createJob, getJob, listJobs, getNextPendingJob, updateJobStatus, getQueueStatus, getRunningJob, cancelJob, cleanupOldJobs)
        - Implemented queue.mjs (queue logic: processJob, startQueueProcessor, submitJob, cancelJob)
        - Implemented index.mjs (HTTP API: POST/GET/DELETE /api/gpu-queue/jobs, GET /api/gpu-queue/status, GET /health)
        - Created package.json with pg dependency
        - Added gpu-queue service to docker-compose.yml (node:20-alpine, depends on postgres)
        - Created systemd service file (~/.config/systemd/user/gpu-queue.service)
        - Added Caddy routing for /api/gpu-queue/* to host.docker.internal:3001
        - Installed dependencies (npm install)
        - Started gpu-queue service (systemctl --user start gpu-queue)
        - Tested API endpoints (health, status, submit job, list jobs)
        - Created orchestrator.mjs for external MCP tool integration
        - Updated orchestrator.mjs with imagen2, llama, and txt2vid job processing
        - Tested full workflow with MCP hold/resume (mcp1_hold_llama, orchestrator process, mcp1_resume_llama)
        - Exposed imagen2-inference on port 8000 for orchestrator access
        - Created process-job.mjs automated workflow script with interactive MCP hold/resume prompts
        - Created queue status UI at /apps/gpu-queue/ with auto-refresh
        - Added Caddy routing for /apps/gpu-queue/* and /api/gpu-queue/*
        - Enhanced queue status UI with job submission form and cancellation controls
        - Wrote unit tests for db.mjs (7 tests passing)
        - Added embedding job support with GPU queue integration
        - Enhanced error handling with retry logic and exponential backoff
        - Implemented comprehensive monitoring system (health checks, performance metrics, error tracking)
        - Added monitoring API endpoints (/api/gpu-queue/monitoring/*)
        - Created automatic queue processor (auto-processor.mjs) with error handling
        - Set up systemd services for auto-processor and daily Weaviate indexing
        - Implemented performance benchmarking system (benchmark.mjs)
        - Enhanced database schema with job statistics and cancellation rate tracking
      next_steps:

    deployment:
      directory: scripts/gpu-queue/
      files:
        - index.mjs: Main queue service with monitoring endpoints
        - queue.mjs: Queue logic with timeout and retry handling
        - db.mjs: Postgres operations with statistics functions
        - orchestrator.mjs: Job processing functions (imagen2, llama, txt2vid, embedding)
        - monitoring.mjs: Health checks and performance metrics
        - benchmark.mjs: Performance benchmarking system
        - auto-processor.mjs: Automatic queue processor
        - package.json: Dependencies
      docker_compose:
        service: gpu-queue
        image: node:20-alpine
        working_dir: /app/gpu-queue
        volumes:
          - ./scripts/gpu-queue:/app/gpu-queue
        environment:
          - DATABASE_URL=postgres://chaba:chabapass@postgres:5432/chaba
          - GPU_QUEUE_PORT=3001
        ports:
          - "3001:3001"
        networks:
          - default
        restart: unless-stopped
      systemd:
        gpu-queue:
          file: ~/.config/systemd/user/gpu-queue.service
          exec_start: /usr/bin/node /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/scripts/gpu-queue/index.mjs
          working_dir: /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell
          restart: on-failure
          environment:
            - GPU_QUEUE_PORT=3001
        gpu-queue-processor:
          file: ~/.config/systemd/user/gpu-queue-processor.service
          exec_start: /usr/bin/node /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/scripts/gpu-queue/auto-processor.mjs
          working_dir: /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell
          restart: on-failure
          environment:
            - NODE_ENV=production
        weaviate-index:
          file: ~/.config/systemd/user/weaviate-index.service
          exec_start: /usr/bin/node /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/scripts/weaviate/auto-index.mjs
          working_dir: /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell
          environment:
            - NODE_ENV=production
        weaviate-index-timer:
          file: ~/.config/systemd/user/weaviate-index.timer
          description: Run Weaviate indexing daily at 2 AM
          onCalendar: "*-*-* 02:00:00"
      caddy_routing:
        - reverse_proxy /api/gpu-queue/* host.docker.internal:3001

hardware:
  gpu: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650
  vram_total_mb: 4096
  host: tony-omen (tony-omen.local)

tools:
  mcp-gpu:
    - mcp1_gpu_status: Check VRAM and compute process summary
    - mcp1_hold_llama: Move llama-server to CPU (n_gpu_layers=0)
    - mcp1_resume_llama: Restore llama-server to original n_gpu_layers
```

```yaml
title: chaba.h3 Page Deployment Flow
subtitle: How to deploy web pages from tony-omen to chaba.h3.gizmo-thailand.com
icon: web
version: 1
last_updated: "2026-08-20"
maintainer: tony

overview:
  source_worktree: /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-h3
  branch: chaba.h3
  target_host: chaba.h3.gizmo-thailand.com
  purpose: Publish static pages and assets for the managed h3 web host

prerequisites:
  - The chaba.h3 branch is checked out at /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-h3
  - The managed host serves files from the chaba.h3 branch public/ directory

steps:
  - id: 1
    action: Work in the h3 worktree
    command: cd /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-h3
  - id: 2
    action: Add or edit pages
    path: chaba-h3/public/
    notes:
      - Place files under chaba-h3/public/
      - The web/public/ path from the master branch is not served
  - id: 3
    action: Test locally
    command: node proxy-server.mjs
    note: Local mimic of the managed host; use it to preview before pushing
  - id: 4
    action: Commit on the chaba.h3 branch
    commands:
      - git add public/...
      - git commit -m "..."
  - id: 5
    action: Push to the remote
    command: git push origin chaba.h3
    note: The managed host picks up the branch and serves public/

  - Use absolute fetch paths such as /data.json inside pages

gotcha:
```
