# Chaba Health Check Configuration

Common health check configuration — profiles, alerts, groups, and recovery actions. Home profile services are split by category into ssot.health.home.<category>.yml; mobile profile services remain in ssot.health.mobile.yml. The `host:` field is supported for `http`, `systemd`, `container`, and `mount` checks; non-local `systemd` units (e.g. `tony_omen`) are verified via `ssh -o BatchMode=yes <host>`, with underscores in the `host` value mapped to dash hostnames.

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.health.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Chaba Health Check Configuration
description: Common health check configuration — profiles, alerts, groups, and recovery actions. Home profile services are split by category into ssot.health.home.<category>.yml; mobile profile services remain in ssot.health.mobile.yml. The `host:` field is supported for `http`, `systemd`, `container`, and `mount` checks; non-local `systemd` units (e.g. `tony_omen`) are verified via `ssh -o BatchMode=yes <host>`, with underscores in the `host` value mapped to dash hostnames.
version: 9
profiles:
  default: auto-detect
  home:
    hostname: tony-dell
    base_url: https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net
    ssids:
      - TONY-WIFI
      - TONY-WIFI_5G
    description: Home network, mcp-health reaches tony-dell as the stable headless-primary host.
    note:
      Do not use .local/mDNS for health checks. Use tailnet hostnames (tony-dell, tony-omen) and Tailscale IPs. .local is unreliable
      when mDNS is slow or when the host is on a different interface/path.
  mobile:
    hostname: tony-dell
    base_url: https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net
    ssids:
      - TONY-IP
    description: Mobile/external network via Tailscale
    note:
      Connect to Tailscale first; use the tailnet hostname `tony-dell` (100.68.142.13) instead of a dynamic IP, DDNS, or .local/mDNS
      hostname. .local is intentionally not used by mcp-health.
alerts:
  enabled: true
  channels:
    - type: log
      enabled: true
      severity:
        - critical
        - error
        - degraded
      description: Log alerts to system journal
    - type: webhook
      enabled: false
      url: ""
      severity:
        - critical
      description: Webhook for external monitoring systems
  thresholds:
    critical_services_down: 3
    sustained_failure_minutes: 5
    recovery_notification: true
    response_time_threshold_ms: 5000
  service_criticality:
    critical:
      - caddy
```

# Home Assistant Branch Model

Git branch and worktree design for the Home Assistant family

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.home-assistant.branches.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Home Assistant Branch Model
subtitle: Git branch and worktree design for the Home Assistant family

branches:
  family:
    id: ha
    repo: chaba
    base: master
    purpose: Shared Home Assistant platform, SSOT, and bridges
    contents:
      - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.home-assistant.yml
      - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.home-assistant.live.yml
      - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.home-assistant.branches.yml
      - scripts/home-assistant/
      - stacks/ha-live/
      - systemd/ha-*.service
      - stacks/tony-dell/home-assistant/
    description: The family branch holds everything that is common to all HA instances.

  instances:
    - id: tony-ha
      repo: chaba
      base: ha
      purpose: tony-dell runtime customizations
      contents:
        - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.home-assistant.tony.yml
        - tony-dell/home-assistant/
        - scripts/home-assistant/ha-live/
      description: Adds tony-dell specific devices, go2rtc, camera scripts, and the HA-MCP integration.

    - id: michael-ha
      repo: chaba-michael
      base: ha
      upstream_remote: chaba
      upstream_branch: ha
      purpose: Michael cloud instance customizations
      contents:
        - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.home-assistant.michael.yml
        - docs/home-assistant/
        - stacks/web/public/apps/michael-live/
      description: Michael-specific dashboard packages and live UI pages, rebased onto chaba/ha for shared updates.

  live_features:
    - id: tony-live
      base: tony-ha
      purpose: Live bridge or UI for the tony-dell instance
      url: "https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net/apps/tony-live/"

    - id: michael-live
      base: michael-ha
      purpose: Michael live dashboard page
      url: "https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net/apps/michael-live/"

worktree_setup:
  chaba:
    - "mkdir -p /home/tony/.local/share/worktrees/chaba"
    - "git -C /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell worktree add /home/tony/.local/share/worktrees/chaba/ha ha"
    - "git -C /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell worktree add /home/tony/.local/share/worktrees/chaba/tony-ha tony-ha"
  chaba-michael:
    - "mkdir -p /home/tony/.local/share/worktrees/chaba-michael"
    - "git -C /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-michael worktree add /home/tony/.local/share/worktrees/chaba-michael/michael-ha michael-ha"
    - "git -C /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-michael worktree add /home/tony/.local/share/worktrees/chaba-michael/michael-live michael-live"

sync_rules:
  tony-ha:
    - "git -C /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell fetch origin"
    - "git -C /home/tony/.local/share/worktrees/chaba/tony-ha rebase origin/ha"
    - "git -C /home/tony/.local/share/worktrees/chaba/tony-ha push origin tony-ha"
  michael-ha:
    - "git -C /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-michael fetch chaba ha"
    - "git -C /home/tony/.local/share/worktrees/chaba-michael/michael-ha rebase chaba/ha"
    - "git -C /home/tony/.local/share/worktrees/chaba-michael/michael-ha push origin michael-ha"
  michael-live:
    - "git -C /home/tony/.local/share/worktrees/chaba-michael/michael-live rebase michael-ha"
    - "git -C /home/tony/.local/share/worktrees/chaba-michael/michael-live push origin michael-live"

recent_changes:
  - date: 2026-09-01
    description: "Create ha, tony-ha, michael-ha, and michael-live branches"
    impact: "Central family branch with per-instance sub-dev branches"

```

# Home Assistant Card Design Conventions

SVG layout, text rendering, and alignment rules for the forked sunsynk-power-flow-card

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.home-assistant.design.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Home Assistant Card Design Conventions
subtitle: SVG layout, text rendering, and alignment rules for the forked sunsynk-power-flow-card

cards:
  sunsynk-power-flow-card:
    repo: ssot.home-assistant.cards.yml::repositories.sunsynk-power-flow-card-fork
    modes:
      - lite
      - compact
      - wide
      - full
      - ss4
      - pfg
      - pfg2
    active_mode: pfg

helpers:
  renderText:
    purpose: Create a direct SVG <text> node
    args: id, x, y, displayCondition, class, fill, text
  createTextWithPopup:
    purpose: Create an SVG <a> wrapping a <text> node for popups
    args: id, x, y, displayCondition, class, fill, text, popupCallback, hideOnCondition

svg_text_rendering:
  note: |
    Visibility is controlled both by the <svg> parent display style and the helper's display attribute.
    With hideOnCondition=true, display is "none" when the condition is true and empty when false.
    Duplicate IDs such as battery_soc_184 and duration_text are intentional across branches and do not alone indicate an overlay.

battery_status_line:
  format: "{target}% | {current}%"
  anchor:
    x: 290
    y: 358
    align: left-align
    class: st13 st8
  text_source:
    plain:
      id: Battery*_SOC
      text: "{current}%"
    shutdown:
      id: Battery*_SOC_Shutdown
      text: "{shutdown_soc}% | {current}%"
    program_capacity:
      id: Battery*_SOC_Program_Capacity
      text: "{capacity}% | {current}%"
  exclusion_logic: |
    The plain Battery*__SOC <svg> is hidden when either the shutdown or program capacity branch
    is visible. This prevents the underlying {current}% from drawing over the digit in the combined
    status text. The display ternary includes:
      data.inverterProg.show || (config.battery*?.shutdown_soc && !config.battery*?.shutdown_soc_offgrid)

battery_state_message:
  anchor:
    x: 169
    y: 311
  examples:
    - "2 hrs, 51 min TO FULL @16:37"
    - "5 hrs, 34 min TO EMPTY @22:20"

battery_runtime_line:
  anchor:
    x: 290
    y: 393.7
    class: st3 left-align
  branches:
    discharge:
      id: duration_text
      example: "RUNTIME TO 20% @22:20"
    charge:
      id: duration_text_charging
      example: "TO 20% CHARGE @22:20"
  note: |
    Both text nodes can be present at the same coordinates. The inactive branch is rendered with
    fill: transparent, so only the active direction text is visually visible. For robust hiding,
    prefer display: none on the inactive parent <svg> group.

battery_direction:
  source_entity: entities.battery_current_direction
  default: sensor.inverters_1_battery_direction
  logic: |
    The card normalizes battery power to a signed value where + means discharging
    and - means charging. This is done in src/index.ts:
      1. Read the main battery direction entity (e.g. sensor.inverters_1_battery_direction).
      2. Convert its state to +1 for discharging, -1 for charging, or null for unknown.
      3. Apply battery.invert_power to the raw power value.
      4. Multiply by the resolved direction: batteryPower = Math.abs(batteryPower) * direction.
    The same resolved direction is used for runtime text, capacity target, colour, and connector animation.
    Pack directions are only overridden when their battery*_current_direction entity is configured; otherwise the raw sign/invert_power is used.

signed_current_in_overall_box:
  note: |
    The aggregate battery box now renders voltage and current on the first line,
    e.g. "53.0 V -34.2 A". The current is always shown with its sign from the
    entities.battery_current_191 entity, regardless of the main battery.show_absolute setting.
    `show_absolute` still controls the power display (absolute kW) and pack power/current display,
    but the overall current intentionally keeps the sign so charge/discharge can be read directly.

pfg_card:
  cardstyle: pfg
  repo_source: src/cards/pfg-card.ts
  test_url:
    - https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net:8124/tony-test/pfg
    - https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net:8124/tony-test/pfg1
  config:
    card_height: 520px
    view_layout: { grid-area: pfg }
    wide: true
  note: |
    The PFG card is a new test layout, not the full card. It uses the same entity
    mapping as PF3/PF4 and the same four-battery aggregate/pack model. It is useful
    for verifying a larger canvas and the pfg render branch without disturbing the
    stable PF3/PF4 lite views. Two pfg test views exist: pfg (original) and pfg1
    (new grid layout with labels).

pfg2_card:
  cardstyle: pfg2
  repo_source: src/cards/pfg2-card.ts
  test_url:
    - https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net:8124/tony-test/pfg2
  config:
    card_height: 520px
    view_layout: { grid-area: pfg }
    wide: true
  note: |
    The PFG2 card is a copy of the PFG grid card with a 15x15 grid by default
    (pfg_grid_size still overrides). It shares the same pfg_* config keys and
    entity/status tile mapping as pfg. First deployed to michael-dev in bundle v33;
    corner anchors and span-aware lines landed in v51, per-line speed scaling in v56,
    pfg_hide_grid in v79.
    As of v71 pfg2-card.ts is removed: cardstyle pfg2 renders via pfgCard with a
    15x15 default grid — one renderer, no drift.

pfg_feature_keys:
  applies_to: [pfg, pfg2]
  grid:
    pfg_grid_size: "N (default 10 for pfg, 15 for pfg2); 1-indexed r,c tile keys"
    pfg_grid_cols: "N (v92+); override cols for non-square grids"
    pfg_grid_rows: "N (v92+); override rows for non-square grids; anchors use cols for x, rows for y"
    pfg_grid_width: 'CSS width of the grid, e.g. "25%" or "360px"'
    pfg_radius: "map r,c -> CSS border-radius for that tile"
    pfg_border: 'map r,c -> CSS border override for that tile (v78+), e.g. "4px solid #ffffff"'
    pfg_hide_grid: "boolean (v79+); hides tile borders, the r,c fallback text, and all pfg_lines connectors. Explicit pfg_labels still render (v87+). Images/icons/values/status colors still render."
    pfg_transparent: "boolean (v93+); removes ha-card background/border/shadow and the theme card-mod frosted-glass ::before/::after layer (v94+)"
    pfg_inverter_at: '"r,c" (v77+); places the built-in inverter image tile at that cell'
    pfg_debug_layers: "boolean (v162+); outlines each render layer and tags it — cell=red, img=green, chart:<position>=cyan, label=yellow. For inspecting layer stacking."
    pfg_tile_style: 'map "r,c" -> {bg, border, radius, image, image_fit} (v162+); consolidated per-tile style that overrides pfg_images/pfg_border/pfg_radius/pfg_image_fit and the implicit cell tint'
  tiles:
    note: "Render priority per tile: label > icon > image > sum/value > r,c coordinate text."
    pfg_labels: 'map "r,c" -> text label; " " blanks a cell; rendered even under pfg_hide_grid'
    pfg_label_pos: 'map "r,c" -> CSS top for the label overlay (default 55% - 26px)'
    pfg_icons: 'map "r,c" -> mdi icon name (e.g. mdi:solar-power)'
    pfg_images: 'map "r,c" -> image URL served from /local/'
    pfg_image_zoom: "number; object-fit:cover plus transform:scale(zoom), applied to all image tiles"
    pfg_image_fit: 'map "r,c" -> contain|cover|fill per tile (default cover; inverter tiles default contain)'
    pfg_values: 'map "r,c" -> {entity, scale?, decimals?, unit?} live sensor value tile'
    pfg_value_labels: 'map "r,c" -> small caption rendered above the tile value (v88+)'
    pfg_value_label_pos: 'map "r,c" -> CSS top for the value label (default calc(55% - 14px))'
    pfg_sums: 'map "r,c" -> {entities[], scale?, decimals?, unit?} summed entity tile'
    pfg_spans: 'map "r,c" -> N (square), "RxC" (rectangular, e.g. "2x3"), or responsive {square,portrait,landscape} resolved from viewport aspect (v96+); covered cells are skipped; anchors are span-aware. PITFALL: responsive spans must keep the same cell coverage per orientation or tiles get swallowed — a 3x3 span at 1,1 covers 3,1 and hides that tile entirely (learned 2026-09-07).'
    pfg_fit_screen: 'boolean|"Npx" (v97/v98+); grid fills 100% width x (100vh - reserve) with free cell stretch — no aspect lock, no scrollbar. Lines stretch via preserveAspectRatio="none".'
  charts:
    key: pfg_charts
    note: 'r,c -> chart def or array of defs; types: gauge, bar, history, cycle, surface3d (v141+). position: center|bottom|top|fill|cycle overlays the tile (works over images). "bg" is a deprecated alias of "fill" (v162+). cycle rotates through step groups at interval seconds; entities[] sums multiple sensors in one def. history uses recorder history_during_period with 5min cache; fields: entity/entities, hours, min/max, scale, decimals, unit, label, stroke, fill, needle, segments, gradient, interval, steps.'
    surface3d: |
      echarts-gl surface, lazy-loaded from /local/echarts-5.5.1.min.js +
      /local/echarts-gl-2.1.0.min.js (vendored to www/ on both hosts, v171 dev /
      v161 ha; jsDelivr CDN fallback if /local missing). Hourly means from
      recorder/statistics_during_period, period=hour, fallback raw history;
      5min localStorage cache.
      Keys: entity, days (default 30, max 90), cache, scale, min/max, unit,
      wireframe, auto_rotate, opacity, bg, alpha/beta (camera, default 18/215),
      rotate_center ('volume'|'front'|[x,y,z]), rotate_mouse_button,
      pan_mouse_button, rotate_sensitivity, zoom_sensitivity,
      hover_plane (bool|opacity, default 0.25), hover_plane_color.
      Hover plane tracks kW via series mousemove -> axisPointer x/y lookup ->
      z-axis pixel projection on walls; click toggles pin (drag-safe 6px
      threshold). NOTE: 'front' preset = axis-max end of depth, affected by
      inverse+camera — prefer 'volume'. Requires WebGL (GPU acceleration).
  layer_order: |
    Tile render stack, bottom -> top (v162+):
      1. ha-card background — transparent when pfg_transparent: true
      2. .container.card div — always transparent
      3. .pfg-cell background + border — implicit rgba(255,255,255,0.05) tint and 1px
         grid border are SKIPPED when the tile has an image or a fill/bg chart
         (v162+); pfg_tile_style.bg/.border overrides everything
      4. chart overlay wrapper — placement via chartOverlayStyle(position): center |
         bottom | top | fill(=bg) | cycle; carries opacity and optional scrim
      5. chart content — svg charts render here; surface3d mounts a div with its own
         bg (def.bg, default rgba(10,14,18,0.45)) + WebGL canvas (transparent)
      6. label/value overlays — z-index:2, pfg_label_pos / pfg_value_label_pos
      7. flow-lines SVG — pfg_lines, inset:0, pointer-events:none
      8. ha-card ::before/::after — disabled under pfg_transparent (card-mod frosted
         glass would otherwise sit on top)
    Inspect with pfg_debug_layers: true.
  view_copy:
    note: 'scripts/home-assistant/apply-tpl.py copies TPL-tab card templates (title -> r,c) onto any view: apply-tpl.py <ha_url> <dashboard> <src_view> <dst_view> --map "Title:r,c;..."'
  values:
    key: pfg_values
    note: "r,c -> entity id string or {entity, scale, decimals, unit, label}"
  preset:
    key: preset
    note: '"pfg" merges standard entity/section defaults (src/cards/pfg-presets.ts) before validation; per-section card config keys override the preset.'
  lines:
    key: pfg_lines
    fields:
      from: "anchor, required"
      to: "anchor, required"
      via: "anchor, optional intermediate point"
      elbow: '"h" horizontal-first or "v" vertical-first route between from and to'
      entity: "numeric sensor driving direction, color, live state, and speed"
      color: "hex override; default is the entity status color, else #FF9100"
      speed: "seconds per dash cycle at max_power (default 0.8)"
      max_power: "watts counted as full speed (default 1000)"
      invert: "boolean; flips the entity sign before direction/speed math (e.g. battery power negative-on-discharge)"
    anchor_syntax: |
      "r,c" = tile centre. Edge/corner suffix after @:
      top | bottom | left | right | topleft | topright | bottomleft | bottomright.
      Anchors are span-aware: an edge/corner of an N x N tile uses the outer boundary.
      Endpoints are raw anchor coordinates (no inset); an earlier cellEdge() inset was
      removed in v50 because it shifted endpoints into neighbouring cells.
    behavior: |
      Lines are an SVG polyline with a stroke-dashoffset animation (pfg-flow keyframes).
      entity state sign picks animation-direction (>=0 flows from->to, <0 reversed).
      Duration = speed / clamp(|value|/max_power, min 0.15, max 1) so higher power runs
      faster. Zero/unavailable pauses the animation and dims the line to 60%.
      Lines use vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke" with stroke-width 2px.
  pfg2_canonical_tilemap:
    note: "Source of truth for TPL->PFG2 tile placement; pass to apply-tpl.py --map or promote-view.sh --map"
    map: "Grid:1,7;Sum:3,1;Inverter:3,4;Battery:5,1;Home:5,7;Living:7,4;Kitchen:7,7;Laundry:9,4;Pool:9,7"
    pv_override: "PV1 1,1 and PV2 1,4 use TPL card PV.b1 (bars); PV2 entities retargeted to *_2"
  tile_workflow_decision_tree: |
    Design/iterate a tile:
      1. Build/edit the single-tile card in the TPL tab (push-dashboard.py mutate, no restart).
      2. Propagate to a target view tile:
         scripts/home-assistant/apply-tpl.py <ha_url> tony-test tpl <view> --map "Title:r,c;..."
         (copies charts/images/labels/etc.; never pfg_spans; same title may map to several cells)
      3. Retarget entity ids on the destination tile if the source is different
         (e.g. PV.b1 hard-wires pv_power_1; swap _1->_2 for a second string).
    Promote dev -> michael-ha:
      4. scripts/home-assistant/copy-view.py dev->ha (re-adds card_mod automatically).
      5. Bundle parity: compare md5 of dist vs each host's /local bundle; deploy-card.sh --host all if source changed.
    New card FEATURE (not config):
      6. Edit card source -> npm run build -> deploy-card.sh --host all -> apply on both.
    Pitfalls:
      - View copies do NOT carry the JS bundle or /local images — check both exist on target.
      - Chart types must exist in the deployed bundle version (a config referencing e.g. 'bars'
        silently renders nothing on an older bundle).
      - Responsive pfg_spans must keep identical cell coverage per orientation or tiles overlap/hide.
      - Tailscale SSH may need periodic browser re-auth (prints a login.tailscale.com link).
  deployment_note: |
    pfg_* config lives entirely in the Lovelace card config. Once the bundle supports a
    key, iterate it live with scripts/home-assistant/push-dashboard.py (websocket save,
    no restart). Only new card code requires a bundle rebuild + version bump + restart.
    Deploy: scripts/home-assistant/deploy-card.sh [--host michael-dev|michael-ha|all]
    (flock-locked, version derived from remote lovelace_resources).

multi_battery_layout:
  note: |
    Compact/lite cards can render up to four batteries. The PF3/PF4 layout (batteryCount === 4):
    - The main battery (aggregate) icon is hidden; its status is shown in the top box.
    - battery2 is top-left, battery3 is top-right, battery4 is bottom-left.
    - battery2 maps to pack 1 (calculated from total minus packs 2 and 3).
    - battery3 maps to pack 2, battery4 maps to pack 3.
    - PFG (cardstyle: pfg, card_height: 520px) uses the same entity mapping on a larger canvas;
      it is not the same as cardstyle: full or ss4.
  battery_total_power_box:
    purpose: Display overall battery status above the centre/battery column.
    location: x=190, y=285, width=100, height=45
    contents: voltage and signed current on the first line, power and SOC on the second line
    fill: rgba(16,32,64,0.85)
    example: "53.0 V -34.2 A / 1.83 kW 77 %"

classes:
  st13:
    usage: Battery combined status text
  st8:
    usage: Font-weight/style modifier
  left-align:
    usage: Left-aligned text anchor
  st3:
    usage: Runtime / duration text
  st14:
    usage: Offgrid / secondary percentage labels

coordinate_system:
  note: |
    SVG coordinates are internal to the card SVG. Screen-space bounding boxes depend on the card
    scale and parent element transforms. Use Playlive or browser dev tools for pixel-level overlay
    verification.

known_patterns:
  - id: duplicate_battery_soc_184
    note: The same id is reused in plain, shutdown, program capacity, and offgrid branches. Use parent <svg> id and display state to distinguish branches.
  - id: parent_svg_display
    note: A <text> node may report a visible display attribute while its parent <svg> is display none.
  - id: transparent_runtime_overlay
    note: The charge/discharge runtime pair uses fill transparency, not display none, for the inactive branch.
  - id: pfg_not_full
    note: |
      PFG (cardstyle: pfg) is a separate render branch in src/cards/pfg-card.ts and is not the
      same as cardstyle: full or ss4. Use /tony-test/pfg to test it and do not confuse it with the
      SS4 or full-card tabs.

  last_verified: "2026-09-16"
  health: active; v79 deployed; pfg/pfg2 feature keys, anchor syntax, speed-scaled flow lines, and pfg_hide_grid documented; signed-current and direction override documented for compact/lite cards; pfg2 deployed to michael-ha after SK with pfg_hide_grid=true
```

```yaml
    repo_dashboards: /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/docs/home-assistant/dashboards
    caddy:
```

```yaml
# SSOT: Home Assistant Voice / Gemini Live Pipeline
title: Home Assistant Voice (Gemini Live)
subtitle: Speech-to-speech voice pipeline, ha-live bridge, and live-model integration knowledge
version: 1
last_updated: 2026-09-08

# ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Current state (tony-ha, container tony-ha, HA 2026.8.3)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
state:
  preferred_pipeline: Gemini            # id 01m20051yb4cb5v1b322zstg8y, language th
  pipelines:
    - name: Gemini
      engine: conversation.gemini_live / stt.gemini_live / tts.gemini_live
      language: th
      note: Preferred. Speech-to-speech via Gemini Live API; no STT->LLM->TTS chain.
    - name: Home Assistant
      engine: conversation.google_ai_conversation + google_ai_stt/tts
      language: en (voice charon)
      note: Fallback 3-stage pipeline.
    - name: Chaba
      engine: conversation.google_ai_conversation + google_ai_stt/tts
      language: th (voice zephyr)
      note: Fallback Thai pipeline.
  integrations:
    gemini_live:
      source: https://github.com/matt123p/ha-gemini-live v1.0.6
      path: /home/tony/.config/home-assistant/custom_components/gemini_live
      provider: gemini
      model: gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview
      voice: Puck
      credentials: reuses the google_generative_ai_conversation config-entry key (no new secret stored)
      requirement_patch: 'manifest relaxed to google-genai>=1.59.0 (container ships 1.59.0; pin ==2.21.0 would break the official google_generative_ai_conversation integration)'
      note: Entities conversation./stt./tts.gemini_live created 2026-09-08; verified via text and Thai turns.
  ha_live_bridge:
    service: ha-live.service (systemd --user, podman exec tony-ha python3 /config/ha-live/bridge.py)
    source_host: /home/tony/.config/home-assistant/ha-live/bridge.py
    source_repo: stacks/ha-live/bridge.py   # keep in sync
    port: 9005 (index /, /snapshot, /snapshot.json, ws /ws)
    note: restart.sh uses stale container name 'home-assistant'; use systemctl --user restart ha-live.service instead.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Improvements applied to ha-live bridge.py (2026-09-08)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
bridge_improvements:
  - streaming_input: >
      Mic PCM chunks now forwarded per-frame via session.send_realtime_input(audio=Blob)
      instead of buffering the whole utterance and using send_client_content.
      Lower latency; lets server-side VAD see speech as it happens.
  - explicit_turn_end: >
      Client 'end' message -> send_realtime_input(text=prompt) +
      send_realtime_input(audio_stream_end=True). audio_stream_end is the
      explicit push-to-talk signal; the model responds without waiting for VAD silence timeout.
  - turn_coverage: >
      realtime_input_config.turn_coverage = TURN_INCLUDES_ONLY_ACTIVITY so each turn
      covers only detected speech (push-to-talk friendly).
  - session_resumption: >
      SessionResumptionConfig(handle=load_session_handle()) — the handle was previously
      saved on session_resumption_update but never used; reconnects now keep context.
      go_away events are logged with time_left.
  - tool_response_fix: >
      send_tool_response(function_responses=[FunctionResponse(...)]) — was a single
      object, not a list (latent bug); also function_calls guarded with `or []`.
  - system_instruction: bilingual EN/TH, 'no markdown/lists, short natural voice replies',
      plus dynamic device-state context (switch/light/media_player/input_boolean from
      /api/states) — replaces the hardcoded two-switch list.
  - tv_commands: >
      Dedicated flat local tools executed by the bridge (not nested MCP calls):
      tv_command(cmd enum nav|scroll|back|stop|camera, arg) and
      photo_slideshow(action enum next|previous|pause|resume). For cmd=camera,
      arg is the HA camera entity name (e.g. 'ip_cam_65', 'xiaomi_c201'),
      defaulting to 'ip_cam_65'. Verified:
      'cast the help' -> tv_command(nav, help) -> cast-browser-server HTTP 200;
      'cast the xiaomi camera' -> tv_command(camera, xiaomi_c201) ->
      camera.play_stream camera.xiaomi_c201 HTTP 200.
  - tool_precision: >
      Precision techniques applied — flat enum-constrained schemas instead of
      nested ha_call_service proxy calls, explicit 'ALWAYS use X tool' +
      few-shot examples in the system instruction, local deterministic execution
      (REST to :8799/cmd and /api/services) instead of MCP round-trips.
  - continuous_pump: >
      Responses are handled by a session-lifetime pump task (pump_responses) instead
      of a per-turn receive loop — VAD-completed turns and barge-in 'interrupted'
      events are handled while mic audio is still streaming.
  - typed_text: client can send {"type":"text","text":...} for a text-only turn.
  - resumption_fallback: >
      A stale resumption handle fails connect with 'session not found'; bridge now
      drops it and reconnects fresh automatically.
  - restart_script: restart.sh now calls systemctl --user restart ha-live.service
      (previously used stale container name 'home-assistant').

# ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Knowledge distilled from matt123p/ha-gemini-live internals
# (applies to ha-live bridge and any future custom Live client)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
live_api_knowledge:
  architecture:
    provider_contract: >
      live.py defines neutral LiveConfig/LiveEvent/LiveSession/LiveToolCall protocol;
      gemini.py + openai.py are adapters. Same pattern lets a client swap
      Gemini Live <-> OpenAI Realtime with one config field.
    session_lifecycle: >
      One session per conversation_id; check websocket is_open before each turn;
      reconnect lazily; retire on conversation end (runtime.py TurnStore/Sessions).
  audio:
    input: 16-bit PCM mono 16kHz; optimal chunk = 100ms = 3200 bytes
    strip_riff: strip RIFF/data WAV header if source sends WAV
    output_rate: Gemini responds at 24kHz -> resample to 16k for HA (utils.resample_24k_to_16k)
    streaming_wav: emit WAV header with data length 0xFFFFFFFF for endless-stream playback (utils.streaming_wav_header)
    diagnostics: per-chunk RMS/peak logging (stt._analyse_pcm) is cheap and invaluable
  turn_taking:
    send_realtime_input: optimized for responsiveness (audio/text/audio_stream_end kwargs)
    send_client_content: deterministic ordering, batch turns
    vad_config: realtime_input_config.automatic_activity_detection can tune/disable VAD; disable -> client must send activity_start/activity_end
  tooling:
    prefer_llm_api_assist: >
      llm.async_get_api(llm.LLM_API_ASSIST) returns all Assist-exposed entities/tools
      plus the official api_prompt — do NOT reimplement tool defs or go through MCP
      for HA device control (fewer hops, avoids ha_mcp_tools API-id mismatch).
    pseudo_tools: add end_conversation (clean hangup) and show_text (render text) tools
    schema_limits: >
      Gemini function declarations accept a subset of JSON Schema only:
      snake_case keys, enum forces STRING, OBJECT requires properties.
      See _gemini_schema() in gemini.py — copy if handing tools to Gemini directly.
    mcp_bridge: >
      bridge.py uses google.genai.live.mcp_to_gemini_tool to expose all ha_mcp_tools
      tools to the model; tool calls are dispatched back through MCP.
  resumption:
    handles: save session_resumption_update.new_handle; pass via SessionResumptionConfig on reconnect
    go_away: server signals imminent termination; reconnect soon using saved handle
  ha_specific:
    tts_placeholder: conversation entity returns '-- gemini live --' so HA's TTS cache never replays stale audio
    stage_decoupling: asyncio.Queue producers (AudioStream/TextStream) decouple STT->conversation->TTS stages
  models:
    default: gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview
    alternate: gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-12-2025
  sdk_version: google-genai 1.59.0 (container) already has client.aio.live, send_realtime_input, send_tool_response, SessionResumptionConfig, RealtimeInputConfig — do not upgrade pin.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Comparison: our pipeline vs alternatives
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
comparison:
  gemini_live_ha_integration:
    pros: [HA-native entities, Assist tool exposure via LLM_API_ASSIST, config flow UI, pipelines selectable per-language]
    cons: [beta third-party code, pinned to HA voice-pipeline contract, requires HA restart for updates]
  ha_live_bridge:
    pros: [full control of prompts/tools/VAD, works outside Assist (web page /snapshot + ws), MCP tool reuse, no HA entity model needed]
    cons: [custom maintenance, mic streaming depends on client page, no wake-word, single shared session per client]
  openai_realtime:
    pros: [same live contract — adapter already exists in gemini_live codebase]
    cons: [second API key/billing, different voice set]
  official_3stage_pipeline:
    pros: [stable, first-party, local intent option]
    cons: [STT->LLM->TTS latency ~1-3s per turn, less natural]

```

```yaml
    python3 scripts/check-host-tools.py --host mn01
    python3 scripts/check-host-tools.py --host tony-dell --install-missing
```

# IP Address Registry

Per-network IP allocations linked to the MAC address registry

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.ip-address-registry.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: IP Address Registry
subtitle: Per-network IP allocations linked to the MAC address registry
icon: 🗺️
version: 1
last_updated: "2026-09-17"
ideas:
  - Every IP allocation links back to a stable device_id in ssot.mac-address-registry.yml
  - One network_record per subnet, with an allocations list
  - Track static reservations, DHCP leases, and discovered hosts
  - Starting with home networks; expand to Tailscale, Docker, etc. later
sections:
  - title: IP Registry Schema
    icon: 🧩
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: network_id
        text: Stable slug (e.g. home-192.168.2.0-24, legacy-192.168.1.0-24).
      - label: cidr
        text: CIDR notation of the subnet.
      - label: ssid / vlan
        text: Wi-Fi SSID, VLAN name, or link type.
      - label: gateway
        text: Router IP for that subnet.
      - label: dhcp_range
        text: DHCP pool as [start, end] (null if unknown).
      - label: allocations
        text:
          "List of ip_record: ip, device_id, interface_id, kind (static/reservation/dhcp/discovered), status, first_seen,
          last_seen, source."
  - title: Home Network 192.168.2.0/24
    icon: 🏠
```

# TCP/IP Link Monitor

Reachability watchdog with cheap probes, escalated scans, and safe fix attempts

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.link-monitor.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: TCP/IP Link Monitor
subtitle: Reachability watchdog with cheap probes, escalated scans, and safe fix attempts
icon: 🛜
version: 1

overview:
  purpose: Watch reachability to headless hosts and macOS/iOS verify hosts, run targeted scans when a link degrades, attempt safe fixes, and create focus-inbox alerts if unresolved.
  scope:
    - tony_omen
    - tony_dell
    - macbook
  mode: continuous background systemd user service on tony_dell
  service: ~/.config/systemd/user/mcp-link-monitor.service

principles:
  - Cheap first: use ping or TCP connect for periodic probes, not mcp_debug.
  - Threshold before scan: require N consecutive misses before escalating.
  - Back-off on failure: increase probe interval while a host is down to avoid hammering.
  - Safe fixes only by default: restart services, run tailscale ping, rebind DHCP only if explicitly enabled.
  - No automatic SSOT rewrites: IP drift creates an inbox alert for human confirmation.
  - Human escalation: if safe fixes fail, create a focus-inbox item with scan output.

checks:
  default_interval: 30
  down_backoff:
    - misses: 3
      interval: 10
    - misses: 6
      interval: 30
    - misses: 12
      interval: 120
  probe_methods:
    icmp:
      command: "ping -c 1 -W 2 {{address}}"
      expected_rc: 0
    tcp:
      command: 'python3 -c "import socket; socket.create_connection((''{{address}}'', {{port}}), timeout=5)"'
      expected_rc: 0
      ports:
        tony_omen: 9100
        tony_dell: 22
        macbook: 22
  address_preference:
    - tailscale_ip
    - magic_dns
    - local_hostname

state_machine:
  - name: healthy
    next: missing
    on: probe fails
  - name: missing
    next: scanning
    on: misses >= threshold
  - name: scanning
    action: run scan commands and classify failure
    next:
      - fixed: healthy
      - not_fixed: fixing
  - name: fixing
    action: apply safe fix actions
    next:
      - fixed: healthy
      - not_fixed: alert
  - name: alert
    action: create focus-inbox item and stop active fixes
    next: healthy
    on: probe succeeds

scan_on_failure:
  commands:
    - "tailscale status --json"
    - "ip -4 route"
    - "ip -4 -br addr show"
    - "ss -tlnp"
    - "tailscale ping {{name}} -c 3"

fix_actions:
  safe:
    - label: restart mcp-debug-cors
      command: "systemctl --user restart mcp-debug-cors.service"
      hosts:
        - tony_dell
    - label: tailscale ping
      command: "tailscale ping {{name}} -c 5"
      hosts:
        - tony_omen
        - tony_dell
        - macbook
  risky:
    - label: release and renew DHCP
      command: "sudo dhclient -r {{iface}} && sudo dhclient {{iface}}"
      require_env: LINK_MONITOR_RISKY=1
    - label: cycle interface
      command: "sudo ip link set {{iface}} down && sleep 1 && sudo ip link set {{iface}} up"
      require_env: LINK_MONITOR_RISKY=1

ip_drift:
  detection: compare current local IP and Tailscale IP against docs/ssot/ssot.mysystem.home.yml
  on_drift:
    action: create focus-inbox item
    allow_auto: false

resource_policy:
  - Probes are stateless and run without mcp_debug; each probe is one ping or one TCP connect.
  - Scans and fixes are triggered only after threshold misses, not on every tick.
  - Back-off while down prevents busy-looping on a failed link.
  - Logs are rotated; no per-probe history kept beyond the last 100 entries.

mcp_integration:
  - Use mcp-health for baseline service health, but the link monitor is independent.
  - On alert, write docs/ssot/focus-inbox/<target>-link-down-YYYY-MM-DD.yml using the focus dispatcher contract.

related_files:
  - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.health.yml
  - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.mcp-debug.cors.yml
  - docs/ssot/ssot.mysystem.home.yml
  - docs/ssot/ssot.mysystem.macbook.yml
  - scripts/mcp-link-monitor.py

```

# MAC Address Registry

Central registry of network interfaces and how to handle duplicate MACs

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.mac-address-registry.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: MAC Address Registry
subtitle: Central registry of network interfaces and how to handle duplicate MACs
icon: 🔗
version: 1
last_updated: "2026-09-11"
ideas:
  - One source of truth for every MAC on the home network
  - MAC is an attribute, not a primary key
  - Track duplicate / reused MACs common in cheap/Chinese IoT devices
  - Link every IP allocation to a stable device_id
sections:
  - title: Why MAC is not the primary key
    icon: 🔑
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: MAC collisions happen
        text:
          Low-cost Tuya, ESP, and off-brand IoT devices sometimes ship with duplicate or randomized MACs. Using mac as the
          primary key breaks as soon as two devices collide.
      - label: device_id is the stable key
        text: Every device gets a stable slug like tuya-plug-coffee, ip-cam-65, or hp-deskjet-2700. It survives IP and MAC changes.
      - label: One device, many interfaces
        text: A workstation may have wired, Wi-Fi, USB-tether, and Tailscale interfaces. Each is a child of the same device_id.
  - title: MAC Registry Schema
    icon: 🧩
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: device_id
        text: Required. Stable unique slug for the device.
      - label: label
        text: Required. Human-readable name.
      - label: local_ids
        text: "Device-native IDs used to disambiguate duplicates: tuya_id, serial, hostname, bluetooth_addr."
      - label: interfaces
        text: "List of interface records: interface_id, mac, oui, vendor, type, source, first_seen, status."
      - label: mac_conflict
        text: true when this device's MAC is also claimed by another device_id.
      - label: conflict_group
        text: Hash of the duplicated MAC, used to link colliding records.
      - label: duplicate_resolution
        text: "Strategy: network_observed, vendor_verified, local_id_tiebreaker."
      - label: status
        text: active / stale / unknown.
  - title: Duplicate MAC Handling
    icon: ⚠️
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Detect
        text: ARP scan, mDNS, or DHCP logs show the same MAC in two places, or two device records share a MAC.
      - label: Triage
        text:
          Compare vendor (OUI), device label/sticker, local control ID, and the network it was observed on. Chinese/white-label
          gear is the usual culprit.
      - label: Resolve
        text:
          Keep both device records. Set mac_conflict=true and the same conflict_group. Use device_id in IP and automation
          references. Treat MAC as a soft lookup key only.
      - label: Example
        text:
          If a new plug also reports 2c:b4:71:e8:aa:06, create device_id tuya-plug-duplicate-01, set mac_conflict=true and
          the same conflict_group, and resolve via Tuya device ID and observed IP.
  - title: Known Devices
    icon: 📋
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: tony-omen
```

# MCP Debug Visual Capture Bridge

Lightweight, opt-in screenshot, window list, clipboard image, and accessibility tree tools

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.mcp-debug.capture.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: MCP Debug Visual Capture Bridge
subtitle: Lightweight, opt-in screenshot, window list, clipboard image, and accessibility tree tools
icon: camera
version: 1

overview:
  purpose: |
    Extend mcp-debug with non-interactive visual capture tools so the assistant can
    observe remote host state without leaving the MCP workflow or duplicating
    PlayLive's browser automation and click/keyboard control.
  scope:
    - Capture the screen or a cropped region as a PNG.
    - List visible windows and their basic metadata.
    - Read an image from the clipboard when explicitly allowed.
    - Accessibility tree is optional for later; not in the first pass.
  out_of_scope:
    - Mouse/keyboard automation, clicks, drags, or live interactions.
    - Browser page capture and DOM inspection (PlayLive).
    - Video or continuous screen recording.
    - Time/clock and calculator/eval tools (use mcp_report timestamps, mcp_stats, and the client for arithmetic).

tools:
  - name: mcp_screenshot
    description: Return a base64-encoded PNG screenshot for a host.
    params:
      - name: host
        type: string
        required: true
      - name: region
        type: object
        required: false
        note: optional {x, y, width, height} crop to avoid leaking full displays
      - name: format
        type: string
        default: png
        note: png only in the first pass
    returns: "{ok, content_base64, width, height, bytes, error}"
    transport:
      macos: screencapture -x -
      linux:
        - gnome-screenshot -f -
        - grim
        - import
    note: always base64-encode; resize/compress if the encoded payload exceeds the soft cap

  - name: mcp_window_list
    description: Return a list of visible windows and metadata for a host.
    params:
      - name: host
        type: string
        required: true
    returns: "{ok, windows: [{id, app, title, pid, focused, bounds}], error}"
    transport:
      macos: lsappinfo / osascript
      linux_x11: xwininfo -root -tree
      linux_wayland: swaymsg -t get_tree
    note: no input/keyboard state is returned

  - name: mcp_clipboard_image_get
    description: Return a base64-encoded image from the host clipboard when allowed.
    params:
      - name: host
        type: string
        required: true
    returns: "{ok, content_base64, format, bytes, error}"
    transport:
      macos: pbpaste -Prefer rtf image path / NSPasteboard read
      linux: xclip -selection clipboard -t image/png -o
    note: never called automatically; explicit opt-in per host

  - name: mcp_a11y_tree
    description: Return a JSON UI element tree for an app or window.
    params:
      - name: host
        type: string
        required: true
      - name: app
        type: string
        required: false
        note: target application or window name
    returns: "{ok, tree, error}"
    transport:
      macos: AppleScript accessibility APIs
    status: experimental
    note: optional for later; do not implement in the first pass

security:
  - "Per-host `capture: true` is required; default is `capture: false` for all hosts."
  - "`mcp_screenshot` must support `region` cropping and avoid full-screen capture when a region is supplied."
  - "Soft size cap: 2 MB encoded base64; hard cap: 4 MB."
  - "Oversize images are downscaled or re-encoded before returning."
  - "All capture calls are logged with host, tool, region, and returned bytes."
  - "`mcp_clipboard_image_get` requires a separate `clipboard_image: true` opt-in."
  - "No capture tool is invoked automatically; the user or an explicit policy must trigger each call."

host_allowlist:
  macbook:
    capture: true
    clipboard_image: true
    note: safest first target; screencapture and pbcopy/pbpaste are well documented
  tony_omen:
    capture: true
    clipboard_image: true
  tony_dell:
    capture: true
    clipboard_image: true
    note: Linux headless host; mcp_screenshot will fail without a display, but mcp_window_list can be tested

limits:
  max_image_bytes_soft: 2097152
  max_image_bytes_hard: 4194304
  default_format: png
  allowed_formats: [png]
  max_window_count: 1000

implementation:
  order:
    - 1. macbook first (screencapture + pbcopy/pbpaste)
    - 2. Linux screenshot fallbacks after macOS path is stable
    - 3. mcp_window_list for macOS and one Linux host
    - 4. mcp_clipboard_image_get for macOS
    - 5. mcp_a11y_tree only if explicitly requested later
  notes:
    - Keep tools small and auditable; avoid shell pipelines that leak display contents to files.
    - Store no temporary image files on the host when possible; prefer stdout/fifo.
    - Update ssot.mcp-debug.yml with tool definitions, per-host flags, and limits.
    - Add smoke tests on macbook and one Linux host before marking completed.

status: active
last_updated: "2026-08-22"

related_files:
  - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.mcp-debug.yml
  - scripts/mcp_debug/server.py
  - scripts/mcp_debug/capture.py
  - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.host-roles.yml
  - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.health.yml

```

```yaml
  allow_headers: "Content-Type"

addressing:
  note: The chaba.h3 page cannot resolve .local mDNS from a public browser, and an HTTPS page cannot fetch an HTTP URL. Use a same-origin PHP proxy on chaba.h3 pointing to the public Tailscale Funnel endpoint on tony-omen.
  preferred:
    - https://chaba.h3.gizmo-thailand.com/api/mcp-savings.php
    - https://tony-omen.taila0626a.ts.net/mcp-savings.json
    - https://tony-omen.taila0626a.ts.net/mcp-table.json
  tailnet_only:
    - http://100.75.102.88:9100/mcp-savings.json
    - http://tony-omen.taila0626a.ts.net:9100/mcp-savings.json
  avoid:
    - http://tony-omen.local:9100/mcp-savings.json

proxy:
  savings:
    path: /api/mcp-savings.php
    source: chaba-h3/public/api/mcp-savings.php
    upstream: https://tony-omen.taila0626a.ts.net/mcp-savings.json
    timeout: 5
    fallback: public/apps/docs/mcp_debug/data/mcp-savings.json
  table:
    path: /api/mcp-table.php
    source: chaba-h3/public/api/mcp-table.php
    upstream: https://tony-omen.taila0626a.ts.net/mcp-table.json
    timeout: 8

resource_policy:
  - mcp_report(format="json") is expensive because it runs all vetted commands on all hosts.
  - The endpoint MUST NOT run mcp_report on every HTTP request.
  - Implement a cache with a refresh interval (default 60s).
  - Serve stale cached JSON on each request; refresh in the background or on a timer.
  - Provide a cache-buster or ?refresh=1 endpoint for on-demand regeneration, rate-limited to once per cache interval.

suggested_cache_implementation:
  refresh_interval: 60
  background_refresh: true
  headers:
    Cache-Control: "public, max-age=60"
  on_refresh:
    - run mcp_report(format="json", save=false)
    - store report string in memory
    - serve from memory until next refresh
  concurrency: single in-flight refresh; reject overlapping refresh requests

security:
  - Expose only pre-generated mcp-savings.json.
  - Do not allow arbitrary command execution via the HTTP endpoint.
  - Bind to 0.0.0.0 only when needed; consider 127.0.0.1 + a reverse proxy for stricter control.
```

# MCP-Debug File and Clipboard Bridge

Design and policy for remote file get/put and optional clipboard tools

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.mcp-debug.files.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: MCP-Debug File and Clipboard Bridge
subtitle: Design and policy for remote file get/put and optional clipboard tools
version: 1

purpose:
  - Extend mcp-debug with small, auditable file-transfer tools.
  - Allow the assistant to fetch remote logs/configs and push small scripts without leaving the MCP workflow.
  - Keep clipboard support experimental and disabled by default.

tools:
  mcp_get_file:
    description: Fetch a remote file as base64 with a hard size cap.
    input:
      host: target host (must be in allowed host list)
      path: absolute or home-prefixed file path
      max_bytes: optional, default 65536, hard cap 1048576
    output:
      ok: true | false
      path: resolved path
      encoding: base64
      content_base64: base64-encoded bytes
      size: bytes read
      truncated: true if file was larger than max_bytes
      error: error message if ok is false
    transport: |
      SSH exec with `cat` or `head -c <max_bytes>` depending on size, then base64-encode the payload.
    security:
      - path must match one allowed_path_prefix for the host
      - max_bytes cannot exceed hard cap
      - all calls logged with host, path, size, truncated flag
      - reads outside allowlist are rejected

  mcp_put_file:
    description: Write a small script or config to a remote host as base64.
    input:
      host: target host (must be in allowed host list)
      path: absolute or home-prefixed file path
      content_base64: base64-encoded file content
      mode: optional file mode, default "644" (octal string)
      overwrite: optional, default false
    output:
      ok: true | false
      path: resolved path
      bytes_written: number of bytes written
      error: error message if ok is false
    transport: |
      SSH exec with a heredoc after path-allowlist vetting. File is written to a temp path and atomically moved.
    security:
      - path must match one allowed_path_prefix for the host
      - size cannot exceed hard cap (1 MiB)
      - overwrite=false by default; confirmation required for writes outside allowlist
      - all calls logged with host, path, size, mode, overwrite
      - writes to paths outside allowlist are rejected

  mcp_eget:
    description: Install or download a prebuilt binary from GitHub/GitLab/Gitea/SourceForge using eget.
    input:
      host: target host (must be in allowed host list)
      repo: source repository or URL, e.g. 'BurntSushi/ripgrep'
      to: target directory (must match an allowed_path_prefix), default ~/.local/bin
      tag: optional release tag
      asset: optional asset filter
      extract_all: extract all archive files
      download_only: use 'eget download' instead of 'eget install'
    output:
      ok: true | false
      h: host
      rc: eget exit code
      out: stdout
      err: stderr
      error: error message if ok is false
    transport: SSH exec; command is 'eget install <repo> --to <allowed_path> ...'
    security:
      - target path is vetted against the host's allowed_path_prefixes
      - all arguments are shlex-quoted
      - no sudo required

  mcp_clipboard_get:
    description: Read the target host's clipboard as text.
    status: experimental
    default: enabled
    transport: macOS `pbpaste`; Linux `xclip -selection clipboard -o` or `wl-paste`
    security:
      - per-host opt-in only
      - host must have clipboard: true in ssot.mcp-debug.capture.yml
      - all calls logged

  mcp_clipboard_set:
    description: Write text to the target host's clipboard.
    status: experimental
    default: enabled
    transport: macOS `pbpaste`; Linux `xclip -selection clipboard -i` or `wl-copy`
    security:
      - per-host opt-in only
      - host must have clipboard: true in ssot.mcp-debug.capture.yml
      - all calls logged

limits:
  max_bytes:
    hard: 1048576
    default: 65536
  default_get_bytes: 65536
  max_path_length: 1024
  allowed_modes: ["400", "600", "644", "664", "755"]
  allowed_path_prefixes:
    tony_omen:
      - /tmp
      - /home/tony/.local
      - /home/tony/.config
      - /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell
      - /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-h3
      - /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-kbman
      - /var/log
    tony_dell:
      - /tmp
      - /home/tony/.local
      - /home/tony/.config
      - /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell
      - /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-h3
      - /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-kbman
      - /var/log
    macbook:
      - /tmp
      - /Users/tony
      - /var/log

logging:
  level: info
  fields:
    - timestamp
    - tool
    - host
    - path
    - size
    - truncated
    - overwrite
    - ok

status: active
last_updated: "2026-08-22"
maintainer: tony

```

```yaml
  hot_reload:
    description: Reload the mcp-debug server in place to pick up code or SSOT config changes without restarting Devin.
    command: mcp_debug
    arguments: '{"command": "reload"}'
    mechanism: |
      The server flushes an ok response, sets MCP_RELOADED=1, and calls os.execv to
      re-execute the same Python module. The stdio/SSH session is preserved.
    notification: notifications/tools/list_changed
    workflow:
      - Make code/SSOT changes in the local chaba repo.
      - scp changed scripts/mcp_debug/*.py and/or docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.mcp-debug.yml to the remote worktree.
      - 'Call mcp_debug { "command": "reload" }.'
      - The server re-execs and re-imports all modules; the client does not need to restart.
    notes:
      - All mcp_debug tools are reloaded (mcp_debug, mcp_query_ssot, mcp_ssot_query, mcp_ssot_get, mcp_raw, etc.).
      - The first load of the reload code itself still requires a normal process restart; after that only mcp_debug reload is needed.
    related_files:
```

# MCP Focus Actions

Per-action routing table for the mcp_focus tool

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.mcp-focus.actions.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: MCP Focus Actions
subtitle: Per-action routing table for the mcp_focus tool
icon: target
version: 2
actions:
  reload:
    when: "User explicitly asks to refresh, reload, or re-read the focus SSOT files.

      "
    output:
      - Re-read docs/ssot/ssot.focus.current.active.yml and backlog.
      - Return the same payload as status with reloaded: true and checked_at timestamp.
    confidence: high
  continue:
    when:
      'A request is empty, is "continue", or matches an active shared or branch focus label or subtask label.

      '
    order:
      - Prefer the active branch focus if the request mentions it.
      - Prefer the active shared focus if the request matches it.
      - If neither matches and one is active, continue the active shared focus.
      - If both active and neither matches, ask the user which to continue.
    output_target: active focus label
    confidence: high when matched, medium otherwise
  quick_win:
    when:
      'The request is small, concrete, and already represented in the Quick Wins section, or uses cue words

      such as "fix", "tweak", "small", "quick", "minor".

      '
    output_target: matching quick-win label
    confidence: high when label matches, medium for cues
  decompose:
    when:
      "The request is too large for a quick win but can be split into a small number of concrete subtasks that can each
      be completed in one session.

      "
    output:
      - Create or update a focus with the subtasks listed.
      - Start the first subtask immediately if the user has already approved.
      - Otherwise return the subtask list under suggestion for review.
    output_target: focus label or inbox path
    confidence: medium
  triage:
    when:
      "The request does not match an active focus or quick win, but an existing parked, backlog, improvement, or inbox item
      is the best next candidate.

      "
    source:
      "docs/ssot/ssot.focus.yml backlog, docs/ssot/ssot.improvements.yml, docs/ssot/focus-inbox/*.yml, scored by
      docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.focus.triage.yml"
    output_target: highest-scoring candidate label
    output:
      - action is always triage
      - triage_type indicates parked, backlog, improvement, or inbox
    confidence: medium
  draft_inbox:
    when:
      "The request does not match any existing active focus, quick win, backlog item, or inbox item.

      "
    output:
      - Create an in-memory draft inbox YAML for review.
      - Do not write the file to disk.
  defer:
    when:
      "The user wants to pause the active focus or its current subtask and resume it in a later session.

      "
    output:
      - Mark the in_progress subtask (or the whole focus if none) as deferred with resume_session and resume_note.
      - Append a session summary with next_action set to resume the focus.
  resume:
    when:
      "The user wants to pick up a previously deferred focus, or no active focus exists and a session has a pending resume
      next_action.

      "
    output:
      - Return the latest candidate focus from ssot.focus.sessions.yml with a resume/continue next_action.
      - If resume_session is provided, only return candidates whose next_action contains that session.
  sweep:
    when:
      "The user wants to review all remaining parked/backlog/inbox foci and choose one to hold while the rest are queued
      for processing.

      "
    output:
      - Return a hold candidate and a sorted process queue of all other parked, backlog, inbox, active, and deferred subtask
        candidates.
      - Default hold is the active branch focus if no hold is specified.
      - If bulk_session or session_map is provided, bulk-defer the process queue to the matched sessions and write the changes.
  next:
    when:
      "The user wants to activate the highest-priority parked or deferred focus and start processing it.

      "
    output:
      - Find the highest-priority parked/deferred focus (optionally filtered by resume_session).
      - Activate it in ssot.focus.current.yml, ssot.focus.yml, or the focus-inbox file.
      - Return the activated focus and a recommendation.
      - Return the draft content under suggestion.
    confidence: low
  technical_decision:
    when: "The assistant needs to record a design trade-off or architecture decision.

      "
    output:
      - Append a structured decision to docs/ssot/decisions/ssot.technical-decisions.yml.
    mode: technical_decision
    input: decision object with id, title, context, options, chosen, reasoning, consequences
  session_summary:
    when:
      "The assistant wants to close a session and record what was decided, planned, and deferred.

      "
    output:
      - Append a summary entry to docs/ssot/ssot.focus.sessions.yml.
    mode: session_summary
    input: summary object with focus, source, plan, done, follow_up, next_action, decisions

```

```yaml
subtitle: Session-start router and focus recommendation policy for the mcp_focus tool
icon: 🎯
version: 2
config:
  version: 2
  last_updated: "2026-08-19"
  maintainer: tony
  status: active
  canonical_implementation: scripts/mcp_debug/focus.py
  related_files:
    - scripts/mcp_debug/focus.py
    - scripts/mcp_focus/server.py
    - scripts/focus_common.py
    - scripts/focus_dispatcher/triage.py
    - scripts/prompt_preprocessor.py
    - docs/ssot/ssot.focus.current.yml
    - docs/ssot/ssot.focus.current.active.yml
    - docs/ssot/ssot.focus.current.backlog.yml
    - docs/ssot/ssot.focus.yml
    - docs/ssot/ssot.focus.sessions.yml
    - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.mcp-focus.actions.yml
    - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.focus.triage.yml
overview:
  purpose: "mcp_focus is the first MCP tool called when a session starts. Given an optional

    request, it recommends the next action without modifying any focus state.

    "
  inputs:
    - request: optional free-text user request
    - mode:
        optional "recommend" (default), "status", "reload", "pre_action", "safe_next", "ready_queue", "defer", "resume",
        "sweep", "next", "technical_decision", or "session_summary"
    - resume_session: target session identifier for defer mode
    - reason: reason for deferring
    - hold: label of the focus to hold while sweeping the rest
    - bulk_session: fallback session for any non-hold candidate not matched by session_map
    - session_map: mapping of focus label, branch, or 'default' to a session name for per-item routing
  guarantees:
    - Read-only. It never writes to ssot.focus.current.yml, ssot.focus.yml, or the focus-inbox/ directory.
    - If no request is provided, it always returns the current active foci and quick wins.
    - If a request is provided, it returns a single recommended action and the supporting reasoning.
    - technical_decision and session_summary modes append only to their respective SSOTs and never modify focus state.
output_schema:
  ok: boolean
  active:
    shared: active shared focus or null
    branch: active branch focus or null
  active_file_state:
    active_shared_focus: list of all shared focus entries with status, priority, and subtask count
    active_branch_focus: list of all branch focus entries with status, priority, and subtask count
  stale_warning: list of detected inconsistencies, e.g. all subtasks completed but focus not closed
  quick_wins: list of completed quick wins
  hand_off_queue: list of hand-off items
  ready_safe: list of safe-to-parallel items
  checked_at: ISO timestamp of the read
  recommendation:
    action: one of [continue, quick_win, triage, draft_inbox]
    triage_type: parked | backlog | improvement | inbox (only when action == triage)
    target: label of the focus, quick win, or inbox item
    confidence: high | medium | low
    reasoning: short human-readable explanation
    next_prompt: what to tell the user or assistant next
    canonical_request: preprocessed canonical request when a command or alias was expanded
    command: detected command metadata for direct dispatch
  preprocessed:
    ok: boolean
    request: original request
    canonical_request: expanded/grounded request string
    confidence: match score 0-1
    suggested_action: continue_focus, quick_win, backlog, inbox, continue_job, or direct
    grounding: source label, file, status, priority, branch
    command: detected command metadata
    similar_items: top similar focus/backlog/job items
decision_tree:
  - step: 1
    check: Is there an active shared or branch focus, or is the request empty / a continuation cue?
    true: continue
    false: go to 2
  - step: 2
    check: Is the request small, concrete, a quick-win cue, or an existing Quick Win label?
    true: quick_win
    false: go to 3
  - step: 3
    check: Is there a matching parked/deferred, backlog, improvement, or inbox item to triage?
    true: triage
    false: go to 4
  - step: 4
    check: No existing match
    true: draft_inbox
confidence_rules:
  high: direct label match or exact keyword hit
  medium: cue word, partial match, or triage score ordering
  low: no match; a draft inbox must be created
safety:
  - mcp_focus must not call focus-dispatcher.py or commit.
  - mcp_focus may append a decision record to docs/ssot/ssot.focus.decisions.yml when a request is provided.
  - mcp_focus may append a technical decision record to docs/ssot/decisions/ssot.technical-decisions.yml in technical_decision
    mode.
  - mcp_focus may append a session summary to docs/ssot/ssot.focus.sessions.yml in session_summary mode.
  - If an active focus exists, the default recommendation is "continue" unless the user explicitly asks to switch.
  - The tool may expose a "status" mode that only returns active foci and quick wins.
  - Any drafted inbox YAML returned to the assistant must be reviewed by the user before activation.
modes:
  - name: recommend
    description: Default. Classify the request and return a recommendation.
    read_only: true
    request_optional: true
  - name: status
    description: Return active foci, quick wins, hand-off queue, ready safe, and session groups.
    read_only: true
    request_optional: true
  - name: pre_action
    description: Summarize the active focus state before an action is taken.
    read_only: true
    request_optional: true
  - name: safe_next
    description: Return the highest-scoring focus that is safe to run in parallel.
    read_only: true
    request_optional: true
  - name: ready_queue
    description: Return the Ready (Safe) queue.
    read_only: true
    request_optional: true
  - name: defer
    description: Defer the active focus subtask or the focus itself.
    read_only: false
    request_optional: true
    extra_inputs:
      - resume_session
      - reason
  - name: resume
    description: Suggest a previously deferred focus to resume.
    read_only: true
    request_optional: true
    extra_inputs:
      - resume_session
  - name: sweep
    description: Review all parked/backlog/inbox foci and optionally bulk-defer.
    read_only: false
    request_optional: true
    extra_inputs:
      - hold
      - bulk_session
      - session_map
  - name: next
    description: Activate the highest-priority parked or deferred focus.
    read_only: false
    request_optional: true
    extra_inputs:
      - resume_session
  - name: preview
    description: Show the highest-priority parked or deferred focus without activating.
    read_only: true
    request_optional: true
    extra_inputs:
      - resume_session
  - name: done
    description: Check whether all open foci are closed and suggest whether to stop.
    read_only: true
    request_optional: true
  - name: technical_decision
    description: Append a structured technical decision.
    read_only: false
    request_optional: false
  - name: session_summary
    description: Append a session summary.
    read_only: false
    request_optional: false
tools:
  - name: mcp_focus
    description: Main focus router; see modes above.
    server: mcp-focus
  - name: mcp_focus_status
    description: Lightweight status endpoint, equivalent to mcp_focus mode=status with no request.
    server: mcp-focus
related_files:
  - docs/ssot/ssot.focus.current.yml
  - docs/ssot/ssot.focus.yml
  - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.focus.triage.yml
  - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.focus-dispatcher.yml
  - scripts/mcp_debug/focus.py
  - scripts/mcp_debug/server.py
  - scripts/focus_common.py
  - scripts/focus_dispatcher/triage.py
  - scripts/focus_dispatcher/cli.py
  - scripts/focus_dispatcher/actions.py
  - scripts/prompt_preprocessor.py
  - scripts/overnight-focus-review.py
  - scripts/overnight-status.py
  - scripts/test-focus-smoke.py
implementation_notes:
  - Implemented in scripts/mcp_debug/focus.py and scripts/mcp_debug/server.py.
  - Shared focus model helpers (triage scoring, safe-to-parallel/ownership/lock checks, active/backlog/inbox extraction, sweep)
    live in scripts/focus_common.py and are imported by scripts/mcp_debug/focus.py, scripts/focus_dispatcher/triage.py, and
    scripts/prompt_preprocessor.py.
  - mcp_focus supports mode=status (read-only active/Quick Wins listing), mode=recommend (decision tree), mode=technical_decision,
    and mode=session_summary.
  - The recommend decision tree maps directly to the assistant-level cases in docs/ssot/ssot.focus.current.yml#decision_tree.
  - mcp_focus appends a decision record to docs/ssot/ssot.focus.decisions.yml whenever a request is provided.
  - mcp_focus mode=technical_decision appends to docs/ssot/decisions/ssot.technical-decisions.yml.
  - mcp_focus mode=session_summary appends to docs/ssot/ssot.focus.sessions.yml.
  - The assistant uses the returned action as the first disposition and only deviates for special cases (live_bug_report, auto_generated_alert,
    requires_mcp_data).
improvements:

    step_3: The assistant/user manually invokes the printed run_subagent JSON.
    step_4: The subagent executes the contract and updates subtask status in docs/ssot/ssot.focus.current.backlog.yml.
```
