# MCP Tools Policy and Catalog

Global selection rules, fallback procedures, and server registry for MCP usage

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.mcp-tools.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: MCP Tools Policy and Catalog
subtitle: Global selection rules, fallback procedures, and server registry for MCP usage
status: active

ideas:
  - Make MCP server selection explicit and repeatable across all projects
  - Consolidate scattered MCP guidance into a single source of truth
  - Prevent silent fallbacks and unauthorized workarounds
  - Keep runtime credentials and secrets out of this SSOT

description: |
  This SSOT catalogs the MCP servers available across the chaba/trade ecosystem
  and defines when to use each one. It is a design-level policy, not the
  runtime config. For credentials, endpoints, and local paths, see the runtime
  MCP config at `~/.config/devin/mcp_config.json` and the infrastructure
  definitions in `docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.mcp.yml`.

ref: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.mcp.yml

# Selection workflow before invoking an MCP server
selection_workflow:
  - Check whether a dedicated project skill already covers the task
  - Prefer this SSOT and project AGENTS.md for the primary/recommended MCP
  - Use `ssot-search` or `grep` to read only the relevant `policy.<domain>` section; avoid full-file reads
  - List tools with `mcp_list_tools` before guessing names or schemas
  - On failure, follow the failure procedure below; do not silently switch services

# Domain-to-MCP mapping and fallback rules
policy:
  documentation_search:
    primary: mddb
    secondary: docs-trade
    tertiary: ssot-search skill
    default: |
      Use mddb semantic search first for all documentation and SSOT
      questions. Use docs-trade for project-agnostic docs, and ssot-search
      for exact YAML pattern matching.
    when_not_to_use: |
      Do not use mddb as a substitute for web search or live API docs.
      Use web_search or docs-trade for external libraries.
    fallback: |
      If MDDB is unavailable, notify the user and propose a fix. Use the
      docs-trade or docs server only after MDDB is confirmed down. Fall back
      to grep or read only with user confirmation.

  trade_ssot_search:
    primary: ssot-search skill
    default: |
      Use ssot-search for exact keyword matches, whitelisted SSOT paths,
      and registry lookups. It is faster and more precise than MDDB for
      structured YAML.
    when_not_to_use: |
      Do not use ssot-search for broad conceptual questions or external
      documentation; use mddb or docs-trade for those.
    note: |
      The ssot-search skill is the preferred tool for searching Trade SSOT
      YAML. Only fall back to docs-mcp for broader documentation searches.

  home_assistant:
    primary: home-assistant
    default: |
      Use the home-assistant MCP server for live Home Assistant lookups
      (states, devices, entities, automations, helpers, dashboards).
      Prefer read-only tools such as `ha_get_state`, `ha_search`,
      `ha_get_device`, and `ha_call_read_tool`.
    when_not_to_use: |
      Do not use the home-assistant MCP to make destructive changes without
      user confirmation. Do not use it for general OS/service health; use
      mcp-health or mcp-debug instead.
    fallback: |
      If the server is unavailable, use `scripts/home-assistant/assess-device.py`
      for direct HA REST state lookups, or query the relevant HA API manually.

  system_health:
    primary: mcp-health
    default: |
      Use mcp-health for all consolidated health checks, service status,
      and host reachability questions. It is the single source of truth.
    when_not_to_use: |
      Do not use mcp-health for real-time logs or deep process debugging;
      use mcp-debug or direct system commands instead.
    fallback: |
      Use mcp-health for consolidated health checks. If unavailable, check
      the underlying service URLs directly before asking the user.

  github_operations:
    primary: github
    default: |
      Use github MCP for creating issues/PRs, searching code, and
      repository operations. Use git CLI only for local read-only history.
    when_not_to_use: |
      Do not use github MCP for local git history, blame, or diff review.
      Use git CLI for those.
    fallback: |
      Use git CLI for local read-only history. Escalate authentication or
      permission errors to the user before retrying.

  financial_data:
    primary: alphavantage
    default: |
      Start with alphavantage for FX, equities, and crypto. For commodities
      (gold, oil) use MetalPrices or Investing.com; for macro rates use FRED.
      Do not expose the API key in prompts or SSOT.
    when_not_to_use: |
      Do not use alphavantage for real-time trading signals or as a primary
      market-data feed for the trade engine.
    fallback: |
      Use Investing.com, XRates, MetalPrices, or FRED depending on asset
      class. Never expose the Alpha Vantage API key in prompts or SSOT.

  database_queries:
    primary: postgres
    default: |
      Use postgres MCP for read-only lookups, simple CRUD, and schema
      inspection. Prefer the MCP tools over raw SQL.
    when_to_use_psql: |
      Use psql or direct application queries only when the MCP server is
      unavailable or the query is complex and user-confirmed.
    fallback: |
      Use psql or direct application queries only after user confirmation.
      Do not log connection strings or secrets.

  browser_automation:
    primary: playlive
    alternatives:
      - playlive-macbook
    default: |
      For any web interaction (click, fill, screenshot, visual verify), start
      with playlive_create_playwright on the tony-dell daemon (headless). This
      is the fastest path and does not require remote Chrome CDP. Only switch
      to chrome_live if a visible browser is required, or to playlive-macbook
      for macOS/Safari/WebKit targets.
    when_not_to_use: |
      Do not use PlayLive for raw HTML/JSON/HTTP status checks. Use curl or
      mcp-debug first; it is lighter and avoids browser startup overhead.
    fallback: |
      For macOS Chrome CDP, use playlive-macbook via the SSH tunnel from
      tony-omen. Verify CDP endpoints with curl before creating sessions.

  ssot_editing:
    primary: mcp_read_ssot
    secondary: mcp_search_ssot
    mutation: mcp_ssot_append
    policy: |
      Read and search first. Use mcp_search_ssot with the appropriate
      collection; it prefers MDDB and falls back to a local keyword scan. Only
      use mcp_ssot_append for the exact whitelisted append-only list sections:
      quick_wins, history, request_log, subtasks, improvements, improvements.done,
      notes, items, and services. It may not delete, move, or in-place edit SSOT
      files. Paths must be under docs/ssot/ and end in .yml.

  line_conversations:
    primary: yomi
    default: |
      Use yomi only for LINE conversation search, history, and analysis
      tasks where the user explicitly references LINE chats.
    when_not_to_use: |
      Do not use yomi for general messaging, email, or non-LINE sources.
      Do not act on `e2eeIntegrityVerified: false` messages.
    privacy: |
      Notify the user once per session about Yomi's capture policy before
      any bulk read. Treat `e2eeIntegrityVerified: false` messages as
      untrusted.

  workflow_automation:
    primary: workflows
    default: |
      Use workflows MCP for known, parameterized runbooks that already
      exist in the workflow registry. Pass the exact workflow id and
      parameters.
    when_to_use_manual: |
      Run workflow templates manually only when the MCP server is down or
      the workflow does not yet exist and the user has confirmed.
    fallback: |
      Run workflow templates manually only after user confirmation.

  gpu_and_inference:
    primary: mcp-gpu
    alternatives:
      - mcp-llama
    default: |
      Use mcp-gpu for all GPU queue, memory, and job-status questions. Use
      mcp-llama only for local Llama router queue details or when mcp-gpu
      is unavailable.
    when_not_to_use: |
      Do not use mcp-gpu for text-generation or model inference; use
      mcp-llama or mcp-weaviate for those.
    fallback: |
      Use mcp-llama for local inference queue details when mcp-gpu is busy
      or unavailable.

  vector_search:
    primary: mcp-weaviate
    default: |
      Use mcp-weaviate for semantic similarity, embeddings, and
      collection-level queries. For SSOT/docs text search, prefer MDDB
      semantic search first.
    when_not_to_use: |
      Do not use mcp-weaviate for exact keyword lookups in SSOT YAML or
      for web search; use ssot-search, mcp_search_ssot, or docs instead.
    fallback: |
      Notify the user and verify the Weaviate service URL before falling back.

  icloud_services:
    primary: icloud
    default: |
      Use the icloud MCP (MrGo2/mcp-icloud, cloud mode on mn01) for iCloud
      Email (IMAP/SMTP), Calendar (CalDAV) and Contacts (CardDAV) — read,
      search, create, update. Syncs to iPhone/iPad automatically.
    when_not_to_use: |
      Notes, Reminders, Messages and Safari return errors in cloud mode —
      they are local-mode only and require a Mac-hosted server. Do not use
      icloud for iCloud Drive or Photos (not covered by this server).
    caution: |
      send-email reaches another person irrevocably — confirm with the user
      before sending. mark-as-read and delete/update tools mutate live state.
    fallback: |
      If auth fails (401/UNAUTHORIZED), the app-specific password is revoked
      or wrong — report and ask the user to regenerate at account.apple.com,
      then update ~/.config/secrets/icloud-mcp.env on mn01 and recreate the
      container (env is baked at podman create time).

  diagnostics:
    primary: mcp-debug
    default: |
      Use mcp-debug when an MCP call returns an unexpected error and you
      need to capture the raw request/response. Start with mcp_debug_health
      and mcp_debug_trace.
    when_not_to_use: |
      Do not use mcp-debug for general health checks, HTTP probes, or
      service logs. Use mcp-health, curl, or systemctl instead.
    note: |
      Use only for debugging MCP calls. Do not leave enabled in normal usage.

# Server registry
servers:
  - name: mddb
    status: active
    category: documentation
    use_cases:
      - Semantic documentation search
      - Cross-collection queries
      - SSOT discovery
    example_tools:
      - semantic_search
      - search_documents
      - get_stats
      - aggregate
    failure_procedure:
      - Check MDDB health endpoint
      - Restart the MDDB container if it is down
      - Request user confirmation before using grep as a fallback

  - name: docs
    status: active
    category: documentation
    use_cases:
      - Project-agnostic documentation search
      - Scrape and index library documentation
      - Offline local docs
    example_tools:
      - search_docs
      - fetch_url
      - list_libraries
      - find_version
      - scrape_docs
      - refresh_version
      - list_jobs
      - get_job_info
      - cancel_job
      - remove_docs
    failure_procedure:
      - Ensure a Chromium/Chrome executable is available (set PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE_PATH to a system Chrome like /usr/bin/google-chrome)
      - Rebuild the docs-mcp cache if results are stale
    note: |
      The @arabold/docs-mcp-server startup blocks if no Playwright Chromium is installed. Use the system Chrome fallback or run `npx playwright install chromium`.

  - name: docs-trade
    status: active
    category: documentation
    use_cases:
      - Trade project docs search
      - Cached local docs
    example_tools:
      - search_docs
      - get_page
    failure_procedure:
      - Rebuild the `trade/.docs-mcp` cache if stale

  - name: mcp-health
    status: active
    category: operations
    use_cases:
      - Service health checks
      - System dependency monitoring
    example_tools:
      - check_health
      - get_status
    failure_procedure:
      - Check the underlying service endpoints directly

  - name: github
    status: active
    category: development
    use_cases:
      - Issues, pull requests, repositories
      - Code review and collaboration
    example_tools:
      - list_issues
      - search_issues
      - create_pull_request
      - pull_request_review_write
    failure_procedure:
      - Verify token permissions
      - Escalate auth issues to the user

  - name: alphavantage
    status: active
    category: financial_data
    use_cases:
      - Stock, commodity, forex, and economic data
      - Technical indicators
    example_tools:
      - TIME_SERIES_DAILY
      - WTI
      - WHEAT
      - CORN
      - BRENT
      - FX_DAILY
    failure_procedure:
      - Do not silently disable
      - Report the specific function and error
      - Use asset-class-specific fallback sources

  - name: postgres
    status: active
    category: database
    use_cases:
      - Database queries and operations
      - CRUD on trade data
    failure_procedure:
      - Verify the database is reachable
      - Use psql only after user confirmation

  - name: playlive
    status: active
    category: browser
```

# Operational Checklists

Canonical pre/post transition checklists for shutdown, restart, deploy, backup, and maintenance

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.operations.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Operational Checklists
subtitle: Canonical pre/post transition checklists for shutdown, restart, deploy, backup, and maintenance
icon: clipboard-check
version: 1
overview:
  purpose: |
    Define the canonical "what must be true" for each operational transition so
    scripts, focus dispatch, and human operators can verify the same conditions
    before and after a change. Each step references the owning SSOT file instead
    of duplicating live data.
  source_of_truth: |
    Checklists describe policy and topology, not live state. Live state is
    reported by mcp-health, focus-dispatcher, and the runtime scripts referenced
    below.

scope:
  - Applies to tony-dell, tony-omen, macbook, michael-ha, and any host or service
    that runs a persistent or scheduled workload.
  - Applies to host restarts, service restarts, image updates, backups, and
    feature deployments.

conventions:
  id_format: transition.name
  evidence: |
    Each step should record what was verified, by whom, and the command or
    report that proves it. Evidence is a short string, not a log dump.
  failure_mode: If a step fails, mark it `blocked` and add a note; do not force
    the next step unless the operator explicitly overrides.
  safe_to_parallel: true only when the step does not change live services and can
    be verified independently.

checklists:
  pre_shutdown:
    id: transition.pre_shutdown
    purpose: |
      Verify the system is in a safe state before a planned shutdown or reboot.
    owner: tony
    steps:
      - id: focus.sync
        label: Sync focus and session state
        action: Run focus-dispatcher and confirm the current focus is captured in ssot.focus.current.active.yml or ssot.focus.yml history.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/ssot.focus.current.active.yml
        must: true
      - id: health.snapshot
        label: Take a final mcp-health snapshot
        action: Run mcp-health for the active profile and confirm the snapshot is stored.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.health.yml
        must: true
      - id: git.clean
        label: Commit or stash pending work
        action: Ensure the canonical worktree is clean or the remaining changes are intentionally uncommitted.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/ssot.dev-system.assessment.yml
        must: true
      - id: services.stop
        label: Stop non-essential services
        action: Stop optional services such as playlived, michael-dev, and experimental GPU jobs unless the operator marks them critical.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.services.yml
        must: false
      - id: backups.verify
        label: Verify last backup timestamp
        action: Confirm the most recent backup timer completed and the archive is readable.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.disaster-recovery.yml
        must: false
      - id: tailscale.up
        label: Verify Tailscale on all reachable hosts
        action: Check tailscale status for tony-dell, tony-omen, macbook, and michael-ha.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.host-roles.yml
        must: false

  post_restart:
    id: transition.post_restart
    purpose: |
      Verify the system is back to the intended state after a restart.
    owner: tony
    steps:
      - id: health.check
        label: Run mcp-health home profile
        action: Run mcp-health and confirm no critical services are error/degraded.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.health.yml
        must: true
      - id: mcp.devin
        label: Verify Devin MCP tools
        action: Run mcp_list_tools for each server in ~/.config/devin/mcp_config.json and mcp-health quick_health. If tony-ha (9584) or michael-dev (9585) does not list tools, restart the HA container and retry.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.mcp-tools.yml
        must: true
      - id: services.start
        label: Start expected services
        action: Restart the units listed in ssot.services.yml that are marked auto-start for the current host.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.services.yml
        must: true
      - id: focus.resume
        label: Resume the previous focus
        action: Run focus-dispatcher and confirm the active focus is the same or the next queued focus is selected.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/ssot.focus.current.active.yml
        must: true
      - id: tailscale.verify
        label: Verify Tailscale connectivity
        action: Confirm the expected hosts are reachable over Tailscale.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.host-roles.yml
        must: true
      - id: logs.sweep
        label: Check recent service logs for errors
        action: Run mcp-logs or journalctl for the services that were restarted.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.mcp-debug.yml
        must: false
      - id: ssot.validate
        label: Validate SSOT
        action: node scripts/ssot-validate-all.mjs
        must: true

  pre_update:
    id: transition.pre_update
    purpose: |
      Verify the system before applying a code, config, or dependency update.
    owner: tony
    steps:
      - id: focus.capture
        label: Capture the active focus
        action: Ensure the current focus or job is recorded in ssot.focus.current.active.yml.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/ssot.focus.current.active.yml
        must: true
      - id: git.baseline
        label: Record the current git state
        action: Note the current commit, branch, and any uncommitted files.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/ssot.dev-system.assessment.yml
        must: true
      - id: health.baseline
        label: Record a health baseline
        action: Run mcp-health so the post-update comparison is meaningful.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.health.yml
        must: false
      - id: deps.lock
        label: Record dependency versions
        action: Note the current package versions or image digests being replaced.
        must: false
      - id: secrets.audit
        label: Confirm secrets are not being exposed
        action: Verify the change does not add credentials or tokens to SSOT or logs.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.mcp-tools.yml
        must: true

  post_update:
    id: transition.post_update
    purpose: |
      Verify the system after a code, config, or dependency update.
    owner: tony
    steps:
      - id: health.compare
        label: Compare health after update
        action: Re-run mcp-health and compare to the pre-update baseline.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.health.yml
        must: true
      - id: git.verify
        label: Verify the commit landed
        action: Confirm the commit is present, pushed, and the working tree is clean.
        must: true
      - id: service.verify
        label: Restart affected services
        action: Restart or reload the service referenced by the update.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.services.yml
        must: true
      - id: logs.watch
        label: Watch for new errors
        action: Check the service logs for the first 5-10 minutes after restart.
        must: false
      - id: focus.update
        label: Update the focus entry
        action: Mark the focus completed or update it with the post-update state.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/ssot.focus.current.active.yml
        must: true

  pre_deploy:
    id: transition.pre_deploy
    purpose: |
      Verify a deploy can happen safely.
    owner: tony
    steps:
      - id: target.reachable
        label: Target host reachable
        action: Confirm the deploy target is reachable over SSH/Tailscale.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.host-roles.yml
        must: true
      - id: backup.recent
        label: Recent backup exists
        action: Confirm the most recent backup is within the retention window.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.disaster-recovery.yml
        must: false
      - id: ssot.clean
        label: SSOT and repo clean
        action: Confirm the target files are staged or the deployment will not overwrite unrelated work.
        must: true
      - id: config.review
        label: Review config diff
        action: Review the diff for the target host/service before applying.
        must: true
      - id: permissions.ok
        label: Permissions verified
        action: Confirm the deploy user has the required sudo/systemd/docker permissions.
        must: true

  post_deploy:
    id: transition.post_deploy
    purpose: |
      Verify a deploy completed safely.
    owner: tony
    steps:
      - id: service.active
        label: Service active
        action: Confirm the service or container is running and healthy.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.services.yml
        must: true
      - id: endpoint.ok
        label: Endpoint reachable
        action: Curl the health or URL endpoint for the deployed service.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.health.yml
        must: true
      - id: ssot.update
        label: Update SSOT
        action: Update the relevant SSOT file with the new state, timestamp, or version.
        must: true
      - id: focus.record
        label: Record the deploy
        action: Add a session note or improvement entry if the deploy changed behavior.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/ssot.focus.sessions.yml
        must: false

  pre_backup:
    id: transition.pre_backup
    purpose: |
      Verify the system is ready for a backup.
    owner: tony
    steps:
      - id: disk.free
        label: Disk space sufficient
        action: Confirm the destination has enough free space for the next backup.
        must: true
      - id: quiesce
        label: Quiesce writers
        action: Pause or stop services that write to the data being backed up if the backup is not crash-consistent.
        must: false
      - id: verify_source
        label: Verify source paths
        action: Confirm the paths listed in ssot.disaster-recovery.yml exist and are readable.
        must: true

  post_backup:
    id: transition.post_backup
    purpose: |
      Verify a backup completed and is restorable.
    owner: tony
    steps:
      - id: backup.verify
        label: Backup integrity check
        action: Run the verification step listed in ssot.disaster-recovery.yml for the backup target.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.disaster-recovery.yml
        must: true
      - id: resume.writers
        label: Resume paused services
        action: Restart any services paused for the backup window.
        must: true
      - id: record.backup
        label: Record the backup
        action: Update the backup log or improvement history with the result.
        must: true

  pre_maintenance:
    id: transition.pre_maintenance
    purpose: |
      Verify the system before a longer maintenance window.
    owner: tony
    steps:
      - id: freeze.changes
        label: Freeze non-essential changes
        action: Confirm no other sessions are actively changing config, deployments, or services.
        must: true
      - id: maintenance.window
        label: Confirm maintenance window
        action: Confirm the planned window and expected duration.
        must: true
      - id: monitor.link
        label: Link to monitoring
        action: Note the monitoring or health endpoint that should be watched during the window.
        must: false

  post_maintenance:
    id: transition.post_maintenance
    purpose: |
      Verify the system after a maintenance window.
    owner: tony
    steps:
      - id: services.back
        label: Services back to expected state
        action: Confirm the intended services are active and reachable.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.services.yml
        must: true
      - id: focus.resume
        label: Resume the previous focus
        action: Run focus-dispatcher and confirm the next focus is selected.
        ssot_ref: docs/ssot/ssot.focus.current.active.yml
        must: true
      - id: improvements.update
        label: Update improvements if needed
        action: Add or update ssot.improvements.yml entries if the maintenance revealed new issues.
        must: false

host_notes:
  tony_dell:
    reboot_role: headless primary and persistent service host
    pre_shutdown:
      - Confirm mcp-health/mcp-focus/mcp-debug SSH wrappers will fail while tony-dell
        is down; interactive sessions on tony-omen should expect MCP tool errors.
      - Verify no active Yomi/Postgres writes that must not be interrupted
        (see ssot.yomi-failover.yml for failover to tony-omen if the window is long).
      - Confirm ha-live / Home Assistant consumers can tolerate the gap.
      - Take a final mcp-health snapshot; note current unknowns so post-reboot
        comparison is meaningful.
    post_restart:
      - >-
        Podman rootless containers auto-start; verify redis, postgres, weaviate,
        raceman, mddb are running (podman ps).
      - >-
        systemd --user units: mcp-debug-sse, yomi timers, chaba-audit timers,
        mcp-health timer, tony-dell-health-snapshot timer.
      - Home Assistant + michael-dev reachable; ha-live via Tailscale Serve 8444.
      - gpu-queue on tony-dell:3001 and Caddy on tony-dell:8080 answer.
      - Re-run mcp-health; compare against pre_shutdown snapshot.
      - >-
        Verify Devin MCP server endpoints on tony-dell; mcp_list_tools for tony-ha (:9584),
        michael-dev (:9585), and all other tony-dell-hosted servers. Restart the HA container
        if the MCP port is not listening.
    refs:
      - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.tony-dell-failover.yml
      - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.yomi-failover.yml
      - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.health.home.tony-dell.yml
      - docs/kb/host-reboot-verification.md
    known_issues:
      - >-
        tailscaled (serve/funnel incl. tailscale-serve-8080.service) binds
        tailnet-IP ports at boot; any 0.0.0.0 container bind on the same port
        gets EADDRINUSE. Policy: containers bind 127.0.0.1, serve handles
        tailnet (decided 2026-09-07; see runbook).
      - barrierc requires DISPLAY=:20 (CRD Xorg) in barrier-client.service.
      - mddb takes ~4-8 min to bind ports after start; wait before restarting.
      - >-
        Physical monitor is on the Intel iGPU (card1-DP-2), NOT the AMD card
        (card2). GDM autologin (Session=Lubuntu) exits immediately on the seat
        (reason unresolved; greeter is Wayland despite WaylandEnable=false).
        Working seat path since 2026-09-07: system unit xorg-seat.service
        (root Xorg :1 on vt7) + user unit lxqt-seat.service (startlxqt,
        waits for /tmp/.X11-unix/X1, chvt 7) + barrier-client.service with
        DISPLAY=:1 (waits for X1 socket). GDM greeter remains on tty1.
      - barrier-client.service now targets DISPLAY=:1 (physical seat), not :20.
        The CRD session :20 no longer has barrier input by design.
  tony_omen:
    reboot_role: interactive primary and GPU host
    pre_shutdown:
      - Save interactive/Devin session state; GPU jobs cannot migrate.
      - Barrier clients (tony-dell barrierc) will disconnect.
      - Stop or checkpoint GPU workloads (ollama models, imagen2, txt2vid).
    post_restart:
      - nvidia-smi shows the GPU with only Xorg attached.
      - tailscale status online as 100.75.102.88 with direct path to tony-dell.
      - >-
        systemd units: barriers.service (user), cpufreq-limit.service (system),
        weaviate-index.timer, arp-inventory-scan.timer.
      - >-
        Verify CPU frequency cap: `cpupower frequency-info` reports a 2.20 GHz
        upper limit and `cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/scaling_max_freq`
        returns 2200000. If the cap is wrong, restart `cpufreq-limit.service`.
      - >-
        Verify monitoring data sources: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}'
        http://100.75.102.88:8001/health` returns 200 and `http://100.75.102.88:8001/api/sensors`
        returns valid JSON with `host.temperatures` and `host.cpu_freq`.
      - sensor-reader container on :8001, Google Drive mount, Ollama, GPU Queue.
      - Re-run mcp-health; expect intentionally-off services to stay off.
      - >-
        Barrier: confirm `barriers.service` is listening on 24800 and has accepted
        the tony-dell client (`ss -tlnp | grep 24800`). If the log repeats
        "primary screen unavailable: unable to open screen", the X display was not
        ready when the unit started; restart with `systemctl --user restart
        barriers.service` once the seat is up.
    refs:
      - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.health.home.system.yml
      - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.gpu.yml
      - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.night-jobs.tony-omen.yml
    known_issues:
      - >-
        `barriers.service` can start before the GDM/Xauthority on DISPLAY :0 is
        ready, leaving it alive but unable to open the screen and not listening on
        port 24800. Applied fix: add an `ExecStartPre` that waits up to 60 s for
        `/tmp/.X11-unix/X0` and `/run/user/1000/gdm/Xauthority`, move
        `StartLimitIntervalSec=0` from `[Service]` to `[Unit]`, then
        `systemctl --user daemon-reload` and restart. The unit now starts reliably
        after the X display is ready.
```

# Overnight Orchestration

DAG-driven overnight workflow for the chaba system

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.orchestration.overnight.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Overnight Orchestration
subtitle: DAG-driven overnight workflow for the chaba system
icon: workflow
version: 1

workflow:
  name: overnight
  description: |
    Replaces the linear overnight-jobs-expanded.sh with a directed acyclic graph.
    Each step declares its dependencies and on_fail policy. The orchestrator
    writes ORCHESTRATION.json and ORCHESTRATION_STATE.json for checkpointing.

config:
  state_file: reports/ORCHESTRATION_STATE.json
  report_file: reports/ORCHESTRATION.json
  default_on_fail: abort

steps:
  - id: ssot_validate
    name: SSOT Validation
    run: node scripts/ssot-validate-all.mjs
    on_fail: abort
    timeout: 120

  - id: health_snapshot
    name: Health Snapshot
    run: node scripts/health-snapshot.mjs
    on_fail: continue
    timeout: 300
    depends_on: [ssot_validate]

  - id: service_log_sweep
    name: Service Log Error Sweep
    run: python3 scripts/overnight/service-logs-sweep.py
    on_fail: continue
    timeout: 600
    depends_on: [ssot_validate]

  - id: dev_system_assess
    name: Development System Assessment
    run: python3 scripts/dev-system-assess.py
    on_fail: continue
    timeout: 120
    depends_on: [service_log_sweep]

  - id: ssot_optimize
    name: SSOT Optimization
    run: node scripts/ssot-optimize.mjs
    on_fail: continue
    timeout: 300
    depends_on: [dev_system_assess]

  - id: promote_reports
    name: Promote Reports to Focus
    run: python3 scripts/overnight/promote-reports.py
    on_fail: continue
    timeout: 120
    depends_on: [ssot_optimize]

```

```yaml
title: Secrets Console manifest — credential -> slot -> consumer map
version: 1
created: '2026-09-21'
maintainer: tony
status: active

# METADATA ONLY — no secret values in this file, ever. Values live in the
# env files below; the console fingerprints them at runtime and never
# returns contents. Slot types:
#   var  — a VAR=value line in an env file (default)
#   file — the whole file is the secret (key JSONs, .txt secrets)
#   unit — an inline Environment=VAR=... line inside a systemd user unit
# sensitivity: high = live credential that grants write/control access;
#   medium = read-only or scoped; low = LAN-local.
# consumer entries are units to `systemctl --user restart` after a write.

credentials:

  - id: gemini-ada
    title: Gemini API key — Ada voice services (LEAKED 2026-09-21, devin-bank transcript)
    kind: api-key
    sensitivity: high
    issuer:
      name: Google AI Studio
      url: "https://aistudio.google.com/apikey"
    rotate:
      url: "https://aistudio.google.com/apikey"
      steps:
        - "Create a new key in AI Studio"
        - "console: set all slots, restart consumers"
        - "Delete the old key in AI Studio (kills leaked copies)"
    slots:
      - {host: mn01, file: "~/.config/secrets/ada-ha-tony.env", var: GEMINI_API_KEY}
      - {host: mn01, file: "~/.config/secrets/ada-ha-michael.env", var: GEMINI_API_KEY}

  - id: gemini-yomi

  - id: ha-michael-live-token
    title: michael-ha long-lived access token (LEAKED 2026-09-21, devin-bank transcript)
    kind: ha-token
    sensitivity: high
    issuer:
      name: michael-ha Profile > Security > Long-lived tokens

    kind: ha-token
```

# Sub-Agent Focus Triage

Read-only subagent prompt for classifying ambiguous focus intake requests

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.subagent-focus-triage.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Sub-Agent Focus Triage
subtitle: Read-only subagent prompt for classifying ambiguous focus intake requests
icon: agent
profile: subagent_explore
version: 1

purpose:
  - When a request is ambiguous or does not clearly match an active focus, quick win, or backlog item, dispatch a subagent with this prompt to classify the request.
  - The subagent does not modify files; it returns a JSON triage recommendation.

inputs:
  request: the raw user request
  ssot_files:
    - docs/ssot/ssot.focus.current.yml
    - docs/ssot/ssot.focus.yml
    - docs/ssot/focus-inbox/*.yml

task: |
  You are a read-only focus triage subagent. Your job is to classify the user's request and recommend the exact intake action.

  Steps:
  1. Read docs/ssot/ssot.focus.current.yml and inspect:
     - Active Shared Focus and Active Branch Focus labels, subtasks, and ownership/lock fields
     - Ready (Safe) section and any already-queued safe foci
     - Quick Wins
     - decision_tree cases and quick_win_criteria
  2. Read docs/ssot/ssot.focus.yml for:
     - Backlog - Triage Queue items, priorities, and safe_to_parallel values
     - Focus History patterns
  3. Read docs/ssot/focus-inbox/*.yml for any pending draft items.
  4. Compare the user's request against the decision_tree cases.
  5. Return ONLY a JSON object with these fields:
     - action: one of [active, safe, quick_win, backlog, inbox, decompose]
     - target: the active focus, safe focus, quick-win label, or null
     - safe_to_parallel: boolean, required when action is safe or backlog; optional otherwise
     - reason: one sentence explaining the choice
     - confidence: one of [high, medium, low]

  Use `decompose` when the request is too large for a quick win but can be split into subtasks; identify the subtasks in the reason.
  Use `safe` when the request can run in parallel with the active focus (different branch, low complication, no missing_info, no approval required).

  Do NOT modify any files. Do NOT create or merge pull requests. Do NOT commit. This is triage only.

outputs:
  format: json
  schema:
    action:
      type: string
      enum: [active, safe, quick_win, backlog, inbox, decompose]
    target:
      type: [string, "null"]
    safe_to_parallel:
      type: boolean
    reason:
      type: string
    confidence:
      type: string
      enum: [high, medium, low]

usage:
  - When the main assistant receives an ambiguous request and the decision_tree case is unclear.
  - When mcp_focus or focus-dispatcher --intake returns low confidence or a tie.
  - When the user wants a second opinion before activating or committing to a new focus.

examples:
  - request: "I have this idea but I am not sure where it belongs"
    output:
      action: inbox
      target: null
      reason: The request is vague and needs missing_info before classification.
      confidence: high
  - request: "Can we improve the dispatcher logging?"
    output:
      action: backlog
      target: null
      safe_to_parallel: true
      reason: The request is a multi-step improvement to an existing system component.
      confidence: medium
  - request: "Can you run a quick py_compile check on mcp_debug?"
    output:
      action: safe
      target: null
      safe_to_parallel: true
      reason: The request is a read-only validation that can run in parallel on a different branch.
      confidence: high

```

# Task Completion Workflow

Standard steps to close out a task and keep SSOT, config, health, and monitoring in sync

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.task-completion.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Task Completion Workflow
subtitle: Standard steps to close out a task and keep SSOT, config, health, and monitoring in sync
icon: clipboard-check
version: 1

purpose: |
  When a task or job finishes, update the canonical records and verify the
  system is healthy before moving on. This file is the checklist and
  reference for that hand-off.

scope:
  - Any focus, inbox item, job, or ad-hoc task that changes code, config,
    deployment, or infrastructure in the chaba ecosystem.
  - Applies across chaba, chaba-h3, and tony-dell deploy worktrees.

triggers:
  - User explicitly says the task is done.
  - Focus-dispatcher detects an active focus with all subtasks completed.
  - A sub-agent reports completion and the user or dispatcher confirms it.

phases:
  - id: ssot
    name: SSOT update
    order: 1
    must: true
    steps:
      - label: Log session
        action: Append an entry to docs/ssot/ssot.focus.sessions.yml
        fields:
          - date
          - session
          - focus
          - source
          - plan
          - done
          - follow_up
          - next_action
          - decisions
          - kb_items
      - label: Update focus status
        action: |
          Move the inbox file to docs/ssot/focus-inbox/processed/ or archive
          the completed focus in docs/ssot/ssot.focus.yml history.
      - label: Capture improvements
        action: |
          If the work revealed a follow-up improvement, add it to
          docs/ssot/ssot.improvements.yml or run scripts/improvements-triage.py.
      - label: Update SSOT index
        action: Register any new canonical SSOT files in docs/ssot/ssot.index.yml.
      - label: Validate
        action: node scripts/ssot-validate-all.mjs

  - id: config
    name: Configuration sync
    order: 2
    must: false
    when: The task changes any runtime config
    steps:
      - label: Caddy
        action: Update stacks/web/Caddyfile or chaba-tony-dell/stacks/web/Caddyfile and reload caddy.
      - label: Docker / Podman Quadlet
        action: |
          Update .container, .build, docker-compose.yml, or build.sh files and
          run systemctl --user daemon-reload where units are affected.
      - label: Environment
        action: |
          Update .env, environment variables, or secrets and note the change in
          ssot.values.yml or ssot.health.yml.
      - label: chaba-h3 proxy
        action: Update proxy-server.mjs or public/apps/apps.yml if the app slug or API changed.

  - id: health
    name: Health check
    order: 3
    must: true
    steps:
      - label: SSOT validation
        action: node scripts/ssot-validate-all.mjs
      - label: Syntax / build checks
        action: node --check changed .mjs files; npm run check:ssot if available.
      - label: Service health endpoints
        action: curl -s http(s)://<host>/<service>/health
      - label: mcp-health snapshot
        action: Run a targeted mcp-health check for the affected host and service.

  - id: monitoring
    name: Monitoring and logging
    order: 4
    must: false
    when: The task touches a service or host
    steps:
      - label: systemd status
        action: systemctl --user status <service>
      - label: Logs
        action: journalctl --user -u <service> -n 50
      - label: Metrics
        action: Verify the service appears in the next overnight-assessment report.
      - label: Alerts
        action: Check ssot.improvements.yml for any new high-priority auto-generated items.

exit_criteria:
  - All changed SSOT files validate.
  - The repo worktree is clean or the remaining changes are intentionally uncommitted.
  - Health endpoint for the changed service returns ok.
  - A session entry exists unless the task was trivial and already captured.

tools:
  - scripts/ssot-validate-all.mjs
  - scripts/ssot-optimize.mjs
  - scripts/improvements-triage.py
  - scripts/mcp-health/run-check.mjs
  - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.health.yml

related_files:
  - docs/ssot/ssot.focus.sessions.yml
  - docs/ssot/ssot.focus.yml
  - docs/ssot/ssot.improvements.yml
  - docs/ssot/ssot.index.yml
  - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.health.yml
  - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.automation.yml
  - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.night-jobs.yml
  - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.operations.yml

```

# Tony-Dell / Tony-Omen Failover Plan

Manual host-level failover for the headless-primary / interactive-primary pair

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.tony-dell-failover.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Tony-Dell / Tony-Omen Failover Plan
subtitle: Manual host-level failover for the headless-primary / interactive-primary pair
version: 1

host_roles:
  tony_omen:
    name: tony-omen
    tailnet: tony-omen
    tailscale_ip: 100.75.102.88
    role: interactive primary and GPU host
    cannot_failover_to: |
      GPU, display, and interactive Devin sessions cannot move to tony-dell or macbook.
      If tony-omen is down, use MacBook for light interactive work and rely on tony-dell
      for persistent services.
    services_primary:
      - llama-router
      - ollama
      - imagen2
      - playlive
      - playlived
      - gpu-queue
      - barrier-server
      - caddy web (tony-dell:8080)
      - bserver
      - mcp-gpu
      - mcp-llama
      - mcp-debug-cors (port 9100)
      - mcp-debug-audit (port 9100)
    services_backup:
      - yomi-api (see ssot.yomi-failover.yml)
      - postgres (see ssot.yomi-failover.yml)

  tony_dell:
    name: tony-dell
    tailnet: tony-dell
    tailscale_ip: 100.68.142.13
    role: headless primary and persistent service host
    cannot_failover_to: |
      Podman rootless containers and systemd --user units cannot move to tony-omen without
      equivalent local units. Some services (weaviate, redis, raceman, postgres, yomi)
      already run on both hosts but are active on tony-dell.
    services_primary:
      - mcp-debug-sse (127.0.0.1:9101, Tailscale Serve 8446)
      - mcp-health execution (mcp-health-ssh wrapper target)
      - mcp-focus execution (mcp-focus-ssh wrapper target)
      - yomi-api
      - postgres
      - redis
      - weaviate
      - raceman
      - home-assistant
      - helm
      - ha-live (Tailscale Serve 8444)
      - mcp-rview
      - mcp-rview-oauth-proxy
      - gpu-queue (tony-dell:3001)
    services_backup:
      - mcp-debug local stdio on tony-omen (mcp-debug.sh)

  mn01:
    name: mn01
    tailnet: mn01
    tailscale_ip: 100.106.196.22
    role: portable home assistant
    cannot_failover_to: |
      Ada HA is stateless; it can be recreated on tony-dell or tony-omen using the chaba/stacks/mn01 templates and the backed-up secrets.
    services_primary:
      - caddy-mn01.service
      - ada-ha-tony.service
      - ada-ha-michael.service
    services_backup:
      - chaba/stacks/mn01/install.sh on tony-dell
      - chaba/scripts/recover-mn01.sh

failover_scenarios:
  - name: tony-omen down, tony-dell up
    trigger: tony-omen is unreachable or needs maintenance; Devin Desktop is unavailable
    user_impact: |
      Interactive/GPU work stops. Persistent services on tony-dell continue.
      Use MacBook or another tailnet host for SSH and web access.
    steps: |
      1. Confirm tony-dell is healthy: ssh tony-dell tailscale status
      2. Access Home Assistant Live bridge (Gemini Live) via tony-dell Tailscale Funnel: https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net:8444
      3. Access Yomi API directly: curl -s http://tony-dell:3000/api/yomi/health
      4. PostgreSQL remains available on tony-dell: postgresql://tony-dell:5432
      5. Wait for tony-omen to recover before resuming interactive/GPU work.

  - name: tony-dell down, tony-omen up
    trigger: tony-dell is unreachable or the persistent services fail
    user_impact: |
      mcp-debug, mcp-health, and mcp-focus over SSH stop. Devin Desktop on tony-omen
      can still run. Yomi/Postgres can be failed back to tony-omen per ssot.yomi-failover.yml.
    steps: |
      1. Confirm tony-omen is healthy: ssh tony-omen tailscale status
      2. Switch mcp-debug to the local stdio wrapper:
         - Edit docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.mcp.yml mcp-debug implementation to bash /home/tony/.config/devin/mcp-scripts/mcp-debug.sh
         - Regenerate configs: python3 scripts/generate-mcp-config.py --profile home
         - Restart Devin Desktop
      3. Run mcp-health and mcp-focus locally if needed:
         - Edit ssot.mcp.yml mcp-health and mcp-focus implementation to local paths
         - Regenerate and restart
      4. For Yomi/Postgres, follow docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.yomi-failover.yml
      5. After tony-dell recovers, revert ssot.mcp.yml to the SSH wrappers, regenerate, and restart

  - name: both hosts down
    trigger: power outage, network loss, or maintenance
    user_impact: Full home stack unavailable
    steps: |
      1. Use MacBook or mobile network to reach any host that comes back first
      2. Start tony-dell first for persistent services, then tony-omen for interactive work
      3. Verify Tailscale: tailscale status on the recovered host

  - name: mn01 down, tony-dell up
    trigger: mn01 is unreachable or the Ada HA services fail
    user_impact: Ada HA Tony and Michael PWAs are unavailable until recreated on tony-dell
    steps: |
      1. Confirm tony-dell is healthy: ssh tony-dell tailscale status
      2. Run the recovery script: bash /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba/scripts/recover-mn01.sh tony-dell
      3. The script clones/copies the Ada Pi repo, restores ~/.config/secrets/ada-ha-*.env from backup, installs the systemd units, and updates Caddyfile.tony-dell.
      4. Public URLs will shift back to https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net/apps/ada_ha_{tony,michael}/ until mn01 recovers.
      5. After mn01 recovers, re-run chaba/stacks/mn01/install.sh on mn01 and stop the temporary tony-dell units.

mcp_client_switch:
  description: |
    The canonical MCP config is generated from ssot.mcp.yml. To move the three
    low-latency MCP servers off or back onto tony-dell, edit the implementation
    field and regenerate.
  devin_config: /home/tony/.config/devin/mcp_config.json
  windsurf_config: /home/tony/.config/windsurf/mcp_config.json
  wrapper_dir: /home/tony/.config/devin/mcp-scripts
  tony_dell_wrappers:
    - mcp-debug-ssh.sh
    - mcp-health-ssh.sh
    - mcp-focus-ssh.sh
  tony_omen_wrappers:
    - mcp-debug.sh

health_checks:
  - name: tony-dell reachability
    command: ping -c 2 tony-dell
    expect: 2 received
  - name: tony-dell gpu queue
    command: curl -s http://tony-dell:3001/health
    expect: ok=true
  - name: tony-dell mcp-debug-sse
    command: ssh tony-dell systemctl --user status mcp-debug-sse
    expect: active (running)
  - name: tony-omen reachability
    command: ping -c 2 tony-omen
    expect: 2 received
  - name: tony-dell Caddy
    command: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net/api/status
    expect: "200"

notes:
  - Always use tailnet hostnames (tony-omen, tony-dell) or Tailscale IPs in failover commands. .local can fail across interfaces.
  - The mcp-health server runs over SSH on tony-dell; if tony-dell is down, mcp-health tool calls will fail until local execution is configured.
  - Failover is intentionally manual for DNS/Caddy/MCP client changes to avoid split-brain.
  - See also docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.yomi-failover.yml for Yomi/PostgreSQL-specific steps.

```

# Tony-Dell 24/7 Monitoring & Recovery

Run tony-dell as a persistent, independent monitor for the Chaba home infrastructure

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.tony-dell-monitoring.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Tony-Dell 24/7 Monitoring & Recovery
subtitle: Run tony-dell as a persistent, independent monitor for the Chaba home infrastructure
icon: 🛰️

ideas:
  - tony-dell is always on and has a stable Tailscale identity; use it as a second vantage point
  - Monitor both tony-dell local health and tony-omen critical services over the tailnet
  - Record health snapshots and a monitor log on tony-dell so failures can be correlated
  - Start in observe-only mode; enable safe auto-recovery after the baseline is trusted
  - Keep recovery actions narrow and well-audited; never restart critical DBs or the Caddy host blindly

sections:
  - title: Current Baseline
    icon: 📍
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: tony-dell snapshot
        text: health-snapshot.sh runs every 5 minutes and writes /home/tony/var/chaba/health/tony-dell-snapshot.json
      - label: mcp-debug host
        text: tony_dell is reachable over ssh tony@tony-dell (Tailnet)
      - label: mcp-health
        text: central mcp-health server runs on tony-omen; tony-dell now queries it via SSH and stores the score at tony-dell-mcp-health.json

  - title: Target State
    icon: 🎯
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Persistent monitor agent
        text: tony-dell runs tony-dell-monitor.sh as a systemd user timer every 2 minutes
      - label: mcp-health schedule group
        text: tony-dell-mcp-health.sh runs every 5 minutes; queries mcp-health critical-only services and caches the score
      - label: Cross-host checks
        text: polls tony-omen HTTP endpoints (caddy, yomi-api, mddb-api, status-api, gpu-queue, playlived, llama-server) and tony-dell local services (barrier-client, Funnel port 8082)
      - label: Recovery policy
        text: observe-only for 1 week, then allow safe restarts (barrierc, playlived, yomi timers, caddy only after confirmation)
      - label: Notifications
        text: failures and recoveries are appended to /home/tony/var/chaba/health/tony-dell-monitor.log; optional yomi/api push
      - label: Log retention
        text: keep 7 days of monitor log, rotate with tail -n 10000

  - title: Services to Monitor
    icon: 🩺
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: tony-omen web
        text: https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net/, http://tony-dell:3000/api/yomi/health, https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net/api/health
      - label: tony-omen AI/data
        text: http://tony-omen:11023/health (MDDB), http://tony-omen:8008/health (llama), http://tony-omen:8000/health (imagen2)
      - label: tony-omen GPU queue
        text: http://tony-omen:3001/health
      - label: tony-omen playlive
        text: http://tony-omen:9230/sessions
      - label: tony-dell local
        text: barrier-client process, Funnel port 8082; disk and memory are already covered by health-snapshot.sh

  - title: Phased Plan
    icon: 🗓️
    layout: timeline
    items:
      - label: Phase 1 — Deploy observe-only monitor
        text: Create scripts/tony-dell-monitor.sh, systemd user timer, run every 2 minutes, log only
        status: completed
      - label: Phase 2 — Add mcp-health integration
        text: Have tony-dell periodically query mcp-health critical services and store the result; do not run the full mcp-health server yet
        status: completed
      - label: Phase 3 — Safe auto-recovery
        text: Enable restart commands for services with a known-good restart path and require two consecutive failures
        status: in_progress
      - label: Phase 4 — Alerting & correlation
        text: Send notifications to yomi/api and add tony-dell monitor log to mcp-debug snapshots
        status: pending

  - title: Recovery Policy
    icon: 🚑
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Allowed manual/semi-auto restarts
        text: barrierc, playlived, yomi-update timers, caddy only after operator confirmation, llama-server only if GPU queue is idle
      - label: Never auto-restart
        text: postgres, weaviate, redis, mddb container, caddy (unless an explicit human confirms)
      - label: Escalation
        text: after 3 failed recovery attempts, stop auto-retry and send critical alert

  - title: Recovery Commands
    icon: 🛠
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: barrier-client
        text: Restart the Barrier KVM client on tony-dell. Safe because it is non-critical and reconnects automatically.
        host: tony_dell
        trigger: 2 consecutive failures of the barrier-client process check
        precheck: pgrep -a barrierc || echo missing
        command: pkill -x barrierc 2>/dev/null; nohup /home/tony/.local/bin/barrierc --no-daemon --disable-crypto --name tony-dell --log /tmp/barrier-client.log tony-omen >/dev/null 2>&1 &
        verify: pgrep -a barrierc

      - label: playlived
        text: Restart the PlayLive daemon on tony-dell. Safe because it is stateless and re-scans sessions on start.
        host: tony_dell
        trigger: 2 consecutive failures of http://tony-dell:9230/sessions
        precheck: systemctl --user is-active playlived.service
        command: systemctl --user restart playlived.service
        verify: curl -s http://tony-dell:9230/sessions

      - label: yomi-update-timers
        text: Reset the Yomi fetch/update timers on tony-dell. Safe when yomi-api itself is healthy but the timers have failed.
        host: tony_dell
        trigger: 2 consecutive failures of the yomi-update-active or yomi-update-all timer unit
        precheck: systemctl --user is-active yomi-update-active.timer yomi-update-all.timer
        command: systemctl --user restart yomi-update-active.timer yomi-update-all.timer
        verify: systemctl --user is-active yomi-update-active.timer yomi-update-all.timer

      - label: llama-server
        text: Restart the Llama router on tony-omen only when the GPU queue is idle and tony-dell is not actively routing.
        host: tony_omen
        trigger: 3 consecutive failures of http://tony-omen:8008/health with GPU queue idle
        precheck: curl -s http://tony-omen:3001/health | grep -q idle
        command: systemctl --user restart thai-legal-inference.service
        verify: curl -s http://tony-omen:8008/health

      - label: caddy
        text: Reload Caddy on tony-omen. Requires operator confirmation because it affects all web endpoints.
        host: tony_omen
        trigger: Caddy returns 5xx or is unresponsive on 3 consecutive checks
        confirmation: true
        precheck: systemctl --user is-active caddy.service
        command: systemctl --user reload caddy.service
        verify: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net/

      - label: ha-live
        text: Restart the tony-dell Home Assistant Live bridge (Gemini Live).
        host: tony_dell
        trigger: 2 consecutive failures of https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net:8444/
        precheck: systemctl --user is-active tony-ha.service
        command: systemctl --user restart tony-ha.service
        verify: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net:8444/

  - title: Files & Paths
    icon: 📁
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Monitor script
        text: /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/scripts/tony-dell-monitor.sh (source); deployed to /home/tony/.local/bin/tony-dell-monitor.sh
      - label: systemd user units
        text: /home/tony/.config/systemd/user/tony-dell-monitor.service and tony-dell-monitor.timer
      - label: mcp-health query script
        text: /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/scripts/tony-dell-mcp-health.sh (source); deployed to /home/tony/.local/bin/tony-dell-mcp-health.sh
      - label: mcp-health systemd user units
        text: /home/tony/.config/systemd/user/tony-dell-mcp-health.service and tony-dell-mcp-health.timer
      - label: Monitor log
        text: /home/tony/var/chaba/health/tony-dell-monitor.log
      - label: mcp-health score cache
        text: /home/tony/var/chaba/health/tony-dell-mcp-health.json
      - label: mcp-health client
        text: /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/scripts/mcp-health-client.py (runs on tony-omen, invoked by tony-dell over SSH)
      - label: Snapshot
        text: /home/tony/var/chaba/health/tony-dell-snapshot.json (already deployed)

  - title: Verification
    icon: 🧪
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Timer status
        text: systemctl --user list-timers --all
        tags: [mcp-debug]
      - label: Latest log
        text: tail -n 50 /home/tony/var/chaba/health/tony-dell-monitor.log
        tags: [mcp-debug]
      - label: Cross-host endpoint
        text: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net/health
        tags: [mcp-debug]

config:

  created: 2026-08-15
  maintainer: tony
  status: draft
```

# Tony-Dell Multi-WAN Active-Backup

Wired ADSL primary with Naris Wi-Fi ADSL backup on tony-dell

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.tony-dell-multi-wan.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Tony-Dell Multi-WAN Active-Backup
subtitle: Wired ADSL primary with Naris Wi-Fi ADSL backup on tony-dell
icon: network

ideas:
  - Use the wired connection on tony-dell as the primary default route with a low metric.
  - Keep the iPhone Personal Hotspot (TONY-IP) Wi-Fi connection active with a high metric as a hot backup.
  - Monitor internet reachability through the wired device and switch the default route to Wi-Fi after repeated failures.
  - Restore the wired default route automatically when the wired internet comes back.
  - Run the check as a root systemd service triggered by a timer so the switch is reliable and auditable.

sections:
  - title: Active Connections
    icon: map
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Wired primary
        text: Connection "Wired connection 1" on enp0s31f6, gateway 192.168.2.1, DHCP source 192.168.2.67/24, default route metric 100.
      - label: iPhone Wi-Fi backup
        text: Connection "TONY-IP" on wlx00761100125e, gateway <IPHONE_USB_GATEWAY>, DHCP source <IPHONE_USB_DHCP_ADDRESS>/28, default route metric 600.

  - title: Failover Mechanism
    icon: workflow
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Script
        text: scripts/tony-dell-wan-failover.sh runs as root and pings 8.8.8.8 through the wired device. After 3 consecutive failures it rewrites the default routes so the TONY-IP Wi-Fi connection becomes metric 100 and wired becomes metric 2000.
      - label: Restoration
        text: When the wired ping succeeds again the script restores wired as metric 100 and demotes TONY-IP back to metric 2000.
      - label: Scheduler
        text: systemd unit /etc/systemd/system/tony-dell-wan-failover.service is triggered by /etc/systemd/system/tony-dell-wan-failover.timer.

  - title: Verification
    icon: check
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Wired disabled
```

# Tony-Omen Multi-WAN ECMP

Use wired Ethernet (eno1) as primary, 5 GHz Wi-Fi (wlo1) as hot backup, and iPhone USB tether (enx) as fallback

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.tony-omen-multi-wan.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Tony-Omen Multi-WAN ECMP
subtitle: Use wired Ethernet (eno1) as primary, 5 GHz Wi-Fi (wlo1) as hot backup, and iPhone USB tether (enx) as fallback
icon: network

ideas:
  - Make eno1 (wired Ethernet) the primary default route on tony-omen.
  - Use wlo1 (5 GHz home Wi-Fi) as a hot-backup path when eno1 is down.
  - Use the iPhone USB tether (enx7ed2da73308a) only as a fallback, with a much higher route metric.
  - Use an iOS Shortcut to turn on the iPhone Personal Hotspot automatically when tony-omen connects.
  - Keep the NetworkManager dispatcher that rebuilds default routes whenever eno1, wlo1, or enx changes state.

sections:
  - title: Active Connections
    icon: map
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: eno1 wired primary
        text: Connection "netplan-eno1" on eno1, Realtek RTL8111/8168/8211/8411, r8169 driver, auto-negotiation on, link 1000 Mb/s Full, gateway 192.168.2.1, DHCP source 192.168.2.84/24.
      - label: enx iPhone USB tether primary
        text: Connection "Wired connection 1" on enx7ed2da73308a, auto-negotiate no (USB Ethernet), gateway <IPHONE_USB_GATEWAY>, DHCP source <IPHONE_USB_DHCP_ADDRESS>/28.
      - label: wlo1 5 GHz Wi-Fi fallback
        text: Connection "TONY-WIFI_5G" on wlo1, Intel Wireless-AC 7265, iwlwifi driver, 866.7 Mb/s link, gateway 192.168.2.1, DHCP source 192.168.2.83/24.

  - title: Fallback Policy
    icon: workflow
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: eno1 primary
        text: default via 192.168.2.1 dev eno1 metric 10.
      - label: wlo1 hot backup
        text: default via 192.168.2.1 dev wlo1 metric 20.
      - label: enx iPhone USB fallback
        text: default via <IPHONE_USB_GATEWAY> dev enx7ed2da73308a metric 100; only used when wlo1 and eno1 are down.
      - label: Hash policy
        text: net.ipv4.fib_multipath_hash_policy=1 remains enabled for any equal-cost paths that may exist.

  - title: Implementation Files
    icon: files
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: ECMP rebuild script
        text: /usr/local/bin/ecmp-up rebuilds the default route from the active interfaces.
      - label: NetworkManager dispatcher
        text: /etc/NetworkManager/dispatcher.d/99-enx-ecmp calls /usr/local/bin/ecmp-up on up/down/dhcp4-change/dhcp6-change.
      - label: Sysctl tuning
        text: /etc/sysctl.d/99-multipath.conf sets net.ipv4.fib_multipath_hash_policy=1.

  - title: Verification
    icon: check
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Primary/secondary/fallback routes present
        text: ip -4 -o route show default reports eno1 metric 10, wlo1 metric 20, and enx metric 100.
      - label: iPhone fallback works
        text: With wlo1 and eno1 disconnected, traffic flows through enx and the iPhone hotspot.

  - title: iOS Hotspot Trigger
    icon: phone
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Pairing
        text: iPhone is paired with tony-omen Bluetooth controller (D0:57:7B:EA:6A:40, device name TONY-IP, MAC 7C:D2:DA:73:68:3B) and trusted.
      - label: iOS Shortcut
        text: Shortcuts automation triggers on Bluetooth connect to tony-omen. Primary action is "Set Personal Hotspot" → On. If that action is unavailable on a specific iOS build, fall back to "Open URL" with "prefs:root=INTERNET_TETHERING" and toggle manually.
      - label: How to use
        text: On the iPhone, Settings → Bluetooth, tap tony-omen to reconnect. The iOS Shortcut turns Personal Hotspot On automatically. tony-omen then uses TONY-IP Wi-Fi or enx USB as the metric-100 fallback.
      - label: Manual command
        text: On tony-omen, "bluetoothctl connect 7C:D2:DA:73:68:3B" can also force the Bluetooth connection and trigger the shortcut.

  - title: Notes
    icon: note
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Single stream limit
        text: One TCP flow still uses one path; parallel connections or a multi-threaded download manager (aria2, etc.) is needed to combine the links.
      - label: Driver
        text: eno1 uses the kernel r8169 driver and reaches 1 Gbps; no need for r8168-dkms.
      - label: enx variability
        text: iPhone tether throughput depends on iPhone Wi-Fi/cellular state; typical observed per-stream 5-32 MB/s.
      - label: Source IP changes
        text: New outbound connections may use either 192.168.2.x or <IPHONE_USB_DHCP_ADDRESS>; applications sensitive to source IP may see occasional re-authentication.
      - label: Same-subnet ARP self-conflict
        text: 'With eno1 and wlo1 on the same 192.168.2.0/24 subnet, NM''s post-activation ACD probe for the new DHCP address leaves one NIC, loops through the router, and is answered by the other NIC (arp_ignore=0 default) — NM logs "conflict detected ... with host <own other NIC MAC>" and strips the interface''s routes. Fixed 2026-09-17: net.ipv4.conf.all.arp_ignore=1 + arp_announce=2 persisted in /etc/sysctl.d/99-multipath.conf. ecmp-up sleep raised 0.5s→2s because NM installs routes ~0.55s after the up event and the rebuild was missing them.'
      - label: NIC tuning 2026-09-17
        text: "eno1 promoted to primary (metric 10) and wlo1 demoted to hot backup (metric 20) on 2026-09-17 — wired latency ~0.5ms vs ~2ms on wifi with identical ~340-390 Mbit/s throughput through the router. TONY-WIFI_5G autoconnect-priority raised to 20 so wlo1 prefers 5 GHz (was stuck on 2.4G/144Mb, now 866Mb VHT). eno1 IRQ coalescing rx-usecs=50 rx-frames=16 applied and re-applied by ecmp-up (r8169 has no adaptive mode). eno1 PCI runtime PM set to auto; EEE already active. Wi-Fi powersave intentionally OFF (conflicting conf.d files exist: default-wifi-powersave-on.conf=3 vs wifi-powersave-off.conf=2, the latter wins) — keeps latency steady for Deskreen/Chrome-debug; enable only if battery/heat matters. eno1 PCIe ASPM is Disabled at LnkCtl — pcie_aspm.policy=powersave added to GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT on 2026-09-17 (takes effect next reboot; revert if eno1 link flaps)."
      - label: Router DHCP reservations
        text: 'Router is a ZTE F688 ONT at 192.168.2.1 (NOT the ASUS — ASUS_ROUTER_* creds in ~/.config/secrets/asus-router.env happen to work on it). Added DHCP bindings "tonyomen"=192.168.2.86/b0:22:7a:f0:73:cd and "omenwlan"=192.168.2.84/d0:57:7b:ea:6a:3c on 2026-09-17, replacing stale "esp32test" (device moved to 192.168.31.x) and "hpdeskjet" (user-approved). Quirks: binding table caps at 10 entries; POSTs need a per-page _sessionTmpToken + RSA-signed "Check" header (sha256 of body, PKCS1v15, pubkey embedded in the login page JS); new binding names must not share a prefix with an existing name (tonyomenwifi was rejected -257, omenwlan accepted).'

```

# Web Stack Standard Ports Migration Appendix

Detailed pre-flight, process, fix, and re-verify/re-fix steps for the 80/443 migration and GEV integration

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.web.standard-ports.appendix.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Web Stack Standard Ports Migration Appendix
subtitle: Detailed pre-flight, process, fix, and re-verify/re-fix steps for the 80/443
  migration and GEV integration
icon: 📎
sections:
- title: Pre-flight
  icon: 🔍
  layout: list
  items:
  - label: 1.1 Inventory the current web stack
    text: "Record the current state of the tony-dell web stack before any changes.\n\
      - Caddy container: web (caddy:latest)\n- Caddyfile: /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/stacks/web/Caddyfile\n\
      - Compose: /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/stacks/web/docker-compose.yml\n\
      - Public root: /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/stacks/web/public\n\
      - Current endpoints:\n  - http://tony-dell:8080/ (Caddy dashboard + apps)\n\
      \  - http://tony-dell:8081/ (chaba-h3 dev)\n  - https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net:8444/\
      \ (Tailscale Funnel → ha-live)\n- Reverse-proxied apps and their upstream ports\
      \ (rview 3007, yomi 3000, trade 9002, etc.)\n"
  - label: 1.2 Confirm port 80/443 are free
    text: "Run on tony-dell:\n  ss -tlnp | grep -E ':80|:443'\n  sudo ss -tlnp | grep\
      \ -E ':80|:443'\nExpected: no listeners. If systemd, docker, or another Caddy\
      \ is bound, stop or reassign it first.\n"
  - label: 1.3 Back up all mutable files
    text: "Copy the current working config to a rollback directory:\n  mkdir -p /home/tony/backups/web-ports-$(date\
      \ +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)\n  cp stacks/web/Caddyfile \"$_/\"\n  cp stacks/web/docker-compose.yml\
      \ \"$_/\"\n  cp stacks/web/public/apps/apps.yml \"$_/\"\n  cp docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.health.home.web.yml\
      \ \"$_/\"\n  cp docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.values.yml \"$_/\"\nCommit the\
      \ repo before the change so you can `git checkout --` the files if needed.\n"
  - label: 1.4 Build God’s Eye View for the /apps/gev base path
    text: "The Vite dev server cannot be reverse-proxied under a sub-path without\
      \ asset 404s.\nBuild the app with the correct base:\n  cd /home/tony/gods-eye-view\n\
      \  npx vite build --base /apps/gev/\n`vite-plugin-cesium` copies the Cesium\
      \ assets under `dist/apps/gev/cesium/` because of the base path. Caddy strips\
      \ `/apps/gev/` when serving the app, so the real Cesium directory must be `dist/cesium/`:\n\
      \  mv dist/apps/gev/cesium dist/cesium\n  rmdir dist/apps/gev 2>/dev/null; rmdir\
      \ dist/apps 2>/dev/null || true\nIf the build succeeds, the dist/ folder will\
      \ contain an index.html that references\n/apps/gev/assets/... and /apps/gev/style.css.\n\
      If the static /style.css or /logo.svg references are still absolute, open dist/index.html\n\
      and change `href=\"/style.css\"` to `href=\"style.css\"` and `src=\"/logo.svg\"\
      ` to `src=\"logo.svg\"`\nso they resolve relative to /apps/gev/.\n"
  - label: 1.5 Stage the built app into the Caddy public tree
    text: "Copy the build output to the web stack:\n  mkdir -p /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/stacks/web/public/apps/gev\n\
      \  cp -r /home/tony/gods-eye-view/dist/* /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/stacks/web/public/apps/gev/\n\
      Verify a file list:\n  ls /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/stacks/web/public/apps/gev/\n"
  - label: 1.6 Verify the Caddy container can bind privileged ports
    text: "The `web` container currently runs as the Caddy image default user. Check:\n\
      \  podman exec web caddy list-modules\n  podman exec web whoami\nIf `whoami`\
      \ is `caddy` (non-root), add `user: root` or `cap_add: [NET_BIND_SERVICE]` in\n\
      docker-compose.yml, then `podman compose down && podman compose up -d` to pick\
      \ it up.\n"
  - label: 1.7 Prepare Tailscale for 443
    text: "If the public funnel currently points 8444 to local 8444/9005, decide whether\
      \ to:\n  a) move the funnel to local 443 and route through Caddy, or\n  b) keep\
      \ ha-live on 8444 and add a second funnel for 443.\nRecord the current funnel\
      \ state:\n  tailscale serve status\n"
- title: Process
  icon: ⚙️
  layout: list
  items:
  - label: 2.1 Update Caddyfile for 80/443
    text: "Replace the `http://127.0.0.1:8080` block with:\n  {\n    auto_https off\n\
      \  }\n  :80 {\n    bind 0.0.0.0\n    root * /srv/public\n    ...existing routes...\n\
      \  }\nFor 443, either:\n  a) Use Tailscale TLS: keep `auto_https off` and terminate\
      \ TLS with Tailscale Funnel, or\n  b) Enable `auto_https on` and use Tailscale-provided\
      \ certs.\nAdd the `handle /apps/gev/` route:\n  handle /apps/gev {\n    redir\
      \ /apps/gev/ 308\n  }\n  handle_path /apps/gev/* {\n    root * /srv/public/apps/gev\n\
      \    file_server\n  }\n"
  - label: 2.2 Update docker-compose.yml port bindings
    text: "Change:\n  ports:\n    - 127.0.0.1:8080:8080\n    - 127.0.0.1:8081:8081\n\
      to:\n  ports:\n    - 80:80\n    - 443:443\n    - 8081:8081   # keep chaba-h3\
      \ until migrated\nIf running rootless Podman with `podman compose`, the host\
      \ ports 80/443 may still require\nroot or `net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=0`.\n"
  - label: 2.3 Update apps.yml
    text: "Edit /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/stacks/web/public/apps/apps.yml:\n\
      \  - id: gods-eye-view\n    title: God’s Eye View\n    description: Real-time\
      \ 3D geospatial intelligence console\n    icon: \U0001F30D\n    href: /apps/gev/\n\
      Also update any existing `href: http://tony-dell:8080/...` links to remove `:8080`.\n"
  - label: 2.4 Update public index.html network options
    text: 'Edit /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/stacks/web/public/apps/index.html:

      - Change `http://tony-dell.local:8080/apps` → `http://tony-dell.local/apps`

      - Change `http://tony-dell:8080/apps` → `http://tony-dell/apps`

      - Change `https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net:8444/` → `https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net/`

      '
  - label: 2.5 Update SSOT health checks and values
    text: '- docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.health.home.web.yml: change `:8080` URLs
      to port 80/443.

      - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.values.yml: update any `public_web_url` or `landing_url`
      values.

      '
  - label: 2.6 Rebuild and restart the web stack
    text: 'cd /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/stacks/web

      podman compose down

      podman compose --profile production up -d

      podman ps | grep web

      '
  - label: 2.7 Update Tailscale Funnel to 443 (if desired)
    text: "If the public URL is being moved to 443:\n  sudo -n tailscale funnel --yes\
      \ --bg --https=443 127.0.0.1:80\n  sudo -n tailscale funnel --yes --bg --https=443\
      \ --set-path /apps/home-assistant/ 127.0.0.1:8123\nVerify with `tailscale funnel\
      \ status`.\n"
- title: Fix
  icon: 🔧
  layout: list
  items:
  - label: 4.1 Caddy fails to bind 80/443
    text: "Symptom: `web` container exits or logs `bind: permission denied`.\nFix:\n\
      \  - Ensure the container user is root or has `CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE`.\n  - On\
      \ the host, run `sudo sysctl net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=0` (ephemeral;\
      \ add to sysctl for persistence).\n  - Or keep 8080/8444 and add a root-level\
      \ `iptables` redirect: `sudo iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -p tcp --dport 80\
      \ -j REDIRECT --to 8080`.\n"
  - label: 4.2 God’s Eye View assets 404
    text: "Symptom: Blank page, browser console shows 404 for /style.css or /src/.../main.js.\n\
      Fix:\n  - Rebuild with the correct base path:\n      npx vite build --base /apps/gev/\n\
      \  - Inspect dist/index.html. If `href` still starts with `/` (not `/apps/gev/`),\
      \ either:\n      a) patch them manually, or\n      b) add Vite `base: '/apps/gev/'`\
      \ in vite.config.js (check the existing defineConfig).\n  - Re-copy dist/ into\
      \ /srv/public/apps/gev/ and hard-refresh the browser.\n"
  - label: 4.3 Mixed content or CORS on 443
    text: "Symptom: HTTPS page blocks an HTTP upstream (OpenSky, AIS, etc.).\nFix:\n\
      \  - The upstream API calls in God’s Eye View are proxied through its own Vite\
      \ dev server, not Caddy.\n  - Since we are serving a static build, the dev-server\
      \ proxy is gone. Either:\n      a) keep the Vite dev server on a dedicated port\
      \ and link to it (revert this runbook), or\n      b) move the API proxy logic\
      \ into Caddy (add `handle_path /api/opensky/*`, `/api/ais/*`, etc.).\n"
  - label: 4.4 Tailscale 8444 still used by ha-live
    text: "Symptom: Public https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net:8444/ stops working.\n\
      Fix:\n  - If you moved the funnel to 443, update any bookmarks/SSOT pointing\
      \ at :8444.\n  - If ha-live must stay on 8444, add a separate Caddy listener\
      \ for 8444 or keep the funnel unchanged\n    and only route 443 through Caddy.\n"
  - label: 4.5 Rollback plan
    text: "If multiple failures occur, restore quickly:\n  cd /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/stacks/web\n\
      \  cp <backup>/Caddyfile .\n  cp <backup>/docker-compose.yml .\n  cp <backup>/apps.yml\
      \ public/apps/\n  podman compose down\n  podman compose --profile production\
      \ up -d\nThen verify with `curl http://tony-dell:8080/apps/`.\n"
- title: Re-verify
  icon: 🔄
  layout: list
  items:
  - label: 5.1 Re-run the Verify checklist after any fix
    text: "Do not consider a fix complete until:\n  - `curl http://tony-dell/` returns\
      \ 200\n  - `curl https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net/` returns 200 (if 443 is\
      \ configured)\n  - `curl http://tony-dell/apps/gev/` returns 200 and HTML contains\
      \ \"God's Eye View\"\n  - `curl http://tony-dell/apps/` returns 200 and lists\
      \ God’s Eye View\n  - Browser network tab shows no 404s for /apps/gev/ assets\n\
      \  - All other sampled apps still return 200\n"
  - label: 5.2 Update health checks and SSOT
    text: "Once stable, update:\n  - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.health.home.web.yml\
      \ with the new URLs\n  - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.values.yml with the canonical\
      \ public/landing URLs\n  - Any HA dashboards or markdown that reference `tony-dell:8080`\
      \ or `tony-dell:8444`\n"
  - label: 5.3 Commit the changes
    text: "After final verification, commit the changed files:\n  git add stacks/web/Caddyfile\
      \ stacks/web/docker-compose.yml stacks/web/public/apps/apps.yml stacks/web/public/apps/index.html\
      \ docs/ssot/infrastructure/\n  git commit -m \"Web stack: move to 80/443 and\
      \ add God’s Eye View under /apps/gev\"\nPush only if requested.\n"
- title: Re-fix
  icon: 🔁
  layout: list
  items:
  - label: 6.1 Re-fix loop
    text: 'If Re-verify fails, return to the appropriate Fix step, apply it, then
      return to Re-verify.

      Do not skip Re-verify after a Re-fix. Track iterations in the runbook notes
      below.

      '
  - label: 6.2 Runbook notes
    text: "Use this section to record what actually happened during the migration:\n\
      \  iteration: 0\n  date:\n  issues_found: []\n  fixes_applied: []\n  final_status:\
      \ applied\nUpdate after each Re-fix/Re-verify cycle.\n"
config:
  version: 1
  created: '2026-09-11'
  maintainer: tony
  status: applied
  deployment: tony-dell
  related_files:
  - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.web.standard-ports.yml
  - chaba-tony-dell/docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.web.standard-ports.appendix.yml

```
