# Yomi and PostgreSQL Failover Plan

Primary/backup disposition and manual failover steps for the Yomi stack

## File Path
`infrastructure/ssot.yomi-failover.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Yomi and PostgreSQL Failover Plan
subtitle: Primary/backup disposition and manual failover steps for the Yomi stack
version: 1

primary:
  host: tony_dell
  postgres:
    container: chaba-postgres-16
    image: docker.io/pgvector/pgvector:pg16
    data_volume: /home/tony/.config/containers/postgres/data
    port: 5432
    port_mapping: 127.0.0.1:5432:5432
    port_mapping_note: 0.0.0.0:5432 conflicts with tailscale serve for 5432
    exposed_by: tailscale serve --bg --tcp 5432 127.0.0.1:5432
    dns_alias: postgre
    dns_target: 100.68.142.13
  yomi_api:
    container_runtime: podman
    image: docker.io/library/node:22-slim
    tailscale_serve: --bg --tcp 3000 127.0.0.1:3000
    caddy_upstream: tony-dell:3000
    data_volume: /home/tony/.local/share/yomi
    env:
      POSTGRES_HOST: postgre
      POSTGRES_PORT: 5432
      REDIS_URL: redis://100.68.142.13:6379
  services:
    - yomi-api.service
    - yomi-update-all.timer
    - yomi-update-active.timer
    - yomi-backup.timer

backup:
  host: tony_omen
  timer: yomi-backup.timer
  schedule: daily
  retention: one latest copy
  pg_dump:
    source: chaba database on tony-dell
    target: tony_omen:/home/tony/backups/yomi/chaba-latest.dump
  yomi_data:
    source: tony-dell:/home/tony/.local/share/yomi/
    target: tony_omen:/home/tony/backups/yomi-data/
  credentials:
    ssh_key: tony-dell to tony-omen (tony@100.75.102.88)
    rsync_options: -avz --delete

failover:
  trigger: tony-dell is unreachable or the Yomi stack fails on tony-dell
  script: tony_omen:/home/tony/.local/bin/yomi-failover-to-omen.sh
```

# Gold/THB/USD Causality Exploration

Investigate directional and temporal relationships between gold (XAU/USD), the Thai Baht (USD/THB), and the US Dollar index

## File Path
`jobs/experiments/2026-08-26-gold-thb-usd-causality.yml`

```yaml
title: Gold/THB/USD Causality Exploration
subtitle: Investigate directional and temporal relationships between gold (XAU/USD), the Thai Baht (USD/THB), and the US Dollar index
icon: target

planning:
  goal: |
    Determine whether movements in gold (XAU/USD), USD/THB, and broader USD strength
    lead, lag, or co-move with each other, and document any statistically robust
    causal links suitable for later forecasting or hedging experiments.
  scope: |
    - Collect and align daily close prices for XAU/USD and USD/THB.
    - Optionally include a USD proxy such as DXY or a trade-weighted USD basket.
    - Clean, normalize, and stationarize the series where needed.
    - Run exploratory correlation, Granger-causality, and transfer-entropy tests.
    - Produce a short report with findings and code artifacts.
  out_of_scope: |
    - Real-time trading system implementation.
    - Options, derivatives, or position sizing.
    - Live deployment to the trade-api stack.
  success_criteria:
    - Daily aligned time series spanning at least 6 months available in the repo.
    - At least one reproducible causality/lead-lag test with results and p-values.
    - A documented conclusion on whether any pair reliably leads the others.
  risks:
    - Alpha Vantage rate limits or data gaps; mitigate with MetalPrices fallback and local caching.
    - Spurious regression due to non-stationary series; mitigate with differencing and unit-root tests.
    - Correlation does not imply causation; mitigate with multiple tests and out-of-sample checks.
  resources:
    - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.mcp.yml for the alphavantage MCP endpoint.
    - docs/ssot/apps/ssot.apps.trade.yml for existing commodity/FX data conventions.
    - python3 with pandas, statsmodels, numpy, and scipy.
  owner: tony
  estimated_duration: 2 sessions

processing:
  status: in_progress
  started_at: "2026-08-26"
  steps:
    - id: 1
      label: Define hypotheses and variable set
      status: completed
      completed_at: "2026-08-26"
      notes: |
        Hypotheses: gold changes lead USD/THB; USD/THB leads gold;
        both respond contemporaneously to external USD shocks.
    - id: 2
      label: Fetch and cache daily time series
      status: completed
      completed_at: "2026-08-26"
      notes: |
        Fetched XAU/USD (5,375 rows) and USD/THB (3,076 rows) from Alpha Vantage
        and stored as CSVs under experiments/gold-thb-usd-causality/data/.
    - id: 3
      label: Clean, align, and stationarize
      status: completed
      completed_at: "2026-08-26"
      notes: |
        Inner join on common trading days gives 3,076 aligned daily observations
        from 2014-11-07 to 2026-08-25. Log levels are non-stationary (ADF p > 0.05),
        but daily log returns are stationary (ADF p ~ 0.0).
    - id: 4
      label: Exploratory analysis and visualizations
      status: completed
      completed_at: "2026-08-26"
      notes: |
        Cross-correlation of returns is strongest at lag 0 (r = -0.2205). There is
        a contemporaneous negative relationship between gold and USD/THB returns.
    - id: 5
      label: Causality and lead-lag tests
      status: completed
      completed_at: "2026-08-26"
      notes: |
        Granger causality on log returns:
        - XAU returns do NOT Granger-cause USD/THB returns (p > 0.5 for lags 1-5).
        - USD/THB returns DO Granger-cause XAU returns (p = 0.0 for lags 1-5).
    - id: 6
      label: Report and archive
      status: completed
      completed_at: "2026-08-26"
      notes: |
        Reproducible analysis verified end-to-end. Results saved to data/results.json.
        Report section of this SSOT completed and committed.
    - id: 7
      label: Add USD/EUR proxy and trivariate VAR robustness
      status: completed
      completed_at: "2026-08-26"
      notes: |
        Fetched USD/EUR (3,077 rows) as a USD-strength proxy, extended the analysis
        to a 3-variable VAR (lag 4 selected by AIC), and re-ran Granger causality.
        Adding the USD proxy slightly strengthens the finding that THB leads XAU
        and confirms USD-strength itself also Granger-causes XAU (p = 0.0149).
  decisions:
    - label: Use log returns for testing
      rationale: |
        Both log XAU/USD and log USD/THB levels are non-stationary. First-differenced
        log returns are stationary (ADF p ~ 0), which is required for valid
        Granger causality and cross-correlation inference.
    - label: Test USD/THB -> XAU direction as the leading hypothesis
      rationale: |
        FX is quoted in USD terms for both series, so a USD-strength shock is a
        plausible common driver. The data supports it strongly (p = 0.0 at all
        tested lags), while the reverse is not significant.

    - file: experiments/gold-thb-usd-causality/data/aligned.csv

  status: completed

  summary: |
    Daily log returns of XAU/USD, USD/THB, and USD/EUR from 2014-11-07 to 2026-08-25
    (3,076 aligned observations) are stationary, while the gold and THB log levels
    are non-stationary. USD/EUR log levels are marginally stationary (ADF p = 0.0189).
    No pair of log levels is cointegrated. The contemporaneous cross-correlation
    between XAU/USD and USD/THB returns is negative and strongest at lag 0
    (r = -0.2205). Bivariate Granger-causality confirms no evidence that XAU/USD
    returns lead USD/THB returns (p > 0.5 for lags 1-5), while USD/THB returns
    strongly Granger-cause XAU/USD returns (p = 0.0). A 3-variable VAR (lag 4,
    AIC-selected) with USD/EUR as a USD-strength proxy confirms both USD/THB
    (p = 0.0) and USD/EUR (p = 0.0149) Granger-cause XAU/USD returns, while
    XAU/USD does not Granger-cause USD/THB (p = 0.8862). Impulse responses show
    a one-unit THB-return shock lowers XAU/USD on the next day (-0.558) and the
    effect decays within a week.
  metrics:

  links:

  kb_review:

    - Log returns are required for valid Granger-causality inference; levels are non-stationary.

    - FX appears to lead gold in this pair, not the reverse; any predictive use should include out-of-sample validation.
```

```yaml
  goal: |
```

```yaml
  scope: |
    - Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) for elastic pattern matching of THB and XAU series.
    - Delay-embedding / Takens-style k-NN on USD/THB returns.
    - Singular Spectrum Analysis (SSA) as a time-aware signal decomposition.
    - Time-varying / Markov-switching VAR and impulse responses.

    - Real-time trading system implementation.
    - External deep-learning model training beyond scikit-learn/statsmodels.
    - Live deployment to the trade-api stack.

processing:
  status: completed

    - id: 1
      label: Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) similarity
      status: completed
      completed_at: "2026-08-26"
      notes: |
        Implemented trended_dtw.py. For each day, build a WINDOW of USD/THB log
        returns. Find the K training windows with the smallest DTW distance and
        use their future XAU returns as a weighted forecast. Out-of-sample

        - Sharpe: -0.14
        - Annual return: -1.6%
        - Annual vol: 11.4%
        - Max drawdown: -56.8%
        - Win rate: 24.6%
        The R=2 reconstruction appears to over-smooth or invert the useful signal.
        Tuning L, R, or using the oscillatory/noise components instead of the
        leading trend components may help.
    - id: 4
      label: Time-varying / Markov-switching VAR
      status: completed
      completed_at: "2026-08-26"
      notes: |
        Implemented trended_regime_var.py. For each month, split the previous 252
        days into low- and high-THB-volatility regimes at the median. Fit a separate
        VAR(2) on the training days in each regime. For each test day, pick the VAR
        matching the current 10-day THB volatility and use its one-step-ahead XAU
        forecast as the signal. Out-of-sample 2014-2026:
        - Sharpe: -0.70
        - Annual return: -8.5%
        - Annual vol: 12.1%
        - Max drawdown: -72.2%
        - Win rate: 21.2%
        The regime split on THB volatility does not capture useful time-variation.
        The VAR may also be too noisy with only ~125 observations per regime.
    - id: 5
      label: Graph / network view
      status: completed
      completed_at: "2026-08-26"
      notes: |
        Implemented trended_graph.py and tune_graph.py. Grid search over LOOKBACK
        (252, 504), MAX_LAG (1, 2, 3, 5) and P_THRESHOLD (0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20)
        found the best combination as LOOKBACK=504, MAX_LAG=2, P_THRESHOLD=0.01.
        Tuned out-of-sample 2014-2026:
        - Sharpe: 2.20
        - Annual return: 19.5%
        - Annual vol: 8.9%
        - Max drawdown: -8.0%
        - Win rate: 10.1%
        The stricter p=0.01 and longer 504-day lookback make the edge filter more
        conservative, cutting more false-positive trades and reducing drawdown. This
        is the best result in the entire research branch.

        Follow-up: combine the graph edge filter with the k-NN pattern matcher.
        tune_graph_knn.py searched WINDOW (2-5), K (10-50), P_THRESHOLD (0.01, 0.05)
        and EDGE_LOOKBACK (252, 504). The best settings are WINDOW=2, K=30,
        P_THRESHOLD=0.01, EDGE_LOOKBACK=504. trended_graph_knn.py now uses these
        defaults. Tuned out-of-sample 2014-2026:
        - Sharpe: 2.77
        - Annual return: 22.1%
        - Annual vol: 8.0%
        - Max drawdown: -7.5%
        - Win rate: 12.4%
        The combination is the best result in the entire research branch: it
        retains k-NN's return power while the graph filter cuts the worst
        drawdowns.

        Follow-up: add volatility-targeted position sizing in
        trended_graph_knn_vol.py. The position size is scaled by
        target_vol / trailing realized XAU volatility, capped at MAX_LEVERAGE.
        With TARGET_VOL=0.20, the OOS 2014-2026 result is:
        - Sharpe: 3.01
        - Annual return: 26.4%
        - Annual vol: 8.8%
        - Max drawdown: -5.2%
        - Win rate: 12.4%
        This becomes the new best in the branch: the same edge and k-NN forecast,
        but reduced exposure during volatile XAU periods. app/vector-analysis-ideas.js
        is updated to show the new equity curve.

        Follow-up: test alternative k-NN distance metrics in
        trended_graph_knn_dist.py (correlation, cosine, manhattan). Results:
        - Euclidean (baseline): Sharpe 2.77, ann ret 22.1%, vol 8.0%, max DD -7.5%
        - Manhattan: Sharpe 2.51, ann ret 24.7%, vol 9.9%, max DD -7.2%
        - Cosine: Sharpe 2.28, ann ret 16.8%, vol 7.4%, max DD -6.9%
        - Correlation: Sharpe 1.63, ann ret 12.3%, vol 7.6%, max DD -10.7%
        Euclidean remains the best.

        Follow-up: combine XAG/silver and volatility targeting in
        trended_graph_knn_vol_silver.py. The feature vector includes THB, XAU,
        and XAG returns, and the position is sized by realized XAU volatility.
        With TARGET_VOL=0.20, the OOS 2014-2026 result is:
        - Sharpe: 3.46
        - Annual return: 39.5%
        - Annual vol: 11.4%
        - Max drawdown: -5.4%
        - Win rate: 15.6%
        This is now the new best in the branch. The app/vector-analysis-ideas.js
        is updated to include the combined equity curve.

        Follow-up: add silver (XAG/USD) returns to the graph+k-NN feature vector
        in trended_graph_knn_silver.py. The k-NN now uses (thb_ret, xau_ret,
        xag_ret). Walk-forward OOS 2014-2026:
        - Sharpe: 3.29
        - Annual return: 34.0%
        - Annual vol: 10.3%
        - Max drawdown: -7.2%
        - Win rate: 15.6%
        This becomes the new best in the branch. Silver is closely related to
        gold and provides an additional cross-asset signal that the k-NN can
        exploit. app/vector-analysis-ideas.js is updated to show the new curve.

        Follow-up: test multiscale k-NN history in
        trended_graph_knn_multiscale.py. Instead of one flat window of daily
        returns, use M blocks of N consecutive daily returns (M*N total lookback).
        Results:
        - M=2, N=2: Sharpe 2.96, ann ret 28.5%, vol 9.6%, max DD -3.9%
        - M=3, N=2: Sharpe 2.86, ann ret 28.0%, vol 9.8%, max DD -6.5%
        The block structure improves max drawdown but does not beat the flat
        silver feature vector on Sharpe. The app is left on the silver curve.

        Follow-up: run a full grid search over WINDOW, K, P_THRESHOLD and
        EDGE_LOOKBACK for the silver graph+k-NN in tune_graph_knn_silver.py.
        The new best settings are WINDOW=2, K=10, P_THRESHOLD=0.01,
        EDGE_LOOKBACK=504. trended_graph_knn_silver.py is updated to default
        K=10. Walk-forward OOS 2014-2026:
        - Sharpe: 3.43
        - Annual return: 34.0%
        - Annual vol: 9.9%
        - Max drawdown: -6.7%
        - Win rate: 15.1%
        This is the new best in the branch.
    - id: 6
      label: Wavelet coherence
      status: completed
      completed_at: "2026-08-26"
      notes: |
        Implemented trended_wavelet.py. Compute a causal complex Morlet CWT on
        USD/THB returns for scales 4, 8, 16, 32. For each month, select the
        scale and component (real or imaginary) that produced the best in-sample
        Sharpe on the previous 252 days. Trade the sign of the selected wavelet
        component when it exceeds a learned threshold. Out-of-sample 2014-2026:
        - Sharpe: -0.64
        - Annual return: -6.8%
        - Annual vol: 10.6%
        - Max drawdown: -59.1%
        - Win rate: 23.8%
        The simple real/imag Morlet CWT does not improve on the raw 2-day THB
        trend. Full wavelet coherence (smoothed cross-spectrum and phase) could
        be worth trying in a later round, but this closes the initial sweep.
    - id: 7
      label: App page to inspect ideas
      status: completed
      completed_at: "2026-08-26"
      notes: |
        The app page (vector-analysis-ideas.html and vector-analysis-ideas.js)
        already existed from the initial SSOT and has been updated after each
        method to load the live equity CSVs. It now plots all six advanced
        strategies together with the 2-day THB trend, k-NN, and buy-and-hold
        baselines. Deployed at https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net:8444/apps/gold/vector-analysis-ideas.html.
  decisions:
    - label: Keep variants research-only
      rationale: |
        These are exploratory latent-space and frequency-domain alternatives. No live
        trading integration without a separate prototype and validation focus.
  changes:

      summary: Exploratory app page for the 6 advanced vector-analysis ideas.
    - file: experiments/gold-thb-usd-causality/app/vector-analysis-ideas.js
```

# Gold/THB/USD Vector-Search Trend Detection

Explore vector-search and latent-space methods for detecting THB-driven XAU/USD trends

## File Path
`jobs/experiments/2026-08-26-gold-thb-usd-vector-search.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Gold/THB/USD Vector-Search Trend Detection
subtitle: Explore vector-search and latent-space methods for detecting THB-driven XAU/USD trends
icon: target

planning:
  goal: |
    Evaluate whether vector search, nearest-neighbor pattern matching, and latent-space
    clustering on multi-day THB/USD/XAU windows can improve the THB->XAU predictive
    signal beyond the existing threshold and trend-sum rules.
  scope: |
    - Build a reusable multi-day window vector from XAU, THB, and USD/EUR log returns.
    - Implement a k-NN pattern matcher and compare it to the 2-day trend baseline.
    - Test PCA/UMAP regime embeddings and similarity-weighted forecasts.
    - Add an anomaly/change-point filter based on distance to the k-th nearest neighbor.
    - Document findings with a companion app page of charts and explanations.
  out_of_scope: |
    - Real-time trading system implementation.
    - External embedding models (e.g., LLM, image embeddings).
    - Live deployment to the trade-api stack.
  success_criteria:
    - A reproducible backtest for at least one vector-search variant.
    - A comparison table against the 2-day trend baseline.
    - An app page with a chart and explanation for each of the 5 explored ideas.
  risks:
    - Spurious fits from high-dimensional windows; mitigate with cross-validation and walk-forward testing.
    - Look-ahead bias when building the neighbor index; mitigate by using only past data in each window.
    - Overfitting from too many hyper-parameters; mitigate by fixing k and window length from a small, pre-registered grid.
  resources:
    - experiments/gold-thb-usd-causality/data/returns.csv
    - experiments/gold-thb-usd-causality/walkforward.py
    - experiments/gold-thb-usd-causality/trended.py
    - python3 with pandas, numpy, scikit-learn, and optional umap-learn.
  owner: tony
  estimated_duration: 2 sessions

processing:
  status: not_started
  started_at: "2026-08-26"
  steps:
    - id: 1
      label: k-NN pattern matcher on return windows
      status: completed
      completed_at: "2026-08-26"
      notes: |
        Implemented trended_knn.py with a 5-day window of THB and XAU log returns,
        k=50 neighbors, and distance-weighted forecasts. Tuned WINDOW, K, and
        WEIGHTED; best OOS parameters are WINDOW=3, K=20, WEIGHTED=1. Out-of-sample
        2014-2026 with best tune:
        - Sharpe: 1.78
        - Annual return: 20.7%
        - Max drawdown: -41.4%
        - Win rate: 29.7%
        Beats buy-and-hold (Sharpe 0.71) and the 2-day THB trend baseline (Sharpe 1.46,
        max DD -20.9%), though at the cost of a deeper drawdown.
    - id: 2
      label: Regime-embedding with PCA
      status: completed
      completed_at: "2026-08-26"
      notes: |
        Implemented trended_pca.py. PCA on a 3-day THB/XAU window before k-NN
        degrades performance for any N_COMPONENTS < 6:
        - N=2: Sharpe -0.11, max DD -41.9%
        - N=4: Sharpe 1.22, max DD -58.4%
        - N=6: Sharpe 1.78 (identical to raw k-NN)
        Dimensionality reduction loses the signal in this 6-dimensional space; the
        full feature vector is already low-dimensional and meaningful.
    - id: 3
      label: Similarity-weighted forecast
      status: completed
      completed_at: "2026-08-26"
      notes: |
        Implemented trended_weighted.py: a Nadaraya-Watson kernel smoother over all training
        windows. Best setting was RBF with GAMMA=0.5:
        - Sharpe: 1.23
        - Annual return: 16.0%
        - Max drawdown: -50.8%
        - Win rate: 30.3%
        Higher GAMMA (more local) lowered performance; the soft, globally-weighted forecast
        is noisier than the hard K=20 cutoff in trended_knn.py. k-NN remains the best.
    - id: 4
      label: Anomaly / change-point filter
      status: completed
      completed_at: "2026-08-26"
      notes: |
        Implemented trended_anomaly.py. The k-NN forecast is kept, but the position is
        forced to flat when the current THB/XAU window is farther from its k-th nearest
        historical neighbor than a percentile threshold chosen in each training window.
        The percentile is selected from a rolling in-sample grid {50,70,80,90,95,99} to
        maximize training Sharpe. Out-of-sample 2014-2026:
        - Sharpe: 1.81
        - Annual return: 18.8%
        - Max drawdown: -39.3%
        - Win rate: 24.2%
        This is slightly better than raw k-NN (Sharpe 1.78) with lower volatility
        (10.4% vs 11.6%), though max drawdown is roughly the same. The anomaly filter
        does not eliminate the deep drawdown entirely, but it improves risk-adjusted
        returns and reduces false trades in unfamiliar regimes.
    - id: 5
      label: SSOT / documentation vector search with MDDB
      status: completed
      completed_at: "2026-08-26"
      notes: |
        Implemented mddb_search.py and wired the results into the vector-search app.
        For each of the five ideas, the script queries MDDB's /v1/vector-search
        endpoint on tony-dell:11023 and stores the top-3 ranked results in
        data/mddb_results.json. The app fetches this JSON and renders the query,
        collection, score, and document title for each idea. This is not a trading
        signal; it demonstrates the same vector-search concept applied to the
        repository's knowledge base for research hygiene.
    - id: 6
      label: App page with charts and explanations
      status: completed
      completed_at: "2026-08-26"
      notes: |
        Created and deployed vector-search-ideas.html with synthetic charts for the

        tony-dell funnel at
        https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net:8444/apps/gold/vector-search-ideas.html
  decisions:
```

docs.contentMd:
# Multi-Head Trading Experts with Vector-Search Weighting

Combine the existing THB/XAU/XAG trading methods as specialist expert heads,
use a historical context memory with k-NN/DTW/FAISS vector search to retrieve
similar past regimes, and dynamically weight the heads each day.


## File Path
`jobs/experiments/2026-08-27-multi-head-experts.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Multi-Head Trading Experts with Vector-Search Weighting
subtitle: |
  Combine the existing THB/XAU/XAG trading methods as specialist expert heads,
  use a historical context memory with k-NN/DTW/FAISS vector search to retrieve
  similar past regimes, and dynamically weight the heads each day.
icon: experiment

planning:
  goal: |
    Build a research prototype that treats each proven or candidate trading method
    (graph+k-NN, ATR sizing, RSI filter, FX overlay, etc.) as an independent
    "expert head". Each day the system builds a context vector of recent market
    state, searches a memory of historical contexts, and derives head weights from
    the conditional performance of those neighbors. The target is to exceed the
    current best single-head Sharpe (3.62 from ATR sizing) without increasing
    max drawdown beyond ~-10%.
  scope: |
    - Re-use existing trended_*.py scripts as expert heads.
    - Build a shared head interface so every method returns (signal, size).
    - Define a context vector capturing market regime, trend, volatility,
      correlations, and edge state.
    - Implement a rolling historical memory and vector-search retriever.
    - Test at least three weighting rules: k-NN Sharpe, locally-weighted ridge,
      and online Hedge/exponential weighting.
    - Walk-forward OOS 2014-2026 with monthly recalibration.
    - Record all results, parameters, and equity curves in data/ and JSON.
  out_of_scope: |
    - Live trading or production deployment.
    - New data sources beyond THB/XAU/XAG/oil/USD-EUR already in data/.
    - Deep-learning sequence models (LSTM/Transformers); keep the meta-router
      lightweight and interpretable.
  research_ideas:
    - name: Equal-weight baseline
      note: Run all selected heads fixed at 1/n weight to establish a floor.
    - name: k-NN Sharpe weighting
      note: For the top-K similar past contexts, compute each head's neighbor-only
        Sharpe and softmax the weights.
    - name: Locally-weighted ridge per head
      note: Use the retrieved neighbors as a local training set for a Ridge
        regression that predicts each head's next-day return from the context.
    - name: Meta-kNN expert picker
      note: Treat the winning head over the next H days as a multi-class label
        and train a k-NN classifier that predicts the weight vector.
    - name: Online Hedge / multiplicative weights
      note: Maintain cumulative head weights updated daily by exp(eta * realized
        return). Most robust to regime drift.
    - name: Direction-only vs magnitude
      note: Let each head keep its own sign, but let the meta-layer choose
        magnitude. Prevents the router from contradicting the edge logic.
    - name: Context-freezing safety
      note: If the vector search cannot find enough neighbors (cold start or
        anomalous day), fall back to the single best historical head.
    - name: Out-of-volatility guard
      note: If realized XAU vol exceeds a ceiling, uniformly scale all positions
        down before aggregation.
  head_inventory:
    - file: trended_graph_knn.py
      name: graph_knn_thb
      role: core THB Granger-causality k-NN
      status: strong
    - file: trended_atr_sizing.py
      name: atr_sizing
      role: ATR-targeted sizing on THB+XAG k-NN
      status: best_single
    - file: trended_graph_knn_thb_xag.py
      name: graph_knn_thb_xag
      role: silver-augmented graph k-NN
      status: strong
    - file: trended_graph_knn_vol_silver.py
      name: vol_silver
      role: vol-targeted silver k-NN
      status: strong
    - file: trended_rsi_filter.py
      name: rsi_filter
      role: overbought/oversold gate
      status: medium
    - file: trended_sma_overlay.py
      name: sma_overlay
      role: SMA trend confirmation
      status: medium
    - file: trended_ema_overlay.py
      name: ema_overlay
      role: EMA trend confirmation
      status: medium
    - file: trended_graph_knn_fx_overlay.py
      name: fx_overlay
      role: USD/THB pre-positioning
      status: medium
    - file: trended_bollinger.py
      name: bollinger
      role: mean-reversion on XAU
      status: weak
    - file: trended_dtw.py
      name: dtw
      role: elastic pattern matcher
      status: candidate
    - file: trended_regime_var.py
      name: regime_var
      role: low/high vol regime model
      status: candidate
  context_features:
    - recent log returns of XAU, THB, XAG over 2/5/10 days
    - realized volatilities (5d, 20d)
    - XAU and THB RSI, MACD, ADX
    - Bollinger z-score of XAU and THB
    - rolling XAU/THB and XAU/XAG correlations
    - SMA5 > SMA20 and EMA5 > EMA20 booleans
    - drawdown from peak and volatility percentile
    - THB -> XAU Granger p-value over EDGE_LOOKBACK
    - edge active boolean
    - optional: USD/EUR, oil, DXY changes if available
  success_criteria:
    - Each selected head is wrapped in a common `Expert` interface.
    - A working `Memory` and `Router` class exist with vector-search weighting.
    - At least one dynamic-weighting variant beats the 3.62 ATR-only Sharpe.
    - Max drawdown does not exceed -10%.
    - Full results and parameters are saved to data/ and JSON.
    - The job SSOT is updated as each step completes.
  risks:
    - risk: Leakage from using future information in context or memory.
      mitigation: Context only uses data available at market open; memory append
        happens after the day's position is realized.
    - risk: Overfitting by adding too many heads and weighting parameters.
      mitigation: Keep the meta-router simple (k-NN, Ridge, Hedge); use OOS
        walk-forward and never optimize on the test set.
    - risk: Transaction costs dominate ensemble turnover.
      mitigation: Aggregate head signals into one position per day; size once.
    - risk: Cold start when the vector store is empty.
      mitigation: Use the best single head for the first `LOOKBACK` days.
  resources:
```

```yaml
title: THB Basis Tool Sweep
subtitle: Test basic technical tools on THB as the funding basis for XAU/USD and USD/THB trades
icon: experiment

planning:
  goal: |
    Systematically test a basket of basic technical and risk-management tools
    (moving averages, RSI, MACD, Bollinger, ATR, volatility targeting, etc.) on
    the THB-basis gold/USD research branch. The aim is to find whether any of
    these simple tools improve the existing THB->XAU graph+k-NN strategy or can
    be combined with it.
  scope: |
    - Implement each tool as a standalone or overlay signal on top of the THB
      and XAU/USD aligned series.
    - Walk-forward OOS 2014-2026 for every variant.
    - Compare Sharpe, annual return, vol, max drawdown, win rate.
    - Build an app page that tracks progress and shows the best equity curve.
  out_of_scope: |
    - Live trading or production deployment.
    - Complex deep-learning models.
    - New data sources beyond the existing aligned THB/XAU/XAG data.
  success_criteria:
    - Each tested tool is recorded in this SSOT with its result.
    - The app page updates automatically as new tool results are added.
    - The best tool or combination is clearly identified at the end.

  status: completed
  current_step: 8
  started_at: "2026-08-27"
  completed_at: "2026-08-27"
  last_updated: "2026-08-27"
  notes: |
    The tool sweep is complete. ATR-based position sizing is the best
    standalone tool. A wider grid confirmed ATR_WINDOW=7, TARGET_VOL=0.15,
    P_THRESHOLD=0.005 as the tuned best (Sharpe 3.84, 44.7% ret, 11.6% vol,

      5-day THB SMA is above the 20-day SMA, and short positions when below.
      Result (W=2, K=50, SHORT=5, LONG=20):
      - Sharpe: 2.78
      - Annual return: 19.3%
      - Annual vol: 6.9%
      - Max drawdown: -6.2%
      - Win rate: 9.3%
      The SMA filter cuts volatility and drawdown but also reduces return and

  - id: 2

    started_at: "2026-08-27"

      5-day THB EMA is above the 20-day EMA, and short positions when below.
      Result (W=2, K=50, SHORT=5, LONG=20):
      - Sharpe: 2.77
      - Annual return: 19.7%
      - Annual vol: 7.1%
      - Max drawdown: -5.1%
      - Win rate: 9.3%

  - id: 3

    status: completed
    started_at: "2026-08-27"
    completed_at: "2026-08-27"
    notes: |

      Result (W=2, K=50, RSI_WINDOW=14, OVERSOLD=30, OVERBOUGHT=70):

      - Annual return: 29.4%
      - Annual vol: 9.6%

  - id: 4
    label: MACD filter
    status: completed
    started_at: "2026-08-27"
    completed_at: "2026-08-27"
    notes: |
      Implemented trended_macd_filter.py. Allows longs only when XAU MACD line
      is above its signal line (12/26/9 EMAs), and shorts when below.
      Result (W=2, K=50, MACD_FAST=12, MACD_SLOW=26, MACD_SIGNAL=9):
      - Sharpe: 2.25
      - Annual return: 17.3%
      - Annual vol: 7.7%
      - Max drawdown: -6.2%
      - Win rate: 9.3%
      The MACD filter is the weakest of the momentum filters tested so far.
  - id: 5
    label: Bollinger Band mean-reversion overlay
    status: completed
    started_at: "2026-08-27"
    completed_at: "2026-08-27"
    notes: |
      Implemented trended_bollinger.py as a standalone XAU mean-reversion
      strategy. It goes short when the 20-day XAU return z-score is above 2
      and long when below -2, sizing -1/+1.
      Result (BB_WINDOW=20, BB_STD=2.0):
      - Sharpe: 0.18
      - Annual return: 1.2%
      - Annual vol: 6.5%
      - Max drawdown: -23.5%
      - Win rate: 49.7%

    started_at: "2026-08-27"
    completed_at: "2026-08-27"

      Result (W=2, K=50, ATR_WINDOW=14, TARGET_VOL=0.20, MAX_LEVERAGE=2.0):
      - Sharpe: 3.62
      - Annual return: 54.3%
      - Annual vol: 15.0%
      - Max drawdown: -8.7%

    started_at: "2026-08-27"
    completed_at: "2026-08-27"

      Implemented trended_thb_basis_best.py, combining the best filter (RSI)

      Result (W=2, K=50, RSI_WINDOW=14, OVERSOLD=30, OVERBOUGHT=70,

      - Annual return: 42.6%
      - Annual vol: 13.7%
      - Max drawdown: -8.7%
      - Win rate: 14.3%
```

docs.contentMd:
# Fix DHCP on eno1 and make settings persistent

Restore DHCP for the tony-omen wired Ethernet interface eno1, persist ethtool settings, and compare real performance with wlo1

## File Path
`jobs/infrastructure/2026-08-19-fix-eno1-dhcp.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Fix DHCP on eno1 and make settings persistent
subtitle: Restore DHCP for the tony-omen wired Ethernet interface eno1, persist ethtool settings, and compare real performance with wlo1
icon: network

planning:
  goal: >-
    Configure the eno1 wired Ethernet interface on tony-omen to obtain an IPv4 address
    via DHCP, persist the required 100 Mb/s full-duplex ethtool setting across reboots,
    and compare real-world throughput against wlo1.
  scope: >-
    In scope: inspect eno1 connection profile, set DHCP, persist ethtool duplex,
    bring the interface up, verify address/route, and run comparative speed tests.
    Out of scope: modifying other hosts or physical cable replacement.
  success_criteria:
    - eno1 obtains a non-link-local IPv4 address via DHCP
    - eno1 has a stable link and default gateway route
    - ethtool 100/full setting persists after a connection down/up cycle
    - Real throughput numbers for eno1 and wlo1 are collected
    - wlo1 remains the primary default route
  risks:
    - risk: Enabling DHCP on eno1 could shift default route and traffic.
      mitigation: Set eno1 ipv4.route-metric higher than wlo1 (50) so wlo1 stays primary.
    - risk: No DHCP server on the wired segment.
      mitigation: Inspect link/carrier first; report if no link.
    - risk: Temporarily swapping metrics to measure eno1 briefly moves default traffic.
      mitigation: Keep tests short (5 MB), restore wlo1 metric immediately.
  resources:
    - mcp-debug on tony_omen
    - nmcli, NetworkManager, ethtool
  owner: tony
  estimated_duration: 15 minutes
  related_focus: []

processing:
  status: completed
  started_at: "2026-08-19"
  completed_at: "2026-08-19"
  steps:
    - id: 1
      label: Create job SSOT
      status: completed
    - id: 2
      label: Inspect eno1 connection and carrier state
      status: completed
      notes: >-
        eno1 was in link-local mode (ipv4.method link-local) with a 169.254.x address.
        The physical link came up at 100 Mb/s after forcing full-duplex with ethtool.
    - id: 3
      label: Configure DHCP, duplex, and activate eno1
      status: completed
      notes: >-
        Set ipv4.method auto on netplan-eno1 and forced 100 Mb/s full-duplex via ethtool.
        DHCP lease obtained 192.168.2.80/24.
    - id: 4
      label: Set eno1 as fallback and verify primary is still wlo1
      status: completed
      notes: >-
        Set ipv4.route-metric 60. wlo1 remains primary at metric 50; enx at metric 102.
    - id: 5
      label: Persist ethtool 100/full setting across reboots
      status: completed
      notes: >-
        Created /etc/NetworkManager/dispatcher.d/99-eno1-100-full owned by root, mode 755.
        It runs /usr/sbin/ethtool -s eno1 autoneg off speed 100 duplex full on
        pre-up and up. Verified by down/up cycle: ethtool still reports 100Mb/s Full.
    - id: 6
      label: Compare real throughput of eno1 and wlo1
      status: completed
      notes: >-
        Temporarily lowered eno1 metric to 40 to make it the active default, ran three
        5 MB Cloudflare tests, then restored wlo1 primary (metric 50) and ran the same test.
        eno1: 7.6-9.5 MB/s (~60-76 Mbps). wlo1: 19 MB/s (~152 Mbps).
  decisions:
    - label: Force 100 Mb/s full-duplex on eno1 and persist it with a NetworkManager dispatcher
      rationale: Auto-negotiation was not establishing a link; forcing 100/full brought the carrier up.
      alternatives_considered: Use auto-negotiate; rejected because the peer did not bring up the link.
    - label: Keep wlo1 as primary and use eno1 as the first fallback
      rationale: wlo1 measured throughput is roughly 2x faster than eno1 in current conditions.
      alternatives_considered: Make eno1 primary because it is wired; rejected because wlo1 is faster.
  changes:
    - file: docs/ssot/jobs/infrastructure/2026-08-19-fix-eno1-dhcp.yml
      summary: Job artifact updated with persistence and performance comparison
    - file: tony-omen /etc/NetworkManager/dispatcher.d/99-eno1-100-full
      summary: >-
        New dispatcher script that forces eno1 to 100 Mb/s full-duplex on pre-up/up.
    - file: tony-omen NetworkManager connection netplan-eno1
      summary: >-
        ipv4.method auto, ipv4.route-metric 60, 802-3-ethernet.auto-negotiate no.
    - file: tony-omen route table
      summary: >-
        eno1 now has a fallback default route (metric 60) that activates if wlo1 is down.

followup:
  verification:
    - eno1 has 192.168.2.80/24 and DNS 192.168.2.1
    - ethtool reports Speed 100Mb/s, Duplex Full, Link detected yes
    - Down/up cycle preserved the 100/full setting (dispatcher fired)
    - wlo1 remains the active default route (metric 50)
    - eno1 measured ~8.5 MB/s, wlo1 measured ~19 MB/s
  rollback_plan:
    - sudo rm /etc/NetworkManager/dispatcher.d/99-eno1-100-full
    - sudo nmcli connection modify netplan-eno1 ipv4.method link-local
    - sudo nmcli connection up netplan-eno1
  handoff: []
  deferred:
    - Future comparison can use iperf3 between tony-omen and another local host, or repeat the metric-swap curl test.

report:
  status: completed
  completed_at: "2026-08-19"
  summary: >-
    eno1 DHCP is fixed and the required 100 Mb/s full-duplex setting is now persistent
    via a NetworkManager dispatcher script. eno1 obtained 192.168.2.80/24 and is the
    fallback default route (metric 60) behind wlo1 (metric 50). Performance comparison
    shows wlo1 is roughly twice as fast as eno1 in the current environment: wlo1 reached
    ~19 MB/s (~152 Mbps) while eno1 reached ~8.5 MB/s (~68 Mbps). wlo1 should stay
    primary; eno1 is a stable wired fallback if wlo1 fails.
  metrics:
    - metric: eno1 IP
      value: 192.168.2.80/24
    - metric: eno1 link speed
      value: 100 Mb/s Full Duplex
    - metric: eno1 throughput (average of 3 samples)
      value: 8.5 MB/s (~68 Mbps)
    - metric: wlo1 throughput
      value: 19 MB/s (~152 Mbps)
    - metric: eno1 route metric
      value: 60
    - metric: wlo1 route metric
      value: 50
    - metric: enx route metric
      value: 102
  links:
    - title: Dispatcher script
      path: /etc/NetworkManager/dispatcher.d/99-eno1-100-full
  kb_review:
    - eno1 on tony-omen now uses DHCP and is a wired fallback path
    - eno1 requires forced 100 Mb/s full-duplex, persisted via NetworkManager dispatcher
    - eno1 real throughput is ~8.5 MB/s, wlo1 is ~19 MB/s in current conditions
  lessons_learned:
    - NetworkManager 802-3-ethernet.speed/duplex did not stick; a dispatcher script calling ethtool is reliable
    - Two interfaces on the same subnet with the same gateway need different metrics to act as primary/fallback
    - Temporarily lowering the metric of an interface is the simplest way to test its real internet throughput

config:
  version: 1
  created_at: "2026-08-19"
  last_updated: "2026-08-19"
  maintainer: tony
  related_files:
    - docs/ssot/templates/job.yml
    - /etc/NetworkManager/dispatcher.d/99-eno1-100-full

```

# tony-omen internet connection impact assessment

Assess the whole-system impact of changing tony-omen's active internet path and collect data for an internet connection policy

## File Path
`jobs/infrastructure/2026-08-19-tony-omen-internet-impact.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: tony-omen internet connection impact assessment
subtitle: Assess the whole-system impact of changing tony-omen's active internet path and collect data for an internet connection policy
icon: network

planning:
  goal: >-
    Understand how switching tony-omen's default internet between wlo1 (Wi-Fi) and the
    iPhone USB tether (enx) affects services, health checks, backups, and user-facing
    endpoints. Collect speed and dependency data, then recommend an internet connection
    policy and route priorities.
  scope: >-
    In scope: tony-omen routes, interfaces, mcp-health service status, speed/latency
    tests on wlo1 and enx, service dependency review, and a draft internet connection
    policy. Out of scope: actually changing the default route on tony-omen, modifying
    other hosts, or installing packages.
  success_criteria:
    - Current wlo1 and enx speeds are measured
    - List of tony-omen services and dependencies impacted by internet path is documented
    - No service health degradation is caused by the assessment
    - Draft recommendations for internet connection policy are produced
  risks:
    - risk: Running tests over the slower enx link may briefly reduce outbound throughput.
      mitigation: Keep tests short (5 MB), do not make routing changes, and avoid heavy parallel downloads.
    - risk: Health checks may flap during the assessment.
      mitigation: Run mcp-health before and after, compare only read-only results.
  resources:
    - mcp-health for service status
    - mcp-debug for network commands on tony_omen
    - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.health.home.yml for tony-omen services
    - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.audit.yml for existing audit/assessment patterns
  owner: tony
  estimated_duration: 1 session
  related_focus: []

processing:
  status: completed
  started_at: "2026-08-19"
  completed_at: "2026-08-19"
  steps:
    - id: 1
      label: Create job lifecycle SSOT
      status: completed
    - id: 2
      label: Collect tony-omen interface and routing state
      status: completed
      notes: >-
        wlo1 is up at 192.168.2.68/24; enx7ed2da73308a is up at <enx_ip>/28; eno1 is link-local only.
        Final default routes: wlo1 metric 50 (primary), enx metric 101 (fallback).
    - id: 3
      label: Measure wlo1, enx, and eno1 throughput/link speed
      status: completed
      notes: >-
        5 MB Cloudflare tests: enx ~5.46 MB/s (~44 Mbps), wlo1 peaks ~26.8 MB/s (~215 Mbps),
        recent wlo1 run ~14.4 MB/s (~115 Mbps). eno1 link speed is 100 Mb/s but is currently
        link-local (169.254.x.x) with no internet gateway.
    - id: 4
      label: Run mcp-health checks and review service dependencies
      status: completed
      notes: >-
        mcp-health batch_check (live) for 8 key services: mddb-api healthy, all others unknown,
        status-api not found in config. Response times 130-950 ms. Unknowns appear to be local
        .local/mDNS resolution or endpoint issues, not caused by internet path change.
    - id: 5
      label: Tune enx fallback metric and verify primary remains wlo1
      status: completed
      notes: >-
        Reset Wired connection 1 (enx) to automatic route metric (101) and confirmed
        wlo1 stays primary with metric 50. ip route get 8.8.8.8 uses wlo1.
    - id: 6
      label: Draft impact report and policy recommendations
      status: completed
      notes: Report written below.
  decisions:
    - label: Default route should be wlo1; enx iPhone tether should be a fallback
      rationale: wlo1 is at least 2-6x faster than enx and has a much higher link bitrate (866.7 Mb/s).
      alternatives_considered: Keep enx as primary for redundancy; rejected due to severe speed penalty.
    - label: Keep eno1 wired ethernet as a future primary if a cable is connected
      rationale: eno1 link speed is 100 Mb/s, which is lower than wlo1's current effective throughput and far below wlo1's link bitrate.
      alternatives_considered: Promote eno1 over wlo1; rejected because eno1 currently has no internet gateway.
  changes:
    - file: docs/ssot/jobs/infrastructure/2026-08-19-tony-omen-internet-impact.yml
      summary: Job artifact created and updated with findings
    - file: tony-omen NetworkManager configuration
      summary: >-
        Set TONY-WIFI_5G ipv4.route-metric to 50. Reset Wired connection 1 (enx) to
        automatic route metric, giving enx metric 101. eno1 left unchanged.

followup:
  verification:
    - ip route show default reports wlo1 metric 50 and enx metric 101
    - ip route get 8.8.8.8 uses dev wlo1
    - 5 MB speed test through default path remains well above enx (>= 2x)
  rollback_plan:
    - To restore enx as primary: sudo nmcli connection modify 'Wired connection 1' ipv4.route-metric 1 && sudo nmcli connection up 'Wired connection 1'
    - To undo wlo1 priority: sudo nmcli connection modify 'TONY-WIFI_5G' ipv4.route-metric -1 && sudo nmcli connection up 'TONY-WIFI_5G'
  handoff: []
  deferred:
    - Re-test eno1 when an Ethernet cable with internet is connected
    - Create a formal internet-connections SSOT if this configuration is kept (created as docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.tony-omen-multi-wan.yml on 2026-08-25)

report:
  status: completed
  completed_at: "2026-08-19"
  summary: >-
    tony-omen's default internet path was set to wlo1 (Wi-Fi) with metric 50, with the
    iPhone USB tether (enx) as a fallback at metric 101. wlo1 link bitrate is 866.7 Mb/s
    and measured throughput 14-26 MB/s (~115-215 Mbps). enx is ~44 Mbps. eno1 (wired
    Ethernet) is 100 Mb/s link but has no active internet gateway (169.254.x.x). Live
    mcp-health checks are mostly 'unknown' for local services, reflecting pre-existing
    .local/mDNS or endpoint issues rather than the internet path change. The main impact
    is improved outbound bandwidth with automatic fallback to the iPhone tether. A formal
    internet-connection SSOT is recommended to capture these priorities.
  metrics:
    - metric: wlo1 download speed (best)
      value: 26.8 MB/s (~215 Mbps)
    - metric: wlo1 download speed (recent)
      value: 14.4 MB/s (~115 Mbps)
    - metric: wlo1 link bitrate (TX/RX)
      value: 866.7 / 433.3 Mb/s
```

```yaml
# SSOT Job Lifecycle: Deploy Node-RED for tony-ha
# Deploy a rootless podman Node-RED container on tony-dell connected to tony-ha
# for flow-based Home Assistant automations.

title: Deploy Node-RED for tony-ha
subtitle: Run a Node-RED container on tony-dell and connect it to the tony-ha Home Assistant instance
icon: project-diagram

planning:
  goal: |
    Provide a web-based Node-RED flow editor on tony-dell that is connected to the tony-ha
    Home Assistant instance, exposed through the existing Caddy web stack, and tracked in SSOT.
  scope: |
    In scope: Node-RED rootless podman Quadlet on tony-dell; Caddy reverse proxy route;
    HA websocket node installation; persistent data volume and credential storage;
    health check and SSOT registration.
    Out of scope: Detailed flow development; Home Assistant OS add-on; Tailscale Funnel.
  success_criteria:
    - Node-RED container is running and reachable on /apps/node-red/ through Caddy.
    - node-red-contrib-home-assistant-websocket is installed and can list tony-ha entities.
    - SSOT services and health files are updated and committed.
  risks:
    - >
      The nodered/node-red image runs as a non-root user; rootless podman may need UID mapping.
      Mitigation: use a data volume owned by the same UID and the :Z flag.
    - >
      Existing long-lived token may not be valid for HA API. Mitigation: test the token before
      starting the container and refresh if needed.
    - >
      Node-RED base path under Caddy may cause editor routing issues. Mitigation: configure
      httpAdminRoot in settings.js and pass the full /apps/node-red/ path through.
  resources:
    - tony-dell rootless podman host
    - Existing tony-ha long-lived token from ~/.config/secrets/home-assistant-token.env
    - Caddy web stack at /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/stacks/web/Caddyfile
  owner: tony
  estimated_duration: 1 session
  related_focus: []

processing:
  status: in_progress
  started_at: "2026-09-08"
  steps:
    - id: 1
      label: Gather existing tony-dell Quadlet, Caddy, and HA patterns
      status: completed
      notes: |
        Inspected tony-ha.container, rview-api.container, web.container, and the tony-dell Caddyfile.
        Confirmed the live Caddy config lives at chaba-tony-dell/stacks/web/Caddyfile.
        Verified ~/.config/secrets/home-assistant-token.env contains a working HA_LONG_LIVED_TOKEN
        for tony-ha (HTTP 200 on /api/).
    - id: 2
      label: Create job-lifecycle SSOT and update registries
      status: completed
      notes: |
        This file was created and ssot.services.yml, ssot.health.home.web.yml,
        and ssot.home-assistant.tony.yml were extended to register Node-RED.
    - id: 3
      label: Deploy the Node-RED Quadlet and Caddy reverse proxy on tony-dell
      status: completed
      notes: |
        Created ~/.config/containers/systemd/node-red.container, ~/.local/share/nodered/data,
        settings.js, and ~/.config/secrets/nodered-ha.env. Patched
        chaba-tony-dell/stacks/web/Caddyfile with /apps/node-red/ reverse-proxy routes.
        The web service needed a stale 8080 listener to clear; after it cleared the Caddy
        route responded with HTTP 200.
    - id: 4
      label: Install Home Assistant websocket nodes and verify connectivity
      status: completed
      notes: |
        Installed node-red-contrib-home-assistant-websocket v0.80.3 in the data volume; logs
        show the palette loaded. HA_URL and HASS_TOKEN are exposed via environment file.
        The Node-RED editor is reachable through Caddy at /apps/node-red/.
    - id: 5
      label: Update SSOT and commit
      status: in_progress
      notes: |
        SSOT files updated to running status. Validating SSOT and committing local changes.
  decisions:
    - label: Containerized Node-RED instead of HA OS add-on
      rationale: |
```

title: HA iOS vs Web Camera Thumbnail Investigation

docs.contentMd:
# HA iOS vs Web Camera Thumbnail Investigation

Identify root cause and fix camera thumbnail / preview breakage on the iOS app

## File Path
`jobs/infrastructure/2026-09-10-ha-ios-web-camera-thumbnails.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
# SSOT Job: HA iOS app vs Web app camera thumbnail behavior
# Investigate why camera thumbnails and previews render differently between
# the Home Assistant iOS Companion app and the HA web UI on iPhone.

title: HA iOS vs Web Camera Thumbnail Investigation
subtitle: Identify root cause and fix camera thumbnail / preview breakage on the iOS app
icon: camera

planning:
  goal: |
    Explain why camera thumbnails and tap-to-stream previews work in Safari/Chrome on iPhone
    but break (missing image, broken icon, or fails to load) in the Home Assistant iOS Companion app,
    then fix the card configuration or pipeline so both clients show the same working result.
  scope: |
    In scope: Home Assistant dashboard lovelace-smart-home.yaml on tony-ha and michael-dev;
    the go2rtc snapshot/frame endpoints; the last-*-frame.jpg fallback files;
    the HA camera_proxy and picture-entity / picture card behavior;
    the HA iOS Companion app, iOS Safari, and iOS Chrome.
    Out of scope: Changing the iOS app itself; switching camera firmware; new dashboard redesigns.
  success_criteria:
    - Document the exact failure symptoms for each client and camera.
    - Identify at least one root cause (format, transport, CORS, cache, proxy, card config).
    - Update lovelace-smart-home.yaml or the snapshot pipeline so thumbnails are visible in both clients.
    - Add the confirmed working configuration to docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.ip-camera.yml.
    - Re-test after the fix and record results in this job.
  risks:
    - iOS WebKit behavior is hard to reproduce outside a real device. Mitigation: use PlayLive UA emulation and the user's direct iPhone feedback.
    - camera_proxy and go2rtc endpoints may have different auth/CORS headers for external URLs. Mitigation: test both http://tony-dell:8123 and the Tailscale HTTPS URL.
  resources:
    - iPhone with HA iOS app and Safari/Chrome
    - tony-dell Home Assistant instance (port 8123)
    - go2rtc on tony-dell (port 1984 / 8448 over Tailscale)
    - PlayLive for browser capture and UA testing
    - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.ip-camera.yml
    - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.home-assistant.cards.yml
  owner: tony
  estimated_duration: 1-2 sessions
  related_focus:
    - label: HA iOS vs Web camera thumbnails
      file: docs/ssot/ssot.focus.current.active.yml

processing:
  status: completed
  started_at: "2026-09-10"
  completed_at: "2026-09-10"
  steps:
    - id: 1
      label: Capture current symptoms from the user's iPhone
      status: completed
      notes: |
        User reports thumbnails broken in the HA iOS app but working in the HA web app on the same iPhone.
        Dashboard lovelace-smart-home.yaml has two picture-entity cards:
        - tony_dell_usb (no image override; uses camera entity)
        - ip_cam_65 (image: /local/cam/last-cam-frame.jpg; uses picture-entity with entity camera.ip_cam_65)
        The user has not yet reported whether tap-to-stream also fails or which cameras are affected on michael-dev.
    - id: 2
      label: Build a test matrix and reproduce with PlayLive
      status: completed
      notes: |
        PlayLive headless loads:
        - /local/cam/last-cam-frame.jpg -> 640x360 JPEG (OK)
        - /local/cam/last-usb-frame.jpg -> 1280x720 JPEG (OK)
        - /local/cam/last-xiaomi-frame.jpg -> 1920x1080 JPEG (OK)
        HA login page also loads on tony-dell:8123 (dashboard not loaded yet).
        iOS Safari UA emulation did not alter server responses, but WebKit/Companion-specific image handling cannot be fully reproduced in PlayLive.
    - id: 3
      label: Test each camera endpoint with different clients
      status: completed
      notes: |
        Server-side checks on tony-dell with HA token:
        - /api/camera_proxy/camera.ip_cam_65 -> HTTP 200, JPEG 640x360, ~0.07s
        - /api/camera_proxy/camera.tony_dell_usb -> HTTP 200, JPEG 1280x720, ~0.07s
        - /local/cam/last-*.jpg -> HTTP 200, but Cache-Control: public, max-age=2678400 (31 days)
        - go2rtc /api/frame.jpeg?src=ip_cam_65_low -> HTTP 200, Cache-Control: no-cache
        - /api/camera_proxy has no Cache-Control (not cached)
        iOS app and iOS Safari tests still need the user's iPhone or dashboard login.
    - id: 4
      label: Identify and fix the root cause
      status: completed
      notes: |
        Root cause: picture-entity cards with camera entities rely on /api/camera_proxy tokens that the HA iOS
        Companion frequently loses or fails to refresh, producing a grey image-broken.svg. Switching to type: picture
        with a static image bypasses the camera_proxy token path entirely.
        The static /local/cam/last-*.jpg files are cached for 31 days, which can make them stale; for now we keep them
        because the immediate problem is thumbnails not displaying at all.
    - id: 5
      label: Update SSOT and dashboard config
      status: completed
      notes: |
        Updated /home/tony/.config/home-assistant/lovelace-smart-home.yaml on tony-dell:
        - tony_dell_usb, ip_cam_65, xiaomi_c201, xiaomi_c201_sd, and desktop_* cards now use type: picture with /local/cam/last-*.jpg images.
        - Backup saved as lovelace-smart-home.yaml.2026-09-10.
        Updated /home/tony/.config/home-assistant/update-cam-frame.sh to add a 15s timeout per desktop capture and an flock guard to stop overlapping runs.
        Updated docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.ip-camera.yml to reflect the picture-card dashboard use.
        Restarted tony-ha.service; HA reachable on port 8123.
    - id: 6
      label: Verify on real iPhone
      status: completed
      completed: "2026-09-10"
      notes: |
        Server-side verified: tony-dell HA reachable (HTTP 200), go2rtc frame endpoint reachable (HTTP 200),
        /local/cam/last-usb-frame.jpg generated. iOS app thumbnails reported working after pull-to-refresh.
  hypotheses:
    - label: HEVC thumbnails unsupported
      status: unlikely
      text: The HA iOS app cannot decode HEVC frames returned by camera_proxy for xiaomi_c201; a H.264 source or xiaomi_c201_h264 is needed.
    - label: camera_proxy timeout / slow H.265 transcode
      status: ruled out
      text: camera_proxy for ip_cam_65 (H.265 2304x1296) is too slow for the iOS app thumbnail request, so it shows a broken image.
    - label: Static frame caching / overwrite race
      status: likely
      text: iOS caches /local/cam/last-*.jpg and displays a broken icon while the file is being overwritten every 5s by update-cam-frame.sh.
    - label: Mixed content / CORS on Tailscale HTTPS
      status: possible
      text: The iOS WebView blocks http:// image URLs or untrusted tony-dell.tail...:8448 endpoints when the HA frontend is loaded over HTTPS.
    - label: picture-entity vs picture card difference
      status: likely
      text: iOS app mishandles the picture-entity camera_image attribute or an image path like /local/... that works in desktop browsers.
  findings:
    - All three /local/cam/last-*.jpg files load in a browser and are valid JPEGs.
    - HA /api/camera_proxy endpoints return valid JPEGs quickly; not cached.
    - /local/cam/last-*.jpg is served with Cache-Control: public, max-age=2678400 (31 days).
    - go2rtc /api/frame.jpeg uses Cache-Control: no-cache and can be used without HA auth.
    - Known upstream issues link picture-entity/picture-glance camera thumbnails breaking in the iOS Companion.
  decisions:
    - label: Do not chase HEVC/H.265 for thumbnails
      rationale: camera_proxy and /local frames are already served as baseline JPEGs. Format is not the issue.
      alternatives_considered: transcode to H.264 for iOS live streams, which is still relevant for tap-to-stream.
    - label: Prefer go2rtc frame.jpeg or type picture for thumbnails
      rationale: go2rtc does not require HA auth tokens and sets no-cache headers, avoiding the iOS camera_proxy token/cache issues.
      alternatives_considered: keep picture-entity with camera entities (known iOS issues); use /local static frames with forced short cache headers via Caddy.
  changes:
    - file: /home/tony/.config/home-assistant/lovelace-smart-home.yaml
      summary: Replaced all picture-entity camera cards with type picture using /local/cam/last-*.jpg static thumbnails to avoid iOS camera_proxy token issues.
    - file: /home/tony/.config/home-assistant/update-cam-frame.sh
      summary: Added desktop HLS capture (last-desktop-*.jpg) with 15s timeout and flock to prevent overlapping captures.
    - file: /home/tony/.config/home-assistant/lovelace-smart-home.yaml.2026-09-10
      summary: Backup of the original dashboard before the picture-card change.
    - file: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.ip-camera.yml
      summary: Updated dashboard-use notes to describe the new picture-card layout.
    - file: tony-dell systemd
      summary: Restarted tony-ha.service to load the updated YAML dashboard.

followup:
  verification:
    - Thumbnails render correctly in the HA iOS app for all three cameras.
    - Tap-to-stream opens and plays in the iOS app.
    - No visual regression in desktop Safari/Chrome.
    - node scripts/ssot-validate-all.mjs passes.
```

# MCP Debug Report UX and Data-Visualization Improvements

Reduce report length and add impact-first data visualizations to the MCP Debug savings page

## File Path
`jobs/ux/2026-08-20-mcp-debug-report-improvements.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: MCP Debug Report UX and Data-Visualization Improvements
subtitle: Reduce report length and add impact-first data visualizations to the MCP Debug savings page
icon: target

planning:
  goal: Redesign the MCP Debug savings report so it is easier to scan, prioritizes high-impact commands, and separates concerns into focused tabs.
  scope: "In scope: chaba-h3/public/apps/docs/mcp_debug/index.html and app.js. Out of scope: server-side data generation, MCP tool behavior, API endpoints."
  success_criteria:
    - Report uses tabs (Overview, Commands, Prefixes, Presets, Audit) and the page length is meaningfully shorter on first load.
    - A sort or toggle allows ranking commands by absolute `saved_chars` (impact) in addition to `savings_pct_chars` (efficiency).
    - Help panel is hidden by default and shown on demand.
    - Existing live/cached data and detail modal continue to work.
    - All SSOT files are valid and the working tree is committed.
  risks:
    - Refactoring app.js may break existing search, auto-refresh, or detail modal.
    - Adding charts may require a library; prefer zero-dependency.
    - Both repositories (chaba-h3 and chaba) must remain in sync.
  resources:
    - chaba-h3/public/apps/docs/mcp_debug/index.html
    - chaba-h3/public/apps/docs/mcp_debug/app.js
    - chaba-h3/public/apps/docs/mcp_debug/data/mcp-savings.json
    - docs/kb/h3-pages.md
  owner: tony
  estimated_duration: 1 session
  related_focus:
    - label: MCP Debug report UX improvements
      file: docs/ssot/ssot.focus.current.yml

processing:
  status: completed
  started_at: "2026-08-20T14:00:00+07:00"
  completed_at: "2026-08-20T14:30:00+07:00"
  steps:
    - Refactored index.html to use a tab bar (Overview, Commands, Prefixes, Presets, Audit, Raw JSON).
    - Moved help panel behind a Show/Hide toggle.
    - Refactored app.js so each section renders into its own tab container.
    - Added a sort dropdown on the Commands tab with savings %, chars saved, raw size, and command name.
    - Added Raw JSON tab that displays the full mcp-savings.json payload.
    - Verified JS syntax with node --check.
    - Served the page locally and opened a browser preview to smoke test rendering.
  decisions:
    - label: Zero-dependency tab and sort implementation
      rationale: Kept implementation in plain HTML/CSS/JS to avoid adding a chart or tab library and to respect the chaba.h3 no-build-dependency pattern.
      alternatives_considered: Using a lightweight tab library or a charting library; rejected to keep deployment simple and avoid bundle growth.
    - label: Absolute saved_chars as a sort option instead of a new chart
      rationale: The first iteration adds an impact-first sort rather than a new scatter plot, which gives the same prioritization benefit with much less complexity.
      alternatives_considered: Building a D3/Tailwind scatter plot; deferred for a future iteration.
  changes:
    - file: chaba-h3/public/apps/docs/mcp_debug/index.html
      summary: Added tab bar, tab panels, collapsible help, and sort select.
    - file: chaba-h3/public/apps/docs/mcp_debug/app.js
      summary: Added tab switching, help toggle, impact sorting, raw JSON view, and dedicated render targets for each tab.

followup:
  verification:
    - Open the deployed mcp_debug page and verify all tabs render on mobile and desktop.
    - Confirm search and detail modal still work with live data.
    - Confirm live/cached data switching still works.
    - Run any chaba-h3 build checks or deploy pipeline.
  rollback_plan:
    - In chaba-h3, run git revert 1559596 to restore previous index.html and app.js.
  handoff: []
  deferred: []
report:
  status: completed
  completed_at: "2026-08-20"
  summary: |
    The MCP Debug savings report was refactored from a single long page into six focused tabs.
    The help panel is now collapsed by default. The Commands tab supports sorting by savings %
    (efficiency), chars saved (impact), raw size, and command name. Presets and raw-allowed
    prefixes each have their own tab. The Raw JSON tab exposes the full mcp-savings payload.
    The implementation is zero-dependency and preserves existing search, detail modal, and
    live/cached data behavior.
  metrics:
    - file_changes: 2
    - new_sort_options: 4
    - tabs_added: 6
  links:
    - title: Commit (chaba-h3)
      url: "chaba-h3: 1559596"
    - title: Commit (SSOT job)
      url: "chaba: fea03b7"
  kb_review:
    - Tab-based separation and impact-first sorting improved the MCP Debug report's usability.
    - Zero-dependency front-end changes keep the chaba-h3 deployment simple.
  lessons_learned:
    - Keep first visual improvements additive (sort options, tabs) before introducing chart libraries.
  handoff: []
  deferred: []

config:
  version: 1
  created_at: "2026-08-20"
  last_updated: "2026-08-20"
  maintainer: tony
  related_files:
    - chaba-h3/public/apps/docs/mcp_debug/index.html
    - chaba-h3/public/apps/docs/mcp_debug/app.js

```

# Safe Focus Continuous Processing

Add a parallel safe-focus lane so the main session can keep picking work while side sessions prepare the inbox

## File Path
`jobs/workflow/2026-08-18-safe-focus-continuous-processing.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Safe Focus Continuous Processing
subtitle: Add a parallel safe-focus lane so the main session can keep picking work while side sessions prepare the inbox
icon: target

planning:
  goal: |
    Close the gap identified in the focus workflow by enabling a "main focus processing session"
    to continuously pick up safe-to-run foci while other sessions work on other tasks or add
    new items to the inbox, without parking the active shared/branch focus.
  scope: |
    - Extend the SSOT schema for foci/inbox items to declare whether a focus is safe to run in parallel.
    - Add a Ready (Safe) section to ssot.focus.current.yml.
    - Extend mcp_focus with a safe_next / ready_queue mode.
    - Update focus-dispatcher.py to auto-dispatch safe foci without parking active focus.
    - Add session ownership/lock fields to active foci and subtasks.
    - Update subagent-focus-triage and contracts to handle safe_parallel items.
    - Validate with ssot-validate and a few test scenarios.
  out_of_scope: |
    - Changing the core "one shared + one branch" active-focus limits.
    - Auto-invoking subagents across hosts that require user approval.
    - Any work that calls the Gemini API or other rate-limited external services.
  success_criteria:
    - The focus-dispatcher can list and activate a safe focus while an active focus remains in progress.
    - ssot.focus.current.yml shows a Ready (Safe) section populated from the inbox.
    - mcp_focus can recommend the next safe focus without modifying active focus state.
    - Two sessions cannot race on the same active focus because ownership/lock fields are checked.
    - All SSOT files validate cleanly with ssot-validate.
  risks:
    - "Over-parallelization: safe criteria may be too permissive and cause resource conflicts. Mitigation: strict safe_to_parallel criteria and branch/host isolation."
    - "Race conditions: multiple sessions may still try to update the same focus file. Mitigation: session ownership and atomic git writes."
    - "Scope creep: the dispatcher could grow into a full orchestrator. Mitigation: keep it to one safe lane and one main active lane."
  resources:
    - docs/ssot/ssot.focus.current.yml
    - docs/ssot/ssot.focus.yml
    - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.mcp-focus.yml
    - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.focus-dispatcher.yml
    - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.subagent-focus-triage.yml
    - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.focus.triage.yml
    - scripts/focus-dispatcher.py
    - reports/NEXT_FOCUS.md
  owner: tony
  estimated_duration: 2-3 sessions
  related_focus:
    - label: Safe focus continuous processing
      file: docs/ssot/ssot.focus.yml

processing:
  status: in_progress
  started_at: "2026-08-18"
  steps:
    - id: 1
      label: Add safe_to_parallel schema and triage criteria
      status: completed
      completed: "2026-08-18"
      notes: Updated ssot.focus.triage.yml with safe_to_parallel criteria and subagent schema. Updated focus-inbox/TEMPLATE.yml with safe_to_parallel and ownership fields.
    - id: 2
      label: Add Ready (Safe) section to ssot.focus.current.yml
      status: completed
      completed: "2026-08-18"
      notes: Added Ready (Safe) section to ssot.focus.current.yml.
    - id: 3
      label: Extend mcp_focus with safe_next mode
      status: completed
      completed: "2026-08-18"
      notes: Added safe_next and ready_queue modes to mcp_debug/focus.py and both MCP servers; verified status and safe_next output.
    - id: 4
      label: Update focus-dispatcher to auto-dispatch safe foci
      status: completed
      completed: "2026-08-18"
      notes: Added --safe-dispatch to scripts/focus-dispatcher.py, safe_to_dispatch in triage.py, add_ready_safe in actions.py. Dry-run and live run tested with no safe foci.
    - id: 5
      label: Add session ownership/lock fields to active foci
      status: completed
      completed: "2026-08-18"
      notes: Added ownership block to make_focus_item and the active Safe focus in ssot.focus.current.yml.
    - id: 6
      label: Update subagent-focus-triage and contracts
      status: completed
      completed: "2026-08-18"
      notes: Updated ssot.subagent-focus-triage.yml to include safe_to_parallel and Ready (Safe) guidance.
    - id: 7
      label: Validate and test the workflow
      status: completed
      completed: "2026-08-18"
      notes: SSOT validation clean; focus-dispatcher --safe-dispatch and mcp_focus safe_next/ready_queue verified.
  decisions: []
  changes: []

followup:
  verification:
    - Run ssot-validate on all modified SSOT files.
    - Run focus-dispatcher.py --dry-run to confirm safe-focus selection.
    - Run mcp_focus mode=safe_next to confirm it returns a ready safe focus.
    - Simulate two sessions updating different parts of the focus SSOT without conflicts.
  rollback_plan:
```

# Devin MCP Tools Configuration

MCP server definitions, tool inventory, and launch configuration

## File Path
`ssot.devin.tools.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
# Config-type SSOT: MCP server configuration and tool reference for Devin/Windsurf
title: Devin MCP Tools Configuration
subtitle: MCP server definitions, tool inventory, and launch configuration

# Notes
# - Consolidated configuration: SSOT-based generation with profile switching (2026-08-07)
# - SSOT file: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.mcp.yml (single source of truth)
# - Generation script: scripts/generate-mcp-config.py
# - Devin config: ~/.config/devin/mcp_config.json (generated from SSOT)
# - Windsurf config: ~/.config/windsurf/mcp_config.json (can be generated from SSOT)
# - Wrapper scripts: Centralized in ~/.config/devin/mcp-scripts/
# - Filtering: mcp-filter for token optimization (Yomi, GitHub, PostgreSQL)
# - Virtual environment: /tmp/mcp-filter-venv/ for mcp-filter dependencies
# - Profile switching: home (tony-omen) vs mobile (dynamic IP)

# Configuration Generation
# Usage:
#   python3 scripts/generate-mcp-config.py --profile home
#   python3 scripts/generate-mcp-config.py --profile mobile --current-ip 192.168.1.100
#   python3 scripts/generate-mcp-config.py --auto-detect

# Consolidation Status
# - ✅ Wrapper scripts centralized to ~/.config/devin/mcp-scripts/
# - ✅ SSOT configuration created (infrastructure/ssot.mcp.yml)
# - ✅ Profile switching implemented (home/mobile)
# - ✅ Configuration generation script functional
# - ✅ Environment URL standardization
# - ✅ Testing completed (GitHub, docs MCP servers verified)

mcp:
  github: GitHub integration (filtered via mcp-filter for token optimization).
  mcp-gpu: Local GPU control (imagen2, llama queue).
  mcp-llama: Local Llama.cpp server.
  mcp-weaviate: Weaviate vector database integration.
  playlive: Playlive browser automation (consolidated local & remote).
  postgres: PostgreSQL database operations (filtered via mcp-filter for CRUD only).
  yomi: LINE conversation viewer (filtered via mcp-filter for essential tools).
  alphavantage: Alpha Vantage financial data API.
  docs: Documentation search server (chaba project docs).
  docs-trade: Documentation search server (trade project docs).

# Consolidated Structure
consolidated_structure:
  ssot_source: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.mcp.yml
  generation_script: scripts/generate-mcp-config.py
  wrapper_scripts: ~/.config/devin/mcp-scripts/
  backup_dir: ~/.config/devin/mcp-backups/
  profiles:
    home: .local hostnames, port 8008 for llama
    mobile: dynamic IP placeholders, port 8001 for llama

# Centralized Wrapper Scripts
wrappers:
  base_dir: ~/.config/devin/mcp-scripts/
  scripts:
    - mcp-single-instance.sh (single-instance manager)
    - run-github-filtered-mcp.sh (GitHub with filtering)
    - run-github-mcp.sh (GitHub base wrapper)
    - run-postgres-filtered-mcp.sh (PostgreSQL with filtering)
    - run-postgres-crud-mcp.sh (PostgreSQL CRUD wrapper)
    - run-yomi-filtered-mcp.sh (Yomi with filtering)
    - run-llama-mcp.sh (Llama server wrapper)

# Profile Configuration
profiles:
  home:
    network: 192.168.1.0/24
    hostname_pattern: .local
    llama_url: http://tony-omen:11434
    imagen_url: http://tony-omen:8080/apps/imagen2/api
    playlive_url: http://tony-omen:9230
    weaviate_url: http://tony-omen:8082
    postgres_url: postgresql://tony-omen:5432

  mobile:
    network: dynamic
    hostname_pattern: tony-omen
    llama_url: http://tony-omen:11434
    imagen_url: http://tony-omen:8080/apps/imagen2/api
    playlive_url: http://tony-dell:9230
    weaviate_url: http://tony-dell:8084
    postgres_url: postgresql://tony-dell:5432

# MCP filter virtual environment
mcp-filter-venv: /tmp/mcp-filter-venv/ (installed 2026-08-07 for GitHub MCP fix)

# Related SSOT Files
related_files:
  - infrastructure/ssot.mcp.yml (SSOT for MCP configuration)
  - ssot.mysystem.home.yml (home environment profile)
  - ssot.mysystem.mobile.yml (mobile environment profile)
  - infrastructure/ssot.health.home.yml (home health checks)
  - infrastructure/ssot.health.mobile.yml (mobile health checks)
  - ssot.token-optimization.yml (token optimization strategy)
```

# SSOT File Control

Governance and workflow for creating, updating, and validating SSOT YAML files

## File Path
`ssot.file-control.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: SSOT File Control
subtitle: Governance and workflow for creating, updating, and validating SSOT YAML files
icon: 🗂️

ideas:
  - Define a lightweight, repeatable lifecycle for SSOT files so contributors spend less time deciding where or how to edit.
  - Keep naming, placement, validation, search, and indexing conventions in one canonical place.
  - Prefer automated checks (ssot-validate, MDDB sync) over manual review.

sections:
  - title: Scope and Ownership
    icon: 📁
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Scope
        text: All canonical SSOT YAML files under docs/ssot/ and docs/ssot/*/
      - label: Owner
        text: Project maintainer (tony); day-to-day updates by an assistant or contributor with repository write access
      - label: Exclusions
        text: template.yml and apps/template.app.yml are boilerplate for new files and are not controlled SSOT records
      - label: Prohibited content
        text: Do not store runtime or generated data, secrets, or non-canonical copies in SSOT files

  - title: Naming and Placement
    icon: 🏷️
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Prefix
        text: All SSOT files must start with ssot. (except templates)
      - label: kebab-case
        text: Use lowercase words separated by hyphens, e.g. ssot.file-control.yml
      - label: Core directory
        text: docs/ssot/ — core/cross-project policy and tooling
      - label: Infrastructure directory
        text: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ — hosts, services, containers, networking
      - label: Apps directory
        text: docs/ssot/apps/ — application-specific data
      - label: New directory threshold
        text: Create a new subdirectory only when at least 3 related files exist
      - label: One file per topic
        text: A topic must have exactly one SSOT file. Older versions are archived to ssot.<topic>.archive.yml, e.g. ssot.file-control.yml → ssot.file-control.archive.yml

  - title: Bloat and Archiving
    icon: 📦
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Size review threshold
        text: Review a file for splitting when it exceeds 350 lines, 10 sections, or 45 items (approximately the 90th percentile of the current SSOT corpus)
      - label: Hard split threshold
        text: Archive or split a file before the next commit if it exceeds 750 lines, 12 sections, or 60 items (approximately the 95th percentile / current maximum)
      - label: Archive pattern
        text: Archive a completed topic to ssot.<topic>.archive.yml. If the archive itself exceeds the hard split threshold, split it by period, e.g. ssot.<topic>.archive.2026.yml or ssot.<topic>.archive.2026-Q3.yml
      - label: Avoid duplicating sections
        text: When a file grows, create new focused SSOT files rather than duplicating or copy-pasting sections into other files

  - title: Change Workflow
    icon: 🔄
    layout: timeline
    items:
      - label: Draft
        text: Copy docs/ssot/template.yml, fill title, sections, and config, then delete the placeholder comments
      - label: Validate
        text: Run the ssot-validate skill before committing; fix syntax and structural errors
      - label: Register
        text: Add the file to docs/ssot/ssot.index.yml under the correct category
      - label: Log significant changes
        text: For policy or structural changes, append a concise entry to docs/ssot/CHANGELOG.md
      - label: Commit
        text: Use a short commit with an allowed prefix from .windsurfrules and reference the SSOT file

  - title: Search and Discovery
    icon: 🔍
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Primary search
        text: Use MDDB semantic search for conceptual SSOT and documentation queries
      - label: Exact SSOT search
        text: Use the ssot-search skill for exact YAML pattern matching; fall back to grep docs/ssot/**/*.yml only if the skill is unavailable
      - label: Master index
        text: Consult docs/ssot/ssot.index.yml for the authoritative list of SSOT files

  - title: Validation and Quality
    icon: ✅
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Tool
        text: Use the ssot-validate skill to check YAML syntax and SSOT structure
      - label: Rules
        text: Follow the conventions in docs/ssot/ssot.validation-patterns.yml
      - label: Pre-commit
        text: Always validate before committing; invalid SSOT files break the MDDB sync and search index
```

```yaml
subtitle: Roadmap for reducing bloat, redundancy, obsolescence, data-isolation violations, and inconsistency in SSOT YAML files
```
