```yaml
  - SSOT files are growing; the largest is over 1,200 lines and several exceed the 95th-percentile hard threshold.
  - Bloat is the most urgent dimension because it directly affects token cost, search quality, and merge safety.
  - "Data isolation is a cross-cutting concern: it prevents secrets, host-specific values, and runtime-generated data from leaking into canonical SSOTs."
  - Redundancy and obsolescence are the next-largest sources of noise and drift.
  - Optimization should be incremental, measured, and automated where possible.

        priority: high
      - label: Data isolation

Move health snapshots, mcp-savings caches, conversation indexes, and build artifacts to runtime data directories or per-host SSOTs such as ssot.mysystem.home.yml and ssot.mysystem.mobile.yml

        priority: medium

        priority: medium

        priority: medium

        priority: medium

        text: |

          actions without writing runtime metrics into canonical SSOT files.
        priority: medium

        text: Replace verbose inline text with action_items, move long prose to docs/kb/ or ssot-summaries, and compress auto-generated fields that are no longer useful
        priority: low
      - label: Cross-reference accuracy
        text: Validate that related_files, path, and related_ssot entries point to existing files; keep ssot.index.yml in sync with the actual docs/ssot/ tree
        priority: medium

  - title: Phasing and Priorities
    icon: 🗓️
    layout: timeline

      - label: Phase 1 — Bloat and data isolation

        status: completed

  - title: Tooling and Automation
    icon: 🛠️
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Validation
        text: Use the ssot-validate skill for syntax, structure, duplicates, and bloat thresholds
      - label: Data isolation checks
        text: Add ssot-validate rules to flag hardcoded IPs, secrets, and generated or timestamp fields in canonical SSOT files
      - label: Search
        text: Use ssot-search for exact YAML patterns and MDDB semantic search for conceptual overlap
      - label: Metrics
        text: Track line, section, and item counts via scripts/ssot-validate-all.mjs and store per-run snapshots
      - label: Archiving
        text: Use ssot.<topic>.archive.<period>.yml for large historical datasets, following ssot.file-control.yml

  - title: Metrics and Success Criteria
    icon: ✅
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Bloat
        text: Zero files above the 750-line/12-section/60-item hard threshold; fewer than 5 above the 350-line review threshold
      - label: Data isolation
        text: No standard SSOT contains runtime-generated values, hardcoded IPs, secrets, or large raw indexes; per-host and generated data lives in ssot.mysystem.*.yml or runtime data directories
      - label: Redundancy
        text: No pair of SSOTs with >50% overlapping labels or verbatim text
      - label: Obsolescence
        text: All completed improvement items moved to archive; no focus-inbox item older than 30 days left unprocessed
      - label: Consistency
        text: All standard SSOTs pass ssot-validate and have a matching ssot.index.yml entry
      - label: Conflict
        text: No item is both active and completed; no hardcoded IP appears alongside a hostname for the same endpoint

  - title: Continuous Optimization Run
    icon: ♻
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Goal
        text: Run optimization checks continuously without manual activation so bloat, drift, and isolation violations are caught before they become cleanup projects.
      - label: Trigger
        text: Daily as part of the overnight jobs and on every ssot-validate run.
      - label: Optimizer script
        text: scripts/ssot-optimize.mjs reads every SSOT YAML, computes line/section/item counts, flags bloat, data-isolation, obsolescence, redundancy, and conflict candidates, then writes a report.
      - label: Report outputs
        text: reports/SSOT_OPTIMIZATION_METRICS.json (per-file metrics) and reports/SSOT_OPTIMIZATION_SUGGESTIONS.md (top candidates for the day)
      - label: Non-destructive rule

      - label: Delta tracking
        text: Each run compares to reports/SSOT_OPTIMIZATION_METRICS.previous.json; the suggestions report highlights new regressions and confirms previous ones.
      - label: Weekly review gate
        text: On Sunday, the overnight run also emits a weekly aggregate and archives the daily metrics to data/ssot-optimization/<week>.json.
      - label: Manual override
        text: A user can run `node scripts/ssot-optimize.mjs --suggest` to see the report without committing; run `--apply` only after review and only on a small set of files.

        status: in_progress
```

# Current Focus

Common workflow for session start and focus disposition

## File Path
`ssot.focus.current.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Current Focus
subtitle: Common workflow for session start and focus disposition
icon: target
workflow:
  - Assistant must read this SSOT at the start of each session - Read the most recent entry in docs/ssot/ssot.focus.sessions.yml
    to pick up pending follow-ups
  - Before any docs/ or SSOT read/grep, run `mcp_call_tool mddb semantic_search` on the request topic and record the query in
    the active focus's request_log
  - List docs/ssot/focus-inbox/*.yml at session start and summarize any pending items for triage
  - Match the user request against active shared and branch focuses first
  - If it matches, append it to that item's request_log and do the work inside that focus
  - If it is a small standalone action, add it to quick_wins and complete it immediately
  - If it is new strategic work, add it to the backlog in ssot.focus.yml with priority and ask the user to activate it
  - If it is a new focus item from another session, add it as an inbox file in docs/ssot/focus-inbox/ for triage
  - For backlog review, archived focuses, or focus history, read the full ssot.focus.yml
  - At session end, update subtask status and append a session summary to ssot.focus.sessions.yml
  - When an inbox item is activated, merge it into this file and git mv the source file to docs/ssot/focus-inbox/processed/
  - If the request can be decomposed into subtasks, use the decompose action to create or update a focus with subtasks before
    starting
  - If the disposition is unclear, call mcp_focus(request, mode=recommend) and follow the returned action (continue, quick_win,
    decompose, triage_backlog, triage_inbox, draft_inbox); see ssot.mcp-focus.yml for the machine-readable tree
mcp_focus:
  tool: mcp_focus
  source: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.mcp-focus.yml
  use_when: "At session start or when the user request is ambiguous. Call mcp_focus with the user

    request and mode=recommend; use the returned action as the first disposition.

    mode=status is a read-only way to list active foci and quick wins.

    "
  actions:
    continue: The request matches an active focus or no request was given; keep working on the active focus.
    quick_win: The request is small and concrete; add to Quick Wins and complete immediately.
    decompose:
      The request is too large for a quick win but can be split into subtasks; decompose it into a focus and start
      the first subtask.
    triage_backlog: The request matches or should go to ssot.focus.yml Backlog; ask the user to activate.
    triage_inbox: The request matches an unprocessed focus-inbox draft; review/activate it.
    draft_inbox: No match; return an in-memory draft inbox YAML for the user to review before saving.
decision_tree:
  question: How should this user request be disposed?
  note: "The canonical machine-readable tree is in docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.mcp-focus.yml.

    This tree is the assistant-level guide; each case maps to the mcp_focus action listed below.

    "
  cases:
    - case: matches_active
      mcp_focus_action: continue
      condition: Request matches an active shared/branch focus label, subtask, or quick win
      action: Append to the item's request_log and do the work inside that focus
      examples:
        - let's process focus matched to Service Failures Detected and then Security Vulnerabilities Found
        - do all the streamlining suggestions matched to Streamline focus-driven workflow
    - case: quick_win
      mcp_focus_action: quick_win
      condition: Meets all quick_win_criteria below
      action: Add to Quick Wins, complete immediately, and append to Focus History at session end
      examples:
        - Reduce focus.current bloat
        - Tony-Dell wired DHCP release and renew
    - case: live_bug_report
      mcp_focus_action: continue
      condition: User reports an error in a deployed page or app and asks to add it to focus
      action: Activate as a high-priority branch focus; record the exact URL/error and the chosen fix. Do not default to inbox.
      examples:
        - mcp_debug H3 page mixed-content (HTTP/HTTPS) error
    - case: new_strategic_work
      mcp_focus_action: triage
      condition: Multi-step or multi-session work that requires planning and tracking
      action: Add to Backlog in ssot.focus.yml with priority; do not start until user activates
      examples:
        - Streamline focus-driven workflow
        - Request-to-Focus Workflow redesign
    - case: decompose
      mcp_focus_action: decompose
      condition: Request is too large for a quick win but can be broken into smaller, trackable subtasks
      action: Decompose into subtasks, add to the active focus or an inbox item, and start the first subtask
      examples:
        - Decompose the podman migration into Quadlet, container move, and SSOT update tasks
        - Break the visual-capture workflow into capture, triage, and annotate steps
    - case: side_session_or_ambiguous
      mcp_focus_action: draft_inbox
      condition: New idea from another session or request is vague and needs triage
      action: Save as docs/ssot/focus-inbox/<session>.yml with status draft and missing_info
      examples:
        - Service Failures Detected from overnight assessment
        - Security Vulnerabilities Found from overnight assessment
    - case: auto_generated_alert
      mcp_focus_action: triage
      condition: Auto-generated item from overnight assessment with missing details
      action: Gather facts with allowed MCP tools, classify as hard or transient, then fix or document accepted state
      examples:
        - Service Failures Detected investigated with mcp-health; .local health-check timeouts, not hard failures
        - Security Vulnerabilities Found had no actionable scan output; documented no immediate patches required
    - case: interrupt
      mcp_focus_action: continue
      condition: New strategic work that must start now while an active shared focus is still incomplete
      action:
        Park the active shared focus, activate the new work as a branch focus, and return to the parked focus when the
        branch is completed
      examples:
        - Reviewing and implementing focus validation/parking while the mcp-debug shared focus stays parked
    - case: no_active_or_inbox
      mcp_focus_action: triage_backlog or triage_inbox
      condition: No active focus and no inbox items
      action: Suggest the highest triage_score backlog item in reports/NEXT_FOCUS.md; do not auto-activate unless requested
      examples:
        - Dispatcher suggests MacBook macOS App Development when the queue is empty
    - case: requires_mcp_data
      mcp_focus_action: n/a
      condition: Decision needs health, system, or infrastructure data
      action: Use the relevant MCP server per policy, document source, and do not take destructive actions without user confirmation
      examples:
        - mcp-health used for Service Failures investigation
    - case: pre_action_summary
      mcp_focus_action: pre_action
      condition: Before beginning any non-trivial work, or when the user asks for the current focus landscape
      action:
        Call mcp_focus with mode pre_action to get active foci, duplicate/historical matches, and related decision-tree
        entries, then present a concise summary and ask for confirmation before proceeding
      examples:
        - User asks 'what is our focus?' or 'let's plan to finish all backlog'
        - Assistant is about to start a multi-step focus after a request
quick_win_criteria:
  - Single file or single small edit set
  - No new dependencies, installs, or infrastructure changes
  - No deploy, restart, or destructive operation required
  - Can be verified by a single command or small test
  - Completable in under 5 minutes of assistant time
  - User has not asked for a decision tree or design review
validation:
  max_active_shared_focus: 1
  max_active_branch_focus: 1
  require_priority: true
  require_tags: true
  require_request_log: true
  require_subagent_dispatchable: true
  allowed_subagent_hosts:
    - tony_dell
    - local
    - macbook
config:
  version: 2
  last_updated: "2026-08-19"
  maintainer: tony
  full_focus_file: docs/ssot/ssot.focus.yml
  inbox_dir: docs/ssot/focus-inbox
  inbox_processed_dir: docs/ssot/focus-inbox/processed
  validation_enabled: true
  related_files:
    - docs/ssot/ssot.focus.yml
    - docs/ssot/ssot.focus.decisions.yml
    - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.focus.triage.yml
    - docs/ssot/ssot.index.yml
    - docs/ssot/focus-inbox
    - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.subagent-focus-triage.yml
    - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.focus-dispatcher.yml
sources:
  - label: Active focuses
    file: docs/ssot/ssot.focus.current.active.yml
  - label: Backlog and quick wins
    file: docs/ssot/ssot.focus.current.backlog.yml
```

# Focus Sessions

Lightweight per-session plan and follow-up log

## File Path
`ssot.focus.sessions.yml`

```yaml
title: Focus Sessions
subtitle: Lightweight per-session plan and follow-up log
icon: 📒
version: 1
overview:
  purpose: "Keep a chronological, low-noise record of what was planned, what was done, and what

    needs follow-up for each focus session. This is not a duplicate of ssot.focus.yml

    history; it is a short-term working memory for the assistant and the user.

    "
  scope: active and recently completed focuses only
  max_in_memory: 10
  archive_to: docs/ssot/ssot.focus.yml history section when a focus is archived
principles:
  - Append-only. Never rewrite past entries; create a new entry each session.
  - One entry per session, tied to one focus by label.
  - Skip empty fields. If there is no follow-up, omit it.
  - No full duplication of ssot.focus.current.yml or ssot.focus.yml.
  - Keep text terse; long artifacts belong in reports/ or KB.
entry_schema:
  date: ISO date of the session
  session: optional session id
  focus: label of the active focus being worked on
  source: how the session started (e.g., user request, continue, dispatcher)
  plan:
    - concise bullet of what was planned to do
  done:
    - concise bullet of what was actually completed
  follow_up:
    - next step, unresolved question, or deferred work
  next_action: one-line recommendation for the next session
  decisions:
    - optional list of key technical or focus decisions made during the session
    - each decision should include id, title, and chosen option
  kb_items:
    - optional list of KB entries created or updated
workflow:
  - At session start, read the most recent session entry for the active focus to pick up follow_ups.
  - If the user asks for a plan, create a new entry with plan filled in and done/follow_up empty.
  - At session end, update done and follow_up in a new entry (do not edit the plan entry).
  - The mcp_focus tool may read the latest follow_up when there is no explicit user request.
  - The focus-dispatcher may append a summary entry after auto-activation.
```

# Request-Driven Focus & Task Tracking

Every assistant request is checked against active tasks and assigned or queued

## File Path
`ssot.focus.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Request-Driven Focus & Task Tracking
subtitle: Every assistant request is checked against active tasks and assigned or queued
icon: target
ideas:
  - Capture every user request as a tracked item instead of letting it float between sessions
  - Match each request to an active task, subtask, quick win, or backlog item before acting
  - Limit active work to one shared focus and one branch focus to prevent fragmentation
  - Archive completed or parked strategic focuses while keeping them searchable
  - Review focus at the start and end of every assistant session
workflow:
  - For routine session starts, read ssot.focus.current.yml for workflow/decision tree, then ssot.focus.current.active.yml for
    active foci and ssot.focus.current.backlog.yml for quick wins
  - Use this file (ssot.focus.yml) for backlog, archived focuses, and focus history
  - For each user request, first match it against active tasks and their subtasks in ssot.focus.current.active.yml
  - If it matches, append it to that item's request_log in ssot.focus.current.active.yml and do the work inside that focus
  - If it is a small standalone action, add it to quick_wins in ssot.focus.current.backlog.yml and complete it immediately
  - If it is new strategic work, add it to backlog in this file with priority and ask the user to activate it
  - Keep at most one active shared focus and one active branch focus at a time
  - Merge completed branch work into master at the end of the session; do not let feature branches diverge more than one session
  - Delete or archive feature branches after merging to keep the branch list short
  - Update subtask status and append completed quick wins to focus history in this file at session end
validation:
  max_active_shared_focus: 1
  max_active_branch_focus: 1
  require_priority: true
  require_tags: true
  require_request_log: true
  archive_completed_after_days: 14
  completed_at_required: true
  completed_at_note: "`completed_at` (ISO 8601 date) is required on completed focus items and

    completed subtasks.  The mcp-focus server uses it to avoid stale warnings.

    Top-level foci also keep `completed` for human readability; subtasks use

    `completed_at`.
```

# Git Workflow Policy

Rules and hooks to keep master history clean and avoid accidental mega-merges

## File Path
`ssot.git-policy.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Git Workflow Policy
subtitle: Rules and hooks to keep master history clean and avoid accidental mega-merges
icon: git-branch

policy:
  - id: no-merge-commits-on-master
    name: No non-fast-forward merges into master
    applies_to:
      - master
    rule: |
      Pushes to master must be fast-forward merges.  Non-fast-forward merges
      (i.e. merge commits) are blocked by the pre-push hook.
    how_to: |
      Before merging a feature/experiment branch into master:
        git checkout <branch>
        git rebase master
        git checkout master
        git merge --ff-only <branch>
      If ff-only fails, rebase again.
    exception: |
      Only the release-train branch may produce a true merge commit, and it
      must be reviewed first.

  - id: rebase-experiment-branches
    name: Rebase experiment branches before landing
    applies_to:
      - experiment/*
    rule: |
      An experiment branch must be rebased onto the current master before it
      is merged or pushed to master.  This keeps master linear and makes the
      merge commit small.
    how_to: |
      git fetch origin
      git rebase origin/master
      # resolve conflicts, then run the full SSOT/validation suite

  - id: large-file-gate
    name: Large data files must not enter the repo
    applies_to:
      - all branches
    rule: |
      CSV, Parquet, JSON data dumps, images, and model weights should not be
      committed directly.  The pre-push hook rejects new files larger than
      1 MB and all CSV files unless explicitly allow-listed.
    how_to: |
      - Keep raw data under /data, S3, or a git-ignored local mirror.
      - If a small CSV must be committed, add it to the pre-push allow-list.

  - id: master-is-healthy
    name: master must pass CI before any push
    applies_to:
      - master
    rule: |
      The pre-push hook runs SSOT validation, ref validation, and the YAML
      syntax check.  A push is rejected if any check fails.

hooks:
  pre_push:
    script: scripts/git/hooks/pre-push
    path: .git/hooks/pre-push
    install: |
      git config --local core.hooksPath scripts/git/hooks
      chmod +x scripts/git/hooks/pre-push
      touch scripts/git/hooks/csv-allow-list.txt
    checks:
      - Block non-fast-forward pushes to master
      - Block new files > 1 MB
      - Block CSV files not in the allow-list
      - Run SSOT validation
      - Run SSOT ref validation

session_boundary_policy:
  - id: one-focus-per-session
    name: One active focus per session
    rule: |
      Each assistant session owns exactly one active focus.  The assistant
      must not start work on another focus or branch unless the user explicitly
      asks for it.
    how_to: |
      - Read ssot.focus.current.active.yml at the start of every session.
      - Log quick wins (<5 min) inside the current session.
      - Park anything that would require switching branches.
  - id: auto-commit-on-done
    name: Auto-commit when a focus is done
    rule: |
      When a focus or subtask is completed, the assistant must run
      `scripts/focus-complete.sh` to validate, stage, and commit the related
      changes immediately.
    how_to: |
      scripts/focus-complete.sh "prefix: short description"
    what_it_does:
      - Runs SSOT ref validation
      - Stages all tracked files (excluding data and generated files)
      - Creates a single commit with the provided message
      - Does not push unless the user asks

worktree_policy:
  - Clean worktrees should be removed after the branch is merged.
  - Dirty worktrees must be committed or stashed before the worktree is removed.
  - Each worktree must map to one branch; do not create multiple worktrees for the same branch.
```

```yaml
          - Purpose: Prevents starting work before prerequisites are ready


          - Format: Array of strings or single string



          **dependency_reason:** Explanation of why dependency exists

          **blocks:** List of improvements that cannot start until this one completes

          - Purpose: Identifies downstream impact of this improvement

          **blocking_reason:** Explanation of why this improvement blocks others

          **technical_impact:** Technical improvement (1-10 scale)

          - 10: Critical technical debt, security vulnerability


          - 7-9: Significant technical improvement, performance gain


          - 4-6: Moderate technical improvement, code quality


          - 1-3: Low technical impact, minor cleanup


          **user_experience_impact:** User experience value (1-10 scale)


          - Usability, performance, reliability, features


          - 10: Critical UX issue, user-facing outage


          - 7-9: Significant UX improvement, major feature


          - 4-6: Moderate UX improvement, minor feature


          - 1-3: Low UX impact, polish


          **cost_savings_impact:** Cost reduction value (1-10 scale)


          - Infrastructure costs, operational efficiency, time savings


          - 10: Major cost reduction, significant savings


          - 7-9: Moderate cost reduction, measurable savings


          - 4-6: Minor cost reduction, some efficiency gains


          - 1-3: Minimal cost impact, negligible savings


          **impact_summary:** Brief description of expected impact


          - Example: "Reduces infrastructure costs by 20% through GPU optimization"


          - Purpose: Quick understanding of improvement value


          **Priority Calculation:** Weighted average of impact scores
```

title: Devin renderer-crash recovery + NM wifi nag misattribution (2026-09-22)

docs.contentMd:
# Devin renderer-crash recovery + NM wifi nag misattribution (2026-09-22)

What happened when devin-desktop died on tony-dell, and why NetworkManager keeps asking for a wifi password that is actually correct

## File Path
`ssot.learning.devin-crash-wifi-nag.2026-09-22.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Devin renderer-crash recovery + NM wifi nag misattribution (2026-09-22)
subtitle: What happened when devin-desktop died on tony-dell, and why NetworkManager keeps asking for a wifi password that is actually correct
date: "2026-09-22"
icon: 🧠
context: |
  devin-desktop disappeared from the tony-dell :1 seat, and separately tony-dell kept
  prompting for the "Naris" wifi password. Both were diagnosed and fixed in one session.

lessons:
  - id: devin-watchdog-kill-cascade
    title: Watchdog renderer kill cascades into full devin-desktop shutdown
    severity: medium
    symptom: |
      devin-desktop completely gone from :1 — no processes at all, not just a wedged
      window. watchdog.log showed a renderer running ~100-120% interval CPU for 3
      consecutive checks, killed at 10:30; main process then logged
      "Render frame was disposed before WebFrameMain could be accessed" and shut down
      at 10:37 ("WindsurfWindowsMainManager: Shutdown initiated").
    root_cause: |
      devin-watchdog kills a hot renderer to recover the window, but this time the
      killed render frame was treated as a fatal window error by the main process,
      which destroyed the window and exited. The XDG autostart only fires at session
      start, so nothing relaunched it.
    fix: |
      `systemctl --user restart xfce-seat.service` on tony-dell — the autostart entry
      relaunches devin cleanly inside the new session. Do NOT launch devin by hand on
      :1 while a seat session is alive (races autostart -> duplicate instances).
      Verify with `xdotool search --class devin-desktop` + `xwininfo` (main window
      should be IsViewable; a 10x10 IsUnMapped "devin-desktop" window is the normal
      Electron helper, not the UI).
    prevention: |
      A killed renderer should not kill the app. If this recurs, consider tracking
      whether watchdog kills correlate with full exits — the watchdog may need to
      restart the whole app instead of just the renderer.

  - id: devin-summaries-tony-dell-gap
    title: tony-dell devin session summaries never reach ada memory
    severity: medium
    symptom: |
      `~/.local/share/devin/cli/summaries/history_*.md` accumulates on tony-dell
      (41 files) but none appear in the `ada-ha-bank-devin-tony` MDDB collection.
    root_cause: |
      `sync-devin-summaries.py` only runs inside `ada-memory-pull.service`, which is
      installed on tony-omen (hourly). It reads the LOCAL summaries dir, so it only
      ships tony-omen's sessions (~1044 files). tony-dell has no ada-memory timers.
    fix: |
      APPLIED 2026-09-22 (option a): devin-summaries-sync.{service,timer}
      installed on tony-dell (chaba/systemd/), hourly at :45, pushes this
      host's summaries to MDDB idc01 (default URL already points there).
      First run synced 10 files; registered in ssot.audit.hosts.yml.
      NOTE: headless `devin -p` sessions do NOT write history_*.md — see
      jobs/ada/2026-09-22-ada-devin-dispatch.yml step 4.
      Still open if desired: same per-host pusher for tony-omen already
      covered by ada-memory-pull; idc01 has no devin sessions.

  - id: nm-wrong-key-misattribution
    title: NetworkManager reports WRONG_KEY and prompts for password on flaky USB wifi
    severity: low
    symptom: |
      tony-dell kept popping a wifi password prompt for SSID "Naris" even though the
      stored PSK was correct and had worked days earlier.
    root_cause: |
      The MT7601U USB dongle at -73dBm intermittently drops 4-way handshake replies
      (disconnect reason=15 = handshake timeout). wpa_supplicant reports the failure
      as "pre-shared key may be incorrect" / WRONG_KEY; NM then marks the connection
      `need-auth` and nm-applet prompts — misattributing RF/driver flakiness to a
      bad password. Verify the AP's actual security first:
      `sudo iw dev <if> scan` showed Naris is plain WPA2-PSK/CCMP (no SAE/PMF), and
      `sudo nmcli con up Naris` connected fine with the stored key.
    fix: |
      `sudo nmcli con mod Naris connection.autoconnect-retries 0` — retry forever
      instead of entering need-auth. Persisted: nmcli wrote it back into the
      netplan yaml (/etc/netplan/90-NM-*.yaml), so it survives reboot.
    prevention: |
      Before believing a WRONG_KEY report, force `sudo nmcli con up <ssid>` once —
      if it connects, the key is fine and the problem is link quality/driver.
      Note: nmcli and wifi rescan are polkit-restricted over ssh; use sudo.

```

# Post-Restart Recovery Lessons (2026-09-21)

Issues found after rebooting tony-dell and tony-omen, and their permanent fixes

## File Path
`ssot.learning.post-restart-fixes.2026-09-21.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Post-Restart Recovery Lessons (2026-09-21)
subtitle: Issues found after rebooting tony-dell and tony-omen, and their permanent fixes
date: "2026-09-21"
icon: 🔧
context: |
  Both tony-dell and tony-omen were rebooted. Post-restart verification revealed three
  configuration issues that caused services to fail on every boot. All three were fixed
  permanently so they won't recur on future reboots.

lessons:
  - id: system-caddy-port-conflict
    title: System caddy.service steals port 80 from podman web.service
    severity: critical
    symptom: |
      After reboot, all HTTPS endpoints on tony-dell returned 502.
      The podman web.service (Caddy with the real chaba Caddyfile) was crash-looping
      (restart count 70) with "bind: address already in use" on port 80.
    root_cause: |
      A system-level caddy.service (default Ubuntu install, enabled) auto-starts on boot
      and binds port 80 with the default Caddyfile (serving /usr/share/caddy).
      The podman web.service (rootless, with the real chaba Caddyfile) cannot bind port 80.
    fix: |
      Stopped and disabled the system caddy.service:
        sudo systemctl stop caddy && sudo systemctl disable caddy
      The podman web.service now binds port 80 correctly on boot.
    prevention: |
      The system caddy.service is now disabled. Do not re-enable it.
      If a package upgrade re-enables it, disable it again.
    files_changed:
      - system: /etc/systemd/system/multi-user.target.wants/caddy.service (removed)

  - id: tailscale-serve-stale-port
    title: Tailscale Serve proxies HTTPS:443 to dead port 8085
    severity: critical
    symptom: |
      Even after Caddy was running, HTTPS via Tailscale (https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net)
      returned 502. HTTP on port 80 worked fine.
    root_cause: |
      Tailscale Serve was configured to proxy HTTPS:443 → http://127.0.0.1:8085,
      but nothing listens on port 8085. No reference to 8085 exists anywhere in the repo.
      The config was stale — likely from a previous architecture where a listener was on 8085.
      Caddy listens on port 80, not 8085.
    fix: |
      Repointed Tailscale Serve to port 80:
        sudo tailscale funnel --bg --https 443 --yes http://127.0.0.1:80
      This also re-enabled Funnel (the `tailscale serve` command removed it; `tailscale funnel`
      re-added it). All HTTPS endpoints now return 200.
    prevention: |
      Tailscale Serve config is now: HTTPS:443 → http://127.0.0.1:80 (Caddy).
      If port 8085 is ever referenced again, it's wrong — Caddy is on port 80.
    note: |
      The `tailscale serve set-config` command with legacy JSON format was ignored
      (warnings about deprecated format). Use `tailscale serve`/`tailscale funnel` CLI
      commands directly to update the config.

  - id: chaba-tunnel-stale-lan-ip
    title: chaba-tunnel uses stale LAN IP for tony-omen
    severity: high
    symptom: |
      chaba-tunnel.service (reverse SSH tunnel from tony-dell to tony-omen) was
      crash-looping with "Connection refused" to 192.168.1.48:22.
    root_cause: |
      The systemd unit hardcoded tony-omen's LAN IP as 192.168.1.48.
      After tony-omen rebooted, its LAN IP changed to 192.168.2.86 (DHCP).
      The tunnel couldn't reach the old IP.
    fix: |
      Updated the ExecStart in chaba-tunnel.service to use the Tailscale hostname
      `tony-omen` instead of the hardcoded LAN IP:
        sed -i 's/tony@192.168.1.48/tony@tony-omen/' \
          ~/.config/systemd/user/chaba-tunnel.service
      Tailscale hostnames are stable across reboots and IP changes.
    prevention: |
      Never hardcode LAN IPs in systemd units or scripts. Use Tailscale hostnames
      (e.g., `tony-omen`) or Tailscale IPs (e.g., `100.75.102.88`) which are stable.
    files_changed:
      - host: /home/tony/.config/systemd/user/chaba-tunnel.service (on tony-dell)

  - id: barrier-client-xauthority-check
    title: barrier-client ExecStartPre waits for non-existent Xauthority file
    severity: high
    symptom: |
      barrier-client.service was stuck in "activating (start-pre)" after every reboot.
      Barrier KVM client never started.
    root_cause: |
      The ExecStartPre checked for /run/user/1000/gdm/Xauthority, but this file is never
      created on tony-dell's setup. The Xorg on :1 runs as root via GDM without a per-user
      Xauthority file. X connections to :1 work without any Xauthority (xhost-based auth).
      The /run/user/1000/gdm/ directory doesn't even exist.
    fix: |
      Removed the Xauthority check from ExecStartPre, keeping only the X socket check:
        [ -S /tmp/.X11-unix/X1 ] && exit 0
      (was: [ -S /tmp/.X11-unix/X1 ] && [ -r /run/user/1000/gdm/Xauthority ] && exit 0)
    prevention: |
      Don't check for Xauthority files that may not exist. The X socket (/tmp/.X11-unix/X1)
      is sufficient to verify the display is ready.
    files_changed:
      - host: /home/tony/.config/systemd/user/barrier-client.service (on tony-dell)

  - id: barrier-client-stale-lan-ip
    title: barrier-client-run.sh hardcodes tony-omen LAN IP
    severity: medium
    symptom: |
      barrier-client-run.sh hardcoded 192.168.2.86 as tony-omen's LAN IP.
      This breaks every time tony-omen's DHCP-assigned LAN IP changes.
    root_cause: |
      The script preferred LAN for lower latency but hardcoded the IP.
      After tony-omen rebooted, the IP changed and the LAN path would fail.
    fix: |
      Updated the script to resolve tony-omen's IP dynamically from
      `tailscale status` output, with a Tailscale IP fallback (100.75.102.88).
      The script now re-evaluates on every service restart.
    prevention: |
      Never hardcode LAN IPs in scripts. Resolve dynamically or use Tailscale
      hostnames/IPs which are stable.
    files_changed:
      - host: /home/tony/.local/bin/barrier-client-run.sh (on tony-dell)

  - id: network-scan-startup-race
    title: network-scan-tony.service races tony-ha on boot
    severity: low
    symptom: |
      network-scan-tony.service failed on first boot attempt because tony-ha wasn't
      ready yet (ConnectionRefused on 127.0.0.1:8123).
    root_cause: |
      The service runs early in boot and tries to connect to tony-ha before HA is
      fully started. No dependency ordering on tony-ha.service.
    fix: |
      Manually restarted after tony-ha was ready. The service has a timer that
      retries every ~15 minutes, so it self-heals.
    prevention: |
      Consider adding After=tony-ha.service or a retry loop in the ExecStartPre
      that waits for port 8123 to be available before running the scan.

general_principles:
  - |
    Never hardcode LAN IPs in systemd units, scripts, or configs. DHCP-assigned IPs
    change on reboot. Use Tailscale hostnames (tony-omen, tony-dell) or Tailscale IPs
    (100.x.x.x) which are stable across reboots and network changes.
  - |
    After a reboot, check for port conflicts between system services and user/podman
    services. A default-installed system service (like caddy.service) can auto-start
    and steal a port that a podman container needs.
  - |
    Tailscale Serve/Funnel config can become stale. Verify the proxy targets after
    architecture changes. Use `tailscale serve status` to audit, and `tailscale serve`/
    `tailscale funnel` CLI commands (not set-config with legacy JSON) to update.
  - |
    Xauthority files are not always present. On GDM-managed Xorg sessions, the X server
    may run as root without a per-user Xauthority. Check whether X connections actually
    need auth before requiring an Xauthority file in ExecStartPre.

```

```yaml
  type: flatbed only (no ADF)
  escl_url: https://192.168.2.74/eSCL   # also http://192.168.2.74:8080/eSCL
  sane_device: "airscan:e0:HP DeskJet 2700 series [05C516]"   # the working backend
  resolutions: [75, 100, 200, 300, 600, 1200]   # discrete steps only
  formats: [image/jpeg, application/pdf, application/octet-stream]
  max_area: 2550x3508 in 1/300in units (~A4/Letter flatbed)
  cli_scan: "scanimage -d 'airscan:e0:HP DeskJet 2700 series [05C516]' --format=png --resolution 300 -o out.png"
  pdf_scan: "scan-doc ~/scan.pdf 300   # ~/bin/scan-doc, raw-eSCL client, most reliable"
  gui: simple-scan (installed 2026-09-21) — pick the "eSCL HP DeskJet 2700" device, not webcam
  disabled_backends:
    - "escl in /etc/sane.d/dll.conf — sends 'escl:ThreeHundredthsOfInches', firmware rejects with HTTP 409, error surfaces as misleading 'Document feeder out of documents'"
    - "hpaio in /etc/sane.d/dll.d/hplip — 'Error during device I/O'; hp-scan hangs"
  thunar_print_action: "uca.xml 'Print' action runs `lp %F` for pdf/jpg/png/gif/tif/bmp/txt/ps → HP-DeskJet-2700 queue"

lessons:
  - id: printer-verification-flow
    title: Verify a network printer without CUPS
    severity: info
    detail: |
      lpinfo -v and ippfind discover it via mDNS. ipptool with a Get-Printer-Attributes
      test file against ipp://<host>.local/ipp/print returns printer-state,
      printer-is-accepting-jobs, and marker-levels (ink %). Ping + /dev/tcp port check
      confirms reachability. A test page via the CUPS queue exercises the full path.

  - id: iphone-wifi-direct-not-a-thing
    title: iOS has no Wi-Fi Direct pairing — "DIRECT-xx" is just a Wi-Fi network
    severity: important
    detail: |
      Android/Mopria negotiate Wi-Fi Direct peer-to-peer; iOS does not. For iPhone,
      "print via Wi-Fi Direct" means: Settings → Wi-Fi → join the printer's DIRECT-xx
      SSID (WPA2 password from the printer's Wi-Fi Direct guide / EWS), accept the
      "no internet" warning, then print via normal AirPrint. If the iPhone is on the
      home LAN instead, plain AirPrint should already work — Wi-Fi Direct is only
      needed away from the home network.

  - id: airprint-mdns-checklist
    title: AirPrint discovery is pure mDNS TXT
    severity: info
    detail: |
      AirPrint needs _ipp._tcp/_ipps._tcp adverts whose TXT includes pdl with
      image/urf, a URF capability string, rp=ipp/print, and ty. Verified with python
      zeroconf ServiceBrowser (avahi-browse not installed). If the phone and printer
      are on different SSIDs (extender, guest VLAN) or the router filters multicast,
      discovery silently fails even though the printer is reachable by IP.

  - id: deskjet-2700-notes
    title: HP DeskJet 2700 quirks seen here
    severity: info
    detail: |
      Tri-color cartridge reported markerInkAlmostEmpty at ~20% (black ~60%). During
      a job the printer reports spool-area-full-report — benign HP quirk, not an
      error. EWS root is a JS SPA; DevMgmt XML endpoints (DiscoveryTree.xml,
      NetAppsDyn.xml) expose real config without a browser.

  - id: escl-scanjob-hp-quirks
    title: HP eSCL ScanJob must be minimal — pwg:InputSource, no ScanRegions
    severity: important
    detail: |
      POST /eSCL/ScanJobs returns 409 Conflict unless the ScanSettings use
      <pwg:InputSource>Platen</pwg:InputSource> (not scan:InputSource) and OMIT
      <pwg:ScanRegions> entirely — sending even a valid region (2550x3508,
      ThreeHundredthsOfInches) gets 409. HTTP 503 means a stale job is still
      open: DELETE it via the JobUri in /eSCL/ScannerStatus. Fetch the page at
      {JobUrl}/NextDocument, then DELETE the job. Working client: ~/bin/scan-doc.

  - id: sane-backend-selection
    title: Scanning this DeskJet requires the airscan backend, not escl/hpaio
    severity: important
    detail: |
      scanimage -L listed escl, hpaio, and airscan devices for the same scanner.
      escl fails (malformed ContentRegionUnits value — see escl-scanjob-hp-quirks),
      hpaio fails I/O, hp-scan hangs on probe. sane-airscan scans fine. Fix:
      comment out `escl` in /etc/sane.d/dll.conf and `hpaio` in
      /etc/sane.d/dll.d/hplip so GUI apps (simple-scan) auto-pick airscan.
      Reversible by uncommenting.

  - id: network-context
    title: LAN context for future debugging
    severity: info
    detail: |
      Home SSIDs: TONY-WIFI_5G, TONY-WIFI_2.4G, TONY-WIFI_2.4G-ext (extender —
      possible client isolation). Router bridges 2.4G/5G and passes mDNS (verified:
      tony-dell on 5G discovered printer on same subnet 192.168.2.0/24). If iPhone
      AirPrint fails on LAN, check for guest network / VPN / Private Relay first.
```

# Session Close & Learning Workflow

How to finish a working session, capture learnings, and improve

## File Path
`ssot.learning.session-close.2026.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Session Close & Learning Workflow
subtitle: How to finish a working session, capture learnings, and improve
icon: 🧠
ideas:
  - Capture the lessons from the first 'finish and close' workflow
  - Define the trigger phrases that mean 'wrap up and commit/push'
  - Document how the agent should respond to 'what have we learnt? how can we improve?'
  - Keep a record of errors, workarounds, and future improvements

sections:
  - title: Finish and Close Trigger Phrases
    icon: 🔚
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Trigger phrases
        text: |
          Phrases like 'Let's finish and close', 'finish and close', 'session closed', or
          'what have we learnt? how can we improve?' are treated as session-end / retrospective
          triggers. Normalize extra whitespace and punctuation before matching.
      - label: Trigger aliases
        text: |
          Also treat these as close/finish triggers when they clearly mean 'end this session':
          'finish', 'close', 'wrap up', 'wrap it up', 'close this out', 'end session',
          'close session', 'session complete', 'we are done', 'done for now', 'that is all'.
      - label: Required actions
        text: |
          When triggered, the agent should summarize the session, run SSOT validation, commit
          pending repo changes with a generated or provided message, push to origin if asked,
          report the final status, and end with 'Session closed.'

  - title: What This Session Taught Us
    icon: 🎓
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Generic checkpoint commits are acceptable
        text: |
          When the user has many mixed, uncommitted edits and explicitly asks for 'everything',
          a generic 'checkpoint' commit is better than losing work or leaving the working tree dirty.
      - label: Pre-commit bloat warnings can block commits
        text: |
          The husky pre-commit hook may fail due to SSOT bloat warnings. Prefer running
          node scripts/ssot-optimize.mjs and splitting the file; if that is not practical for
          the current session, use git commit --no-verify and document the reason.
      - label: Always double-check git status
        text: |
          After a large git add -A and any git reset HEAD, run git status --short. A malformed
          reset can accidentally unstage unrelated files and leave them out of the commit.
      - label: Push only when explicitly requested
        text: |
          Do not push unless the user explicitly asks for it ('push', 'push/etc.', or similar).
          When pushing, use git push -u origin <branch> and report the remote tracking status.
      - label: Remote macbook services can be started via mcp_debug
        text: |
          macbook podman/redis and playlived/Chrome CDP can be started remotely using python3
          subprocess.Popen with start_new_session=True and full paths to podman/node. The
          playlive-macbook-tunnel service on tony-dell must forward to macbook 127.0.0.1:9222
          because headless Chrome binds to the IPv4 loopback address.

  - title: MCP and VMS session lessons
    icon: book
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: MCP list_tools is the real post-restart health check
        text: |
          Service active, port listening, and HTTP 200 are not enough for embedded MCP servers.
          A successful mcp_list_tools call validates transport, auth, server startup, and
          protocol compatibility. The post-restart SSOT now includes an explicit step that runs
          mcp_list_tools for every configured Devin MCP server after restart.
      - label: ha_mcp_tools needs a longer startup timeout
        text: |
          The in-process HA MCP server can take minutes to start on HA 2026.9.0 under load.
          The _READY_STALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS/_READY_TOTAL_CAP_SECONDS constants in
          embedded_server.py were raised from 90s/600s to 300s/900s for both tony-ha and
          michael-dev to prevent false timeout and port-collision retries.
      - label: GitHub MCP needs a stdio handshake proxy
        text: |
          The github-mcp-server stdio transport is sensitive to early reads and large tool
          catalog responses. Using mcp-github-proxy.py to gate the handshake and read the
          token from ~/.config/secrets/github-mcp.env makes tool listing reliable.
      - label: michael-dev cannot run Home Assistant add-ons
        text: |
          michael-dev is a Home Assistant Container install (rootless Podman), not HA OS,
          so Grafana and other add-ons cannot be installed inside it. A standalone Grafana
          plus InfluxDB container on tony-dell would be required for dashboard development.
      - label: cast-browser-server can cast any workspace to the TV
        text: |
          POST /nav with {"url": "workspace:4"} captures the X desktop of workspace 4 and
          casts a PNG to media_player.tony_tv_cast. For live streaming use
          screenlive:workspace:4, which starts cast-desktop@1 and plays the HLS camera
          stream on the selected TV.

  - title: tony-omen crash-check lessons (2026-09-11)
    icon: 🖥️
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Verify 'crashed' hosts over Tailscale, not LAN DNS
        text: |
          tony-omen looked down because LAN resolution returned the stale IP 192.168.1.48
          (LAN is now 192.168.2.x). tailscale ping + ssh tony-omen showed it was up 4 days.
          Always confirm via tailnet hostname/IP before assuming a host crashed.
      - label: dockerd/containerd churn can look like a crash
        text: |
          The reported 'crash' was actually ~23% CPU each on dockerd and containerd since
          Sep 10, driving load to ~5.9. Check ps aux --sort=-%cpu before rebooting so the
          real culprit is recorded; an unhealthy container (mddb-chat-widget) was present.
      - label: Journal vacuum is the defined pre-reboot 'vacuum'
        text: |
          'Run vacuum' maps to sudo journalctl --vacuum-size=500M in
          scripts/system-maintenance.mjs. sudo -n works over SSH on tony-omen.
          Freed 44.7M (530.3M -> 485.6M).

  - title: How to Improve
    icon: 🚀
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Create a finish-and-close skill
        text: |
          Add .devin/skills/finish-and-close/SKILL.md that formalizes the trigger phrases,
          validation, commit / push flow, and the 'Session closed.' response.
      - label: Better commit messages
        text: |
          When the user does not supply a commit message, inspect git diff --stat and split
          changes into 1-2 focused commits with descriptive messages instead of one large 'checkpoint'.
      - label: Auto-catch leftover changes
        text: |
          After git commit, run git status --short. If anything remains, do a second focused
          commit automatically and warn the user before closing.
      - label: SSOT bloat handling
        text: |
          When ssot-optimize reports bloat, try to extract a child SSOT or split the section
          before falling back to --no-verify. Update the parent SSOT to reference the child.
      - label: Persistent macbook services
        text: |
          Create launchd plists for playlived + Chrome and for redis-macbook via podman so the
          services survive reboot without manual SSH commands.

  - title: Devin sessions.db cleanup on tony-omen (2026-09-12)
    icon: 🗄️
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Time-based pruning misses the real bloat
        text: |
          sessions.db was 71G but 0 sessions were older than 7 days and only 20 (small) older
          than 3. ~66G sat in 7 sessions from the last 48h. Before pruning, check per-session
          size: SELECT s.id, COUNT(m.row_id), SUM(LENGTH(m.chat_message)) FROM sessions s
          JOIN message_nodes m ON m.session_id=s.id GROUP BY s.id ORDER BY 3 DESC.
          Targeted session-id deletes may beat retention windows.
      - label: Corrupt DB breaks mid-prune and hides rows
        text: |
          DELETE FROM sessions failed with 'database disk image is malformed' (likely from the
          Sep 10-11 crash). A damaged index under-counted sessions (156 visible vs 180 real).
          Fix: rebuild with `sqlite3 sessions.db .recover | sqlite3 sessions-new.db`, prune the
          clean copy, verify `PRAGMA integrity_check`, then swap files. prune-devin-sessions.sh
          now runs a quick_check preflight (SKIP_INTEGRITY_CHECK=1 to bypass).
      - label: .recover notes
        text: |
          .recover exits non-zero after hitting the bad page but still writes all salvageable
          rows — do not trust set -e/pipefail around it; verify the new DB with integrity_check.
          The 'sqlite_sequence reserved name' parse error in the replay is harmless.
      - label: Operational details
        text: |
          Killed mid-VACUUM leaves a hot -journal file; the next sqlite3 open rolls it back
          automatically (run a trivial query first). A plain `cp` backup of a WAL-mode DB
          captures only the main file, not uncheckpointed -wal commits. Final result:
          sessions.db 71G -> 4.0G, cli dir 65G -> 4.6G, 153 sessions kept, integrity ok.

  - title: Future Triggers
    icon: 🔔
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: "what have we learnt? how can we improve?"
        text: |
          When asked, produce a brief summary and then create or append a learning/improvement
          SSOT like this one. Validate the new SSOT, commit it to the current branch, and end
          with 'Session closed.'
```

# SSOT Maintenance Framework

## File Path

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: SSOT Maintenance Framework
subtitle: Systematic maintenance schedule, quality metrics, and change tracking for SSOT files
icon: 🔧

ideas:
  - Ensure SSOT files remain accurate, consistent, and valuable over time
  - Prevent drift between SSOT and actual system state
  - Maintain high quality standards for SSOT content
  - Provide systematic approach to SSOT updates and reviews
  - Enable rollback capability for critical changes

maintenance_schedule:
  - title: Daily Automated Checks
    icon: 📅
    frequency: daily
    automated: true
    owner: system
    tasks:
      - label: YAML Syntax Validation
        description: Run automated YAML syntax check on all SSOT files
        tool: pre-commit hook
        failure_action: block commit
      - label: Hostname Compliance Check
        description: Check for IP addresses vs .local hostnames
        tool: pre-commit hook
        failure_action: warning
      - label: URL Placeholder Validation
        description: Ensure URL placeholders are properly quoted
        tool: pre-commit hook
        failure_action: block commit
      - label: Cross-Reference Validation
        description: Validate references between SSOT files
        tool: ssot-validate skill
        failure_action: warning
      - label: Bloat Threshold Check
        description: Count lines, sections, and items per SSOT file and warn when review or hard thresholds are exceeded
        tool: ssot-validate skill
        failure_action: warning

  - title: Weekly Quality Review
    icon: 📊
    frequency: weekly
    automated: false
    owner: tony
    tasks:
      - label: SSOT Health Check
        description: Review SSOT file health, completeness, and consistency
        metrics:
          - File count and growth rate
          - Validation error rate
          - Outdated entry count
          - Cross-reference accuracy
          - Bloat threshold exceedance count (files above review / hard thresholds)
      - label: Content Freshness Check
        description: Review and update outdated entries, archive completed items
        focus:
          - Completed improvements in ssot.improvements.yml
          - Outdated service configurations
          - Stale documentation references
      - label: Index Consistency Check
        description: Ensure ssot.index.yml reflects actual file structure
        validation: compare index entries with actual files

  - title: Monthly Comprehensive Review
    icon: 🔄
    frequency: monthly
    automated: false
    owner: tony
    tasks:
      - label: Architecture Alignment Review
        description: Ensure SSOT reflects current system architecture
        checks:
          - Service configurations match actual deployments
          - Health check endpoints are accurate
          - MCP server definitions are current
          - Network profiles are valid
      - label: Dependency Analysis
        description: Review and update dependency relationships
        focus:
          - Service dependencies in health config
          - SSOT file cross-references
          - Tool and service dependencies
      - label: Documentation Sync
        description: Ensure SSOT and KB documentation are consistent
        validation: cross-reference SSOT with KB entries

  - title: Quarterly Strategic Review
    icon: 🎯
    frequency: quarterly
    automated: false
    owner: tony
    tasks:
      - label: SSOT Structure Evaluation
        description: Review SSOT organization and suggest improvements
        analysis:
          - File organization effectiveness
          - Information accessibility
          - Search result quality
          - User satisfaction metrics
      - label: Tool and Process Improvement
        description: Evaluate and improve SSOT maintenance tools
        focus:
          - Validation tool effectiveness
          - Automation coverage
          - Maintenance efficiency
          - User experience

quality_metrics:
  - title: File Health Metrics
    icon: 📈
    metrics:
      - label: YAML Syntax Validity
        target: 100%
        measurement: percentage of files with valid YAML syntax
        tracking: automated
      - label: Required Fields Coverage
        target: 100%
        measurement: percentage of files with all required fields
        tracking: automated
      - label: Hostname Compliance
        target: 95%
        measurement: percentage of hostnames using .local format
        tracking: automated
      - label: Cross-Reference Accuracy
        target: 95%
        measurement: percentage of valid cross-references
        tracking: manual

  - title: Content Quality Metrics
    icon: ✨
    metrics:
      - label: Content Freshness
        target: 90%
        measurement: percentage of entries updated in last 6 months
        tracking: manual
      - label: Completeness
        target: 85%
        measurement: percentage of entries with complete information
        tracking: manual
      - label: Consistency
        target: 90%
        measurement: percentage of entries following SSOT patterns
        tracking: manual
      - label: Accuracy
        target: 95%
        measurement: percentage of entries matching actual system state
        tracking: manual

change_tracking:
  - title: Change Management Process
    icon: 📝
    process:
      - label: Pre-Change Validation
        steps:
          - Run automated validation (pre-commit hook)
          - Review impact on dependent SSOT files
          - Check for breaking changes
          - Plan rollback strategy if needed
      - label: Change Documentation
        steps:
          - Update ssot.improvements.yml for significant changes
          - Document rationale and expected impact
          - Update related KB entries
          - Note any migration requirements
      - label: Post-Change Verification
        steps:
          - Validate all SSOT files pass validation
          - Test cross-references and dependencies
          - Verify index consistency
          - Run health checks if service config changed

  - title: Backup Strategy
    icon: 💾
    strategy:
      - label: Git-Based Versioning
        description: Use git for all SSOT file versioning
        benefits:
          - Complete change history
          - Easy rollback capability
          - Branch-based development
          - Automatic backup with every commit
      - label: Critical File Protection
        description: Additional protection for critical SSOT files
        files:
          - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.health.yml
          - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.mcp.yml
          - docs/ssot/ssot.improvements.yml
        protection:
          - Create backup tags before major changes
          - Maintain change log for critical modifications
          - Test changes in staging environment if applicable

  - title: Rollback Procedures
    icon: ↩️
    procedures:
      - label: Git Rollback
        steps:
          - Identify commit to rollback to: git log --oneline docs/ssot/
          - Create backup branch: git branch backup-$(date +%Y%m%d)
          - Rollback changes: git revert <commit-hash>
          - Validate rollback: run validation checks
      - label: Single File Recovery
        steps:
          - Find previous version: git log --follow --oneline <file>
          - Checkout specific version: git checkout <commit-hash> -- <file>
          - Validate recovered file
          - Commit restored version

automation_tools:
  - title: Pre-Commit Hook
    icon: 🔗
    location: .git/hooks/pre-commit
    features:
      - YAML syntax validation
      - Hostname compliance checking
      - URL placeholder validation
      - Required fields verification
    status: implemented

  - label: SSOT Validation Skill
    icon: 🛠️
    location: .agents/skills/ssot-validate/SKILL.md
    features:
      - Cross-file validation
      - Dependency checking
      - Pattern validation
      - Quality scoring
    status: available

  - label: SSOT Search Skill
    icon: 🔍
    location: .agents/skills/ssot-search/SKILL.md
    features:
      - Pattern-based SSOT search
      - Cross-reference discovery
      - Content analysis
    status: available

alerting:
  - title: Validation Failures
    icon: 🚨
    conditions:
      - label: Critical Validation Failure
        severity: critical
        action: block commit, notify user
        examples:
          - YAML syntax errors
          - Missing required fields
          - Invalid cross-references
      - label: Warning Level Issues
        severity: warning
        action: allow commit with warning
        examples:
          - Hostname compliance issues
          - Trailing whitespace
          - Minor formatting issues

  - title: Quality Degradation
    icon: 📉
    conditions:
      - label: Metric Threshold Breach
        severity: warning
        action: add to ssot.improvements.yml
        triggers:
          - YAML validity below 100%
          - Cross-reference accuracy below 90%
          - Content freshness below 80%
```

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Registry
subtitle: Master catalog of project assets — scripts, SSOTs, services, apps, and related artifacts
icon: 🗃️
version: 1
overview:
  purpose: 'One place to answer: "What things do we have, where do they live, what are they for,

    and what is their current status?" It does not replace per-file documentation; it

    provides a lightweight index and a status-aware map.

    '
  scope:
    - SSOTs and docs that are part of an active workflow
    - Scripts and daemons we maintain
    - Systemd user services and timers
    - h3 app pages under chaba-h3
    - Repos and stacks with active configuration
  out_of_scope:
    - Every line of source code
    - Generated build artifacts
    - Transient logs
schema:
  required:
    - id
    - name
    - type
    - path
    - purpose
    - status
  optional:
    - project
    - environment
    - owner
    - tags
    - related
    - added
    - last_verified
    - notes
types:
  - ssot
  - script
  - service
  - timer
  - h3-app
  - kb
  - repo
  - stack
  - config
statuses:
  - draft
  - active
  - stable
  - experimental
  - parked
  - deprecated
  - unknown
rules:
  - One entry per top-level asset; do not list every module inside a package.
  - The canonical id is kebab-case and stable.
  - The path should be the primary human-findable location.
  - "For user-config files outside the repo, set project: chaba and location: user."
  - Use related to link to SSOTs, services, scripts, or parent repos.
  - Keep purpose to one or two short sentences.
  - When a status changes to deprecated, add a deprecation note and keep the entry for 90 days.
  - Run scripts/registry-drafts.py periodically to find missing assets.
```

# Project Terminology

Canonical definitions for the Chaba assistant context, SSOT, and focus-decision vocabulary

## File Path
`ssot.terminology.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Project Terminology
subtitle: Canonical definitions for the Chaba assistant context, SSOT, and focus-decision vocabulary
icon: "\ud83d\udcd6"

ideas:
  - text: Reduce ambiguity between rules, memories, SSOT, KB, context, and focus/decision terms.
  - text: Provide a shared vocabulary for assistants, sub-agents, and users.
  - text: Feed the decision-tree optimization by making request-disposition terms explicit.

sections:
  - title: Core Concepts
    icon: "\ud83e\udde9"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Context
        text: The combined procedural and factual information an assistant uses in a session. Includes rules, memories, SSOT, and the KB.
      - label: Knowledge Base (KB)
        text: The markdown corpus in docs/kb/ plus the session memories tracked in docs/overview/ssot.kb.yml. Searched via MDDB.
      - label: Rules
        text: Always-on behavior instructions. Per-repo rules live in .windsurfrules; global/user-level rules live in ~/.codeium/windsurf/memories/global_rules.md and ~/.config/devin/ rules.
      - label: Memories
        text: Session-specific or user-specific learnings persisted for future sessions, including focus sessions, KB entries, and ai-context-*.md files.
      - label: SSOT
        text: Single Source of Truth. Authoritative, structured YAML files in docs/ssot/ that describe infrastructure, focus, apps, and policies.
      - label: MDDB
        text: Local semantic-search database that indexes the KB, SSOT, and other documentation for AI retrieval.
      - label: MCP
        text: Model Context Protocol. The server/tool layer that exposes services (mddb, github, health, etc.) to the assistant.

  - title: Focus and Decision Vocabulary
    icon: "\ud83c\udfaf"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Focus
        text: A tracked unit of multi-step work. A shared focus is not tied to a branch; a branch focus is.
      - label: Shared Focus
        text: A focus that is not tied to a specific branch or host.
      - label: Branch Focus
        text: A focus that is tied to a specific branch or host, such as tony-dell or macbook.
      - label: Parked
        text: A focus that was active but set aside, usually with the intent to return when the active work is completed.
      - label: Quick Win
        text: A small, concrete action completable in under ~5 minutes with no deploy, install, or destructive operation. Captured in ssot.focus.current.yml quick_wins.
      - label: Backlog
        text: Pending strategic work in ssot.focus.yml waiting for activation.
      - label: Inbox
        text: Draft focus items in docs/ssot/focus-inbox/ awaiting triage.
      - label: Triage
        text: Classifying an incoming request and recommending the correct focus action.
      - label: Disposition
        text: The outcome of triage, mapping to a canonical mcp_focus action.
      - label: Decision Tree
        text: The set of cases and conditions in ssot.focus.current.yml and docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.mcp-focus.yml that map a user request to a disposition.
      - label: mcp_focus actions
        text: Canonical actions returned by the focus tool — continue, quick_win, decompose, triage_backlog, triage_inbox, draft_inbox.
      - label: Subtask
        text: A smaller step within a focus.
      - label: Request Log
        text: A per-item record of user requests that map to a focus or quick win.
      - label: Session
        text: A single assistant-user interaction. Decisions, discoveries, and request logs are recorded per session.

  - title: Common Terminology Ambiguities
    icon: "\u26a0\ufe0f"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: momeries
        text: Misspelling of memories.
        recommendation: Use memories or session memories.
      - label: rules/momeries
        text: Ambiguous slash.
        recommendation: Use rules and memories or Devin/Windsurf rules and session memories.
      - label: both area
        text: Area should be plural or replaced with a single noun.
        recommendation: Prefer both areas or the combined space.
      - label: correct word to call both area
        text: Vague phrasing that conflates singular and plural.
        recommendation: Rephrase to What is the umbrella term for ...? or What should we call the combined ...?
      - label: decission
        text: Misspelling of decision.
        recommendation: Use decision.
      - label: adn
        text: Misspelling of and.
        recommendation: Use and.
      - label: ssot (lowercase)
        text: SSOT is an acronym.
        recommendation: Use SSOT when referring to the Single Source of Truth system or docs/ssot/.

  - title: Recommendations for Clearer Terminology
    icon: "\ud83d\udca1"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: Use the umbrella term context
        text: When you mean rules + memories + SSOT + KB together, say AI/project context or simply context.
      - label: Keep SSOT for structured YAML state
        text: Do not call the rules or the KB SSOT. SSOT is the docs/ssot/ YAML corpus.
      - label: Distinguish rules from memories
        text: Rules are static instructions; memories are session-generated learnings saved to the KB or ssot.kb.yml.
      - label: Use disposition for triage outcomes
        text: In decision-tree work, call the result of classifying a request its disposition, not answer or choice.
      - label: Prefer canonical action names
        text: When discussing the decision tree, use the exact mcp_focus action names — continue, quick_win, decompose, triage_backlog, triage_inbox, draft_inbox — to avoid misalignment.

  - title: Canonical Sources
    icon: "\ud83d\udccc"
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: docs/overview/ssot.kb.yml
        text: Chaba Knowledge Base & Session Memories — session learnings and corpus structure.
      - label: docs/kb/ai-context-*.md
        text: Personal context and preferences (general knowledge, tech stack, preferences).
      - label: docs/ssot/ssot.focus.current.yml
        text: Active focuses, quick wins, and the assistant-level decision tree cases.
      - label: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.mcp-focus.yml
        text: Machine-readable mcp_focus policy and canonical action definitions.
      - label: docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.focus-dispatcher.yml
        text: Focus-dispatcher runner, sub-agent contracts, and focus selection rules.
      - label: docs/ssot/ssot.file-control.yml
        text: SSOT file governance, naming, validation, and change workflow.
      - label: docs/ssot/ssot.validation-patterns.yml
        text: Validation rules and standard SSOT structure.
```

Comprehensive approach to reducing AI token costs across Devin and MCP infrastructure

## File Path

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: Token Optimization Strategy
subtitle: Comprehensive approach to reducing AI token costs across Devin and MCP infrastructure
icon: 💰

# Ideas and notes about token optimization
# This SSOT file serves as the central repository for token optimization strategies
ideas:
  - Reduce token consumption through multi-layered optimization approach
  - Implement filtering at MCP server level to reduce tool schema overhead
  - Add compression layer for data-heavy operations (database queries, file reads)
  - Optimize Devin configuration and usage patterns
  - Monitor and measure token usage to identify optimization opportunities
  - Balance cost reduction with operational efficiency

# Validation rules for token optimization
validation:
  require_benchmark: true
  require_rollback: true
  require_testing: true
  max_mcp_tools: 100
  enable_monitoring: true

# Main optimization sections
sections:
  - title: Token Optimization Tools
    icon: 🛠️
    layout: list
    items:
      - label: TokenShift
        text: Local Go binary for 10-20% token reduction via real-time tool-result filtering, CLI output trimming, and context deduplication
        type: endpoint-optimization
        savings: 10-20%
        installation: Single binary via MDM or manual
        best_for: Teams using multiple coding agents needing governance
        status: evaluated
        priority: medium
        implementation_effort: medium
        pros:
          - Cross-agent visibility and governance
          - Per-team model policies and tool restrictions
          - On-device security (only metrics leave machine)
          - Admin console for spend tracking
        cons:
          - Commercial product (not open-source)
          - Requires MDM or manual installation per endpoint
          - Overkill for single-user setups

      - label: Headroom
        text: Open-source proxy for 60-95% JSON reduction, 15-20% coding agent reduction, content-aware compression
        type: compression-layer
        savings: 15-95% (varies by content type)
        installation: uv tool install --python 3.13 "headroom-ai[all]"
        best_for: Data-heavy workflows, maximum compression
        status: operational
        priority: high
        implementation_effort: low
        pros:
          - Open-source and free
          - Transparent proxy (zero code changes)
          - Content-aware compressors (JSON, code, logs, diffs)
          - Reversible compression with caching
          - Multiple deployment modes
        cons:
          - Requires Python 3.13
          - Additional service to maintain
          - Proxy adds slight latency

      - label: MCP Filters (mcp-filter)
        text: Proxy MCP server for 72-91% reduction by filtering tool surfaces to only needed tools
```

# UI Policy

Decision rules and guardrails for chaba.h3, 8080 web stack, and Trade UI

## File Path
`ssot.ui.policy.yml`

## YAML Content
```yaml
title: UI Policy
subtitle: Decision rules and guardrails for chaba.h3, 8080 web stack, and Trade UI
icon: 🛡️
version: 1

overview:
  purpose: |
    Capture guardrails that shape UI implementation decisions. This SSOT is the
    authority for "what is allowed" and "what is preferred" so that design
    choices are consistent across chaba.h3, chaba (tony-omen) 8080 apps, and trade
    canvas pages. It does not describe tokens or components; see ssot.libs.yml
    for the component reference.
  scope:
    - Hosting and runtime constraints
    - URL/path conventions
    - Link, asset, and fetch rules
    - Branch, deploy, and synchronization rules
    - Security and mixed-content rules
  out_of_scope:
    - Color, typography, and spacing tokens (ssot.libs.yml)
    - Component API definitions (ssot.libs.yml)

policies:
  - id: h3-static-only
    title: chaba.h3 is static-only on Plesk
    status: accepted
    rule: |
      The chaba.h3 public site is served by Plesk PHP. Do not add Node, Docker,
      WebSocket, LAN-only APIs, or server-side state. PHP file IO is allowed but
      shell/process functions are blocked by disable_functions.
    applies_to:
      - chaba-h3/public/
    rationale: |
      Plesk shared hosting does not support long-running processes or dynamic
      runtimes. PHP same-origin proxies are acceptable if they only fetch
      public/cached data and do not shell out.
    consequences:
      - All dynamic APIs live in chaba (tony-omen) stacks or the 8080 Caddy stack
      - PHP proxies must keep upstream URLs server-side (e.g., mcp-savings.php)

  - id: explicit-index-paths
    title: Link to explicit /foo/index.html paths
    status: accepted
    rule: |
      Use explicit `/foo/index.html` URLs unless proxy-server.mjs has a directory
      special case. Do not rely on bare /foo/ redirects in Plesk or local dev.
    applies_to:
      - chaba-h3/public/apps
    rationale: |
      Directory-index and bare-URL behavior differs between local preview, Caddy,
      and Plesk. Explicit index.html avoids 404s and asset resolution bugs.
    consequences:
      - All internal app links use /foo/index.html
      - Proxy server directory special cases must be documented in ssot.h3.yml

  - id: absolute-asset-paths
    title: Use absolute asset/fetch paths
    status: accepted
    rule: |
      Use absolute paths such as `/data.json` and `/apps/foo/asset.css` instead of
      relative `data.json` or `asset.css`. This is required for directory-index
      pages and nested routes.
    applies_to:
      - chaba-h3/public/apps
    rationale: |
      Relative paths break when a page is served through a directory-index
      redirect or a nested URL.
    consequences:
      - All fetch calls use absolute paths
      - CSS/JS imports use /apps/... paths

  - id: chaba-h3-branch
    title: chaba-h3 work lives on the chaba.h3 branch
    status: accepted
    rule: |
      Work for chaba.h3.gizmo-thailand.com is done in /home/tony/CascadeProjects/chaba-h3
      and pushed to the chaba.h3 branch. Files are placed under chaba-h3/public/.
      The main web/public/ path is not served.
    applies_to:
      - chaba-h3
    rationale: |
      The deployed chaba.h3 site is built from a dedicated worktree and branch to
      avoid mixing Plesk PHP with Caddy 8080 content.
    consequences:
      - PRs for chaba.h3 target the chaba.h3 branch
      - Changes in chaba/stacks/web/public/ do not affect chaba.h3

  - id: https-mixed-content
    title: Avoid mixed-content HTTP requests from HTTPS chaba.h3
    status: accepted
    rule: |
      Pages served over HTTPS on chaba.h3 must not directly fetch HTTP endpoints.
      Use same-origin PHP proxies or HTTPS upstreams. Provide a cached fallback
      so the page still renders if the upstream is unreachable.
    applies_to:
      - chaba-h3/public
    rationale: |
      Browsers block public-HTTPS pages from fetching private HTTP .local or
      tailnet endpoints. A same-origin PHP proxy hides the HTTP upstream and
      allows a local cached fallback.
    consequences:
      - mcp-savings.php proxies tony-dell:9100 and falls back to a committed JSON
      - Any new live data needs a same-origin proxy or HTTPS upstream

  - id: 8080-tailnet-routing
    title: Caddy 8080 routes to tailnet IPs, not docker network names
    status: accepted
    rule: |
      For migrated services on tony-dell, Caddy reverse_proxy must use the
      100.68.142.13 tailnet IP and port, not docker network hostnames. Restart
      the web container after Caddyfile changes because bind mounts can retain
      stale inodes.
    applies_to:
      - stacks/web/Caddyfile
    rationale: |
      Cross-host services are not resolvable from the tony-omen Docker bridge.
      The tailnet IP and explicit port are reachable. Caddy container bind mounts
      can cache the old inode after the file is replaced.
    consequences:
      - Caddyfile upstreams use 100.68.142.13:<port>
      - docker restart web is required after Caddyfile edits

  - id: trade-ssot-driven
    title: Trade Canvas UI is SSOT-driven
    status: accepted
    rule: |
      Trade Canvas pages are configured by YAML SSOTs in trade/config/ssot/.
      Features are promoted from experimental (ssot.ui.compare2.yml / ssot.ui.feature.*.yml)
      to stable family SSOTs using promote-ui-feature.sh. Shared scripts are listed
      in family SSOTs and page SSOTs reference family defaults.
    applies_to:
      - trade/config/ssot
      - trade/tradecanvas-ui
    rationale: |
      SSOT-driven configuration makes page layout, feature activation, and
      script/version management auditable and scriptable.
    consequences:
      - promote-ui-feature.sh moves feature refs from compare2 to family SSOT
      - Family SSOTs (ssot.ui.compare-family.yml) hold shared scripts and defaults

related_files:
  - docs/ssot/ssot.libs.yml
  - docs/ssot/ssot.ui.yml
  - docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.h3.yml
  - stacks/web/Caddyfile

```
